assumptions_latex: After row and column permutations, variables are partitioned as \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_K)\).
Each local feasible set \(X_k\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n_k}\) may impose integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation has primal block-angular structure and becomes block-separable after removing its linking rows.

notation.meaning: local constraint matrix of block k
contribution of block k to the linking constraints

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the diagonal local blocks plus a common linking-row border convention.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer formulation has primal block-angular structure if, after permutations, it can be written as \[\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_k^{\mathsf T}x_k:\ A_kx_k=b_k\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K,\ \sum_{k=1}^{K}D_kx_k=d,\ x_k\in X_k\right\}.\] Equivalently, its constraint matrix has diagonal blocks \(A_1,\ldots,A_K\) and one linking-row border \((D_1,\ldots,D_K)\). Deleting the linking rows leaves \(K\) independent mixed-integer subsystems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A primal block-angular model consists of independent variable blocks and local constraints, coupled only by a common set of linking rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Primal Block-Angular Structure

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

assumptions_latex: After row and column permutations, variables are partitioned into local blocks \(x_k\) and a shared block \(y\).
The sets \(X_k\) and \(Y\) may include integrality restrictions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The formulation has dual block-angular structure and separates by block when the shared variables \(y\) are fixed.

notation.meaning: coefficient matrix of shared variables in subsystem k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the diagonal local blocks plus a common variable-column border convention.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer formulation has dual block-angular structure if, after permutations, it can be written as \[\min\left\{q^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_{k=1}^{K}c_k^{\mathsf T}x_k:\ A_kx_k+B_ky=b_k\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K,\ x_k\in X_k,\ y\in Y\right\}.\] Its constraint matrix has diagonal local blocks \(A_k\) and a common column border formed by the matrices \(B_k\). For every fixed feasible value of \(y\), the remaining optimization over \(x_1,\ldots,x_K\) decomposes into \(K\) independent subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual block-angular model has separate local variable blocks connected through a common block of border variables; fixing those variables yields independent subproblems.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Block-Angular Structure

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Shared-variable block-angular quadratic structure and splitting size
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic block-angular sparsity with peripheral blocks coupled through a common final variable block, together with the induced splitting scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P=\{J_1,\ldots,J_p\}\) partition the variable indices, with \(n_k=|J_k|\). A quadratic model has the stated block-angular structure if every relevant coefficient matrix has the form \[A_i=\begin{pmatrix}A_{i,1}&&&B_{i,1}\\&\ddots&&\vdots\\&&A_{i,p-1}&B_{i,p-1}\\B_{i,1}^T&\cdots&B_{i,p-1}^T&A_{i,p}\end{pmatrix}.\] For the associated splitting scheme, \(R_k=J_p\) for \(k<p\) and \(R_p=\varnothing\); its block sizes are \(n_1+n_p,\ldots,n_{p-1}+n_p,n_p\), and it introduces exactly \((p-1)n_p\) additional variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each peripheral variable block is coupled only to one common final block. The induced splitting scheme copies that common block for every peripheral block, giving the stated block sizes and exactly (p−1)n_p additional variables.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P=\{J_1,\ldots,J_p\}\) is a partition of the variable indices
Every relevant quadratic coefficient matrix \(A_i\) has the displayed shared-final-block sparsity pattern
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k=J_p\ \text{for }k<p,\quad R_p=\varnothing,\quad N_{\mathrm{additional}}=(p-1)n_p.

children.title: Bordered Block Structures
children.top_down_role: Block systems coordinated through a common border of variables or constraints.

assumptions_latex: Rows and columns have been partitioned into \(K\) local groups and optional border groups.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A bordered block matrix consists of a block-diagonal core together with row, column, or two-sided borders that contain all cross-block coupling.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers row-bordered, column-bordered, and doubly bordered block matrices.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming
Model Building in Mathematical Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix has bordered block structure if permutations put it in the form \[M=\begin{pmatrix}A_1&0&\cdots&0&B_1\\0&A_2&\cdots&0&B_2\\\vdots&\vdots&\ddots&\vdots&\vdots\\0&0&\cdots&A_K&B_K\\C_1&C_2&\cdots&C_K&E\end{pmatrix},\] with any of the row border \((C_1,\ldots,C_K,E)\), column border \((B_1^{\mathsf T},\ldots,B_K^{\mathsf T},E^{\mathsf T})^{\mathsf T}\), or both permitted to be absent. Thus every nonzero connecting distinct local blocks occurs through a designated border.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A bordered block matrix has a block-diagonal core, while all interactions among local blocks pass through designated border rows or columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Bordered Block Structures

children.title: Staircase Block Structures
children.top_down_role: Sequentially linked block systems with localized interstage coupling.

knowledge_statements.title: Staircase Block Structures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses a directed finite-width block-staircase convention; transposition gives the opposite orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=(M_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{K}\) be a matrix partitioned by ordered row and column stages. It has lower block-staircase structure of width \(w\) if \[M_{ij}=0\qquad\text{whenever}\qquad j>i\ \text{or}\ i-j>w.\] Thus block row \(i\) can contain nonzero blocks only in column stages \(\max\{1,i-w\},\ldots,i\). The upper block-staircase convention is obtained by transposition. In the one-step case \(w=1\), nonzero blocks occur only on the block diagonal and the first subdiagonal under the lower-staircase convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed staircase block matrix is ordered by stages, and each block row can involve only its own stage and a fixed number of immediately preceding stages; transposition gives the opposite orientation.
assumptions_latex: Rows and columns are ordered into stages \(1,\ldots,K\).
A fixed integer \(w\geq 0\) specifies the coupling width.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The matrix is a directed block staircase of width \(w\); each block row involves only its own stage and at most \(w\) immediately preceding stages.

notation.meaning: matrix block in row stage i and column stage j
maximum backward stage distance of a nonzero block

children.title: Border-to-Staircase Transformations
children.top_down_role: Structural reformulations connecting bordered layouts with staircase layouts.

assumptions_latex: A bordered formulation contains a shared variable vector \(y\) in every local subsystem.
Copies inherit the domain and integrality restrictions of \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing the border by local copies and connected consensus equalities yields an extended staircase formulation whose projection is exactly the original feasible set.

notation.meaning: copy of the border variable at stage k
projection that identifies the common copy value with y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extended-formulation transformation using chained equality constraints.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the original feasible set is \(F=\{(x,y): (x_k,y)\in F_k,\ k=1,\ldots,K\}\). Introduce local copies \(y_1,\ldots,y_K\) and define \[\widehat F=\{(x,y_1,\ldots,y_K):(x_k,y_k)\in F_k,\ y_k=y_{k+1}\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K-1\}.\] The copy equalities form a block-bidiagonal staircase. Under the projection \(\pi(x,y_1,\ldots,y_K)=(x,y_1)\), \[\pi(\widehat F)=F.\] Hence the transformation preserves feasibility and objective values when every occurrence of \(y\) in the objective is replaced consistently by an equal copy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Copy the border variables into each block and connect adjacent copies by equalities. The resulting staircase formulation projects exactly to the original bordered model.
knowledge_statements.title: Border-to-Staircase Transformations

source_witnesses.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88

assumptions_latex: The feasible set is represented in variables \((x_1,\ldots,x_K,y)\).
All cross-block dependence is mediated by \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(y\) is complicating precisely when fixing it leaves a Cartesian product of local feasible sets.

notation.meaning: local feasible set at parameter y
fiber of the global feasible set at y

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines complicating variables by conditional separability of the feasible fiber.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X_1\times\cdots\times X_K\times Y\) be a mixed-integer feasible set, and for \(y\in Y\) define its fiber by \[F(y)=\{(x_1,\ldots,x_K):(x_1,\ldots,x_K,y)\in F\}.\] The vector \(y\) is a set of complicating variables for the prescribed block partition if there exist sets \(F_k(y)\subseteq X_k\) such that \[F(y)=F_1(y)\times\cdots\times F_K(y)\qquad\text{for every }y\in Y.\] Thus fixing \(y\) removes all coupling among the local variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complicating variables are shared variables whose fixation makes the remaining feasible set a Cartesian product of independent block feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Complicating Variables

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

assumptions_latex: Variables are partitioned into local vectors \(x_1,\ldots,x_K\).
Local restrictions are represented by sets \(X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraints \(\sum_k L_kx_k\in Q\) are linking constraints because deleting them leaves the Cartesian product \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_K\).

notation.meaning: block contribution to the coupling system

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Covers equality and inequality coupling through a common affine system.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a block-partitioned feasible set \[F=\left\{(x_1,\ldots,x_K):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^{K}L_kx_k\in Q\right\},\] the system \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}L_kx_k\in Q\) is a set of linking constraints if deleting that system leaves exactly \(X_1\times\cdots\times X_K\). Equality linking uses \(Q=\{b\}\); componentwise inequality linking uses \(Q=\{u:u\leq b\}\). Each linking constraint contains variables from at least two prescribed blocks, while every remaining constraint belongs to one block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linking constraints are the cross-block constraints whose removal leaves independent local feasible sets.
knowledge_statements.title: Linking Constraints

children.title: Variable Copying Constructions
children.top_down_role: Duplicated local representations used to separate coupled blocks.

assumptions_latex: A variable vector \(y\in Y\) occurs in each local feasible relation \((x_k,y)\in F_k\).
Every copy \(y_k\) has the same domain and integrality restrictions as \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The copied formulation with \(y_k=y\) is an exact extended formulation of the original model.

notation.meaning: local copy assigned to block k

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact copying construction before relaxation or dualization of consensus.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \[F=\{(x,y):(x_k,y)\in F_k\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K,\ y\in Y\},\] introduce one copy \(y_k\in Y\) per block and define \[\widehat F=\{(x,y,y_1,\ldots,y_K):(x_k,y_k)\in F_k,\ y_k=y\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K\}.\] Projection onto \((x,y)\) satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,y}(\widehat F)=F\). If the objective is block-separable after replacing occurrences of \(y\) by \(y_k\), the only remaining cross-block restrictions are the copy equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replace each occurrence of a shared variable by a block-local copy and equate every copy to the original; projection recovers the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable Copying Constructions

children.title: Consensus Constraint Systems
children.top_down_role: Consistency structures that reconcile local variable copies.

assumptions_latex: There are copies \(y_1,\ldots,y_K\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\).
An undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) has \(V=\{1,\ldots,K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The edge equalities enforce global consensus exactly if and only if the copy graph is connected.

notation.meaning: oriented node-edge incidence matrix of G

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Graph-incidence characterization of exact equality consensus.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an arbitrary orientation of \(G\). The edge-consensus system is \[y_i-y_j=0\quad\text{for every }\{i,j\}\in E,\] equivalently \[(B_G^{\mathsf T}\otimes I_p)\mathbf y=0.\] This system implies \(y_1=\cdots=y_K\) if and only if \(G\) is connected. More generally, its solutions are constant on each connected component of \(G\); hence a disconnected copy graph enforces only componentwise consensus and does not reproduce a single shared variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise equality constraints enforce one common copy value exactly when their graph is connected; otherwise consensus holds only within connected components.
knowledge_statements.title: Consensus Constraint Systems

children.title: Copy-Consensus Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination implications of coupling local copies through consistency requirements.

assumptions_latex: Each block has a nonempty feasible set \(Z_k\) and local objective \(f_k\).
Consensus is represented by \(\sum_{k=1}^{K}C_ky_k=0\).
Each block subproblem is solved globally at every iteration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a multiplier iterate and block solutions, with consensus residual \(r^t\) providing the stopping test.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian multiplier coordination for equality-coupled copy formulations.

source_refs.locator: 3.6 Lagrangian Decomposition via Copying Constraints p. 88
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming
Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\lambda^0\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\), and step sizes \(\alpha_t>0\), iteration \(t\) solves in parallel \[(x_k^t,y_k^t)\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{(x_k,y_k)\in Z_k}\bigl(f_k(x_k,y_k)+(\lambda^t)^{\mathsf T}C_ky_k\bigr),\qquad k=1,\ldots,K.\] It computes \(r^t=\sum_{k=1}^{K}C_ky_k^t\). If \(\|r^t\|\leq\varepsilon\), it stops and outputs \((\lambda^t,(x_k^t,y_k^t)_{k=1}^{K})\); otherwise it updates \[\lambda^{t+1}=\lambda^t+\alpha_t r^t\] and repeats. A prescribed iteration limit may replace successful residual termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve copy-separated Lagrangian subproblems, measure their consensus violation, update the consensus multipliers, and stop when the residual is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.title: Copy-Consensus Coordination

children.title: Complicating-Variable Projection
children.top_down_role: Projected representations over variables retained for coordination.

assumptions_latex: The feasible set satisfies \(F\subseteq X\times Y\), where \(Y\) is the domain of the complicating variables.
Projection is taken onto the \(y\)-coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The projected set \(P\) contains exactly those complicating-variable values admitting at least one feasible completion.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility projection onto a designated complicating-variable space.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) be the feasible set of a mixed-integer optimization problem in local variables \(x\) and complicating variables \(y\). The complicating-variable projection is \[P=\operatorname{proj}_{Y}(F)=\{y\in Y:\exists x\in X\ \text{such that }(x,y)\in F\}.\] Consequently, \(y\in P\) is equivalent to feasibility of the completion problem in \(x\), while \(y\notin P\) certifies that no assignment of the eliminated variables can extend \(y\) to a feasible point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The complicating-variable projection is the set of shared-variable values that can be completed by local variables to form a feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Complicating-Variable Projection

children.title: Parametric Value Functions
children.top_down_role: Subproblem value representations indexed by retained decisions.

assumptions_latex: For each \(y\in Y\), the fiber \(F(y)=\{x:(x,y)\in F\}\) is defined.
The extended-real convention assigns \(+\infty\) to an empty fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing the original objective over \(F\) is equivalent to minimizing the parametric value function \(v\) over \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extended-real value-function representation after eliminating local variables.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F\subseteq X\times Y\) and objective \(f:X\times Y\to\overline{\mathbb{R}}\), define \[v(y)=\inf\{f(x,y):x\in F(y)\},\qquad F(y)=\{x\in X:(x,y)\in F\},\] with \(\inf\varnothing=+\infty\). Then \[\inf_{(x,y)\in F}f(x,y)=\inf_{y\in Y}v(y)=\inf_{y\in\operatorname{proj}_{Y}(F)}v(y).\] If \(y^*\) minimizes \(v\) and some \(x^*\in F(y^*)\) attains its defining infimum, then \((x^*,y^*)\) is globally optimal for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A parametric value function records the best local objective attainable for each shared-variable value; minimizing it reproduces the original optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Parametric Value Functions

children.title: Projected Master Coordination
children.top_down_role: Master-level coordination induced by projected subproblem information.

knowledge_statements.title: Projected Master Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact value-function master coordinated through successively refined lower models and outer approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\inf\{c^{\top}y+d^{\top}x:(y,x)\in F\}\), define \(P=\{y:\exists x\ (y,x)\in F\}\) and \(\theta(y)=\inf\{d^{\top}x:(y,x)\in F\}\) for \(y\in P\). Initialize an outer approximation \(Y_0\supseteq P\) and a master function \(\underline{\theta}_0\) satisfying \(\underline{\theta}_0(y)\leq\theta(y)\) for every \(y\in P\). At iteration \(k\), solve \(y^k\in\arg\min_{y\in Y_k}\{c^{\top}y+\underline{\theta}_k(y)\}\). Evaluate the subordinate problem at \(y^k\); if it is infeasible, add a valid projected-feasibility constraint, and otherwise update an incumbent and add a valid value-function cut. Maintain \(P\subseteq Y_{k+1}\subseteq Y_k\) and \(\underline{\theta}_{k+1}(y)\geq\underline{\theta}_k(y)\) with \(\underline{\theta}_{k+1}(y)\leq\theta(y)\) for every \(y\in P\). Stop upon a valid infeasibility certificate or when the incumbent upper bound minus the master lower bound is at most \(\varepsilon\); in the latter case return the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coordinate projected variables by repeatedly solving an outer master, evaluating its subordinate problem, adding valid feasibility or value-function cuts, and returning an incumbent once its certified absolute gap is at most the tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is a specified mixed-integer feasible set, and all displayed infima are interpreted in the extended reals.
Every generated feasibility constraint preserves the exact projection \(P\), and every value-function cut underestimates \(\theta\) on \(P\).
Each solved master supplies a valid lower bound, and each finite incumbent supplies a valid upper bound.
\(\varepsilon\geq0\) is an absolute optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The maintained master value is a valid lower bound; if the stated finite-gap test is met, the returned incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal in absolute objective gap.

notation.meaning: exact projection of the original feasible set onto the coordinating variables
current outer approximation of the exact projection
current lower model of the value function

children.title: Projection Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits caused by weak, incomplete, or computationally inaccessible projected representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness boundary for projected feasibility and value-function models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\{y:\exists x\ (y,x)\in F\}\) and \(\theta(y)=\inf\{d^{\top}x:(y,x)\in F\}\) for \(y\in P\). The projected master \(\inf_{y\in\widehat P}\{c^{\top}y+\widehat\theta(y)\}\) is an exact value-function reformulation when \(\widehat P=P\) and \(\widehat\theta(y)=\theta(y)\) for every \(y\in P\). If instead \(P\subseteq\widehat P\) and \(\widehat\theta(y)\leq\theta(y)\) for every \(y\in P\), the projected-master infimum is a lower bound on the original infimum. Such a relaxation need not recover an original solution: a master optimizer may lie in \(\widehat P\setminus P\), may exploit a strict underestimate \(\widehat\theta(y)<\theta(y)\), or may correspond to a value-function infimum that is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using the exact projected domain and exact value function guarantees an exact reformulation. An outer projected domain or underestimated value function still yields a lower bound but need not yield a recoverable original solution.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is nonempty, and the original objective has a finite lower bound.
\(\widehat P\) and \(\widehat\theta\) define the proposed projected master.
All displayed infima are interpreted in the extended reals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outer projection and value underestimation preserve lower-bound validity under the stated conditions but do not by themselves preserve feasibility, attainment, or solution recovery.

notation.meaning: exact projection of the original feasible set

children.title: Inverse-Projection Representations
children.top_down_role: Extended representations that recover original feasible structures through generated objects.

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Projection Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifted convex-hull representation for a finite union of polyhedra.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\bigcup_{j=1}^{q}P_j\), where \(P_j=\{x:A_jx\leq b_j\}\) are nonempty bounded polyhedra. Define the lifted set by variables \(x^j\) and \(\lambda_j\): \[Q=\left\{(x,(x^j)_j,\lambda):x=\sum_{j=1}^{q}x^j,\ A_jx^j\leq b_j\lambda_j,\ \lambda_j\geq0,\ \sum_{j=1}^{q}\lambda_j=1\right\}.\] Then the inverse image \(Q\) is an extended convex formulation and its projection satisfies \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(S)\). Thus convex combinations are represented before eliminating the lifting variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite union of bounded polyhedra has a lifted perspective formulation whose projection onto the original variables equals its convex hull.
assumptions_latex: Each \(P_j\) is a nonempty bounded polyhedron.
The index set \(\{1,\ldots,q\}\) is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)=\operatorname{conv}(\bigcup_{j=1}^{q}P_j)\).

children.title: Block Convexification
children.top_down_role: Convexified descriptions of decomposable block feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of an uncoupled Cartesian product of blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty sets \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), the convex hull of their Cartesian product separates by block: \[\operatorname{conv}\left(\prod_{i=1}^{m}S_i\right)=\prod_{i=1}^{m}\operatorname{conv}(S_i).\] Consequently, before imposing any cross-block constraint, each nonconvex block may be replaced by its convex hull without changing the convex hull of the product. If block objectives \(f_i\) are also convexified through their epigraphs, the separable lifted relaxation is obtained by taking the product of the blockwise convexified epigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex hull of an uncoupled finite Cartesian product equals the product of the individual block convex hulls.
assumptions_latex: There are finitely many nonempty block sets \(S_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\).
Convex hull means the set of finite convex combinations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{conv}(\prod_i S_i)=\prod_i\operatorname{conv}(S_i)\).

children.title: Extended-Master Recovery
children.top_down_role: Recovery of original-space decisions from extended-master representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Extended-Master Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery from a finite-column blockwise convexified master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(i\), let available points be \(v_{ir}\in S_i\). Solve the extended master in weights \(\lambda_{ir}\): enforce \(x_i=\sum_r\lambda_{ir}v_{ir}\), \(\sum_r\lambda_{ir}=1\), \(\lambda_{ir}\geq0\), together with the coupling constraints. If every selected block has one positive weight, return those points as an original feasible solution. Otherwise, use the fractional weights to identify active block points, invoke a pricing or branching step to add points or enforce integrality, and re-solve. Stop with an original-feasible incumbent and a certified bound gap at most \(\varepsilon\), or with a valid infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a lifted column master, directly recover integral block selections when possible, and otherwise use pricing or branching until feasibility and the required bound gap are certified.
assumptions_latex: Every column \(v_{ir}\) belongs to the original block set \(S_i\).
Master coupling constraints are valid for the original model.
Pricing or branching preserves valid global bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A returned point assembled from one selected original column per block is feasible for the original block sets and satisfies the master coupling constraints.

children.title: Convexification Fidelity Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural limits of approximate or incomplete block convexification.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Fidelity Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cross-block constraints need not commute with blockwise convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For block sets \(S_i\) and a coupling set \(C\), one always has \[\operatorname{conv}\left(C\cap\prod_iS_i\right)\subseteq C\cap\prod_i\operatorname{conv}(S_i)\] when \(C\) is convex, but equality may fail. For example, take \(S_1=S_2=\{0,1\}\) and \(C=\{(x_1,x_2):x_1+x_2=1/2\}\). Then \(C\cap(S_1\times S_2)=\varnothing\), whereas \((1/2,0)\in C\cap([0,1]\times[0,1])\). Hence exact block convex hulls can still yield an inexact globally coupled relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexifying every block exactly may still lose global fidelity because convexification need not commute with intersection by coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a convex cross-block coupling set.
Each \(S_i\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Blockwise convexification is generally only a relaxation of the convex hull of the coupled nonconvex feasible set.

children.title: Coupling-Constraint Dualization
children.top_down_role: Dual treatment of constraints that link otherwise separable blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Coupling-Constraint Dualization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian dualization of linear equality constraints coupling nonconvex blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,m\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty, let \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\), let \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{p\times n_i}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Consider \(p^*=\inf\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}A_ix_i=b\}\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), define \(L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\top}(\sum_{i=1}^{m}A_ix_i-b)\) and \[q(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\top}b+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\inf_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\top}A_ix_i\}.\] The Lagrangian-dual value is \(d^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^p}q(\lambda)\). Weak duality gives \(q(\lambda)\leq p^*\) for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), hence \(d^*\leq p^*\), and evaluation of \(q\) separates across the blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing the linear coupling equality produces a separable Lagrangian dual function whose value at every multiplier is a lower bound on the primal minimization value.
assumptions_latex: All block and primal infima are interpreted in the extended reals.
The primal constraints and objective have exactly the displayed block-separable form.
The primal feasible set is nonempty and \(p^*>-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^p\), \(q(\lambda)\leq p^*\); consequently \(d^*\leq p^*\), and computing \(q(\lambda)\) decomposes into \(m\) block infima.

notation.meaning: linear contribution of block i to the coupling equality

children.title: Coordination Price Signals
children.top_down_role: Economic signals passed between coordinating systems plus local subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Coordination Price Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupling residuals are supergradients of the concave dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i(\lambda)\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+\lambda^{\top}A_ix_i\}\), and define the coupling residual \(g(\lambda)=\sum_iA_ix_i(\lambda)-b\). For every multiplier \(\mu\), \[q(\mu)\leq q(\lambda)+g(\lambda)^{\top}(\mu-\lambda).\] Thus \(g(\lambda)\) is a supergradient of the concave dual function. The component \(\lambda_j\) acts as the marginal coordination price for coupling row \(j\), while the sign and magnitude of \(g_j(\lambda)\) indicate the direction and scale of price adjustment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Block solutions produce a coupling residual that is a dual supergradient, so residual components provide mathematically valid price-adjustment signals.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed block minimum is attained at \(x_i(\lambda)\).
The coupling constraints are equalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g(\lambda)\) is a supergradient of \(q\) at \(\lambda\).

children.title: Price-Based Block Coordination
children.top_down_role: Organization of block responses around shared coordination prices.

knowledge_statements.title: Price-Based Block Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected supergradient coordination for a Lagrangian dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\), stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\geq0\). At iteration \(k\), independently compute \(x_i^k\in\arg\min_{x_i\in X_i}\{f_i(x_i)+(\lambda^k)^{\top}A_ix_i\}\), form \(g^k=\sum_iA_ix_i^k-b\), and update \[\lambda^{k+1}=\Pi_{\Lambda}(\lambda^k+\alpha_kg^k).\] Track the best dual value and any recovered primal-feasible incumbent. Stop when a prescribed iteration limit, \(\|g^k\|\leq\varepsilon\), or a certified primal-dual gap criterion holds; output the best dual bound and incumbent, if one exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve priced blocks independently, update prices by the projected coupling residual, and retain the best dual bound and any recovered feasible incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\Lambda\) is a nonempty closed convex multiplier set.
Each block subproblem is solved globally.
Projection \(\Pi_{\Lambda}\) is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every evaluated dual value is a valid lower bound, while primal optimality is certified only when a valid incumbent closes the stated gap.

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the multiplier set

children.title: Price Reliability Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Degeneracy, instability, or duality limitations affecting coordination signals.

knowledge_statements.title: Price Reliability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvex duality gaps limit the primal reliability of prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the integer problem \(p^*=\min\{x:x\in\{0,1\},\ x\geq1/2\}=1\), dualize \(1/2-x\leq0\) with \(\lambda\geq0\). Its dual function is \[q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}\left\{x+\lambda(1/2-x)\right\}=\min\{\lambda/2,1-\lambda/2\}.\] Hence \(d^*=\max_{\lambda\geq0}q(\lambda)=1/2<p^*\). Even the optimal price \(\lambda=1\) therefore supplies only a lower bound and does not certify primal optimality or uniquely recover the feasible optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In mixed-integer models, even an optimal coordination price can leave a positive duality gap and cannot alone certify or recover a primal optimum.
assumptions_latex: The inequality is dualized using a nonnegative multiplier.
Block minimization is performed over the original binary set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The example has duality gap \(p^*-d^*=1/2\), demonstrating the reliability boundary of price-only coordination.

children.title: Single-Block Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition centered on one distinguished separable block.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Block Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One subordinate optimization block coordinated through complicating variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A single-block decomposition of \[\min\{c^{\top}y+f(x):(y,x)\in F\}\] consists of a coordinating variable \(y\in Y\) and one subordinate block with feasible correspondence \(X(y)=\{x:(y,x)\in F\}\). Its block value is \(\theta(y)=\inf_{x\in X(y)}f(x)\), and the coordinated formulation is \[\inf_{y\in Y}\{c^{\top}y+\theta(y):X(y)\neq\varnothing\}.\] The designation concerns decomposition granularity: all variables optimized after fixing \(y\) belong to one block, regardless of internal sparsity within that block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A single-block decomposition fixes coordinating variables and sends all remaining variables to one subordinate problem represented by its parametric value function.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq Y\times\mathbb R^n\) is the original mixed-integer feasible set.
The infimum defining \(\theta(y)\) is interpreted in the extended reals.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value-function formulation has the same infimum as the original problem.

notation.meaning: single subordinate feasible set at y

children.title: Multiblock Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition with several independently represented or solved blocks.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiblock Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two or more subordinate blocks linked only through explicit coordination structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiblock decomposition of a structured problem uses \(m\geq2\) block variables \(x_i\in X_i\) and isolates all cross-block dependence in explicit coordinating variables or constraints. In the linearly coupled separable form, the problem is \[\inf\left\{\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^{m}A_ix_i=b\right\}.\] Conditional on a coordinating decision or multiplier, the block optimizations over \(X_i\) can be evaluated independently. Integrality and nonconvexity may remain inside any block; decomposition does not itself convexify them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A multiblock decomposition partitions variables into at least two locally constrained blocks and makes their remaining interaction explicit through coordination constraints or variables.
assumptions_latex: \(m\geq2\) and every \(X_i\) is nonempty.
The objective is block-separable and all cross-block constraints are displayed explicitly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing or fixing the explicit coordination structure leaves \(m\) independent block optimization problems.

notation.meaning: local feasible set of block i

children.title: Cross-Block Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination structures arising when multiple blocks share master decisions or resources.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination for block-separable MIP formulations with shared linking variables or constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider blocks indexed by \(k\in K\), local variables \(x^k\in X_k\), and a coordinator variable \(y\in Y\). Cross-block coordination is the enforcement of a coupling system \[A_0y+\sum_{k\in K}A_kx^k=b\] while block objectives and local constraints remain separable. A coordination state consists of common values of \(y\), or multipliers or cuts representing the linking system, communicated among block solves. It is consistent exactly when every block uses the same coordinator state and the assembled solution satisfies the coupling system.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cross-block coordination reconciles independently solved blocks by exchanging shared variables, multipliers, or cuts until all linking constraints and shared-variable agreements hold.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite and each \(X_k\) may contain continuous and integer restrictions.
The only interactions between distinct blocks occur through \(y\) or the displayed linking system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_0y+\sum_{k\in K}A_kx^k=b\) holds for the assembled coordinated solution.

notation.meaning: local feasible set of block k

children.title: Nested Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Decomposition in which one subproblem contains a further decomposition.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive decomposition in which a child subproblem is itself decomposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_0\) be an optimization problem and let \(T\) be a rooted tree. A nested decomposition assigns a subproblem \(P_v(z_{p(v)})\) to each nonroot node \(v\), parameterized by the decision \(z_{p(v)}\) of its parent. For every internal node \(v\), the value of \(P_v\) is represented using the value functions or valid approximations returned by its children. Evaluation therefore proceeds recursively from a node to its descendants, while bounds, cuts, or solutions are returned toward the root. Leaves are subproblems solved without further decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nested decomposition recursively decomposes subproblems; children evaluate or approximate value functions and return bounds, cuts, or solutions to their parents.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is finite and rooted.
Every child problem has a well-defined value, including an explicit infeasibility convention, for each parent decision passed to it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root representation composes the value information returned along the edges of \(T\).

children.title: Hierarchical Decomposition

knowledge_statements.title: Hierarchical Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tree-structured allocation of decisions and subproblems across modeling levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A hierarchical decomposition of an optimization problem is a rooted-tree organization \(T=(V,E)\) in which each node \(v\in V\) owns variables \(x_v\), local constraints, and an objective contribution, while each edge \((v,w)\in E\) carries specified coupling data between parent \(v\) and child \(w\). Variables or constraints not assigned to a common node may interact only through their ancestor-descendant interface data. The undecomposed feasible solutions are exactly the collections \((x_v)_{v\in V}\) satisfying every local constraint and every edge-coupling condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hierarchical decomposition assigns variables and constraints to levels of a rooted tree, with interactions confined to explicit parent-child interfaces.
assumptions_latex: \(T=(V,E)\) is a finite rooted tree.
Every original variable, constraint, and objective term has an assigned node or edge interface.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The original feasible set equals the set of nodewise-feasible assignments satisfying all edge interfaces.

children.title: Interlevel Coordination

knowledge_statements.title: Interlevel Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency and value-information exchange between adjacent levels of a decomposition hierarchy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every parent-child edge \((v,w)\), let \(s_{vw}\) be the interface decision supplied by parent \(v\), and let \(\phi_w(s_{vw})\) be the child value function. Interlevel coordination holds when the child is evaluated at the interface selected by its parent, the parent uses either \(\phi_w(s_{vw})\) or a valid bound on it, and all duplicated interface variables satisfy \[s_{vw}^{(v)}=s_{vw}^{(w)}.\] At termination, each retained child bound must be valid at the reported parent decision, and every edge-interface equality must hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adjacent levels are coordinated when they agree on interface decisions and parents use valid child value information at those decisions.
assumptions_latex: Each child value function has an explicit convention for infeasible interface decisions.
Any approximation communicated upward is a valid bound on the corresponding child value function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_{vw}^{(v)}=s_{vw}^{(w)}\) for every edge \((v,w)\), with valid child value information at the coordinated interfaces.

children.title: Recursive Decomposition Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Structural or computational limits on nesting depth plus hierarchical consistency.

knowledge_statements.title: Recursive Decomposition Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stopping boundary for finite recursive decomposition of structured subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(P)\) denote the children produced by decomposing a problem \(P\), and let \(\tau(P)\) be a terminal predicate. A recursive decomposition boundary is valid when: every recursive branch reaches some \(P\) with \(\tau(P)=1\) after finitely many calls; each terminal problem is solved or bounded by a specified nonrecursive oracle; and each nonterminal parent value is recovered exactly or bounded validly from its children. Equivalently, there exists a rank \(r(P)\in\mathbb{N}\) such that \(r(Q)<r(P)\) for every \(Q\in D(P)\) whenever \(\tau(P)=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recursive boundary is valid when every branch terminates at an oracle-solvable problem and child results yield valid parent values or bounds.
assumptions_latex: Every nonterminal decomposition produces finitely many children.
The terminal oracle declares infeasibility or returns a valid value or bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No recursive branch is infinite, and information propagated to the root remains valid.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Separable Benders value-function and master representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function representation obtained when fixing coupling variables separates an additively separable problem into independent block subproblems; includes the nonconvex-MINLP regularity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(P=\min\{\sum_{k=1}^p f_k(x_{J_k},y):g_k(x_{J_k},y)\le 0,\ k=1,\ldots,p,\ y\in Y\}\). If fixing \(y\) yields independent block subproblems \(P_k[y]\), then, for every \(y\) for which \(P[y]\) is feasible, \(v(y):=\operatorname{val}(P[y])=\sum_{k=1}^p\operatorname{val}(P_k[y])\). Hence the master representation is \(\operatorname{val}(P)=\inf_{y\in\widehat Y}v(y)\), where \(\widehat Y=\{y\in Y:P[y]\text{ is feasible}\}\); this infimum is a minimum when it is attained. For general nonconvex MINLP instances, \(v\) need not be convex or differentiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When fixing the coupling variable y separates an additively separable problem into independent block subproblems, the fixed-y value is the sum of the block optimal values. The original value is the infimum of this value function over feasible fixed-y choices, and it is a minimum when attained. For nonconvex MINLP instances, the value function need not be convex or differentiable.
assumptions_latex: Y\text{ is an arbitrary set}
P=\min\left\{\sum_{k=1}^p f_k(x_{J_k},y):g_k(x_{J_k},y)\le0,\ k=1,\ldots,p,\ y\in Y\right\}
\text{For each fixed }y,\text{ the variables and constraints separate into independent block subproblems }P_k[y]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v(y)=\sum_{k=1}^p\operatorname{val}(P_k[y])\quad(y\in\widehat Y),\qquad \operatorname{val}(P)=\inf_{y\in\widehat Y}v(y),\quad \widehat Y=\{y\in Y:P[y]\text{ is feasible}\};\text{ if attained, the infimum is a minimum.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Benders master reformulation via extreme rays and extreme points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear nonnegative recourse that is not unbounded above, represented by feasibility and optimality inequalities in the retained variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\phi(x)=\max\{hy:Gy\le d-Fx,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^p\}\) and \(U=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^m:uG\ge h\}\). Suppose \(\phi(x)<+\infty\) for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\). If \(\{v^t\}_{t=1}^T\) and \(\{u^s\}_{s=1}^S\) are the extreme rays and extreme points of \(U\), respectively, then the recourse problem at \(x\) is feasible if and only if \(v^t(d-Fx)\ge0\) for every \(t\). When it is feasible, \(\phi(x)=\min_{1\le s\le S}u^s(d-Fx)\). Consequently, \(\max_{x\in X}\{cx+\phi(x)\}\) has the Benders master reformulation \(\max\{cx+\eta:x\in X,\ \eta\in\mathbb R,\ v^t(d-Fx)\ge0\ \forall t,\ u^s(d-Fx)\ge\eta\ \forall s\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linear nonnegative recourse problem that is never unbounded above, the extreme rays of the dual polyhedron characterize subproblem feasibility. When the subproblem is feasible, the dual extreme points represent its value, yielding the feasibility and optimality inequalities of the Benders master problem.
assumptions_latex: \(\phi(x)=\max\{hy:Gy\le d-Fx,\ y\in\mathbb R_+^p\}\)

knowledge_statements.title: Complicating-Variable Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection underlying the exact Benders master feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=\{(y,x)\in Y\times X: Ay+Bx\ge b\}\), where \(y\) contains the complicating variables retained by the master. Their exact projected feasible set is \[\operatorname{proj}_y(F)=\{y\in Y:\exists x\in X\text{ such that }Ay+Bx\ge b\}.\] A Benders master represents this projection explicitly or through valid feasibility cuts. Thus a master point \(y\) is feasible for the original formulation exactly when the associated subproblem feasibility system in \(x\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact Benders master domain is the projection onto complicating variables: a master point is feasible precisely when some subproblem completion exists.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) and \(X\) include all domain restrictions on \(y\) and \(x\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y\in\operatorname{proj}_y(F)\iff\exists x\in X:Ay+Bx\ge b\).

knowledge_statements.title: Master Value-Function Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization representation of the Benders master using a recourse value function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+q^{\mathsf T}x:y\in Y,\ x\in X,\ Ay+Bx\ge b\},\] define \(Q(y)=\inf\{q^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Bx\ge b-Ay\}\), with \(Q(y)=+\infty\) when the subproblem is infeasible. The problem is exactly \[\inf_{y\in Y}\bigl(c^{\mathsf T}y+Q(y)\bigr).\] Introducing \(\theta\) gives the exact master \(\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\theta:y\in Y,\ \theta\ge Q(y)\}\); Benders cuts provide an outer description of the epigraph condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminating subproblem variables yields a master minimizing direct cost plus the subproblem value; an epigraph variable is constrained by Benders cuts.
assumptions_latex: The extended-real convention \(Q(y)=+\infty\) is used for infeasible subproblems.
The original objective is bounded below whenever its feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{(y,x)}(c^{\mathsf T}y+q^{\mathsf T}x)=\inf_{y\in Y}(c^{\mathsf T}y+Q(y))\).

knowledge_statements.title: Continuous Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders master whose retained complicating variables are continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A continuous Benders master is an epigraph master \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\theta:y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m,\ \theta\ge \ell_j(y)\ (j\in J),\ f_i(y)\le0\ (i\in I)\},\] in which every component of \(y\) is continuous. The functions \(\ell_j\) are valid lower estimators of the subproblem value function for minimization, and the inequalities \(f_i(y)\le0\) are valid feasibility cuts. With all necessary cuts included, its feasible epigraph equals the exact value-function epigraph over the projected feasible domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous Benders master retains only continuous complicating variables and represents recourse through valid optimality and feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) imposes no integrality restrictions.
Every retained optimality and feasibility cut is valid on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With a complete cut family, the master represents \(\min_{y\in Y}(c^{\mathsf T}y+Q(y))\).

notation.meaning: valid lower estimator of the subproblem value

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders master whose retained complicating variables are all integer-restricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) be cut index sets. An integer Benders master is an epigraph master \[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}y+\theta:y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^m,\ \theta\ge \ell_j(y)\ (j\in J),\ f_i(y)\le0\ (i\in I)\},\] where each \(\ell_j\) is a valid lower estimator of the subproblem value function \(Q\) and each \(f_i\) is a valid feasibility cut on \(Y\). A complete cut family is exact when, for every \(y\in Y\), the feasibility cuts admit \(y\) exactly when \(Q(y)<+\infty\), and \(\sup_{j\in J}\ell_j(y)=Q(y)\) at every admitted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An integer Benders master retains only integer complicating variables. Its complete feasibility cuts identify exactly the extendable integer points, and its complete optimality cuts reproduce the subproblem value at those points.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^m\) contains all master-domain restrictions.
\(Q(y)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), with \(Q(y)=+\infty\) exactly at nonextendable master points.
All displayed cuts are valid on \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With a complete cut family, the master epigraph is \(\{(y,\theta):y\in Y,\ Q(y)<+\infty,\ \theta\ge Q(y)\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Domain Benders Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders master retaining both integer and continuous complicating variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) be cut index sets, and partition the retained variables as \(y=(u,v)\), where \(u\in U\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^p\) and \(v\in V(u)\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\). With \(Y=\{(u,v):u\in U,\ v\in V(u)\}\), a mixed-domain Benders master has the form \[\min\{c_u^{\mathsf T}u+c_v^{\mathsf T}v+\theta:(u,v)\in Y,\ \theta\ge\ell_j(u,v)\ (j\in J),\ f_i(u,v)\le0\ (i\in I)\}.\] Each \(\ell_j\) is a valid lower estimator of the subproblem value function \(Q\), and each \(f_i\) is a valid feasibility cut on \(Y\). A complete cut family is exact when the feasibility cuts admit exactly the points with \(Q(u,v)<+\infty\) and \(\sup_{j\in J}\ell_j(u,v)=Q(u,v)\) at every admitted point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-domain Benders master retains both integer and continuous complicating variables. Complete feasibility cuts identify its extendable joint-domain points, and complete optimality cuts reproduce the subproblem value there.
assumptions_latex: \(Y=\{(u,v):u\in U,\ v\in V(u)\}\) includes all linking restrictions among retained variables.
\(Q(u,v)\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), with \(+\infty\) assigned to nonextendable points.
All displayed cuts are valid throughout \(Y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: With a complete cut family, the master epigraph is \(\{(u,v,\theta):(u,v)\in Y,\ Q(u,v)<+\infty,\ \theta\ge Q(u,v)\}\).

children.title: Master-Regime Transitions
children.top_down_role: Changes in cut interpretation, certification, or search caused by master-domain choice.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Regime Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bound and cut-validity effects of relaxing or imposing master integrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the common Benders objective be \(F(y)=c^{\mathsf T}y+Q(y)\), and let \(Y_I\subseteq Y_M\subseteq Y_C\) be integer, mixed-domain, and continuous master domains. Whenever the three infima are well defined, \[\inf_{y\in Y_C}F(y)\le\inf_{y\in Y_M}F(y)\le\inf_{y\in Y_I}F(y).\] Thus relaxing master integrality can only decrease the relaxation value used as a minimization lower bound; a relaxed solution is not generally a feasible incumbent for a stricter regime. Any cut valid on \(Y_C\) remains valid after restriction to \(Y_M\) or \(Y_I\), whereas a cut valid only on \(Y_I\) need not remain valid after relaxation to \(Y_M\) or \(Y_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing master integrality enlarges the domain and can only weaken a minimization lower bound. Cuts valid on the continuous domain remain valid after restriction, but integer-only cuts may fail after relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The objective \(F\) and its extended-real value-function convention are identical in all three regimes.
\(Y_I\subseteq Y_M\subseteq Y_C\).
Each stated infimum is well defined in \(\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{y\in Y_C}F(y)\le\inf_{y\in Y_M}F(y)\le\inf_{y\in Y_I}F(y)\), and cut validity is inherited from a domain by each of its subsets.

notation.meaning: integer, mixed-domain, and continuous master domains

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Continuous Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LP dual representation generating classical Benders optimality and feasibility cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed master decision \(y\), let \[Q(y)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}x:Wx\ge h-Ty,\ x\ge0\}.\] If this linear program is feasible and has finite value, strong duality gives \[Q(y)=\max\{\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty):W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q,\ \pi\ge0\}.\] Hence every dual-feasible \(\pi\) yields the valid optimality cut \(\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\). If the primal is infeasible, any dual recession ray \(r\ge0\) with \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)>0\) yields the feasibility cut \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A continuous linear Benders subproblem equals its LP dual; dual points generate optimality cuts and dual rays generate feasibility cuts.
assumptions_latex: \(x\) is continuous and all displayed data are finite-dimensional real matrices or vectors.
For the equality, the primal subproblem is feasible with finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(y)=\max_{\pi\ge0,\,W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q}\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Ty)\), with dual points and rays producing valid Benders cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer Benders Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer recourse subproblem obtained after fixing the Benders master variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the master decision be \(x\in X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{n_1}\times\mathbb{R}^{n_2}\). An integer Benders subproblem has value function \[Q(x)=\inf\{d^{\mathsf T}y: Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\in Y\},\] where \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{m_1}\times\mathbb{R}^{m_2}\). Its outcome is a finite optimal value with a feasible optimizer, infeasibility, or unboundedness. Because integrality is retained in \(Y\), ordinary linear-programming dual points and rays need not describe \(Q\) or its domain; valid master cuts therefore require integer-programming bounds, logical explanations, or other discrete certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing the master variables leaves a mixed-integer recourse problem whose value, infeasibility, or unboundedness must be communicated through discrete rather than ordinary LP-dual certificates.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{n_1}\times\mathbb{R}^{n_2}\) and \(Y\subseteq\mathbb{Z}^{m_1}\times\mathbb{R}^{m_2}\).
\(W,T,h,d\) have compatible finite dimensions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Integer Benders Subproblem and Branching Viewpoints
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the discrete Benders subproblem when all subproblem variables are nonnegative integers and distinguishes two basic search-space viewpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \(x^*\), if all subproblem variables are integer with \(y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^p\), then
\[
\phi^I(x^*)=\max\{hy:Gy\le d-Fx^*,\ y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^p\}.
\]
This subproblem is an integer program rather than a linear program. Two basic approaches are to search in the \((x,y,\eta)\)-space, allowing branching on both \(x\) and \(y\), or to search in the \((x,\eta)\)-space, branching only on \(x\) while solving integer subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed master solution, the Benders subproblem maximizes h y subject to G y being at most d minus F x-star, with y in a subset of the nonnegative integer lattice. It is an integer program. One approach searches in the joint x, y, eta space; another searches only in the x, eta space and solves an integer subproblem for each evaluated master assignment.
assumptions_latex: x=x^*\text{ is fixed}
Y\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^p

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Benders Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility or optimization subproblems represented by finite combinatorial structures.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in X\) encode a master assignment and let \(\mathcal F(x)\) be the finite set of combinatorial objects satisfying the constraints activated by \(x\). A combinatorial Benders subproblem is the oracle problem \[Q(x)=\min\{q(x,z):z\in\mathcal F(x)\},\] with value \(+\infty\) when \(\mathcal F(x)=\varnothing\). A returned optimizer establishes an upper bound at the queried assignment. An infeasibility response supports a globally valid Benders cut only when accompanied by a verifiable conflict or implication whose validity extends to a specified family of master assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The subproblem searches a finite combinatorial structure. Global cuts require reusable conflicts or implications, not merely an infeasibility response at one assignment.

\(q(x,z)\in\mathbb{R}\) for every \(z\in\mathcal F(x)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Subproblem Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable optimality, bound, or infeasibility information returned by a discrete subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a discrete subproblem value function \(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\), a certificate valid on \(U\subseteq X\) is either: a verifiable function \(L:U\to\mathbb{R}\) satisfying \(L(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in U\), or a verifiable predicate \(C\) satisfying \(C(x)=1\Rightarrow Q(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\in U\). The first certificate yields the master constraint \(\theta\ge L(x)\); the second yields any master constraint excluding all \(x\in U\) for which \(C(x)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A discrete certificate is a checkable lower bound or infeasibility explanation valid over a stated set of master decisions and therefore convertible into a valid master cut.

\(Q:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\).

children.title: Discrete Oracle Limitations
children.top_down_role: Limits on extracting valid master information from discrete subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Oracle Limitations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise discrete-oracle answers generally do not determine globally strong Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{0,1\}\) and define \(Q_0(0)=Q_1(0)=0\), \(Q_0(1)=0\), and \(Q_1(1)=1\). A value oracle queried only at \(x=0\) returns the identical answer \(0\) for both functions. Nevertheless, the tight affine lower bound through that observation may have slope at most \(0\) for \(Q_0\), while slope \(1\) is valid for \(Q_1\). Hence a pointwise value, optimizer, or infeasibility flag does not by itself justify a globally strong Benders cut; additional structural or region-valid certification is necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two discrete value functions can agree at the queried assignment but admit different global cuts, so pointwise oracle output alone cannot justify a strong cut.
assumptions_latex: The oracle reveals information only at the queried point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_0(0)=Q_1(0)\) does not determine a common tight affine lower bound on \(X\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Independent Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable Benders recourse represented by independent scenario or block subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose fixing \(x\in X\) separates the recourse variables into \(S\) independent blocks: \[Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}Q_s(x),\qquad Q_s(x)=\min\{d_s^{\mathsf T}y_s:W_sy_s\ge h_s-T_sx,\ y_s\ge0\}.\] If every block is feasible and bounded and \(\pi_s\ge0\), \(W_s^{\mathsf T}\pi_s\le d_s\), then \[\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sx)\] is a valid aggregate optimality cut. Equivalently, a multicut master may impose \(\theta_s\ge\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sx)\) and \(\theta=\sum_s\theta_s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent recourse blocks add their values. Their dual bounds may be aggregated into one cut or retained as separate multicuts.
assumptions_latex: The recourse feasible set is the Cartesian product of \(S\) block feasible sets.
Each block linear program is feasible and has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^{S}Q_s(x)\) and \(\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^{S}\pi_s^{\mathsf T}(h_s-T_sx)\).

notation.meaning: master epigraph variable for block s

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical affine epigraph cuts generated from dual-feasible subproblem points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(x)=\min\{d^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\), define \(P=\{\pi\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\}\). Weak duality gives \(Q(x)\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) for every \(\pi\in P\) whenever the primal subproblem is feasible. Therefore the Benders master epigraph variable \(\theta\) may be constrained by \[\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx).\] If \(\pi\) is dual-optimal at the incumbent \(\bar x\), the cut is tight there: \(Q(\bar x)=\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every dual-feasible point gives an affine lower bound on recourse; a dual optimum produces an optimality cut tight at the current master decision.
assumptions_latex: The subproblem is a feasible linear program with finite optimum at \(\bar x\).
\(\pi\ge0\) and \(W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\), with equality at \(x=\bar x\) when \(\pi\) is dual-optimal there.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Feasibility Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical master cuts generated by recession rays certifying subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the feasibility system \(Wy\ge h-Tx\), \(y\ge0\), define the dual recession cone \(R=\{r\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\}\). Farkas' alternative implies that feasibility requires \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) for every \(r\in R\). Thus each such ray gives the Benders feasibility cut \[r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0.\] If the subproblem at \(\bar x\) is infeasible, a certifying ray satisfies \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\), so its cut excludes \(\bar x\) while retaining every master decision having feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual recession ray with positive violation proves incumbent recourse infeasibility and yields a cut satisfied by every decision with feasible recourse.
assumptions_latex: The recourse constraints are \(Wy\ge h-Tx\) and \(y\ge0\).
\(r\ge0\) and \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\), while \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\) certifies infeasibility at \(\bar x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Point Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-feasible points certify affine lower bounds and, with matching primal values, optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(Q(x)=\min\{d^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\). A vector \(\pi\) is a dual-point certificate when \(\pi\ge0\) and \(W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\). These inequalities are directly checkable and weak duality certifies \[\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le Q(x)\] for every master decision with feasible recourse. At \(\bar x\), if a primal-feasible \(\bar y\) also satisfies \(d^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)\), the pair certifies both optimality of \(\bar y\) and exactness of the associated Benders cut at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual feasibility certifies a global affine recourse lower bound; equality with a primal feasible value additionally certifies subproblem optimality and cut tightness.

\(\pi\ge0\) and \(W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le d\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Ray Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual recession directions certify infeasibility of a fixed linear recourse system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(W\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times m}\), \(T\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(h\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\), and \(\bar x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\). For the system \(Wy\ge h-T\bar x\), \(y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}_{+}\), a nonzero vector \(r\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\) is a dual-ray certificate if \(r\ge0\), \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\), and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\). Such a certificate establishes that the system is infeasible. It also defines the inequality \[r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0,\] which is valid for every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) admitting feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero dual recession direction having a positive pairing with the fixed right-hand side certifies recourse infeasibility and defines a feasibility cut valid for every master decision with feasible recourse.

\(r\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\setminus\{0\}\), \(r\ge0\), \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\), and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}_{+}:Wy\ge h-T\bar x\}=\varnothing\), and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) for every master decision \(x\) with feasible recourse.

children.title: Optimality Certificate Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Master implications associated with valid dual-point evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Optimality Certificate Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-dual equality interprets a dual point as an exact subproblem optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a master decision \(\bar x\), let \(\bar y\ge0\) satisfy \(W\bar y\ge h-T\bar x\), and let \(\bar\pi\ge0\) satisfy \(W^{\mathsf T}\bar\pi\le d\). If \[d^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x),\] weak duality makes both solutions optimal and certifies \(Q(\bar x)=d^{\mathsf T}\bar y\). The same dual point supplies the globally valid lower bound \(Q(x)\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\), so the resulting Benders optimality cut is exact at \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matching primal and dual objectives certify the exact recourse value, while the dual solution also defines a global cut tight at the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(\bar y\) is primal-feasible at \(\bar x\).
\(\bar\pi\) is dual-feasible.
\(d^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\bar x)=d^{\mathsf T}\bar y=\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)\).

children.title: Feasibility Certificate Interpretation
children.top_down_role: Master implications associated with valid dual-ray evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Certificate Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A violated Farkas inequality interprets a dual ray as an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\bar x\), let \(r\ge0\) satisfy \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\). These relations form a Farkas certificate that \(Wy\ge h-T\bar x\), \(y\ge0\), has no solution. Moreover, every \(x\) admitting feasible recourse must satisfy \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\). Thus the certificate has two interpretations: it verifies infeasibility of the queried subproblem and simultaneously defines a Benders feasibility cut that removes \(\bar x\) without removing any recourse-feasible master decision.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ray’s positive violation proves incumbent infeasibility, and its nonpositive inequality over feasible recourse decisions is exactly the associated feasibility cut.
assumptions_latex: \(r\ge0\) and \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\).
\(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{y\ge0:Wy\ge h-T\bar x\}=\varnothing\) and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) for every recourse-feasible \(x\).

children.title: No-Good Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts excluding previously evaluated discrete master assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: No-Good Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary master cut excluding exactly one previously evaluated assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\) and let \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\) be an assignment that must be excluded, for example because its discrete subproblem is infeasible. Define \(I_0=\{i:\bar x_i=0\}\) and \(I_1=\{i:\bar x_i=1\}\). The no-good Benders cut is \[\sum_{i\in I_0}x_i+\sum_{i\in I_1}(1-x_i)\ge1.\] Its left side equals the Hamming distance from \(x\) to \(\bar x\); consequently the cut rejects \(\bar x\) and is satisfied by every other binary assignment. It conveys no exclusion beyond that single assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For binary master variables, the no-good cut requires at least one bit to differ from the rejected assignment and excludes no other assignment.
assumptions_latex: The assignment \(\bar x\) is validly identified for exclusion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\).

notation.meaning: indices assigned zero by the rejected assignment
indices assigned one by the rejected assignment

review_flags: exact source for the no-good Benders cut is missing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The binary no-good inequality is mathematically correct and representation fits the cut-family leaf, but no citation or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied for its identification as a no-good Benders cut.

children.title: Combinatorial Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts exploiting discrete subproblem structure beyond a single assignment exclusion.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean master cuts obtained from certified combinatorial implications of the subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) be the master-assignment set and let \(F\subseteq X\) contain the assignments having feasible subproblems. A combinatorial Benders feasibility cut is an inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) satisfying \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge b\) for every \(x\in F\), derived from a finite logical implication certified by the subproblem. In particular, if a certificate establishes that every feasible assignment differs from \(\bar x\) on some index in \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\), the associated cut is \[\sum_{i\in C:\,\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\,\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A combinatorial Benders cut converts a certified subproblem implication into a valid inequality on binary master assignments.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(C\) is certified to contain a changed component of every feasible assignment relative to \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\) is valid for \(F\).

notation.meaning: master assignments whose subproblems are feasible
certificate support or conflict index set

children.title: Partial-Assignment Exclusions
children.top_down_role: Exclusions supported by infeasible or dominated partial master assignments.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Assignment Exclusions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: No-good inequality supported only on a certified partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\), fix \(C\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and values \(v_i\in\{0,1\}\) for \(i\in C\). If every \(x\in X\) satisfying \(x_i=v_i\) for all \(i\in C\) induces an infeasible subproblem, then the forbidden partial assignment has the linear representation \[\sum_{i\in C:\,v_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\,v_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1.\] The inequality leaves assignments outside the specified coordinates unrestricted and excludes every completion of the certified partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If fixing selected binary variables makes every completion infeasible, one mismatch inequality excludes all those completions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\).
\(x_C=v_C\) implies subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible master assignment satisfies \(\displaystyle \sum_{i\in C:v_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:v_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\).

notation.meaning: indices fixed by the partial assignment
forbidden binary values on the selected indices

children.title: Combinatorial Cut Strength
children.top_down_role: Relative exclusion power of discrete Benders cut families.

knowledge_statements.title: Combinatorial Cut Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dominance ordering of assignment-exclusion cuts by conflict support inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an infeasible binary assignment \(\bar x\), define \(d_C(x)=\sum_{i\in C:\,\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in C:\,\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\). If \(C\subseteq D\) are both valid conflict supports, then \(d_C(x)\le d_D(x)\) for every \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\). Consequently, the cut \(d_C(x)\ge1\) dominates \(d_D(x)\ge1\): every binary assignment admitted by the former is admitted by the latter, while strict containment can exclude additional assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among valid exclusion cuts for one assignment, a smaller conflict support yields a cut at least as strong as one using a superset.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq D\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\).
Both supports certify infeasibility of their corresponding partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:d_C(x)\ge1\}\subseteq\{x:d_D(x)\ge1\}\).

notation.meaning: number of mismatches from the incumbent on support C
