children.title: Conflict-Based Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master cuts derived from conflicting discrete decisions or constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Conflict-Based Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Master cuts derived from conflicting bound literals in an infeasible subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(l_j(x)\in\{0,1\}\) indicate whether master assignment \(x\) satisfies bound literal \(j\). A conflict-based Benders cut is obtained from a finite set \(E\) such that simultaneous satisfaction of all literals in \(E\) makes the subproblem infeasible. Its Boolean master form is \[\sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\ge1.\] Thus every feasible master solution must falsify at least one literal in the conflict. When the literals are binary variable fixings, this formula is a linear assignment-exclusion inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict-based cut requires every feasible master assignment to violate at least one bound literal from a certified infeasible conflict.
assumptions_latex: \(l_j(x)\in\{0,1\}\) for every \(j\in E\).
\(l_j(x)=1\) for all \(j\in E\) implies subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\displaystyle \sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\ge1\) is valid for feasible master assignments.

notation.meaning: truth indicator of literal j under assignment x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean conflict cut is coherent and the definition kind fits, but no inspectable citation supports its identification as a conflict-based Benders cut.

children.title: Infeasibility-Explanation Cuts
children.top_down_role: Master cuts supported by structured explanations of subproblem infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Infeasibility-Explanation Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A checkable infeasibility explanation and its associated master inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a set of master literals and let \(P(E)\) denote the subproblem restricted by those literals. If a verifiable subproblem certificate establishes \(P(E)=\varnothing\), then \(E\) is an infeasibility explanation. The inequality \[\sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\ge1\] is an infeasibility-explanation cut: violation means that all explaining literals hold, which recreates the certified empty restriction. Verification consists of checking the emptiness certificate for \(P(E)\) and the literal values induced by \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A certified empty subproblem under selected literals yields a cut forcing every feasible master solution to break the explanation.
assumptions_latex: \(P(E)=\varnothing\) has a checkable infeasibility certificate.
\(l_j(x)\) exactly represents satisfaction of literal \(j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every master assignment with a feasible subproblem satisfies \(\displaystyle \sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\ge1\).

notation.meaning: subproblem restricted by all literals in E

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate and resulting inequality are internally consistent, but the specialized infeasibility-explanation construction has no cited source.

children.title: Minimal Conflict Explanations
children.top_down_role: Reduced explanatory sets supporting more focused exclusions.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Conflict Explanations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimality condition for a set of infeasibility-explaining literals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite literal set \(E\), let \(P(S)\) be the subproblem obtained by imposing every literal in \(S\subseteq E\). The set \(E\) is a minimal conflict explanation precisely when \[P(E)=\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad P(E\setminus\{j\})\ne\varnothing\ \text{for every }j\in E.\] This is inclusion minimality, not minimum cardinality. Its exclusion cut cannot be strengthened merely by deleting one explaining literal while retaining a valid infeasibility implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conflict explanation is minimal when it is infeasible, but removing any one of its literals restores subproblem feasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is finite.
\(P(S)\) consistently denotes the subproblem restricted by literals in \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E\) is inclusion-minimal infeasible if and only if \(P(E)=\varnothing\) and \(P(E\setminus\{j\})\ne\varnothing\) for every \(j\in E\).

notation.meaning: subproblem under the literals in S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated single-deletion condition correctly expresses inclusion-minimal infeasibility for restrictions formed by imposing literals, and condition is an appropriate kind, but no citation is supplied.

children.title: Explanation-to-Cut Translation
children.top_down_role: Interfaces that convert subproblem explanations into valid master restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Explanation-to-Cut Translation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanical conversion of a finite Boolean infeasibility explanation into a master cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input an explanation \(E\) whose simultaneous literals imply subproblem infeasibility. For each \(j\in E\), construct its truth indicator \(l_j(x)\). Initialize \(h(x)=0\), update \(h(x)\leftarrow h(x)+1-l_j(x)\) for every \(j\in E\), and append the master constraint \(h(x)\ge1\). If each literal is \(x_i=v_i\), substitute \(1-l_j(x)=x_i\) when \(v_i=0\) and \(1-l_j(x)=1-x_i\) when \(v_i=1\). Output the resulting linear cut; stop after all explanation literals are processed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate each explaining literal into a mismatch indicator, sum the indicators, and require at least one mismatch.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) certifies that simultaneous satisfaction of its literals is infeasible.
Each \(l_j(x)\) has an exact binary or linear representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output constraint \(h(x)=\sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\ge1\) is valid.

notation.meaning: truth indicator for explanation literal j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite translation procedure is mathematically sound and algorithm is the correct role, but it lacks an inspectable source for the specialized explanation-to-cut calculus.

knowledge_statements.title: Inference-Based Optimality Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional lower bounds translated into master inequalities for the recourse-value variable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q:X\to\mathbb R\) be the subproblem value, let \(\bar L\in\mathbb R\) satisfy \(Q(x)\ge\bar L\) for every \(x\in X\), and let \(\theta\) be the master recourse-value variable. Suppose simultaneous satisfaction of the premises in a finite set \(E\) implies \(Q(x)\ge L_E\), and define \(d_E(x)=\sum_{j\in E}(1-l_j(x))\), where \(l_j(x)\in\{0,1\}\) is the truth indicator of premise \(j\). For any \(M_E\ge L_E-\bar L\), the inference-based optimality cut is \[\theta\ge L_E-M_Ed_E(x).\] When all premises hold, it imposes \(\theta\ge L_E\); when at least one premise fails, its right-hand side is at most \(\bar L\), so it is implied by the global master bound \(\theta\ge\bar L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A conditional subproblem lower bound becomes a master optimality cut by penalizing failed premises; outside the premise set, the cut is redundant with the global lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)\ge\bar L\) for every \(x\in X\).
Simultaneous satisfaction of all premises in \(E\) implies \(Q(x)\ge L_E\).
\(l_j(x)\in\{0,1\}\) exactly indicates satisfaction of premise \(j\).
\(M_E\ge L_E-\bar L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint \(\theta\ge L_E-M_Ed_E(x)\) is a valid lower-bounding master constraint and is redundant with \(\theta\ge\bar L\) whenever \(d_E(x)\ge1\).

notation.meaning: subproblem value at master assignment x
global lower bound on the subproblem value

children.title: Pareto-Optimal Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Nondominated Benders cuts assessed relative to the relevant master region.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Optimal Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nondominated affine Benders lower bounds over the master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), and let two valid Benders optimality cuts be \(\theta\ge g_k(x)=\alpha_k+\beta_k^{\mathsf T}x\) for \(k\in\{1,2\}\). Cut 1 dominates cut 2 on \(X\) when \(g_1(x)\ge g_2(x)\) for every \(x\in X\) and strict inequality holds for some \(x\in X\). A valid Benders cut is Pareto-optimal relative to \(X\) if no other valid Benders cut dominates it on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders cut is Pareto-optimal when no other valid cut gives an everywhere stronger and somewhere strictly stronger lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is the master domain.
Each compared affine function is a valid lower bound for the subproblem value on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pareto optimality is equivalent to absence of a valid \(g\) with \(g(x)\ge g_1(x)\) on \(X\) and strict inequality somewhere.

notation.meaning: affine lower bound defining Benders cut k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dominance definition is precise and appropriate for this leaf, but no citation supports the stated Benders-specific Pareto terminology and comparison domain.

children.title: Magnanti–Wong Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Pareto-oriented cut selection associated with a core-point framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Magnanti–Wong Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary dual selection on the incumbent-optimal face using a relative-interior core point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\), let \(\bar x\in X\), and choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\). Solve \[\max_{u\in U}\ u^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx^0)\quad\text{subject to}\quad u^{\mathsf T}(b-B\bar x)=Q(\bar x).\] For an optimizer \(u^*\), append \(\theta\ge {u^*}^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\). Thus initialization chooses \(x^0\), the update selects a dual point on the incumbent-optimal face, and the output is a Pareto-optimal Benders cut under the stated finite-dual representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize over incumbent-optimal dual solutions at a relative-interior core point, then use the selected dual solution to generate a Pareto-optimal cut.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\) is finite on \(X\).
\(x^0\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\).
The auxiliary dual problem attains an optimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\ge {u^*}^{\mathsf T}(b-Bx)\) is valid, tight at \(\bar x\), and Pareto-optimal on \(X\).

notation.meaning: dual feasible region of the subproblem

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The auxiliary optimization has the standard Magnanti–Wong form and algorithm is the appropriate kind, but the Pareto-optimality guarantee requires an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Core-Point Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Use of interior reference points to distinguish stronger dual alternatives.

knowledge_statements.title: Core-Point Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection and maintenance of a relative-interior point for Pareto cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose an initial \(x^0\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\). At iteration \(k\), use \(x^k\) as the secondary evaluation point in the Pareto-cut auxiliary problem. After obtaining a master point \(\hat x^k\in\operatorname{conv}X\), select \(\lambda_k\in(0,1]\) and update \[x^{k+1}=\lambda_k x^k+(1-\lambda_k)\hat x^k.\] Because the coefficient of the relative-interior point is positive, convexity preserves \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\). Stop when the surrounding Benders algorithm terminates and output the cuts selected using these core points.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a relative-interior core point by convex averaging with a positive weight on the current core point, and use it to select strong cuts from the incumbent-optimal dual face.
assumptions_latex: \(x^0\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\).
\(\hat x^k\in\operatorname{conv}X\).
\(\lambda_k\in(0,1]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{k+1}\in\operatorname{relint}(\operatorname{conv}X)\) at every iteration.

notation.meaning: new master point used in averaging

children.title: Pareto-Dominance Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on dominance comparisons across changing or restricted master regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto-Dominance Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of core-point tie breaking when the evaluation point lies on the domain boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The relative-interior hypothesis cannot generally be replaced by boundary membership. Let \(X=[0,1]\), \(Q(x)=x\), and consider the valid lower bounds \(g_1(x)=x\) and \(g_2(x)=0\). At the incumbent and boundary core point \(\bar x=x^0=0\), both cuts are tight and have equal core-point value, yet \(g_1(x)\ge g_2(x)\) throughout \(X\), strictly for every \(x>0\). Hence auxiliary selection at a boundary point may return the dominated cut \(g_2\); equality at that point does not certify Pareto optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a boundary core point, a dominated and a dominating cut can tie, so core-point maximization may select the dominated cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Boundary-point equality does not imply Pareto optimality; \(g_1\) dominates \(g_2\) despite \(g_1(x^0)=g_2(x^0)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-contained example correctly shows that boundary-point tie breaking need not distinguish a dominating cut from a dominated one, and failure_boundary is the correct role. A citation is nevertheless required for the general Magnanti–Wong boundary claim.

children.title: Facet-Seeking Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts selected to favor high-dimensional supporting faces.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Seeking Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection rule seeking facet-defining inequalities for a polyhedral Benders value-function epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) be the full-dimensional polyhedral epigraph of a Benders value function, and let \(\mathcal C\) be a finite family of normalized valid cuts \(a^{\mathsf T}x+b\theta\geq d\). For each cut define \(F(a,b,d)=\{(x,\theta)\in E:a^{\mathsf T}x+b\theta=d\}\). Select a cut maximizing \(\dim F(a,b,d)\), breaking ties by a prescribed depth score at the current master point. A selected cut is facet-defining exactly when \(\dim F(a,b,d)=n\); otherwise the rule returns the candidate exposing the highest-dimensional proper face.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among normalized candidate cuts, select one exposing the highest-dimensional face of the value-function epigraph, using depth only to break ties.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is a full-dimensional polyhedron in \(\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\).
\(\mathcal C\) is finite and its cuts share a fixed normalization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c\in\mathcal C}\dim F(c)\), and \(c^*\) is facet-defining when \(\dim F(c^*)=n\).
review_flags: Exact Benders-specific facet-seeking rule lacks a supplied supporting locator.
Normalization and tie-breaking conventions require source confirmation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the facet-seeking leaf, and the face-dimension criterion is mathematically coherent, but no source supports this Benders-specific selection rule, normalization, or depth tie-breaker.

children.title: Deep Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts selected for strong separation of a current master point.

knowledge_statements.title: Deep Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Depth relative to a reference master point, a norm, and a nonempty finite family of valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\), let \(z^0=(x^0,\theta^0)\notin E\), and let \(\mathcal C\) be a nonempty finite family of valid inequalities \(u^{\mathsf T}z\geq\beta\) for \(E\), each with \(u\neq0\). For a fixed norm whose dual norm is \(\|\cdot\|_*\), define \(D(z^0;u,\beta)=(\beta-u^{\mathsf T}z^0)/\|u\|_*\). A deepest Benders cut in \(\mathcal C\) is any member maximizing \(D\); it is a separating cut when its maximum depth is positive.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within a nonempty finite candidate family, a deepest Benders cut maximizes dual-norm-normalized violation at the specified master point and separates that point when the maximum is positive.
assumptions_latex: \(E\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n+1}\) and \(z^0\notin E\).
\(\mathcal C\) is nonempty and finite, and every member is valid for \(E\) with a nonzero normal.
A norm and its dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((u^*,\beta^*)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{(u,\beta)\in\mathcal C}D(z^0;u,\beta)\), and the selected inequality separates \(z^0\) if \(D(z^0;u^*,\beta^*)>0\).

notation.meaning: Benders epigraph or other closed master-valid set
dual norm applied to inequality normals

children.title: Cut-Depth Metrics
children.top_down_role: Geometric measures used to compare separation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Depth Metrics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-invariant depth metrics for comparing valid Benders cuts at one reference point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a violated valid inequality \(u^{\mathsf T}z\geq\beta\) and reference point \(z^0\), define raw violation by \(V=\beta-u^{\mathsf T}z^0\). Given a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\), define normalized depth by \(D_*=V/\|u\|_*\). If a positive scale \(s(u,\beta)\) is fixed, define scaled efficacy by \(D_s=V/s(u,\beta)\). The latter two scores are invariant under multiplying the inequality by a positive scalar whenever \(s(\lambda u,\lambda\beta)=\lambda s(u,\beta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut depth may be raw violation or violation divided by a homogeneous normalization; only the normalized forms are invariant to positive rescaling.
assumptions_latex: \(s(u,\beta)>0\) is positively homogeneous of degree one.

children.title: Facet-Depth Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Tensions between face quality, local separation, plus computational effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Facet-Depth Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical independence of face dimension and local separation depth for valid cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be a full-dimensional polyhedron, \(z^0\notin E\), and let two normalized valid cuts expose faces \(F_1\) and \(F_2\). In general, neither \(\dim F_1>\dim F_2\) implies \(D(z^0;c_1)\geq D(z^0;c_2)\), nor does greater depth imply a higher-dimensional exposed face. Thus facet status is a global geometric property of \(E\), whereas depth is local to \(z^0\), the normalization, and the norm. A lexicographic or weighted selection policy must state which objective has priority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Facet dimension and depth are generally incomparable: a facet cut may be shallow, while a deeper cut may expose a lower-dimensional face.
assumptions_latex: \(E\) is full-dimensional.
The compared cuts use the same normalization and depth convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\dim F_1>\dim F_2\not\Rightarrow D(z^0;c_1)\geq D(z^0;c_2)\), and the converse ordering also need not hold.

notation.meaning: face exposed by candidate cut i

children.title: Minimal Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Benders cuts minimal under a stated support or coefficient criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality under dominance within a normalized family of valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(E\) be the Benders epigraph and \(\mathcal C\) a normalized family of valid inequalities. For \(c_i(z)\geq0\), say that \(c_1\) dominates \(c_2\) on a comparison domain \(Z\) when \(\{z\in Z:c_1(z)\geq0\}\subseteq\{z\in Z:c_2(z)\geq0\}\). A cut \(c\in\mathcal C\) is minimal when no distinct \(c'\in\mathcal C\) dominates it strictly on \(Z\). The normalization and domain are part of the definition because changing either may change the dominance relation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimal Benders cut is not strictly dominated, on the stated comparison domain, by another cut in the normalized candidate family.
assumptions_latex: Every member of \(\mathcal C\) is valid for \(E\).
A common normalization and comparison domain \(Z\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\) is minimal exactly when no \(c'\in\mathcal C\setminus\{c\}\) strictly dominates \(c\) on \(Z\).

notation.meaning: domain on which cut dominance is compared

review_flags: The intended local meaning of minimality may instead be coefficientwise or support minimality.
A Benders-specific authoritative definition is required.

children.title: Irreducible Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Benders cuts supported by irreducible infeasibility or explanation structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Irreducible Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Irreducibility with respect to deleting active certificate components from a fixed representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a valid Benders cut \(c_I(z)\geq0\) is generated from a finite indexed certificate \(I\), with each index contributing a nonzero term. The cut is irreducible relative to this representation when, for every proper subset \(J\subsetneq I\), the reduced expression \(c_J(z)\geq0\) is not a valid cut for the same Benders epigraph. Irreducibility concerns deletion of certificate components; it does not by itself imply facet-defining status, maximum depth, or nondominance among cuts arising from different representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A represented Benders cut is irreducible when deleting any nonempty collection of its certificate components destroys validity.
assumptions_latex: The certificate has a fixed finite indexed representation.
Validity is tested against the same Benders epigraph after deletion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_I\) is irreducible exactly when \(c_J\) is invalid for every \(J\subsetneq I\).

notation.meaning: support of the original certificate representation
cut expression retained on support J

children.title: Support-Minimal Certificates
children.top_down_role: Certificates whose explanatory support cannot be reduced under the chosen criterion.

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Minimal Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable minimal-support certificate for a Benders cut within a fixed oracle representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y\in K^*\) be a dual certificate generating a valid Benders cut, and define \(S=\{i:y_i\neq0\}\). It is support-minimal within a certificate class \(\mathcal Y\subseteq K^*\) when no \(\widehat y\in\mathcal Y\) generating the same normalized cut has \(\operatorname{supp}(\widehat y)\subsetneq S\). A finite verification certificate consists of \(y\), its generated cut, and evidence that every proper supported restriction fails dual feasibility or fails to generate that normalized cut. This certifies minimality only relative to \(\mathcal Y\) and the chosen representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A support-minimal certificate generates the cut and admits no same-cut certificate with strictly smaller support in the declared representation class.
assumptions_latex: \(K^*\) is the dual certificate cone.
The cut normalization and admissible certificate class \(\mathcal Y\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists\widehat y\in\mathcal Y\) with \(\operatorname{supp}(\widehat y)\subsetneq\operatorname{supp}(y)\) that generates the same normalized cut.
review_flags: No supplied locator specifies a support-minimal Benders certificate model.
The finite verification requirement depends on the certificate cone representation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The support-minimality definition fits the leaf, but checking only supported restrictions of the displayed certificate does not exclude every different certificate with smaller support. A source and a certificate model are needed to justify the claimed finite verification procedure.

children.title: Minimality Criterion Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Dependence of minimality claims on representation, normalization, or admissible reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimality Criterion Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries separating dominance, irreducibility, and support minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Cut minimality is not representation-free. Positive rescaling preserves the feasible halfspace but changes coefficientwise comparisons unless cuts are normalized. An invertible reformulation of the dual certificate can preserve the generated cut while changing certificate support. Consequently, dominance-minimality of a cut, irreducibility of one certificate expression, and support-minimality of a dual certificate need not imply one another. Such implications are valid only after fixing the master comparison domain, cut normalization, certificate cone, and coordinate representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimality notions can diverge unless normalization, comparison domain, certificate class, and coordinates are fixed; support minimality is especially representation-dependent.
assumptions_latex: Equivalent positive scalings or certificate reformulations are permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{dominance-minimal}\not\Leftrightarrow\text{irreducible}\not\Leftrightarrow\text{support-minimal}\) without additional fixed conventions.
review_flags: Explicit sourced examples are needed for the asserted non-equivalences.
The intended local minimality conventions are not supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation-dependence warning suits a failure-boundary leaf, but the asserted pairwise non-implications need sourced examples. The chained \(\not\Leftrightarrow\) notation also does not precisely state all claimed pairwise relationships.

children.title: Benders Cut Selection Criteria
children.top_down_role: Criteria for choosing among valid candidate Benders cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Selection Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic scoring and admissibility framework for choosing cuts returned by a Benders oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master iterate \(z^k\), let \(\mathcal C_k\) be the finite set of valid oracle cuts. Discard every cut whose violation is below \(\varepsilon\), whose coefficients violate numerical tolerances, or whose normalized form duplicates an active cut. For each remaining cut \(c\), compute a declared score \(S_k(c)\), which may combine normalized violation, exposed-face dimension, sparsity cost, orthogonality to active cuts, and estimated computational cost. Select an element of \(\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c}S_k(c)\), apply a fixed tie rule, and add it to the master; return no cut if the admissible set is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter invalid, weak, unstable, or duplicate candidates; score the survivors by declared quality measures; add a maximizer using a fixed tie rule.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C_k\) is finite and every candidate is valid.
All scores use specified normalization and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_k\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{c\in\mathcal A_k}S_k(c)\) when the admissible set \(\mathcal A_k\) is nonempty.

children.title: Benders Cut Portfolio Policies
children.top_down_role: Policies governing complementary cut families admitted to the master.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Portfolio Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Budgeted policy for selecting a diverse subset from multiple Benders cut classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), partition valid candidates into portfolios \(\mathcal C_k^1,\ldots,\mathcal C_k^p\). Given a cut budget \(B_k\), assign each candidate a utility \(q_k(c)\) and each pair a redundancy penalty \(r_k(c,d)\geq0\). Select a subset \(P_k\) with \(|P_k|\leq B_k\) maximizing \(\sum_{c\in P_k}q_k(c)-\lambda\sum_{\{c,d\}\subseteq P_k}r_k(c,d)\), subject to any declared per-class quotas. Add \(P_k\), update utilities from observed master improvement and generation cost, and stop selecting when no candidate has positive marginal utility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a budgeted, diverse subset of candidate cuts across cut classes, then update class utilities from observed benefit and cost.
assumptions_latex: Every portfolio contains only valid cuts.
\(B_k\) and all class quotas are finite nonnegative integers.
\(\lambda\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_k\) is a feasible budgeted subset maximizing declared utility minus redundancy penalty.
review_flags: No supplied source locator supports this Benders-specific portfolio policy.
Utility updating and diversity penalties admit several incompatible formulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record proposes a specific budgeted quadratic portfolio algorithm, adaptive utility update, and stopping rule without a supporting source. These are design choices rather than a source-grounded canonical policy.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Nonlinear Subproblem Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle contract for generalized Benders decomposition with parameterized convex subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master point \(x^k\), the interface receives the convex subproblem \(v(x^k)=\inf_{y\in Y}\{f(x^k,y):g(x^k,y)\leq0\}\). If it is feasible and strong duality holds, it returns an optimal primal-dual pair \((y^k,\lambda^k)\), the value \(v(x^k)\), and a subgradient \(s^k\in\partial v(x^k)\). If it is infeasible, it returns a verifiable separating certificate for the feasible master domain. Numerical status and tolerances accompany either response; an uncertified solver termination produces no valid Benders cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The convex subproblem oracle returns certified value and subgradient data when feasible, or a certified separator when infeasible.
assumptions_latex: For fixed \(x\), the subproblem is a proper closed convex optimization problem in \(y\).
A constraint qualification ensures strong duality at feasible queried points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq v(x^k)+(s^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\) is a valid value-function cut after a certified feasible response.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlinear Value-Function Cut Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Supporting-hyperplane representation returned by a convex nonlinear Benders oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v:X\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be a proper closed convex subproblem value function. At a queried point \(x^k\in\operatorname{dom}v\), the interface returns \(v_k=v(x^k)\) and \(s^k\in\partial v(x^k)\). Its cut is the affine minorant \(\ell_k(x)=v_k+(s^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\), represented in the master by \(\theta\geq\ell_k(x)\). The subgradient inequality gives \(\ell_k(x)\leq v(x)\) for every \(x\in X\), with equality at \(x^k\). Approximate data define a valid cut only when accompanied by a certified global error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A value-function oracle returns a value and subgradient whose affine support underestimates the convex value function and is exact at the query point.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is proper, closed, and convex on a convex set \(X\).
\(x^k\in\operatorname{dom}v\) and \(s^k\in\partial v(x^k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\theta\geq v(x^k)+(s^k)^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\) is valid for \(\theta\geq v(x)\) and is tight at \(x=x^k\).

children.title: Inference-Dual Oracles
children.top_down_role: Oracles exposing inference-based dual information from nonclassical subproblems.

assumptions_latex: The subproblem inference system is sound.
The inferred bound is valid for every master assignment satisfying the certificate's antecedent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A_t(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\ge\beta_t\) for every \(x\in X\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inference duality is treated as a certificate system, not LP duality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An inference-dual oracle queried at \(x^t\in X\) returns a finite derivation certificate \(\pi_t\), an antecedent \(A_t:X\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\), and a bound \(\beta_t\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\). Soundness requires \(A_t(x^t)\) and \(A_t(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)\ge\beta_t\) for every \(x\in X\). The case \(\beta_t=+\infty\) certifies infeasibility throughout the antecedent region. The corresponding master cut is \(A_t(x)\Rightarrow\theta\ge\beta_t\), interpreted as exclusion of \(A_t(x)\) when \(\beta_t=+\infty\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An explanation oracle for an infeasible query \(x^t\in X\) returns a master-expressible predicate \(E_t:X\to\{\mathrm{false},\mathrm{true}\}\) such that \(E_t(x^t)\) and \(E_t(x)\Rightarrow Q(x)=+\infty\) for every \(x\in X\). Thus the cut \(\neg E_t(x)\) is globally valid. children.title: Oracle Certificate Translation

assumptions_latex: The oracle certificate is sound in the subproblem inference system.
The translation preserves the certificate's validity over every master assignment.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity requirements for translating inference certificates into master constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A certificate translation is a mapping \(T\) sending an oracle certificate \(\pi_t\) to a master-representable constraint \(C_t=T(\pi_t)\). It is valid when every feasible epigraph point satisfies the translated constraint: \(Q(x)<+\infty\) and \(\theta\ge Q(x)\) imply \(C_t(x,\theta)\) for all \(x\in X\). It separates the queried point when \(C_t(x^t,\theta^t)\) is false for the incumbent master value \(\theta^t<Q(x^t)\), or when it excludes \(x^t\) after certified infeasibility. Translation need not preserve the certificate syntax, but must preserve soundness and master representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certificate translation is valid precisely when its master constraint contains the true value-function epigraph and rejects the certified incumbent.

children.title: Oracle Completeness Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on validity or progress when oracle explanations are incomplete.

assumptions_latex: The master domain \(X\) is finite.
Each infeasible query is excluded, and each feasible query receives an exact value cut at that query.
The master never repeats a certified assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure terminates after at most \(|X|\) distinct subproblem queries; without elimination or exactness, this conclusion need not hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain completeness and its failure when oracle progress is absent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite \(X\), an oracle is assignment-complete if every queried \(x^t\) either is excluded by a valid infeasibility explanation or receives a valid lower-bound cut \(L_t\) with \(L_t(x^t)=Q(x^t)\). Exact master reoptimization then requires at most \(|X|\) distinct queries before proving infeasibility or returning a globally optimal assignment. This guarantee fails if a returned cut neither excludes an infeasible query nor closes its value gap, because the same unresolved assignment may recur. For infinite \(X\), assignment completeness alone gives no finite-termination bound without additional compactness, separation, or convergence hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite termination follows from exact certification of every queried finite-domain assignment; merely valid but nonprogressing cuts, or an infinite domain, defeat that guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Completeness Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the finite-query theorem requires a source and a precise master-selection or nonrepetition condition; exact reoptimization alone does not prevent recurrence under ties.

notation.meaning: optimal value over the fiber above x

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integer Benders performed solely in projected master variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(Q(x)=\inf\{d(y):(x,y)\in F\}\), with \(Q(x)=+\infty\) when the fiber is empty. Initialize a master in \((x,\theta)\) over \(x\in X\). At a master solution \((x^t,\theta^t)\), solve the entire fiber defining \(Q(x^t)\). If empty, add a projected cut valid for every \(x\) having a nonempty fiber and excluding \(x^t\). Otherwise add \(\theta\ge L_t(x)\), where \(L_t(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(L_t(x^t)=Q(x^t)\). Reoptimize until the bounds coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected-space integer Benders solves each complete fiber and expresses every feasibility or value cut only in the retained master variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected-Space Integer Benders

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The projected-fiber algorithm matches the local topic, but no source supports the assumed availability of globally valid projected cuts that are exact at every queried assignment.

children.title: No-Good Integer Benders
children.top_down_role: Integer Benders regimes driven primarily by assignment-exclusion cuts.

assumptions_latex: The queried assignment \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\) has a certified infeasible subproblem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequality \[\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge 1\] excludes exactly \(\bar x\) from \(\{0,1\}^n\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary no-good cut generation for certified infeasible master assignments.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a certified infeasible assignment \(\bar x\in\{0,1\}^n\), no-good integer Benders adds the master inequality \[\sum_{i:\bar x_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i:\bar x_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge 1.\] Its feasible binary set is \(\{0,1\}^n\setminus\{\bar x\}\). The algorithm resolves the master and adds the corresponding inequality whenever a newly queried binary assignment has a certified infeasible subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: No-good integer Benders excludes a certified infeasible binary master assignment by adding an inequality that requires a future assignment to differ in at least one coordinate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: No-Good Integer Benders Node Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives feasibility exclusion, assignment-specific optimality bounding, incumbent updating, and the limited strengthening reach of no-good cuts for a binary master assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a branch-and-cut node whose relaxation solution is \((x^*,\eta^*)\) with \(x^*\in\{0,1\}^n\), solve \(\mathrm{SP}^I(x^*)\). If it is infeasible, add
\[
\sum_{j:x_j^*=0}x_j+\sum_{j:x_j^*=1}(1-x_j)\ge 1.
\]
If \(\phi'\) is an upper bound on \(\phi^I(x^*)\), \(\phi'<\eta^*\), and \(M\) is an upper bound on \(\max_{x\in X}\phi^I(x)\), add
\[
\eta\le \phi'+(M-\phi')\left(\sum_{j:x_j^*=0}x_j+\sum_{j:x_j^*=1}(1-x_j)\right).
\]
If \(\phi'=\phi^I(x^*)=\eta^*\), then the associated \((x^*,y^*)\) is feasible for the original problem; update the incumbent if it improves the best known solution and prune the node. The no-good cuts exclude the evaluated assignment or its current \(\eta\)-value but provide essentially no strengthening at other integer master assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a node with a binary master solution x-star, solve its integer subproblem. If the subproblem is infeasible, add a no-good cut excluding x-star. If an upper bound on the subproblem value is below eta-star, add an assignment-specific big-M optimality cut. If the exact subproblem value equals eta-star, the combined solution is feasible; update the incumbent when improved and prune the node. These cuts have essentially assignment-local reach.
assumptions_latex: (x^*,\eta^*)\text{ is a relaxation solution at the current branch-and-cut node}
\phi'\ge\phi^I(x^*)\text{ and }\phi'<\eta^*\text{ in the optimality-cut case}
M\ge\max_{x\in X}\phi^I(x)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathrm{SP}^I(x^*)\text{ determines whether to add a feasibility no-good cut, add an assignment-specific optimality cut, or update the incumbent and prune; these cuts have essentially assignment-local reach.}

children.title: Projected Assignment Exclusions
children.top_down_role: Translation of excluded discrete assignments into projected master space.

assumptions_latex: The projected master vector is binary.
A set of projected coordinate values is sufficient to imply subproblem infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequality excludes every assignment matching the certified projected pattern and preserves every feasible projected assignment.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exclusion of a certified partial pattern in projected binary space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and \(a\in\{0,1\}^S\). Suppose the certificate establishes that every \(x\in X\subseteq\{0,1\}^n\) satisfying \(x_i=a_i\) for all \(i\in S\) has an infeasible subproblem. Then the projected assignment exclusion \[\sum_{i\in S:a_i=0}x_i+\sum_{i\in S:a_i=1}(1-x_i)\ge1\] is valid for all feasible projected assignments. It excludes the entire cylinder determined by \(a\), not merely the queried full vector. Soundness therefore requires the infeasibility certificate to cover every completion of the unspecified projected coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A projected exclusion removes every binary assignment sharing a certified infeasible partial pattern, provided all completions of that pattern are infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Assignment Exclusions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partial-pattern exclusion is mathematically coherent and certificate is the correct role, but no source supports the projected-cylinder interpretation or its all-completions requirement.

children.title: Projection-Induced Weakness
children.top_down_role: Loss of discrimination or cut strength caused by projection.

assumptions_latex: A projection \(p:U\to X\) identifies multiple expanded assignments.
The oracle certificate concerns only one expanded assignment rather than its entire projection fiber.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Excluding \(p(\bar u)\) from the certificate for \(\bar u\) can remove a feasible point and is therefore invalid.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of validity or strength when certificates do not cover projection fibers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u^0,u^1\in U\) satisfy \(p(u^0)=p(u^1)=\bar x\). If the subproblem extension associated with \(u^0\) is infeasible but the extension associated with \(u^1\) is feasible, then a certificate for \(u^0\) does not justify excluding \(\bar x\) in projected space. More generally, a projected infeasibility cut is sound only if its antecedent implies infeasibility for every expanded assignment in each excluded fiber. Even when sound, projection can weaken separation because distinct expanded certificates may collapse to the same coarse master description, leaving only assignment-level exclusions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection loses information: an infeasible lifted extension cannot exclude its projected assignment when another extension in the same fiber is feasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Induced Weakness

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample-style invalidity boundary is sound in its stated two-extension setting and fits the leaf, but the broader claim about systematic loss of separation strength requires an inspectable source.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Lower-Bound Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted-master bound for a minimization problem with valid Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the original value be \(v^*=\min_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+Q(x)\}\). Suppose every retained cut \(\theta\ge \ell_j(x)\), indexed by \(j\in J_k\), satisfies \(\ell_j(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Define \[L_k=\min_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\left\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\theta:\theta\ge \ell_j(x)\ \text{for all }j\in J_k\right\}.\] If the restricted master is bounded below, then \(L_k\le v^*\). Moreover, if cuts are only added, so that \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\), then \(L_k\le L_{k+1}\le v^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master containing only globally valid underestimating cuts yields a lower bound on the minimization optimum; retaining cuts makes these bounds nondecreasing.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and \(v^*\) is finite.
Every master cut globally underestimates \(Q\) on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_k\le L_{k+1}\le v^*\) whenever \(J_k\subseteq J_{k+1}\).

notation.meaning: optimal subproblem value at master decision x

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Subproblem Certificate Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-point and dual-ray certificates for a linear Benders subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(x\), consider \(Q(x)=\min\{q^{\mathsf T}y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\) with dual feasible set \(D=\{\pi\ge0:W^{\mathsf T}\pi\le q\}\). Any \(\bar\pi\in D\) certifies the globally valid optimality cut \(\theta\ge\bar\pi^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\) by weak duality. If instead \(r\ge0\), \(W^{\mathsf T}r\le0\), and \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-T\bar x)>0\), then Farkas' alternative certifies infeasibility of the subproblem at \(\bar x\), while \(r^{\mathsf T}(h-Tx)\le0\) is a valid feasibility cut for every master point having a feasible subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dual-feasible point certifies an optimality cut; an improving recession ray certifies subproblem infeasibility and supplies a feasibility cut.
assumptions_latex: The displayed primal and dual use the stated inequality and sign conventions.
Linear-programming weak duality and Farkas' alternative apply.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed optimality and feasibility cuts are valid for every admissible master decision.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Incumbent Upper-Bound Validity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasible incumbent certificate for a minimization-form Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v^*=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x+q^{\mathsf T}y:(x,y)\in F\}\). If \((\bar x,\bar y)\in F\), then \(U(\bar x,\bar y)=c^{\mathsf T}\bar x+q^{\mathsf T}\bar y\) is a valid upper bound, so \(v^*\le U(\bar x,\bar y)\). For a nonempty index set \(I_k\) and feasible incumbent pairs \((x^i,y^i)\in F\) for every \(i\in I_k\), define \[U_k=\min_{i\in I_k}\left(c^{\mathsf T}x^i+q^{\mathsf T}y^i\right).\] Then \(v^*\le U_k\). If incumbents are retained, so that \(\varnothing\ne I_k\subseteq I_{k+1}\), then \(v^*\le U_{k+1}\le U_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every feasible master–subproblem pair gives an upper bound on a minimization optimum. For a nonempty retained collection of feasible incumbent pairs, the best upper bound is valid and nonincreasing.
assumptions_latex: The original problem is a minimization problem with finite optimum.
\(I_k\neq\varnothing\), and every indexed pair \((x^i,y^i)\) is feasible for all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^*\le U_{k+1}\le U_k\) whenever \(\varnothing\ne I_k\subseteq I_{k+1}\).

notation.meaning: feasible set of the undecomposed problem
nonempty index set of feasible incumbent pairs available through iteration k
best incumbent objective value through iteration k

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Dual-Certificate Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination from a finite pool of exact extreme-point and extreme-ray cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider exact Benders decomposition for a feasible problem whose linear subproblem dual polyhedron has finitely many relevant extreme points and extreme rays. At each nonterminal iteration, require the subproblem oracle to return a previously absent valid cut generated by one such extreme certificate, and retain every generated cut. Then only finitely many nonterminal iterations are possible. Once no violated certificate exists, the restricted master represents all needed subproblem epigraph and feasibility inequalities at its optimizer; hence its feasible incumbent and master bound coincide, and the algorithm terminates with an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact Benders terminates finitely when all possible cuts come from a finite certificate pool and every nonterminal iteration adds a new retained cut.
assumptions_latex: The relevant dual extreme-point and extreme-ray certificate pool is finite.
Subproblems and restricted masters are solved exactly.
Every nonterminal iteration adds a new violated certificate cut.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method terminates after at most as many cut-generating iterations as there are relevant certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Integer-Master Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination based on exhaustive separation over a finite master domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a finite set of admissible integer master decisions. Suppose an exact Benders method never discards cuts and, whenever the current master optimizer \(x^k\) is not certified optimal or infeasible, exact subproblem separation adds a cut that excludes its current underestimated epigraph value or excludes \(x^k\) as infeasible. If the method does not revisit an already fully separated master state, then after finitely many separations every remaining candidate is correctly evaluated. Consequently the best feasible incumbent is globally optimal, or infeasibility is certified when no master candidate remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many integer master candidates, exact retained separation terminates after all necessary candidates are correctly evaluated or excluded.
assumptions_latex: The admissible master set \(X\) is finite.
Master and subproblem computations are exact.
Cuts are retained and fully separated states are not repeated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite termination occurs with either a globally optimal feasible incumbent or an infeasibility certificate.

notation.meaning: finite set of admissible integer master decisions

children.title: Inexact Benders Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Convergence limitations arising from approximate subproblem or master information.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Benders Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating controlled oracle error from persistent invalid gaps or premature stopping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an inexact oracle produce lower models \(\widehat Q_k(x)\le Q(x)+\varepsilon_k\) and feasible incumbent values no smaller than \(v^*\). If \(\varepsilon_k\to0\), every material model violation is eventually separated, and termination uses the certified gap enlarged by current oracle error, then vanishing-error limit convergence may be retained. Without such control, convergence is not guaranteed: for \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(c=0\), \(Q(0)=0\), and \(Q(1)=-1\), an oracle that always reports both values as \(0\) can repeatedly select \(0\) and certify the false value \(0>v^*=-1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing, gap-accounted oracle errors can preserve convergence; persistent error can hide the optimal master point and produce a false stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: The problem is minimized and incumbent upper bounds come only from feasible solutions.
Inexactness affects subproblem value or separation information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent unaccounted error can invalidate convergence and stopping, whereas vanishing controlled error is the natural convergence boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample illustrates a genuine failure phenomenon, but the positive convergence side uses undefined notions such as material violation and only states that convergence may be retained. A method-specific source and precise error, separation, and stopping hypotheses are required.

children.title: Stabilized Benders Convergence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Convergence limitations introduced by stabilization restrictions or persistent regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilized Benders Convergence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence boundary for stabilization that restricts or penalizes master movement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_k\) be the ordinary Benders master objective and let the stabilized trial point minimize \(M_k(x)+S_k(x;x^k)\) over a restricted region \(R_k\). Global convergence requires a mechanism ensuring that stabilization does not permanently exclude every global master optimizer: for example, unsuccessful restrictions are relaxed and accepted serious steps eventually use globally valid master bounds. If instead \(R_k=\{x^0\}\) for all \(k\), then the algorithm never evaluates another master point. For \(X=\{0,1\}\), \(Q(0)=0\), and \(Q(1)=-1\), initialization at \(x^0=0\) therefore stalls at a nonoptimal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization must eventually release persistent restrictions or otherwise permit global progress; a fixed trust region can trap Benders at a nonoptimal point.
assumptions_latex: Stabilization modifies trial-point selection but not the validity of accumulated cuts.
The original problem is minimized over the stated master domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Permanent exclusion of all global optimizers destroys convergence; an effective release or global-progress mechanism is necessary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-region counterexample is valid, but the asserted global-convergence boundary and examples of sufficient release behavior depend on the stabilization method and acceptance rules. No supporting source is supplied.

children.title: Error-Control Regimes
children.top_down_role: Accuracy regimes under which inexact Benders information remains certifiable.

knowledge_statements.title: Error-Control Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient asymptotic regimes for controlling inexact Benders oracle errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(e_k\ge0\) bound every iteration-\(k\) error entering cut validity, separation, or the computed optimality gap. An error-control regime is convergence-compatible when either \(e_k=0\) eventually, \(e_k\to0\) with stopping and separation tolerances dominating \(e_k\), or \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}e_k<\infty\) in an analysis whose accumulated perturbation is additive. In every regime, a reported termination gap \(g_k\) must be corrected to a certified gap \(g_k^{\mathrm{cert}}\ge g_k+e_k\). A fixed positive unaccounted error floor does not certify convergence to arbitrarily small optimality tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact eventual solves, vanishing tolerance-aware errors, or summable additive errors are compatible regimes; a hidden positive error floor prevents arbitrary-accuracy certification.
assumptions_latex: \(e_k\) is a valid uniform bound for all oracle errors relevant to certification.
The chosen convergence analysis matches the stated error aggregation rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Error control must vanish, terminate, or be summable as appropriate, and stopping gaps must explicitly include the remaining error.

notation.meaning: certified oracle-error bound at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Eventual exactness, vanishing errors, and summability are not interchangeable without a specific convergence analysis. The universal correction g_k^{cert} >= g_k+e_k is also unsupported because multiple error contributions may require different aggregation.

children.title: Stabilization Release Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing the relaxation or removal of stabilization influence.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Release Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditions preventing stabilization from permanently blocking globally relevant master decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For stabilized master regions \(R_k\subseteq X\) and penalties \(S_k(\cdot;x^k)\ge0\), a release regime must ensure global accessibility. Sufficient alternatives include finite release, meaning \(R_k=X\) and \(S_k=0\) for all sufficiently large \(k\); expanding coverage, meaning every \(x\in X\) belongs to \(R_k\) infinitely often; or safeguard release, meaning failure to obtain certified progress triggers an enlargement of \(R_k\) or reduction of the penalty until an unstabilized master optimizer is admissible. A regime allowing one strict region to persist forever without a global safeguard does not ensure Benders convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stabilization is safely released by eventual removal, recurrent global coverage, or a no-progress safeguard that restores access to an unstabilized master optimizer.
assumptions_latex: Cuts remain globally valid independently of stabilization.
Trial points are chosen from \(R_k\) using the stated penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The release rule must eventually admit globally relevant master minimizers; permanent unsupported restriction is insufficient.

notation.meaning: stabilized master region at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Mere membership of every point in R_k infinitely often does not ensure that globally relevant points are selected or evaluated when penalties remain active. The sufficient alternatives require a sourced, method-specific formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Cut Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated optimality-cut algorithm for separable scenario subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\), probabilities \(p_s>0\) with \(\sum_s p_s=1\), costs \(c\), and scenario values \(Q_s(x)\), initialize a master with one variable \(\theta\) approximating \(\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \(x^k\), solve every scenario subproblem, and obtain valid affine cuts \(Q_s(x)\ge\ell_s^k(x)\). Add the single aggregated cut \[\theta\ge\sum_s p_s\ell_s^k(x).\] Form a feasible incumbent when recourse solutions exist. Stop when the certified incumbent–master gap meets tolerance; otherwise retain the cut and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-cut Benders combines all scenario subproblem cuts into one probability-weighted master inequality per iteration.
assumptions_latex: Each scenario oracle returns a globally valid affine lower bound.
Scenario weights are positive and sum to one.
Feasibility cuts are added separately if complete recourse fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration adds at most one aggregated optimality cut, valid for \(\sum_s p_sQ_s(x)\).

notation.meaning: iteration-k affine lower bound for scenario s

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Cut Benders
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disaggregated scenario-wise optimality-cut algorithm for separable recourse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(X\), probabilities \(p_s>0\), costs \(c\), and scenario values \(Q_s(x)\), initialize a master with variables \(\theta_s\) and objective \(c^{\mathsf T}x+\sum_s p_s\theta_s\). At iteration \(k\), solve the master for \(x^k\); solve every scenario subproblem and obtain valid affine bounds \(Q_s(x)\ge\ell_s^k(x)\). For each scenario add \[\theta_s\ge\ell_s^k(x).\] Update a feasible incumbent when possible. Stop when the certified incumbent–master gap meets tolerance; otherwise retain all cuts and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multi-cut Benders adds a separate recourse epigraph variable and valid cut for each scenario, preserving scenario-level information in the master.
assumptions_latex: Every scenario oracle supplies a globally valid affine lower bound.
Scenario probabilities are positive.
Feasibility cuts are handled whenever a scenario lacks feasible recourse.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The master receives one disaggregated optimality cut per separated scenario at each iteration.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Cut Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders algorithm that changes the scenario partition used for cut aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P_k\) be a partition of the scenario set. Associate one epigraph variable \(\theta_B\) with each block \(B\in\mathcal P_k\). After solving the master at \(x^k\), compute scenario cuts \(Q_s(x)\ge\ell_s^k(x)\) and add, for every block, \[\theta_B\ge\sum_{s\in B}p_s\ell_s^k(x).\] Using a prescribed indicator, split blocks whose scenario cuts exhibit excessive heterogeneity and optionally merge blocks satisfying a stated similarity test. When changing partitions, retain or translate all inequalities so the master remains a valid lower model. Stop only using certified global lower and incumbent upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adaptive aggregation dynamically splits or merges scenario blocks, while preserving valid blockwise cuts and certified global bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P_k\) partitions all scenarios and \(p_s>0\).
Every scenario cut is globally valid.
Partition changes preserve every lower-model inequality needed for bound validity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each block cut validly underestimates \(\sum_{s\in B}p_sQ_s(x)\), and adaptation preserves the master lower bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Adaptive aggregation is method dependent. The split/merge indicators and the claimed preservation or translation of inequalities across changing partitions require a precise algorithm and authoritative source before validity can be assessed.

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Benders Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Continuous-master trust-region stabilization; integrality restrictions may be retained in \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(c_k\) and \(\Delta_k\), solve \[(x^{k+1},\theta^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\{f(x)+\theta:\theta\ge m_k(x),\ \|x-c_k\|\le\Delta_k\}.\] Evaluate the Benders subproblems at \(x^{k+1}\), append every resulting valid feasibility or optimality cut, and update the incumbent bounds. If the actual improvement relative to the predicted model improvement passes the prescribed acceptance test, set \(c_{k+1}=x^{k+1}\); otherwise retain \(c_{k+1}=c_k\). Update \(\Delta_k\) by the specified contraction or expansion rule and stop when the certified upper-lower bound gap meets the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restrict each stabilized Benders master trial to a trust region around a reference point, update that center and radius by model agreement, and terminate by the certified bound gap.
assumptions_latex: The current Benders master has feasible set \(X\), known master-objective term \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), epigraph variable \(\theta\), cut model \(m_k(x)=\max_{j\in J_k}\{\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\}\), and reference point \(c_k\in X\).
A radius \(\Delta_k>0\) and norm \(\|\cdot\|\) are specified, and the displayed stabilized master attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The next trial point satisfies the current master cuts and lies in the trust region about \(c_k\).

notation.meaning: Current lower model of the Benders value function.

knowledge_statements.title: Level-Set Benders Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Level-set stabilization of a Benders cutting-plane master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(\ell_k\in(L_k,U_k)\), commonly \(\ell_k=L_k+\lambda_k(U_k-L_k)\) with \(\lambda_k\in(0,1)\), and compute \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{D(x,c_k):f(x)+m_k(x)\le\ell_k\}.\] Evaluate the Benders subproblems at \(x^{k+1}\) and add their valid cuts. If the level set is empty, its infeasibility raises the valid lower bound to at least \(\ell_k\); if a feasible evaluated point improves the incumbent, lower \(U_k\). Choose the next level between the updated bounds and stop when \(U_k-L_k\) meets the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a level between current bounds and find the model-feasible point nearest the center; an empty level set improves the lower bound, while evaluated incumbents improve the upper bound.
assumptions_latex: The master domain is \(X\), the known master-objective term is \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(m_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is a globally valid lower model of the Benders value function.
The current master lower bound is \(L_k=\inf_{x\in X}\{f(x)+m_k(x)\}\), the incumbent upper bound is \(U_k\), and \(L_k<\ell_k<U_k\).
A reference center \(c_k\in X\) and distance-generating function \(D(\cdot,c_k)\) are given, and the displayed level subproblem attains a minimizer whenever its feasible set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial point minimizes distance to the center over the selected model level set; emptiness of that set certifies the lower bound \(L_{k+1}\ge\ell_k\).

notation.meaning: Current master lower bound and incumbent upper bound.
Level strictly between the current bounds.
Proximity measure to the reference center.

children.title: Proximal Benders Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization centered on proximity to a reference master solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Benders Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean proximal stabilization of the Benders master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(c_0\in X\) and \(\rho_0>0\). At iteration \(k\), compute \[(x^{k+1},\theta^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\left\{f(x)+\theta+\frac{\rho_k}{2}\|x-c_k\|_2^2:\theta\ge m_k(x)\right\}.\] Evaluate all required Benders subproblems at \(x^{k+1}\), append their valid cuts, and update certified bounds. Accept \(x^{k+1}\) as the next center only under the prescribed serious-step test; otherwise keep \(c_{k+1}=c_k\). Update \(\rho_k\) according to model agreement and stop when the certified gap meets the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add a positive quadratic penalty around a reference center to the cut master, evaluate the resulting trial, and move the center only after an accepted serious step.
assumptions_latex: The Benders master domain \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, \(f:X\to\mathbb R\) is the known master-objective term, and \(m_k\) is the maximum of the accumulated affine Benders cuts.
A center \(c_k\in X\) and parameter \(\rho_k>0\) are specified, and the displayed proximal master attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The quadratic term selects a stabilized master trial while all accumulated Benders cuts remain enforced.

notation.meaning: Maximum of the active affine Benders cuts.
Proximal center and positive penalty weight.

children.title: Regularized Benders Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Broader regularization structures used to control master movement.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Benders Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic additive regularization, including proximal and separable master penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), solve the regularized master \[(x^{k+1},\theta^{k+1})\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X,\,\theta\in\mathbb R}\{f(x)+\theta+\lambda_kR_k(x):\theta\ge m_k(x)\}.\] Evaluate the Benders subproblems at \(x^{k+1}\), add every selected valid cut, and separately compute valid bounds for the original unregularized problem. Update \(R_k\), its reference data, or \(\lambda_k\) using the prescribed acceptance rule. The algorithm must not report the regularized objective as a lower bound on the original objective unless that implication is established independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize the cut master with an added regularizer to control trial points, but compute certificates for the original objective separately unless the regularized value is itself a valid bound.
assumptions_latex: The unstabilized Benders master objective is \(f(x)+\theta\), with \(x\in X\), \(f:X\to\mathbb R\), and \(\theta\ge m_k(x)\).
A proper regularizer \(R_k:X\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and weight \(\lambda_k>0\) are given, and the displayed regularized master attains a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Regularization changes trial-point selection but not the validity of the Benders cuts; original-problem bounds must be certified independently unless the regularized value is known to be valid for that purpose.

children.title: Reference-Center Management
children.top_down_role: Policies for maintaining or replacing stabilization centers.

knowledge_statements.title: Reference-Center Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Serious-step/null-step center policy for stabilized Benders masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After evaluating trial \(x^{k+1}\), classify it as a serious step exactly when \(p_k>0\) and \(a_k\ge\eta p_k\). Set \[c_{k+1}=\begin{cases}x^{k+1},&p_k>0\text{ and }a_k\ge\eta p_k,\\c_k,&p_k=0\text{ or }a_k<\eta p_k.\end{cases}\] In either case, retain every selected valid cut generated at \(x^{k+1}\). On a null step, modify the stabilization parameter so the next trial is more strongly localized when the prescribed policy requires it. Stop only from an original-problem certificate, not merely because the center is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Move the reference center only when positive predicted improvement is accompanied by sufficient evaluated improvement; otherwise keep the center, retain new cuts, and adjust stabilization.
assumptions_latex: Each trial produces a predicted decrease \(p_k\ge0\), an evaluated actual decrease \(a_k\in\mathbb R\), and a threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\).
The current center \(c_k\) and trial \(x^{k+1}\) are evaluated master points for which the prescribed decreases are defined consistently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The center changes only after a serious step; a null step retains the evaluated center while enriching the cut model.

children.title: Regularization Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Performance or certification effects caused by regularization strength.

assumptions_latex: For fixed center \(c\), define \(V(\rho)=\inf_{x\in X}\{F_k(x)+(\rho/2)\|x-c\|_2^2\}\), where \(F_k=f+m_k\).
The infimum is attained for every compared \(\rho>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Increasing the proximal weight cannot increase the distance of a selected minimizer from the center and cannot decrease the regularized optimal value.

notation.meaning: Regularized master value at penalty weight rho.
A minimizer defining the regularized value.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic sensitivity for Euclidean quadratic master regularization.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0<\rho_1<\rho_2\), and choose minimizers \(x_{\rho_i}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{F_k(x)+(\rho_i/2)\|x-c\|_2^2\}\). Then \[ \|x_{\rho_2}-c\|_2\le\|x_{\rho_1}-c\|_2 \quad\text{and}\quad V(\rho_1)\le V(\rho_2). \] Thus a larger weight localizes the master trial more strongly. These monotonicities concern the regularized master only; they do not imply monotone improvement of the evaluated Benders upper bound, nor may \(V(\rho)\) automatically replace the unregularized master lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed center and cut model, increasing the quadratic penalty weakly decreases the trial's distance from the center and weakly increases the regularized master value.
knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Sensitivity

children.title: Benders Cut Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies for admitting candidate Benders cuts to the active master.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Most-violated selection from a finite Benders cut pool.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(j\in P_k\), compute \[v_j^k=\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}\bar x_k-\bar\theta_k.\] Let \(M_k\subseteq P_k\) be the mandatory retention set. Order the indices in \(P_k\setminus M_k\) by nonincreasing \(v_j^k\), and choose \(O_k\subseteq P_k\setminus M_k\) containing at most \(q_k\) indices with the largest positive scores. Activate \(S_k=M_k\cup O_k\) and impose \(\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(j\in S_k\). Resolve ties by the prescribed deterministic rule. If no optional score is positive, set \(O_k=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain every mandatory cut and additionally activate, up to the optional-cut budget, the stored cuts having the greatest positive violations at the candidate master point.
assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), a finite pool \(P_k\) contains valid cuts \(\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\).
A candidate master point \((\bar x_k,\bar\theta_k)\), a mandatory retention set \(M_k\subseteq P_k\), and an optional-cut budget \(q_k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule activates all mandatory cuts and at most \(q_k\) additional cuts having the greatest positive violations at the candidate point.

notation.meaning: Violation score of cut j at the candidate point.
Maximum number of optional selected cuts.
