children.title: Benders Cut Pools
children.top_down_role: Repositories for inactive, deferred, or reusable Benders cuts.

assumptions_latex: Every generated Benders cut has immutable coefficients and validity metadata.
The pool state distinguishes active, inactive, and deleted cuts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A cut pool supports state changes without altering cut validity or confusing inactive storage with permanent deletion.

notation.meaning: Complete set of stored cut records.
Active and inactive subsets of the pool.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract lifecycle state for stored Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Benders cut pool at iteration \(k\) is a finite indexed set \(P_k\) of records \((\alpha_j,\beta_j,\tau_j,s_j,h_j)\), where \(\theta\ge\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}x\) is a valid cut, \(\tau_j\) identifies its cut type, \(s_j\in\{\mathrm{active},\mathrm{inactive}\}\) is its master state, and \(h_j\) stores lifecycle statistics. The sets \(A_k=\{j:s_j=\mathrm{active}\}\) and \(I_k=\{j:s_j=\mathrm{inactive}\}\) partition \(P_k\). A deleted identifier belongs to \(D_k\) and no longer belongs to \(P_k\); deactivation alone moves an index from \(A_k\) to \(I_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders cut pool stores valid cut coefficients, type, active state, and lifecycle statistics, explicitly distinguishing temporary inactivity from permanent deletion.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Pools

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation supports the proposed record schema or the exact active, inactive, and permanently deleted lifecycle semantics.

children.title: Benders Cut Deletion
children.top_down_role: Policies for removing inactive or low-value cuts from the active master.

assumptions_latex: The active master contains a finite set \(A_k\) of valid Benders cuts.
A protected subset \(M_k\subseteq A_k\) contains cuts that the convergence or bound certificate requires to remain available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only unprotected cuts satisfying the declared inactivity criterion are eligible for deletion.

notation.meaning: Recorded age since cut j was last active or violated.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Age-and-slack deletion with explicit protection of certificate-critical cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an age threshold \(T\ge1\) and slack threshold \(\varepsilon\ge0\), compute each active cut's slack at the current master solution, \[ s_j^k=\bar\theta_k-\alpha_j-\beta_j^{\mathsf T}\bar x_k. \] Form \(E_k=\{j\in A_k\setminus M_k:a_j^k\ge T,\ s_j^k>\varepsilon\}\). Delete or deactivate only indices in \(E_k\), update the remaining ages, and preserve sufficient metadata for reactivation whenever the policy permits it. A deletion rule is admissible only if its protected set and regeneration mechanism preserve the convergence assumptions of the underlying Benders method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete only old, sufficiently slack cuts that are not protected by the convergence certificate, retaining metadata when later reactivation is part of the policy.
knowledge_statements.title: Benders Cut Deletion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The age-and-slack deletion rule and the conditions under which protected cuts or regeneration preserve convergence are policy-dependent and uncited.

children.title: Cut Reactivation Policies
children.top_down_role: Conditions for returning pooled cuts to active master use.

assumptions_latex: An inactive pool \(I_k\) stores valid Benders cuts.
A candidate master point \((\bar x_k,\bar\theta_k)\) and activation tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every stored inactive cut violated beyond tolerance is returned to the active master before accepting the candidate point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Violation-triggered reactivation of inactive Benders cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Compute \[ R_k=\left\{j\in I_k:\alpha_j+\beta_j^{\mathsf T}\bar x_k-\bar\theta_k>\varepsilon\right\}. \] Move every \(j\in R_k\) from the inactive pool to the active master and resolve the master before accepting \((\bar x_k,\bar\theta_k)\). If a reactivation budget is imposed, process cuts by nonincreasing violation but continue the resolve-and-scan cycle until no inactive cut exceeds \(\varepsilon\). Update each reactivated cut's age and activity statistics. Permanently deleted cuts can participate only if they are regenerated by a valid separation oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scan inactive cuts at each candidate point, reactivate those violated beyond tolerance, and re-solve until no stored inactive cut remains materially violated.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut Reactivation Policies

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The resolve-and-scan reactivation policy is plausible but has no cited source supporting its exact tolerance, batching, and termination requirements.

children.title: Parallel Benders Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Concurrent solution of separable Benders subproblem systems.

assumptions_latex: For a fixed master trial \(x^k\), the recourse function separates as \(Q(x^k)=\sum_{s=1}^S p_sQ_s(x^k)\).
Each subproblem returns a valid scenario cut or a valid infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Concurrent solution of all independent subproblems yields the same collection of iteration cuts as serial solution, up to solver choices among alternative certificates.

notation.meaning: Common master trial broadcast to workers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of separable Benders subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Broadcast \(x^k\) to workers \(s=1,\ldots,S\). Concurrently solve each subproblem defining \(Q_s(x^k)\) and return either an optimal dual certificate generating \(\theta_s\ge\alpha_s^k+(\beta_s^k)^{\mathsf T}x\), or a valid feasibility certificate. Wait at a barrier until every required worker has returned, verify and aggregate the certificates, append the resulting single-cut or multi-cut representation to the master, and solve for \(x^{k+1}\). Stop when the synchronized master and incumbent bounds certify the requested gap; wall-clock completion alone is not a stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Broadcast one master point, solve all independent Benders subproblems concurrently, synchronize their verified certificates, add the resulting cuts, and then solve the next master.
knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Benders Subproblems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: An authoritative parallel-Benders source is required for the synchronization protocol and the claimed equivalence with serial cut generation, including treatment of alternative certificates.

children.title: Asynchronous Benders Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Subproblem processing without iteration-wide synchronization.

assumptions_latex: Worker \(s\) evaluates master points tagged by monotonically increasing versions \(t\).
Every returned certificate records its generating point and defines a globally valid Benders cut, not merely a local approximation.
Communication delays are finite, and every required subproblem is processed infinitely often unless termination occurs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cuts may be incorporated without a global barrier because global validity is independent of the master version at which they arrive.

notation.meaning: Master version attached to a dispatched point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barrier-free Benders with globally valid, version-tagged cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dispatch each versioned point \((t,x^t)\) to available workers without waiting for all earlier tasks. When worker \(s\) returns a certificate tagged \((s,t)\), verify that it yields a globally valid cut and append that cut to the current master even when \(t<k\); discard only duplicates or invalid certificates. Re-solve the master after the prescribed number or batch of arrivals and dispatch the new point. Maintain outstanding-work records so every required subproblem is eventually evaluated. Declare convergence only after the current incumbent and master bound certify the tolerance and all certificates required by the stopping protocol have been collected.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Workers evaluate versioned master points without barriers; globally valid returned cuts enter the current master despite delay, while fairness and a synchronized final certificate govern termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Benders Subproblems

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The barrier-free incorporation rule and its fairness, delay, outstanding-work, and stopping conditions are convergence-sensitive and have no authoritative citation.

children.title: Stale Subproblem Results
children.top_down_role: Validity plus usefulness of results returned after the master state has changed.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Subproblem Results
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity boundary for delayed results in asynchronous Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master iteration \(k\), let a worker return a cut \(c_j(x,\theta)\le 0\) computed from an earlier point \(x^j\), where \(j<k\). The result may be inserted without recomputation if its certificate establishes \(c_j(x,Q(x))\le 0\) for every \(x\in X\). Its age does not affect validity. If the certificate establishes validity only near \(x^j\), depends on superseded data, or satisfies an error tolerance not accepted at iteration \(k\), the stale result must be revalidated or discarded; otherwise it can remove a feasible epigraph point and invalidate the Benders bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A delayed cut remains usable only when its certificate proves current global validity; age alone is harmless, but local, obsolete, or excessively inexact certificates require revalidation.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and the recourse function \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) define the current master epigraph.
The returned cut and its certificate identify the data version and oracle tolerance used.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c_j(x,Q(x))\le 0\ \forall x\in X\) permits insertion; absence of this guarantee does not.

notation.meaning: recourse value at master point x
cut returned from an earlier worker evaluation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the conditions for accepting stale cuts, including data-version and tolerance handling, require a specific asynchronous or inexact Benders source.

children.title: Distributed Certificate Collection
children.top_down_role: Collection plus reconciliation of certificates from distributed subproblem workers.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Certificate Collection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance certificate for cuts assembled from distributed subproblem workers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(s=1,\ldots,S\), worker \(s\) returns coefficients \((\alpha_s,\beta_s)\) and a checkable dual-feasibility or infeasibility certificate proving \(q_s(x)\ge \alpha_s+\beta_s^{\mathsf T}x\) for every \(x\in X\). A collector verifies worker identity, data version, certificate feasibility, and coefficient consistency. If all required blocks pass, then \(\theta\ge\sum_{s=1}^S(\alpha_s+\beta_s^{\mathsf T}x)\) is a valid aggregate optimality cut. With only a subset \(I\), aggregation is valid only when certified lower bounds for every omitted block are included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Verified block certificates may be summed into an aggregate Benders cut; omitted blocks require certified lower bounds before collection is complete.
assumptions_latex: \(Q(x)=\sum_{s=1}^S q_s(x)\) on the master domain \(X\).
Every accepted worker certificate refers to the same model-data version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(x)\ge\sum_{s=1}^S(\alpha_s+\beta_s^{\mathsf T}x)\) for all \(x\in X\).

notation.meaning: recourse value of distributed block s
certified affine lower-bound coefficients from worker s
subset of workers whose results have arrived

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role and summation argument fit the leaf, but the distributed verification protocol and treatment of omitted blocks lack supporting evidence.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Benders Oracle Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut acceptance and termination rules for certified inexact subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(x^k\in X\), tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\), and master variable \(\theta\), query an oracle for \((\ell_k,u_k,g_k)\) satisfying \(\ell_k\le Q(x^k)\le u_k\), \(u_k-\ell_k\le\varepsilon_k\), and \(Q(x)\ge \ell_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\) for all \(x\in X\). Insert the certified cut \(\theta\ge\ell_k+g_k^{\mathsf T}(x-x^k)\), update global bounds, and reduce \(\varepsilon_k\) whenever oracle error prevents the prescribed optimality-gap test. Stop only when the master lower bound and a certified feasible upper bound differ by at most the requested tolerance; output the incumbent and both certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The manager accepts only certified affine lower bounds, tightens oracle accuracy when errors obstruct progress, and terminates using certified global bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) admits certified affine lower estimators.
A finite incumbent upper bound is obtained whenever termination is declared.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inserted cut is valid on \(X\), and declared termination has a certified optimality gap.

notation.meaning: certified lower and upper recourse values at iteration k
slope of a certified affine recourse underestimator

children.title: Weak Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Valid cuts providing limited separation or bound improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative weakness of a valid cut at a designated master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a(x)=\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) be a valid Benders underestimator of \(Q\) on \(X\), and let \(\bar x\in X\) be the point at which cut quality is assessed. For a prescribed threshold \(\tau\ge0\), the cut is \(\tau\)-weak at \(\bar x\) when its local underestimation gap satisfies \(Q(\bar x)-a(\bar x)>\tau\). Equivalently, in a master solution \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), its violation \(a(\bar x)-\bar\theta\) is too small to meet a specified separation threshold. Weakness is relative to the point and threshold and does not imply invalidity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A valid Benders cut is weak when its underestimator is insufficiently tight, or insufficiently violated, at the point being separated.
assumptions_latex: \(a(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\).
\(\bar x\in X\) and the quality threshold \(\tau\ge0\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q(\bar x)-a(\bar x)>\tau\) defines \(\tau\)-weakness at \(\bar x\).

children.title: Dominated Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts superseded by stronger valid cuts over the relevant master region.

knowledge_statements.title: Dominated Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise dominance between valid Benders recourse underestimators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a_1,a_2:X\to\mathbb R\) be valid affine Benders underestimators, so \(a_i(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). The cut \(\theta\ge a_1(x)\) is dominated on \(X\) by \(\theta\ge a_2(x)\) if \(a_1(x)\le a_2(x)\) for all \(x\in X\), with strict inequality for at least one \(x\in X\). Consequently, replacing the first cut by the second cannot weaken the master epigraph relaxation and strictly strengthens it at some master point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One Benders cut is dominated when another valid cut has an everywhere larger right-hand side and is strictly larger somewhere.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\) is the master domain.
\(a_i(x)\le Q(x)\) for all \(x\in X\) and \(i\in\{1,2\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(a_1\le a_2\) on \(X\) implies that \(\theta\ge a_2(x)\) subsumes \(\theta\ge a_1(x)\).

notation.meaning: valid affine recourse underestimator defining cut i

children.title: Redundant Benders Cuts
children.top_down_role: Cuts adding no effective restriction to the current master description.

knowledge_statements.title: Redundant Benders Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Redundancy relative to the current Benders master relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\subseteq X\times\mathbb R\) be the feasible region defined by the master constraints and the current cut pool, excluding a candidate cut \(c:\theta\ge a(x)\). The cut \(c\) is redundant relative to \(M\) if every \((x,\theta)\in M\) already satisfies \(\theta\ge a(x)\). Equivalently, \(\inf_{(x,\theta)\in M}(\theta-a(x))\ge0\). Adding a redundant cut leaves the master feasible region and its optimal value unchanged, although it may alter the numerical behavior of the solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders cut is redundant when all points allowed by the remaining master constraints already satisfy it.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is the master feasible region before insertion of the candidate cut.
\(a(x)\) is finite on the projection of \(M\) onto \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\cap\{(x,\theta):\theta\ge a(x)\}=M\).

notation.meaning: master feasible region without the candidate cut

children.title: Cut Quality Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Structural indicators used to distinguish weak, dominated, or redundant cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Quality Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable diagnostics for validity, violation, efficacy, dominance, and redundancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a candidate cut \(\theta\ge a(x)=\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\), a master point \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), domain \(X\), and current master region \(M\), compute violation \(v=a(\bar x)-\bar\theta\) and normalized efficacy \(e=v/\max\{1,\|(\beta,-1)\|_2\}\). Verify the oracle certificate for global validity. Test dominance against a stored cut \(a_i\) by minimizing \(a-a_i\) over \(X\), and test redundancy by minimizing \(\theta-a(x)\) over \(M\). Report validity status, \(v\), \(e\), detected dominators, and redundancy; reject any cut lacking a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic checks certification, violation, normalized efficacy, pointwise dominance, and redundancy against the current master region.
assumptions_latex: The auxiliary minimizations over \(X\) and \(M\) can be solved or bounded reliably.
All compared cuts use the same master-variable and data conventions.

children.title: Benders Master Oscillation
children.top_down_role: Repeated movement among materially different master solutions with limited progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent alternation of master solutions without proportional bound progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For master iterates \(x^k\in X\), define oscillation over a window of length \(w\ge2\) by repeated large moves \(\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\ge\delta_x\) while the lower-bound improvement satisfies \(0\le L_k-L_{k-w}\le\delta_L\). A two-region oscillation is witnessed more specifically when \(x^k\) repeatedly returns within radius \(r\) of \(x^{k-2}\) but remains farther than \(\delta_x\) from \(x^{k-1}\). This behavior does not by itself violate cut validity, but it marks a failure of stable master progress and can justify stabilization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Master oscillation is repeated substantial movement, often between regions, while the certified lower bound improves little.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a nondecreasing certified master lower bound.
\(w,\delta_x,\delta_L>0\) and \(r\ge0\) are prescribed diagnostic parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Persistent satisfaction of the movement and low-progress tests identifies an oscillatory instability regime.

notation.meaning: certified master lower bound at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role is appropriate, but the windowed oscillation criteria and two-region test are algorithm-dependent conventions with no cited source.

children.title: Benders Master Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of master solutions or dual information to small model changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Master Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Windowed condition detecting unstable master movement and inadequate progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^k\) be master solutions and \(L_k\) their certified lower bounds. For fixed \(w\ge2\), define \(D_k=\max_{k-w<i\le k}\|x^i-x^{i-1}\|\) and \(P_k=L_k-L_{k-w}\). The master is diagnostically unstable at iteration \(k\) when \(D_k\ge\delta_x\) and \(P_k\le\delta_L\), or when repeated changes of active cuts produce distinct master solutions with the same lower bound within tolerance \(\delta_L\). This is an operational condition, not a claim that the unstabilized Benders method is mathematically divergent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Instability is flagged when master solutions move substantially or change active faces repeatedly while the certified lower bound barely improves.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\ge L_{k-1}\) for every recorded iteration.
\(w,\delta_x,delta_L\) are fixed diagnostic parameters with \(w\ge2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D_k\ge\delta_x\) and \(P_k\le\delta_L\) trigger the instability flag.

notation.meaning: largest consecutive master displacement in the window

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits, but the proposed instability definition has no source and the assumptions contain an unformatted delta_L rather than the introduced symbol \(\delta_L\).

children.title: Degeneracy-Driven Cycling
children.top_down_role: Recurrent master behavior associated with degeneracy or alternate optima.

knowledge_statements.title: Degeneracy-Driven Cycling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated master states caused by alternative degenerate optima and nonprogressing cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Degeneracy-driven cycling occurs when there exist indices \(i<j\) such that the master state repeats, \((x^j,	heta^j)=(x^i,	heta^i)\), the certified lower bound is unchanged, \(L_j=L_i\), and every intervening generated cut is valid but fails to exclude the repeated state. A sufficient mechanism is a degenerate subproblem dual face from which the oracle repeatedly selects different multipliers inducing identical or nonseparating master cuts. Without deterministic tie-breaking, cut strengthening, or a rule forbidding repeated ineffective oracle outputs, finite termination cannot be inferred merely from repeated subproblem solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cycling arises when degeneracy permits repeated master states and valid but ineffective cuts, so solving subproblems repeatedly does not ensure progress.
assumptions_latex: Master and subproblem solves may return alternative optima under ties.
No rule requires a newly generated cut to separate the repeated master state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A repeated state with unchanged bound and no separating cut is a certificate of algorithmic cycling.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A single repeated master state with unchanged bounds does not by itself certify indefinite cycling unless the full algorithmic state and deterministic transition behavior also repeat. The degeneracy and finite-termination claims require a source.

children.title: Stabilization Trigger Diagnostics
children.top_down_role: Indicators that master behavior warrants stabilization or regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Trigger Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for activating stabilization from windowed progress and movement statistics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a window \(w\ge 2\), movement threshold \(\delta_x>0\), progress threshold \(\delta_L\ge 0\), and repeat limit \(r\ge 1\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(D_k=\max_{k-w<i\le k}\lVert x^i-x^{i-1}\rVert\), \(P_k=L_k-L_{k-w}\), and the number \(R_k\) of previously visited master states repeated within a chosen tolerance. Activate stabilization when \(D_k\ge\delta_x\) and \(P_k\le\delta_L\), or when \(R_k\ge r\). Deactivate it only after a prescribed number of windows exhibit adequate bound progress; record the triggering statistic and parameter values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The diagnostic activates stabilization after large low-progress movement or repeated states, and releases it only after sustained certified progress.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a certified nondecreasing lower bound.
Distances and repeated-state tests use fixed scaling and tolerances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule produces a reproducible stabilization decision from \((D_k,P_k,R_k)\).

notation.meaning: number of repeated master states in the diagnostic history

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertified Subproblem Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary when subproblem outputs lack validity certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a subproblem oracle queried at \(x^k\) returns an affine function \(a_k(x)\) but provides no verifiable guarantee that \(a_k(x)\le Q(x)\) for every \(x\in X\). Inserting \(\theta\ge a_k(x)\) as a Benders optimality cut is then uncertified: if some \(\hat x\in X\) satisfies \(a_k(\hat x)>Q(\hat x)\), the cut removes the valid epigraph point \((\hat x,Q(\hat x))\). Consequently, neither the master bound nor a termination claim based on that bound is certified unless the oracle output is independently validated or replaced by a rigorously error-adjusted cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle output without a global validity certificate may exclude feasible epigraph points, invalidating master bounds and any resulting termination claim.
assumptions_latex: \(Q:X\to\overline{\mathbb R}\) is the recourse value function.
The master interprets \(a_k\) as a global lower estimator of \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Without a verifiable guarantee that \(a_k(x)\le Q(x)\) on \(X\), the generated cut and derived master bound are uncertified.

notation.meaning: affine function returned by the subproblem oracle

A master incumbent \(\bar y\in Y\) and a proposed reconstruction \(\hat x\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\hat x\notin X\) or \(B\hat x<b-A\bar y\), then \((\bar y,\hat x)\) is not a feasible incumbent of the original problem.

notation.meaning: Master incumbent and reconstructed subproblem point.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility failure in primal reconstruction from a Benders master incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the original problem \(\min\{c^\top y+d^\top x: Ay+Bx\ge b,\ y\in Y,\ x\in X\}\). A Benders master solution \(\bar y\) does not by itself define a feasible incumbent. A proposed reconstruction \(\hat x\) is valid only if \(\hat x\in X\) and \(B\hat x\ge b-A\bar y\). If either condition fails, then \((\bar y,\hat x)\) is infeasible for the original formulation, irrespective of master feasibility, the value of an auxiliary recourse variable, or satisfaction of accumulated Benders cuts. Consequently, its objective value cannot be used as a primal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Benders master solution becomes a valid incumbent only after reconstructing a subproblem point satisfying every original constraint; otherwise its objective is not a primal bound.
knowledge_statements.title: Invalid Incumbent Reconstruction

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a block \(i\). Let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron with extreme-point set \(V_i\), let \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\) be its linking matrix, and let \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be its objective vector. An extreme-point column indexed by \(v\in V_i\) has a nonnegative weight \(\lambda_{iv}\ge 0\), contributes \(v\lambda_{iv}\) to the block reconstruction, has linking entries \(A_i v\), and has objective coefficient \(c_i^\top v\). The point-column weights satisfy \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1\) when they represent one convex combination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed block, each extreme point defines a nonnegative master column whose linking entries and cost are obtained by applying the block linking matrix and objective vector to that point.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a block \(i\). Let \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be a nonempty pointed unbounded polyhedron with extreme-point set \(V_i\) and extreme-ray set \(R_i\). Let \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\) and \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\) define its linking and objective coefficients. A ray column indexed by \(r\in R_i\) has a nonnegative weight \(\mu_{ir}\ge0\), contributes \(r\mu_{ir}\) to the block reconstruction, has linking entries \(A_i r\), and has objective coefficient \(c_i^\top r\). In the representation \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}+\sum_{r\in R_i}r\mu_{ir}\), only the point weights satisfy the convexity equation \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1\); ray weights represent conic recession directions and are excluded from that equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each extreme ray defines a nonnegative recession column with its own linking entries and cost, while its weight is excluded from the block convexity equation.

The reconstructed aggregate block vector is \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}\). For \(m_i=1\), the row reduces to the usual convexity equation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) be a finite set of block indices. For every \(i\in I\), let \(V_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be a nonempty set of point generators and impose \(\lambda_{iv}\ge0\) for every \(v\in V_i\). A block-indexed convexity system consists of \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1\) for every \(i\in I\). Each equation normalizes only the point weights of its own block, so \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}\) lies in \(\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\) independently for every \(i\). Global linking constraints may then couple the reconstructed block vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A block-indexed convexity system gives each block its own normalization equation, preserving separate convex combinations while global linking constraints may coordinate the blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}\) and impose \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=m_i\). Although each pattern column is generated from the same block set, its coefficient cannot be chosen independently: increasing one \(\lambda_{iv}\) consumes part of the common multiplicity \(m_i\) and restricts all other weights of type \(i\). Moreover, the aggregate linking contribution is \(A_i x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}A_i v\lambda_{iv}\). Thus the multiplicity row couples within-type pattern selection, while linking rows transmit the aggregate choice across block types.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common multiplicity budget couples pattern weights within a block type, and their aggregate resource use then couples that type to the global master.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each block feasible set \(P_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be a nonempty polytope with extreme-point set \(V_i\). In any optimization model whose objective and linking constraints are linear in \(x_i\), replace \(x_i\in P_i\) by \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i}v\lambda_{iv}\), \(\sum_{v\in V_i}\lambda_{iv}=1\), and \(\lambda_{iv}\ge0\). Because \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)\), the extended formulation projects exactly onto the original block-feasible region. Corresponding feasible solutions have identical linking activity and objective value, so the original and Dantzig–Wolfe formulations have the same optimum.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_i\) be a nonempty pointed polyhedron with extreme-point set \(V_i\) and extreme-ray set \(R_i\). By the Minkowski–Weyl representation \(P_i=\operatorname{conv}(V_i)+\operatorname{cone}(R_i)\), this substitution is exact. Omitting ray columns generally destroys equivalence by excluding feasible recession directions and may incorrectly make the reformulated master bounded or infeasible.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_i=P_i\cap(\mathbb Z^{p_i}\times\mathbb R^{n_i-p_i})\), and suppose its integer hull \(H_i=\operatorname{conv}(X_i)\) is a polytope with extreme-point set \(V_i^I\). Substituting \(x_i=\sum_{v\in V_i^I}v\lambda_{iv}\), \(\sum_{v\in V_i^I}\lambda_{iv}=1\), and \(\lambda_{iv}\ge0\) represents \(H_i\) exactly. Therefore the resulting master is equivalent to replacing every block set by its blockwise integer hull. Under cross-block linking constraints, this relaxation need not equal the convex hull of the globally feasible mixed-integer set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns from each block’s integer hull exactly convexify that block, but blockwise convexification can remain weaker than the global mixed-integer hull.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dantzig–Wolfe formulation for block-diagonal binary programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multi-block specialization with one convexity equation per independent block and coupling through linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For j=1,\ldots,p, let Q_j=\{z\in\{0,1\}^{n_j}:B_jz\le b^j\}. For a binary program whose blocks are coupled by \sum_{j=1}^pD_jx^j\le d, its Dantzig\text{--}Wolfe relaxation is \max\sum_{j=1}^p\sum_{v\in Q_j}(c^jv)\lambda_v^j subject to \sum_{j=1}^p\sum_{v\in Q_j}(D_jv)\lambda_v^j\le d, \sum_{v\in Q_j}\lambda_v^j=1 for every j, and \lambda_v^j\ge0. In the pure binary case, imposing \lambda_v^j\in\{0,1\} for every j and v\in Q_j yields the Dantzig\text{--}Wolfe reformulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Represent each independent binary block as a convex combination of its feasible binary vectors, retain the linking constraints, and impose one convexity equation per block. Requiring the block weights to be binary gives the corresponding pure-binary reformulation.
assumptions_latex: x^j\in\{0,1\}^{n_j}\quad(j=1,\ldots,p).
B_jx^j\le b^j\quad(j=1,\ldots,p),\qquad \sum_{j=1}^pD_jx^j\le d.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\ge0,\quad \sum_{v\in Q_j}\lambda_v^j=1\ (j=1,\ldots,p),\quad \sum_{j=1}^p\sum_{v\in Q_j}(D_jv)\lambda_v^j\le d\text{ define the block Dantzig--Wolfe relaxation; binary }\lambda\text{ yields the pure-binary reformulation.}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given finite sets \(R_k\subseteq\mathcal P_k\), the block-separable restricted master is
\[
\min_{\lambda\ge 0}\ \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in R_k}c_k^{\mathsf T}v^{kp}\lambda_{kp}
\]
subject to
\[
\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in R_k}A_kv^{kp}\lambda_{kp}=b,\qquad
\sum_{p\in R_k}\lambda_{kp}=1\quad(k\in K).
\]
Its reconstructed block solution is \(x^k=\sum_{p\in R_k}v^{kp}\lambda_{kp}\). Enlarging any \(R_k\) preserves every previously feasible master solution and cannot increase the restricted-master optimum in this minimization convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted master selects convex combinations of retained columns independently by block while enforcing the shared linking constraints.

children.title: Cross-Block Column Coordination

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Column Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous coordination of independently priced blocks through shared dual prices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and initialize finite column sets \(R_k\) for which the restricted master is feasible and has a finite optimum, using a feasibility phase if necessary. At iteration \(t\), solve the restricted master and obtain a linking-row price \(\pi^t\) and convexity-row prices \(\sigma_k^t\). For every block \(k\in K\), solve
\[
x_k^t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_k} r_k^t(x),\qquad r_k^t(x)=c_k^{\mathsf T}x-(\pi^t)^{\mathsf T}A_kx-\sigma_k^t.
\]
Add one or more columns from blocks satisfying \(r_k^t(x_k^t)<-\varepsilon\), and reoptimize the common master. Stop when \(r_k^t(x_k^t)\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(k\in K\). For \(\varepsilon=0\) and exact pricing, this stopping test certifies optimality for the full master LP; for \(\varepsilon>0\), it is a tolerance-based pricing termination test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All blocks receive the common linking prices, solve their pricing problems independently, and return sufficiently negative-reduced-cost columns to one master. Exact zero-tolerance pricing certifies full-master LP optimality when no block finds a negative reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The block index set is \(K\), and block \(k\) has pricing set \(X_k\), cost vector \(c_k\), and linking matrix \(A_k\).
The current restricted master is feasible, has a finite optimum, and supplies an optimal dual solution.
The tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and every stated pricing problem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Shared master prices coordinate independent block pricing; exact pricing with \(\varepsilon=0\) terminates precisely when no block violates a full-master dual inequality.

notation.meaning: dual price of block \(k\)'s convexity equation at iteration \(t\)
reduced cost of candidate \(x\) from block \(k\) at iteration \(t\)

knowledge_statements.title: Identical-Block Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregation under complete block interchangeability and permutation symmetry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K=\{1,\ldots,m\}\) index \(m\ge1\) interchangeable blocks, let \(\mathcal P\) be a finite common column index set, and let \(v^p\in X\) for every \(p\in\mathcal P\). Suppose \(\lambda_{kp}\ge0\), \(\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\lambda_{kp}=1\), and \(x^k=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}v^p\lambda_{kp}\) for every \(k\in K\). Defining \(\mu_p=\sum_{k\in K}\lambda_{kp}\) gives
\[
\mu_p\ge0,\qquad \sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\mu_p=m,\qquad \sum_{k\in K}x^k=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}v^p\mu_p.
\]
If every master coefficient and objective coefficient depends on the block variables only through \(\sum_{k\in K}x^k\), the variables \(\lambda_{kp}\) may be replaced by the aggregate weights \(\mu_p\). Conversely, every \(\mu\ge0\) satisfying \(\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}\mu_p=m\) admits the disaggregation \(\lambda_{kp}=\mu_p/m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When identical blocks are completely permutation-symmetric and enter the master only through their sum, their individual column weights can be replaced by aggregate column weights totaling the number of blocks.
assumptions_latex: There are \(m\ge1\) interchangeable blocks with the same feasible set \(X\), finite column family \(\{v^p:p\in\mathcal P\}\), costs, and linking coefficients.
The master formulation is invariant under permutations of block labels and depends on block variables only through their sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Individual block weights may be replaced by aggregate weights \(\mu_p\) without changing the projected aggregate feasible set or objective value.

notation.meaning: aggregate weight assigned to common column \(p\)

knowledge_statements.title: Additional Original Variables in the Master
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Partial reformulation retaining nondecomposed original variables explicitly; pricing duals refer to the master LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be the block index set. If \(x^k=\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}v^{kp}\lambda_{kp}\) is reformulated for each \(k\in K\), while \(y\in Y\) remains explicit, the master representation is
\[
\min\ d^{\mathsf T}y+\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}c_k^{\mathsf T}v^{kp}\lambda_{kp}
\]
subject to
\[
Dy+\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}A_kv^{kp}\lambda_{kp}=b,
\qquad \sum_{p\in\mathcal P_k}\lambda_{kp}=1\quad(k\in K),
\qquad y\in Y,
\qquad \lambda\ge0.
\]
Thus only the decomposed blocks are replaced by columns, while \(y\) retains its native bounds and, when applicable, integrality restrictions. Reduced-cost pricing based on master dual prices applies to the LP relaxation of this representation or to a node relaxation in which the required integer decisions are fixed or relaxed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial Dantzig–Wolfe reformulation can retain selected original variables directly in the master while columnizing only decomposable blocks; dual-price pricing is performed on the relevant master LP relaxation.
assumptions_latex: The variables \(y\in Y\) are not represented by block columns.
The matrix \(D\) and vector \(d\) are respectively the linking coefficients and linear costs of \(y\).
For each \(k\in K\), \(\mathcal P_k\) indexes structural columns \(v^{kp}\) for the reformulated block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Keeping \(y\) explicitly produces a partial Dantzig–Wolfe master; when \(Y\) imposes integrality, column-pricing duals are taken from the applicable LP relaxation.

notation.meaning: original variables retained explicitly in the master

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Restricted-master column-generation test and pricing step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation for a maximization-form Dantzig–Wolfe relaxation with point and extreme-ray columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a feasible restricted master using K'\subseteq K and H'\subseteq H, unboundedness of the restricted master implies unboundedness of the full Dantzig\text{--}Wolfe relaxation. Otherwise, let (\bar\pi,\bar\sigma) be an optimal restricted-master dual solution. The reduced costs are \bar c_k=(c-\bar\pi A_1)v^k-\bar\sigma and \bar c_h=(c-\bar\pi A_1)r^h. Solve \zeta=-\bar\sigma+\max_{x\in Q}(c-\bar\pi A_1)x. If pricing is unbounded, a positive-reduced-cost extreme-ray column exists. If pricing is bounded and \zeta>0, a positive-reduced-cost point column exists. If pricing is bounded and \zeta\le0, all omitted columns have nonpositive reduced cost and the restricted-master optimum, extended by zero-valued omitted variables, is optimal for the full relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a feasible restricted master and use its optimal dual prices to price omitted columns. Unbounded pricing identifies an improving ray, a positive finite pricing value identifies an improving point column, and a nonpositive finite value certifies full-master optimality. An unbounded restricted master implies that the full relaxation is unbounded.
assumptions_latex: K'\subseteq K,\ H'\subseteq H\text{ define a feasible restricted master}.
(\bar\pi,\bar\sigma)\text{ is an optimal restricted-master dual solution when the restricted master is bounded}.
\zeta=-\bar\sigma+\max_{x\in Q}(c-\bar\pi A_1)x.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Bounded pricing with }\zeta\le0\text{ certifies full-master optimality; }\zeta>0\text{ yields an improving point column; unbounded pricing yields an improving extreme-ray column.}

knowledge_statements.title: Structural Initial Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and feasibility conditions for genuine starting columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each block \(k\in K\), let \(\mathcal P_k\) index structural columns \(v^{kp}\in X_k\), and let \(R_k^0\subseteq\mathcal P_k\) be finite and nonempty. The retained family is a structural initialization because every retained column is a genuine point of its block set. It gives a feasible initial restricted master exactly when there exist weights \(\lambda_{kp}^0\ge0\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{p\in R_k^0}\lambda_{kp}^0=1\quad(k\in K),
\qquad \sum_{k\in K}\sum_{p\in R_k^0}A_kv^{kp}\lambda_{kp}^0=b.
\]
Structural validity alone does not imply linking-row feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initial structural columns must be genuine block-feasible points; they yield a feasible initial master exactly when blockwise convex combinations satisfy all linking rows.
assumptions_latex: The set \(K\) indexes the blocks, and \(\mathcal P_k\) indexes columns \(v^{kp}\in X_k\) for block \(k\).
For every \(k\in K\), a finite nonempty initial set \(R_k^0\subseteq\mathcal P_k\) is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initial columns are structurally valid when they belong to their block sets; master feasibility additionally requires compatible convex combinations satisfying the linking rows.

children.title: Artificial Master Columns
children.top_down_role: Temporary columns used to establish an initial restricted-master representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial Master Columns
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Signed artificial unit columns for equality-form restricted-master feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider an equality-form structural restricted master \(B\lambda=d\) with \(\lambda\in\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\), where \(\Lambda\) contains the structural side constraints on the retained column weights. Artificial master columns are auxiliary signed unit columns that produce
\[
B\lambda+a^+-a^-=d,
\qquad \lambda\in\Lambda,\quad a^+,a^-\ge0.
\]
For any \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), choosing \(a^+=(d-B\lambda)_+\) and \(a^-=(B\lambda-d)_+\) satisfies the augmented equations. The artificial variables are bookkeeping devices rather than structural block columns: they are excluded from block reconstruction and must be zero before the solution is feasible for the structural master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Signed artificial unit columns absorb equality-row infeasibility while preserving the structural side constraints, but they must vanish before a structural solution is accepted.
assumptions_latex: The structural restricted master has equality rows \(B\lambda=d\) and an admissible nonempty set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R_+^n\) for its column weights.
Artificial variables are introduced only to relax the equality rows and do not represent feasible block points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Artificial master columns make the augmented equality rows feasible for any \(\lambda\in\Lambda\), but structural feasibility requires \(a^+=a^-=0\).

notation.meaning: structural master matrix and structural column weights
admissible set defined by the structural side constraints on \(\lambda\)
nonnegative positive and negative artificial variables

children.title: Phase-I Restricted Masters

knowledge_statements.title: Phase-I Restricted Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary feasibility optimization before the true master objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), denote the structural master over the current columns, and augment it as \(B\lambda+a^+-a^-=d\) with \(a^+,a^-\ge0\). Repeatedly solve
\[
\phi^*=\min\left\{\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}(a^++a^-):B\lambda+a^+-a^-=d,\ \lambda,a^+,a^-\ge0\right\},
\]
use an optimal Phase-I dual vector to price structural columns, add any improving structural columns, and reoptimize. If \(\phi^*=0\), retain \(\lambda\) and remove the artificial variables to obtain a feasible structural initialization. If exact pricing over the complete structural-column family finds no improving column while \(\phi^*>0\), then the full structural master is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Phase I minimizes total artificial activity while generating structural columns. Zero activity yields a feasible structural initialization; positive terminal activity certifies full-master infeasibility only after exact pricing over every structural column finds no improvement.
assumptions_latex: The matrix \(B\) contains the current structural master columns and \(d\) is the master right-hand side.
Signed nonnegative artificial variables \(a^+,a^-\) make the augmented equality system feasible.
Any asserted infeasibility conclusion uses exact pricing over the complete structural-column family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Phase I either reaches \(\phi^*=0\) and supplies a feasible structural master point, or, after exact exhaustive pricing, certifies infeasibility of the full structural master.

children.title: Artificial-Column Penalties
children.top_down_role: Penalty structures controlling the use of artificial columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Artificial-Column Penalties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exactness requirement for finite penalties on artificial master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the structural master be \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), with objective \(q^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), and let \(Ea\) be the contribution of nonnegative artificial variables \(a\ge0\). Consider
\[
\min\left\{q^{\mathsf T}\lambda+M\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}a:B\lambda+Ea=d,\ \lambda,a\ge0\right\}.
\]
A coefficient \(M>0\) is an exact artificial-column penalty if, whenever the structural system \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), is feasible, every optimum of the penalized problem satisfies \(a=0\). A finite value of \(M\) has this property only when a problem-specific bound establishes that retaining positive artificial mass cannot be optimal; choosing a large finite value without such a bound does not certify structural feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite artificial-column penalty is exact only when a problem-specific bound ensures that every penalized optimum eliminates artificial activity whenever the structural master is feasible.
assumptions_latex: The structural master is \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), with linear objective \(q^{\mathsf T}\lambda\) and a finite attained optimum whenever it is feasible.
The matrix \(E\) gives the master-row coefficients of nonnegative artificial variables \(a\), which are absent from the original formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalty \(M\) is valid for feasibility restoration only if structural feasibility implies \(a=0\) at every penalized optimum; this exactness requires a justified problem-specific bound.

artificial-column matrix and nonnegative artificial variables

knowledge_statements.title: Structural-Column Transition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transition from feasibility restoration to ordinary column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), be the current structural restricted master, and let \((\bar\lambda,\bar a)\) be a Phase-I optimum. Test whether \(\bar a=0\). If the test fails, continue feasibility pricing. If it holds, delete the artificial variables or fix them at zero, restore the structural objective \(q^{\mathsf T}\lambda\), warm-start the restricted master at \(\bar\lambda\), and resume structural reduced-cost pricing. Because \(B\bar\lambda=d\), deleting zero-valued artificial columns preserves primal feasibility. Subsequent column admission and termination tests use reduced costs for the structural objective rather than Phase-I feasibility reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Once every artificial variable is zero, remove or fix the artificials, restore the structural objective, retain the feasible structural solution, and continue ordinary reduced-cost pricing.
assumptions_latex: The current structural master is \(B\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), with objective vector \(q\).
Phase I has produced an augmented-master optimum \((\bar\lambda,\bar a)\) satisfying \(\bar a=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Removing zero-valued artificial columns preserves feasibility, after which optimization continues under the structural objective using structural reduced costs.

assumptions_latex: The current restricted master is infeasible.
A Farkas ray for its equality rows and nonnegative variables is available.
Each block pricing problem is solved exactly over its full column set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Either pricing finds a column that violates the Farkas inequality, or the ray certifies infeasibility of the full master.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-form feasibility pricing under the stated Farkas sign convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the infeasible system \(B_R\lambda=d\), \(\lambda\ge0\), let \(y\) satisfy
\[
B_R^{\mathsf T}y\le0,
\qquad d^{\mathsf T}y>0.
\]
Farkas pricing searches the full structural column family \(\mathcal B\) for
\[
b^*\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{b\in\mathcal B} b^{\mathsf T}y.
\]
If \((b^*)^{\mathsf T}y>0\), adding \(b^*\) invalidates the ray and may restore restricted-master feasibility. If the exact maximum is nonpositive, then every full-master column satisfies \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\), so \(y\) is a verifiable Farkas certificate that the full structural master is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible master supplies a Farkas ray; pricing either finds a column that cuts off the ray or certifies full-master infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the restricted master
\[
\min\{c_R^{\mathsf T}\lambda:B_R\lambda=d, \lambda\ge0\},
\]
the dual-price problem is
\[
\max\{d^{\mathsf T}y:B_R^{\mathsf T}y\le c_R, y\in\mathbb R^m\}.
\]
At optimal solutions \(\lambda^*\) and \(y^*\), strong duality gives \(c_R^{\mathsf T}\lambda^*=d^{\mathsf T}y^*\), and complementary slackness gives \(\lambda_j^*(c_j-b_j^{\mathsf T}y^*)=0\) for every retained column \(j\). The vector \(y^*\), including convexity-row components, is the restricted-master price signal passed to pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master dual prices value the master rows, satisfy all retained-column inequalities, and provide the multipliers used by pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Cost Pricing Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost signal and full-master LP optimality certificate for a minimization master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a candidate full-master column \(b\) with objective coefficient \(c(b)\), its reduced cost at a restricted-master dual optimum \(y^*\) is
\[
\bar c(b)=c(b)-b^{\mathsf T}y^*.
\]
In a minimization master, \(\bar c(b)<0\) means that the omitted full-dual inequality \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le c(b)\) is violated by \(y^*\). Adding such a column cannot increase the restricted-master optimum and provides a candidate for primal improvement, although degeneracy can prevent strict improvement. If exact pricing establishes \(\min_{b\in\mathcal B_k}\bar c(b)\ge0\) for every block \(k\), then \(y^*\) is feasible for the full master dual, so the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master LP.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Negative reduced cost identifies a violated full-dual inequality and a candidate improving column, though degeneracy may prevent strict objective improvement. Exact absence of negative reduced costs certifies full-master LP optimality.

The full master LP is feasible and has a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A negative reduced cost identifies a violated omitted dual inequality, while nonnegative exact minimum reduced cost over every block certifies full-master LP optimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Block-Specific Price Signals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost signals for a block-angular Dantzig–Wolfe restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let block \(k\) have columns \(p\in P_k\), original costs \(c_{kp}\), linking-column vectors \(a_{kp}\), and convexity coefficients equal to one. If \(\pi\) is the restricted-master multiplier for the linking constraints and \(\sigma_k\) is the multiplier for block \(k\)'s convexity equation, then the block-specific reduced cost is
\[\bar c_{kp}=c_{kp}-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_{kp}-\sigma_k.\]
Thus block \(k\)'s pricing oracle minimizes \(c_k(x)-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_kx-\sigma_k\) over its feasible set \(X_k\). Under minimization, a negative optimum identifies an improving column for that block.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each block receives common linking prices and its own convexity price; minimizing the induced reduced cost either produces an improving block column or certifies none exists.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization linear program.
Each block has a convexity equation \(\sum_{p\in P_k}\lambda_{kp}=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X_k}\{c_k(x)-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_kx-\sigma_k\}<0\) identifies an improving block-\(k\) column.

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for block k's convexity equation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact and certified-inexact reduced-cost signals for a solved restricted master.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose the current restricted master is solved to primal-dual optimality, with linking multiplier \(\pi\) and block-convexity multiplier \(\sigma_k\). For block \(k\), define the reduced-cost function \(r_k(x)=c_k(x)-\pi^{\mathsf T}A_kx-\sigma_k\) on the complete feasible set \(X_k\), and let
\[z_k=\min_{x\in X_k} r_k(x).\]
For a minimization master, \(z_k<0\) exhibits an improving column, whereas \(z_k\ge 0\) certifies that block \(k\) contains no negative-reduced-cost column. If pricing is inexact, a feasible returned column \(\hat x_k\in X_k\) with \(r_k(\hat x_k)<0\) still certifies improvement, while absence of an improving column requires a valid global lower bound \(L_k\le z_k\) satisfying \(L_k\ge 0\). Approximate master multipliers do not provide these conclusions unless a separate certificate accounts for their error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is reliable when exact master prices and a global pricing optimum are available. With inexact pricing, a feasible negative-cost column certifies improvement, while a nonnegative global lower bound certifies that none exists.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Degeneracy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal degeneracy of the linear restricted master at a basic solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a restricted master in equality form
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}\lambda:B\lambda=b,\ \lambda\ge 0\},\]
where \(B\) has row rank \(m\). A feasible basis \(J\) is degenerate if at least one component of the basic vector \(\lambda_J=B_J^{-1}b\) equals zero. Equivalently, fewer than \(m\) basic variables are strictly positive. Restricted-master degeneracy may permit distinct feasible bases to represent the same primal solution and may cause pivots or newly generated columns to yield no immediate objective improvement; it does not by itself imply multiple primal or dual optimal solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-master basis is degenerate when one of its basic variables is zero, allowing basis changes without movement or objective improvement.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has rank \(m\).
\(J\) indexes a feasible nonsingular basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The basis \(J\) is degenerate exactly when \((B_J^{-1}b)_i=0\) for some basic index \(i\).

notation.meaning: basis matrix formed from restricted-master columns indexed by J

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). For the restricted master
\[\min\{c^{\mathsf T}\lambda:B\lambda=b,\ \lambda\ge0\},\]
the dual-optimal set is
\[D^*=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:B^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ b^{\mathsf T}y=v_R\},\]
where \(v_R\) is the finite restricted-master optimum. Alternate dual optima exist precisely when \(D^*\) contains two distinct vectors. Although all members of \(D^*\) give the same restricted-master bound, they can assign different reduced costs \(c_p-y^{\mathsf T}B_p\) to columns absent from the restricted master and therefore induce different pricing searches.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternate dual optima are distinct dual-feasible price vectors attaining the same restricted-master value; they may generate different reduced costs for missing columns.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a finite set of decomposition blocks and let \(P_k\) be the complete family of feasible Dantzig-Wolfe columns for each \(k\in K\). A restricted-master column pool consists of a finite subset \(P_k^R\subseteq P_k\) for every \(k\in K\), together with any required artificial columns, such that the linear restricted master uses only genuine column variables \(\lambda_{kp}\) with \(p\in P_k^R\). The pool is valid for an iteration when the resulting restricted master is feasible or its artificial-variable phase is well defined. Pricing enlarges the pool by the update
\[P_k^R\leftarrow P_k^R\cup Q_k,\]
where \(Q_k\subseteq P_k\setminus P_k^R\) is a finite set of generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The column pool is the finite active subset used by the restricted master; pricing adds newly generated feasible columns to it.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed network with node-arc incidence matrix \(N\), integral balance vector \(d\), integral arc-capacity vector \(u\ge0\), and reduced arc costs \(\bar c_e=c_e-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_e\). A network pricing problem has the form
\[z^*=\min\{\bar c^{\mathsf T}x:Nx=d,\ 0\le x\le u\}.\]
When \(d\) and \(u\) are integral, total unimodularity of \(N\) permits an integral optimal solution whenever the problem is feasible and bounded. Under minimization, \(z^*<0\) yields a negative-reduced-cost network column, while \(z^*\ge0\) certifies that this pricing family contains none.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Network pricing minimizes reduced arc cost over a flow polyhedron; integral data yield integral columns, and the optimum's sign determines improvement.

children.title: Path Pricing Problems

knowledge_statements.title: Path Pricing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained source-to-sink path pricing by reduced arc costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and dual-adjusted arc lengths \(\bar c_e\). Path pricing solves
\[z^*=\min_{P\in\mathcal P_{st}}\left\{\sum_{e\in P}\bar c_e-\sigma\right\},\]
where \(\mathcal P_{st}\) is the admissible family of \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths and \(\sigma\) is any path-family convexity price. If repeated vertices are permitted, finiteness requires no reachable negative-cost cycle lying on an \(s\)-to-\(t\) walk. A shortest path attaining \(z^*<0\) defines an improving master column; \(z^*\ge0\) excludes improving columns from this path family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path pricing is a shortest-path problem in dual-adjusted arc costs; a negative optimum supplies an improving path column.
assumptions_latex: At least one admissible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path exists.
The pricing value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizing path is an improving column if and only if \(z^*<0\).

notation.meaning: convexity-row dual price for the path family

children.title: Resource-Constrained Path Pricing
children.top_down_role: Path pricing subject to resource, timing, or capacity restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Constrained Path Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Path pricing with additive upper-bounded resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a directed graph \(G=(V,E)\), let each arc \(e\) have reduced cost \(\bar c_e\) and nonnegative resource consumption \(r_e\in\mathbb R_+^q\). Given resource limits \(R\in\mathbb R_+^q\), resource-constrained path pricing is
\[z^*=\min_{P\in\mathcal P_{st}}\left\{\sum_{e\in P}\bar c_e-\sigma:\sum_{e\in P}r_e\le R\right\}.\]
The resource inequality is componentwise. Any feasible minimizing path with \(z^*<0\) yields an improving column. A conclusion that no improving column exists requires a global lower bound of at least zero, not merely failure of a heuristic labeling or search procedure to find a negative path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource-constrained pricing finds a minimum-reduced-cost path satisfying additive resource limits; only global optimization can certify that no improving path exists.
assumptions_latex: Arc resource consumptions and limits are componentwise nonnegative.
The constrained path family is nonempty and the pricing value is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible path is improving when its reduced cost is negative; \(z^*\ge0\) certifies absence of improving feasible paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Path Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-constrained path pricing restricted to vertex-simple paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be directed and let \(P=(v_0,e_1,v_1,\ldots,e_ell,v_ell)\) be an \(s\)-to-\(t\) path candidate. The elementary-path condition is
\[v_i\ne v_j\quad\text{for all }0\le i<j\le ell.\]
Elementary path pricing minimizes the applicable reduced-cost function over the subset \(\mathcal P_{st}^{\mathrm{el}}\) satisfying this condition and any stated resource bounds. Because every feasible column visits each vertex at most once, negative cycles cannot be exploited by repetition. A negative global optimum yields an improving elementary column; a nonnegative global optimum certifies that no improving elementary path exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Elementary path pricing restricts candidates to paths visiting every vertex at most once; the globally minimum reduced cost determines whether an improving column exists.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite directed graph.
All additional resource constraints defining admissibility are explicitly imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P\in\mathcal P_{st}^{\mathrm{el}}\) exactly when its vertex sequence has no repetition.

notation.meaning: vertex at position i in the path sequence

children.title: Knapsack Pricing Problems
children.top_down_role: Pricing problems governed by capacity-constrained item selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Knapsack Pricing Problems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-capacity integer knapsack representation of reduced-cost pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let item \(i\) have nonnegative integer weight \(w_i\), integer multiplicity bound \(u_i\), and dual-adjusted profit \(p_i\). A bounded integer knapsack pricing problem is
\[z^*=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i x_i:\sum_{i=1}^n w_i x_i\le W,\ x_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,u_i\}\right\}.\]
If the associated master column has reduced cost \(\sigma-z^*\), the maximizing pattern is improving exactly when \(z^*>\sigma\). The binary case is obtained by setting \(u_i=1\); unbounded multiplicities are represented by omitting finite upper bounds while retaining a finite capacity and positive weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Knapsack pricing maximizes dual-adjusted item profit within one capacity; the resulting pattern improves the master when its profit exceeds the convexity price.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb Z_+\), \(w_i\in\mathbb Z_{>0}\), and \(u_i\in\mathbb Z_+\).
The master uses the reduced-cost convention \(\bar c=\sigma-z^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal knapsack pattern is improving if and only if \(z^*>\sigma\).

Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z_+^n\) be the set of feasible patterns and let each pattern \(x\in X\) contribute master coefficients \(Ax\) with original cost \(c(x)\). Given linking-row prices \(\pi\) and convexity price \(\sigma\), pattern pricing solves

Under a minimization convention, \(z^*<0\) identifies an improving pattern, whereas \(z^*\ge0\) certifies that the modeled pattern family contains no negative-reduced-cost column. If the reduced-cost objective is linear in \(x\) and \(X\) is defined by one additive capacity inequality with integer multiplicities, the pricing problem is an integer knapsack problem; multiple additive capacity inequalities give a multidimensional-knapsack representation.

knowledge_statements.title: Multidimensional Knapsack Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiple-capacity integer knapsack representation of pattern pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let item \(i\) have a nonnegative resource vector \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), multiplicity bound \(u_i\), and dual-adjusted profit \(p_i\). With capacity vector \(b\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), multidimensional knapsack pricing solves
\[z^*=\max\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n p_i x_i:\sum_{i=1}^n a_i x_i\le b,\ x_i\in\{0,1,\ldots,u_i\}\right\},\]
where the capacity inequality is componentwise. If the corresponding master reduced cost is \(\sigma-z^*\), an optimal pattern is improving exactly when \(z^*>\sigma\). Setting \(m=1\) recovers single-capacity bounded knapsack pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multidimensional knapsack pricing maximizes dual-adjusted profit subject to several capacities; improvement occurs when optimal profit exceeds the convexity price.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), \(b\in\mathbb Z_+^m\), and \(u_i\in\mathbb Z_+\).
The master reduced-cost convention is \(\bar c=\sigma-z^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal pattern is improving if and only if \(z^*>\sigma\).

children.title: Bounded Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing oracles equipped with certified objective or reduced-cost bounds.

assumptions_latex: The pricing solver maintains a valid global lower bound \(L\le\rho^*\) and a feasible incumbent value \(U\ge\rho^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The interval \([L,U]\) bounds \(\rho^*\); \(U<0\) proves improvement and \(L\ge0\) proves its absence.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anytime pricing represented by certified lower and upper objective bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bounded pricing call returns \((L,U,\hat y)\) such that \[L\le\rho^*:=\min_{y\in Y}\rho(y)\le U=\rho(\hat y),\qquad \hat y\in Y.\] The interval width \(U-L\) measures unresolved pricing error. If \(U<0\), \(\hat y\) is a verifiably improving column. If \(L\ge0\), no improving column exists. When \(L<0\le U\), the sign of \(\rho^*\) remains undecided, and neither column-generation termination nor absence of an improving column is certified.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded pricing returns certified lower and upper bounds on minimum reduced cost; their signs can prove improvement, prove its absence, or leave the issue unresolved.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The bound interval and its sign implications are correct and certificate is an appropriate kind, but the proposed meaning of bounded pricing has no cited source and may be terminology-dependent.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned feasible point satisfies \(g(\hat y)\ge\alpha g^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative approximation stated on nonnegative improvement gain, avoiding ratios of negative reduced costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An \(\alpha\)-approximate pricing oracle returns a feasible \(\hat y\in Y\) satisfying \[g(\hat y)\ge\alpha g^*,\qquad g(y)=\max\{0,-\rho(y)\},\qquad g^*=\max_{y\in Y}g(y).\] Hence, whenever an improving column exists and \(g^*>0\), the returned column is also improving. For \(\alpha<1\), the oracle does not generally reveal the exact minimum reduced cost. The gain convention is essential because a direct multiplicative ratio for negative reduced-cost minimization is sign-dependent and may be ill-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximate pricing returns a feasible column capturing at least an alpha fraction of the largest available nonnegative reduced-cost improvement.
knowledge_statements.title: Approximate Pricing

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gain-based approximation condition is internally consistent, but it selects a specialized multiplicative convention for approximate pricing without evidence that this is the intended local sense of the leaf.

children.title: Pricing Accuracy Calibration
children.top_down_role: Choice of pricing accuracy across master iterations or search states.

assumptions_latex: A pricing call returns a feasible incumbent value \(U\) satisfying \(0\le U-\rho^*\le\varepsilon\).
The master uses a reduced-cost tolerance \(\tau\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U\ge-\tau\), then \(\rho^*\ge-(\tau+\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive calibration between oracle error and the master reduced-cost threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the pricing oracle guarantees \(0\le U-\rho^*\le\varepsilon\), where \(U\) is the reduced cost of its returned feasible column. If the master accepts pricing as inactive when \(U\ge-\tau\), then \[\rho^*\ge U-\varepsilon\ge-(\tau+\varepsilon).\] Thus the effective worst-case reduced-cost tolerance is \(\tau+\varepsilon\). To enforce a prescribed total tolerance \(\delta\), choose nonnegative budgets satisfying \(\tau+\varepsilon\le\delta\). This calibration is additive and must be applied separately wherever independent pricing errors enter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle error and the master's acceptance threshold add: budgets epsilon and tau guarantee that no omitted column has reduced cost below minus their sum.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Accuracy Calibration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive inequality is mathematically correct and the principle kind fits calibration, but no source supports its use as the intended pricing-accuracy regime or the statement about applying independent errors separately.

children.title: Single-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing iterations that admit one selected improving column.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: At most one newly generated column is admitted after each pricing solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given current dual multipliers, solve \[y^*\in\arg\min_{y\in Y}\rho(y).\] If \(\rho(y^*)<0\) and its column is not already in the restricted master, insert that one column and reoptimize the restricted master. If the selected optimizer is already represented, use another minimum-reduced-cost optimizer not yet represented when one is available; otherwise insert no column on that call. If \(\rho(y^*)\ge0\) under exact pricing, terminate pricing because no improving column exists in \(Y\). Thus each pricing call inserts either zero or one distinct column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Single-column pricing inserts at most one distinct minimum-reduced-cost improving column per pricing call; an exact nonnegative optimum certifies that no improving column exists.
assumptions_latex: The current dual solution defines a pricing problem over a nonempty set \(Y\), and the minimum of \(\rho\) over \(Y\) is attained.
Only columns not already represented in the restricted master are eligible for insertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At most one distinct minimum-reduced-cost improving column is inserted per pricing call.

children.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing iterations that admit several improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite batch insertion from one pricing problem at fixed dual multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(q\in\mathbb N\) and \(\tau\ge0\). At the current dual solution, generate distinct feasible pricing points and form a set \(S\subseteq Y\) satisfying \[|S|\le q,\qquad \rho(y)<-\tau\quad\text{for every }y\in S.\] Insert all columns represented by \(S\) that are not already in the restricted master, and then reoptimize. If \(S=\varnothing\), termination is justified only when a valid exact pricing bound proves \(\min_{y\in Y}\rho(y)\ge-\tau\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple-column pricing may batch up to q distinct columns satisfying the reduced-cost threshold at one dual solution before reoptimizing the restricted master.
assumptions_latex: The pricing procedure can enumerate or retain several distinct feasible solutions in \(Y\).
The batch limit satisfies \(q\in\mathbb N\), and the reduced-cost tolerance satisfies \(\tau\ge0\).
Only distinct columns satisfying \(\rho(y)<-\tau\) and not already present in the restricted master are admitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each call inserts a set of between zero and \(q\) distinct columns satisfying the current reduced-cost threshold.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for adaptively choosing single or batch column insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), a regime selector chooses an integer \(q_t\ge1\), obtains a set \(S_t\) with \(|S_t|\le q_t\), and admits only distinct columns satisfying \(\rho_t(y)<-\tau_t\). The choice \(q_t=1\) gives single-column pricing, while \(q_t>1\) permits batch pricing. Batch size may depend on pricing time, master reoptimization cost, or recent column yield. Regardless of this choice, optimal termination requires a valid exact bound establishing \(\min_{y\in Y}\rho_t(y)\ge-\tau_t\) for every required pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selector may vary the number of accepted columns using computational feedback, provided all columns improve and exact bounds support final termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Column-Multiplicity Regime Selection

assumptions_latex: The decomposed formulation has blocks \(k\in K\) with independent feasible sets \(Y_k\).
At fixed master dual multipliers, each block reduced cost depends only on its own variable \(y_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Global pricing separates into independent block problems, and the best reduced cost is \(\min_{k\in K}\rho_k^*\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-separable Dantzig-Wolfe pricing at fixed dual multipliers.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each \(k\in K\), define an independent pricing optimum \[\rho_k^*=\min_{y_k\in Y_k}\rho_k(y_k).\] Because no pricing constraint couples variables from different blocks, these problems may be solved separately or concurrently at the same master dual solution. The minimum reduced cost over their disjoint union is \[\min_{k\in K}\rho_k^*.\] Any block with \(\rho_k^*<0\) supplies an improving column. Certification that no improving column exists requires \(\rho_k^*\ge0\) for every block whose columns are required by the formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When pricing blocks are uncoupled, each has an independent pricer; any negative block optimum yields a column, while termination requires all block optima nonnegative.
