children.title: Pricing-Problem Selection
children.top_down_role: Policies for choosing which pricing problem receives computational effort.

assumptions_latex: There is a finite active index set \(K_t\) of pricing problems at iteration \(t\).
Each problem has stored state such as its last bound, solution time, and iteration of last exact solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selector returns a nonempty subset \(S_t\subseteq K_t\), while certified termination requires exact coverage of all required indices.

notation.meaning: active pricing-problem indices at iteration t

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Adaptive subset selection among finitely many independent pricing problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(t\), compute for every \(k\in K_t\) a score \(s_{k,t}\) from information available before solving, such as a valid bound, recent improving-column yield, elapsed solution time, and age since last selection. Choose a nonempty subset \[S_t\in\arg\max_{\varnothing\ne S\subseteq K_t,\ |S|\le m_t}\sum_{k\in S}s_{k,t},\] where \(m_t\) is the pricing budget, and solve only problems in \(S_t\). Update their stored states after completion. Before declaring column-generation termination, override selective scheduling and obtain valid exact nonimprovement certificates for every required \(k\in K_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing-problem selection scores active pricers, solves a budgeted nonempty subset, updates their histories, and requires full exact coverage before certified termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Problem Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The score-maximization rule is a framework-specific algorithm rather than a standard consequence of independent pricing, has no supporting citation, and does not explicitly require the budget \(m_t\) to be an integer between one and \(|K_t|\).

children.title: Pricing-Problem Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Timing, ordering, frequency, or interruption policies for pricing problems.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Problem Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A fair scheduler for multiple Dantzig–Wolfe pricing subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given block set \(K\), scheduler state \(s^t\), and restricted-master dual solution \((\pi^t,\sigma^t)\), assign each block a priority \(q_k^t=Q_k(s^t,\pi^t,\sigma^t)\). Select a nonempty set \(S_t\subseteq K\), solve pricing for every \(k\in S_t\), add every returned column having negative reduced cost, and update \(s^{t+1}\) from observed costs, solution times, and reduced costs. If no column is returned, continue until every block has been priced exactly at the current dual solution. Output completion only when all exact pricing minima are nonnegative. Fairness requires that each persistently unresolved block be selected after finitely many scheduling steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Priorities determine which block pricers run. Completion is declared only after every block has been priced exactly and no negative-reduced-cost column exists.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Exact pricing is eventually performed for every persistently unresolved block.
Columns with negative reduced cost are retained for the next restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The scheduler outputs completion only after a complete exact-pricing sweep certifies nonnegative reduced costs for all blocks.

notation.meaning: current linking and convexity dual multipliers

children.title: Adaptive Pricer Coordination
children.top_down_role: Coordination policies that respond to observed pricer performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Pricer Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Online coordination of pricing effort across heterogeneous block pricers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(k\in K\), maintain a state \(s_k^t\) containing its last reduced-cost bound, runtime, and success indicator. After solving the restricted master, choose pricing tolerances \(\varepsilon_k^t\), resource limits \(r_k^t\), and an active set \(S_t\) as functions of the current states. Run selected pricers, add certified negative-reduced-cost columns, and update each observed state. Blocks not proving nonnegativity remain unresolved. Tighten their tolerances and reschedule them under a fairness rule. Terminate only after each block supplies an exact minimum or a valid nonnegative lower bound at the same master-dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinator reallocates pricing accuracy and effort from observed performance, while fairness and a final common-dual certification preserve completion validity.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) is finite.
Every reported pricing lower bound is valid at the stated dual solution.
The fairness rule eventually allocates exact or certifying effort to every unresolved block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies that no block contains a column with negative reduced cost at the final dual solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Improving-Column Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for a minimization-form Dantzig–Wolfe master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider block \(k\) and a column \(j\) with cost \(c_{kj}\) and linking vector \(a_{kj}\). At restricted-master dual multipliers \((\pi,\sigma_k)\), its reduced cost is \(\bar c_{kj}=c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\). The displayed column together with the exact arithmetic inequality \(\bar c_{kj}<0\) is an improving-column certificate: it exhibits a violated full-master dual constraint \(a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sigma_k\le c_{kj}\). The certificate is checked using only the column data and current dual multipliers; it warrants adding the column, although degeneracy may prevent an immediate strict decrease of the restricted-master objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column with negative reduced cost explicitly violates a missing dual constraint and is therefore a verifiable candidate for master improvement.
assumptions_latex: The full master is a minimization problem with block convexity equations.
\((\pi,\sigma)\) is an optimal dual solution of the current restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_{kj}<0\) certifies violation of the full-master dual constraint associated with column \((k,j)\).

notation.meaning: linking vector of column j in block k
dual multiplier of block k's convexity equation

knowledge_statements.title: No-Improving-Column Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact reduced-cost optimality certificate for the full linear master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each block \(k\), solve the complete pricing problem \(\rho_k=\min_{j\in J_k}\{c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\}\) at an optimal restricted-master dual solution \((\pi,\sigma)\). If \(\rho_k\ge0\) for every \(k\), then every full-master dual inequality is satisfied. Hence \((\pi,\sigma)\) is feasible for the full-master dual. The restricted-master primal solution is feasible for the full primal and has the same objective value as this dual solution, so both are optimal for the full linear master. The pricing solutions and their exact lower bounds form the verifiable certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact nonnegative pricing minima for every block make the restricted dual feasible for the full master and certify full-master LP optimality.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is feasible and solved to primal-dual optimality.
Every block pricing problem is solved globally over its complete column set.
Primal and dual objective values use consistent minimization-form conventions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(\rho_k\ge0\) for all \(k\), the current restricted-master primal solution is optimal for the full linear master.

notation.meaning: complete column index set of block k
minimum reduced cost in block k

knowledge_statements.title: Full-Master Bound Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual lower-bound correction using complete blockwise pricing information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z_R=b^{\mathsf T}\pi+\sum_{k\in K}\sigma_k\) be the optimal restricted-master value, and let \(\rho_k=\min_{j\in J_k}(c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k)\). Define \(\widehat\sigma_k=\sigma_k+\min\{0,\rho_k\}\). Then \(a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi+\widehat\sigma_k\le c_{kj}\) for every full-master column. Thus \((\pi,\widehat\sigma)\) is full-dual feasible and
\[
L=z_R+\sum_{k\in K}\min\{0,\rho_k\}
\]
is a certified lower bound on the optimum of the minimization-form full master. Exact pricing values, or valid lower bounds substituted for them, make the certificate directly checkable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Decreasing each convexity dual multiplier by its negative pricing violation yields a feasible full-master dual solution and a certified lower bound.
assumptions_latex: Each block has the convexity equation \(\sum_{j\in J_k}\lambda_{kj}=1\).
The restricted master is solved to dual optimality.
Each \(\rho_k\) is exact, or is replaced by a valid lower bound on the minimum reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L=z_R+\sum_{k\in K}\min\{0,\rho_k\}\le z^*\), where \(z^*\) is the full-master minimum.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Pricing Completeness Condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Condition ensuring that pricing-based completion covers every omitted column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let the full column set be the disjoint union \(J=\bigcup_{k\in K}J_k\). Exact pricing completeness holds at dual point \((\pi,\sigma)\) precisely when, for every block \(k\), the pricing domain equals the entire generating set \(J_k\) and the returned value satisfies
\[
\rho_k=\min_{j\in J_k}\bigl(c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi-\sigma_k\bigr).
\]
The condition excludes omitted blocks, truncated column domains, heuristic-only searches, and unproved local minima. Under it, \(\rho_k\ge0\) for all blocks is equivalent to satisfaction of every column-indexed inequality of the full-master dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing is complete only when every block searches its full column domain globally; then nonnegative minima cover all omitted dual constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(K\) indexes all blocks represented in the full master.
Every full-master column belongs to at least one declared pricing domain \(J_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact pricing completeness makes \(\rho_k\ge0\) for all \(k\) equivalent to full satisfaction of all column-indexed dual constraints.

notation.meaning: complete generating column set for block k
global minimum reduced cost over block k

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Finite Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-column termination theorem for exact, noncycling column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every block column set \(J_k\) is finite. At each iteration, solve the restricted master to optimality, solve every pricing problem exactly at a selected optimal dual solution, and stop if all minimum reduced costs are nonnegative. Otherwise add at least one previously absent column with negative reduced cost. If generated columns are never permanently excluded from subsequent restricted masters, then the procedure terminates after at most \(\lvert J\setminus J^0\rvert\) column-adding iterations. At termination, the restricted-master solution is optimal for the full linear master. Degenerate reoptimization does not invalidate finiteness because each nonterminal iteration enlarges the retained column set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With finitely many columns, exact pricing, and permanent retention, each nonterminal iteration adds a new column, so full-master LP optimality is reached finitely.
assumptions_latex: \(J=\bigcup_{k\in K}J_k\) is finite.
Restricted masters and pricing problems are solved exactly.
Every nonterminal iteration permanently retains a previously absent negative-reduced-cost column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination occurs within \(\lvert J\setminus J^0\rvert\) adding iterations, and the terminal solution is full-master optimal.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact-Pricing Bound Correction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certified lower-bound correction when pricing returns rigorous error bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At a restricted-master dual optimum \((\pi,\sigma)\), suppose block \(k\) supplies a certified number \(\ell_k\) satisfying \(\ell_k\le\rho_k\), where \(\rho_k\) is its unknown exact minimum reduced cost. Set \(\widehat\sigma_k=\sigma_k+\min\{0,\ell_k\}\). Since every column reduced cost is at least \(\rho_k\ge\ell_k\), the adjusted multipliers satisfy all full-master dual constraints. Consequently
\[
L_{\mathrm{inexact}}=z_R+\sum_{k\in K}\min\{0,\ell_k\}
\]
is a valid lower bound for the minimization-form full master. An incumbent upper bound \(U\) therefore has certified gap at most \(U-L_{\mathrm{inexact}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rigorous lower bounds on unknown pricing minima can replace exact minima in the dual correction, preserving a valid full-master lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is solved to dual optimality with value \(z_R\).
For every block, \(\ell_k\le\rho_k\) is rigorously certified.
The master contains one unit convexity equation per block.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_{\mathrm{inexact}}\le z^*\), and any feasible incumbent \(U\) satisfies \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L_{\mathrm{inexact}}\).

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on block k's minimum reduced cost

children.title: Box Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Coordinatewise dual-region stabilization using bounded neighborhoods.

knowledge_statements.title: Box Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise trust-region restriction around a dual stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a restricted-master dual feasible region \(D_R\), center \(\bar\pi^t\), and positive radii \(\Delta^t\), solve the stabilized dual master over
\[
D_R\cap B_t,\qquad B_t=\{\pi:\lvert\pi_i-\bar\pi_i^t\rvert\le\Delta_i^t\text{ for every }i\}.
\]
Use its solution for pricing. After evaluating generated columns, accept a productive dual point as the new center; otherwise retain the center. Enlarge radii when boundary activity obstructs progress and shrink them when dual oscillation is excessive. Before declaring column-generation completion, remove inactive artificial box restrictions or verify exact pricing at an unrestricted restricted-master dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Box stabilization confines dual multipliers to componentwise intervals around a center, with adaptive radii and an unrestricted final optimality check.
assumptions_latex: \(D_R\) is the current restricted-master dual feasible set.
Every radius satisfies \(\Delta_i^t>0\).
Final completion is tested without an improperly binding stabilization box.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each stabilized dual iterate lies in \(D_R\cap B_t\), while the final unrestricted check preserves the ordinary column-generation certificate.

children.title: Trust-Region Stabilization

knowledge_statements.title: Trust-Region Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm-based restriction of successive restricted-master dual solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose a norm \(\lVert\cdot\rVert\), dual center \(\bar\pi^t\), and radius \(\Delta_t>0\). Compute a stabilized restricted-master dual solution over
\[
D_R\cap T_t,\qquad T_t=\{\pi:\lVert\pi-\bar\pi^t\rVert\le\Delta_t\},
\]
and use it for pricing. Compare actual master improvement with the improvement predicted at the center. On a successful step, accept the trial point and optionally enlarge \(\Delta_t\); on an unsuccessful step, retain the center and reduce \(\Delta_t\). A full column-generation completion claim requires either a nonbinding region at an unrestricted dual optimum or a separate exact unrestricted pricing check.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Trust-region stabilization restricts dual movement in a chosen norm and adjusts the radius according to agreement between predicted and observed progress.
assumptions_latex: \(D_R\) is the restricted-master dual feasible set.
The chosen norm and radius define a nonempty trial region containing \(\bar\pi^t\).
Completion is validated at an unrestricted dual optimum or by an equivalent exact check.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The trial multiplier satisfies \(\pi^t\in D_R\cap T_t\), and stabilization alone is not used as a full-master optimality certificate.

notation.meaning: dual trust region at iteration t

children.title: Stabilization-Region Geometry

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization-Region Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Polyhedral representation and norm geometry of dual stabilization regions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A polyhedral dual stabilization region centered at \(\bar\pi\in\mathbb R^m\) has the representation
\[
S=\{\pi\in\mathbb R^m:H(\pi-\bar\pi)\le d\},
\]
where \(d\ge0\) ensures \(\bar\pi\in S\). It is bounded exactly when its recession cone \(\{v:Hv\le0\}\) equals \(\{0\}\). A componentwise box is obtained with \(H=(I,-I)^{\mathsf T}\), while a polyhedral norm trust region \(\{\pi:\lVert\pi-\bar\pi\rVert_P\le\Delta\}\) admits such a finite halfspace representation. Intersecting \(S\) with the restricted-master dual feasible polyhedron preserves polyhedrality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Polyhedral stabilization regions are halfspace intersections around a center; boundedness is characterized by a trivial recession cone, and boxes are a special case.
assumptions_latex: \(H\in\mathbb R^{q\times m}\) and \(d\in\mathbb R_+^q\).
The restricted-master dual feasible set is polyhedral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S\cap D_R\) is polyhedral, and \(S\) is bounded if and only if \(\{v:Hv\le0\}=\{0\}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized maximization of the restricted-master dual function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_R(\pi)\) be the concave restricted-master dual objective, let \(\bar\pi^t\) be a stability center, and choose \(\tau_t>0\). Compute
\[
\pi^t\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\pi}\left\{D_R(\pi)-\frac{1}{2\tau_t}\lVert\pi-\bar\pi^t\rVert_2^2\right\},
\]
then price columns at \(\pi^t\). If the resulting master information produces sufficient actual improvement, set \(\bar\pi^{t+1}=\pi^t\); otherwise retain \(\bar\pi^{t+1}=\bar\pi^t\) and adjust \(\tau_t\). The quadratic term discourages large dual displacement and yields a unique trial point whenever \(D_R\) is closed concave and the maximization is attained. Final completion uses the unstabilized pricing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal stabilization penalizes squared distance from a dual center, updates that center after successful steps, and retains an unstabilized final certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(D_R\) is proper, closed, and concave.
The regularized maximization is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized subproblem has at most one maximizer, and its trial point is used for pricing without replacing the final unstabilized optimality test.

children.title: Bundle Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization based on accumulated dual information.

assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) is a nonempty closed convex dual search region, and \(D:\Pi\to\mathbb R\) is finite and concave.
For every \(i\in I_k\), \(D_i=D(\pi^i)\) and \(g^i\) is a supergradient of \(D\) at \(\pi^i\).
\(\bar\pi_k\in\Pi\), \(t_k>0\), \(\eta\in(0,1)\), and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update satisfies \(\bar\pi_{k+1}\in\{\bar\pi_k,z_k\}\); a serious step occurs only when \(D(z_k)-D(\bar\pi_k)\ge\eta\Delta_k\), and the stopping test is \(\Delta_k\le\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: bundle of evaluated dual points, values, and supergradients
polyhedral upper model of the dual objective

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal bundle control of the concave restricted-master dual used in column generation.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(\mathcal B_k=\{(\pi^i,D_i,g^i)\}_{i\in I_k}\), define the upper cutting-plane model \(m_k(\pi)=\min_{i\in I_k}\{D_i+(g^i)^{\mathsf T}(\pi-\pi^i)\}\). Compute \(z_k\in\arg\max_{\pi\in\Pi}\{m_k(\pi)-\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2/(2t_k)\}\) and define \(\Delta_k=m_k(z_k)-\|z_k-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2/(2t_k)-D(\bar\pi_k)\). If \(\Delta_k\le\varepsilon\), stop. Otherwise evaluate \(D(z_k)\) and a supergradient by pricing and append the resulting cut. If \(D(z_k)-D(\bar\pi_k)\ge\eta\Delta_k\), set \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=z_k\); otherwise set \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\bar\pi_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The bundle model proposes a proximal dual trial point and quantifies its predicted improvement. A sufficiently successful trial becomes the new center; otherwise the center is retained and the trial only enriches the bundle.

children.title: Proximal–Bundle Hybridization
children.top_down_role: Hybrid regimes combining reference-point regularization with accumulated dual information.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal–Bundle Hybridization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hybrid stabilization combining accumulated bundle cuts with a movable proximal center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Maintain a bundle model \(m_k\), a stability center \(\bar\pi_k\), and bounds \(0<t_{\min}\le t_k\le t_{\max}\). Compute \(z_k\in\arg\max_{
\pi}\{m_k(\pi)-\|\pi-\bar\pi_k\|_2^2/(2t_k)\}\), obtain \(D(z_k)\) and a supergradient from pricing, and add the resulting cut to \(m_k\). Declare a serious step and set \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=z_k\) when actual improvement reaches a fraction \(\eta\in(0,1)\) of predicted improvement; otherwise take a null step, retain the center, and reduce or retain \(t_k\). Output the center when predicted improvement is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The method couples bundle cuts with an adaptive proximal penalty, moving the center after successful trials and tightening stabilization after unsuccessful ones.
assumptions_latex: \(m_k\) is a valid polyhedral upper model of the finite concave dual function \(D\).
\(0<t_{\min}\le t_k\le t_{\max}<\infty\).
\(\eta\in(0,1)\) and \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration produces either a serious step \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=z_k\) or a null step \(\bar\pi_{k+1}=\bar\pi_k\), while retaining all selected bundle information.

children.title: Dual-Price Smoothing
children.top_down_role: Stabilization through controlled averaging or filtering of dual prices.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Smoothing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-combination smoothing of raw restricted-master dual prices before pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\hat\pi_k\) be an optimal dual solution of the current restricted master and let \(\bar\pi_{k-1}\) be the previously stabilized price. Choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1]\) and define \(\bar\pi_k=(1-\alpha_k)\bar\pi_{k-1}+\alpha_k\hat\pi_k\). Invoke every pricing subproblem with \(\bar\pi_k\), add any columns whose reduced costs satisfy the prescribed improving threshold, and then resolve the restricted master. If pricing certifies no improving column at \(\bar\pi_k\) but \(\bar\pi_k\ne\hat\pi_k\), perform a final pricing call at \(\hat\pi_k\) before declaring termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Raw master prices are averaged with the previous stabilized prices; exact pricing at the raw optimum protects the final optimality test.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master has an optimal dual solution \(\hat\pi_k\).
Pricing can evaluate reduced costs at any supplied dual price.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\pi_k\) lies on the segment joining \(\bar\pi_{k-1}\) and \(\hat\pi_k\), while termination requires pricing at \(\hat\pi_k\).

children.title: Interior Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Stabilization using dual points away from unstable boundary regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Interior Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection of a central restricted-master dual optimum for less oscillatory pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), let \(F_k=\arg\max\{b^{\mathsf T}\pi:A_k^{\mathsf T}\pi\le c_k\}\) be the optimal dual face of the restricted master. Given a reference point \(q_k\in\operatorname{ri}(F_k)\) or a barrier center, choose \(\mu_k>0\) and compute \(\bar\pi_k\in\arg\max_{\pi\in\operatorname{ri}(F_k)}\{\mu_k\sum_{j=1}^{n_k}\log(c_{kj}-a_{kj}^{\mathsf T}\pi)-\tfrac12\|\pi-q_k\|_2^2\}\), with the logarithmic terms restricted to inequalities not identically tight on \(F_k\). Use \(\bar\pi_k\) for pricing, add improving columns, and recompute the optimal face; exact termination still requires a valid pricing certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing uses a central point of the master’s optimal dual face instead of an arbitrary extreme dual optimum, reducing degeneracy-driven oscillation.
assumptions_latex: The restricted-master dual optimum is attained and its optimal face \(F_k\) is nonempty.
The barrier is applied only to inequalities having positive slack in \(\operatorname{ri}(F_k)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar\pi_k\in\operatorname{ri}(F_k)\) is an optimal restricted-master dual price selected by an interior centering criterion.

notation.meaning: optimal dual face of the restricted master

children.title: Smoothing–Interior Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Selection between trajectory smoothing versus interior-point guidance.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing–Interior Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational rule selecting price averaging or optimal-face centering from master geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F_k\) be the restricted-master optimal dual face, let \(d_k=\dim(F_k)\), and let \(r_k=\|\hat\pi_k-\bar\pi_{k-1}\|_2\) measure raw-price displacement. For prescribed thresholds \(d_{\min}\ge1\) and \(r_{
max}>0\), select interior stabilization when \(d_k\ge d_{\min}\) and a relative-interior point of \(F_k\) is available; otherwise select smoothing when \(r_k>r_{\max}\), using \(\bar\pi_k=(1-\alpha_k)\bar\pi_{k-1}+\alpha_k\hat\pi_k\). If neither predicate holds, use \(\hat\pi_k\). Regardless of the selected regime, an optimality declaration requires exact pricing at a dual-optimal price.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use face centering for substantial dual degeneracy, averaging for large price jumps, and raw prices otherwise; preserve an exact final pricing test.
assumptions_latex: \(F_k\ne\varnothing\) and \(\hat\pi_k\in F_k\).
The dimension or an equivalent degeneracy indicator is computable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rule selects exactly one of interior, smoothing, or raw-price regimes and does not replace the exact pricing certificate.

notation.meaning: dimension of the optimal dual face

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A condition is an appropriate kind for a regime-selection leaf, but the dimension and displacement thresholds define an implementation-specific policy rather than a standard consequence. No source supports these predicates, their priority order, or the claim that they form the intended smoothing-interior selection rule.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Selection Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible policies for selecting improving priced columns under a batch-size limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For candidate columns \(C_k\), reduced costs \(\bar c_j(
\pi_k)
\), tolerance \(\varepsilon_{
p}>0\), and capacity \(B_k\in\mathbb N\), define the eligible set \(E_k=\{j\in C_k:\bar c_j(\pi_k)<-\varepsilon_p\}\) for a minimization master. A valid selection policy returns \(S_k\subseteq E_k\) with \(|S_k|\le B_k\), and it must satisfy \(S_k\ne\varnothing\) whenever \(E_k\ne\varnothing\) and \(B_k\ge1\). Examples include choosing the \(B_k\) most negative reduced costs or all eligible columns when \(|E_k|\le B_k\); ties are resolved by a fixed deterministic rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A selection policy chooses a nonempty capacity-limited subset of genuinely improving columns whenever such columns exist.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is written as a minimization problem.
Every candidate reduced cost \(\bar c_j(\pi_k)\) is available.
\(\varepsilon_p>0\) and \(B_k\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_k\subseteq E_k\), \(|S_k|\le B_k\), and \(E_k\ne\varnothing\Rightarrow S_k\ne\varnothing\).

children.title: Column Batch Construction
children.top_down_role: Composition and sizing of column groups admitted together.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Batch Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy construction of a bounded improving-column batch from pricing output.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given eligible columns \(E_k\), scores \(s_j=-\bar c_j(\pi_k)>0\), capacity \(B_k\), and an optional compatibility predicate \(Q(j,S)\), initialize \(S_k=\varnothing\). While \(|S_k|<B_k\) and some \(j\in E_k\setminus S_k\) satisfies \(Q(j,S_k)\), append a feasible maximizer of \(s_j\), breaking ties deterministically. Remove duplicates having identical master coefficient and objective vectors. Return \(S_k\); if \(E_k\ne\varnothing\), require \(Q(j,\varnothing)\) for at least one \(j\), so the returned batch is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Build a bounded batch greedily from the strongest compatible improving columns, removing duplicate master representations.
assumptions_latex: \(E_k\) is finite and every \(j\in E_k\) has \(s_j>0\).
At least one eligible column is compatible with the empty batch whenever \(E_k\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output satisfies \(S_k\subseteq E_k\), \(1\le|S_k|\le B_k\) when \(E_k\ne\varnothing\), and contains no duplicate master columns.

notation.meaning: compatibility predicate for adding a column

children.title: Batch Diversity Control
children.top_down_role: Control of redundancy, coverage, or diversity within admitted batches.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch Diversity Control
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise separation requirement preventing nearly redundant columns in one batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each eligible column \(j\) by a normalized feature vector \(u_j\in\mathbb R^m\) derived from its master coefficients, and fix \(\delta\in[0,1]\). A batch \(S_k\) is diversity-admissible when \(j\ne\ell\) implies \(|u_j^{\mathsf T}u_\ell|\le1-\delta\). During greedy construction, a candidate is accepted only if it satisfies this inequality against every selected column. If no further candidate is admissible, construction stops before reaching capacity. The rule controls redundancy but does not permit a column with nonimproving reduced cost to enter the batch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Accepted columns must be sufficiently separated in normalized master-coefficient space; the batch may stop early but never admits nonimproving columns.
assumptions_latex: Each candidate has a nonzero feature vector normalized so that \(\|u_j\|_2=1\).
Eligibility is determined independently by the reduced-cost test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
Every distinct \(j,\ell
i S_k\) satisfies \(|u_j^{\mathsf T}u_\ell|\le1-\delta\), and \(S_k\) remains a subset of the improving columns.

notation.meaning: normalized feature vector of column j

children.title: Column Pooling
children.top_down_role: Persistent storage and organization of inactive or previously generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Pooling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lifecycle storage of inactive generated columns outside the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain an active set \(A_k\) and an inactive pool \(P_k\) of uniquely keyed columns. After pricing, insert each newly generated column into \(A_k\) if selected for the restricted master and otherwise into \(P_k\); merge duplicates by retaining one representation and its best available metadata. After solving the master, columns removed from \(A_k\) are transferred to \(P_k\), not destroyed. Before invoking expensive pricing, recompute the reduced cost of every eligible pooled column at the current dual price and offer improving pooled columns for reactivation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generated columns are deduplicated and retained outside the active master so they can be reconsidered cheaply at later dual prices.
assumptions_latex: Each column has a stable key determined by its master coefficient and objective vectors.
Reduced costs of stored columns can be recomputed from current dual prices.
\(A_k\cap P_k=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every retained column belongs to exactly one of \(A_k\) or \(P_k\), and improving pooled columns are reconsidered before new pricing.

children.title: Column Reactivation
children.top_down_role: Criteria for returning pooled columns to active master status.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Reactivation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost screening that returns useful pooled columns to the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given inactive pool \(P_k\), current dual price \(\pi_k\), tolerance \(\varepsilon_p>0\), and reactivation capacity \(R_k\ge1\), compute \(\bar c_j(\pi_k)=c_j-a_j^{\mathsf T}\pi_k\) for every eligible \(j\in P_k\). Let \(E_k^P=\{j
i P_k:\bar c_j(\pi_k)<-\varepsilon_p\}\). Move up to \(R_k\) elements of \(E_k^P\), ordered by increasing reduced cost with deterministic tie-breaking, from \(P_k\) to the active set \(A_k\). Resolve the restricted master whenever at least one column is reactivated; otherwise proceed to ordinary pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pooled columns with sufficiently negative current reduced cost are moved back to the master before a new pricing solve.
assumptions_latex: The master is a minimization problem.
Stored coefficient and objective data permit exact reduced-cost recomputation.
\(\varepsilon_p>0\) and \(R_k\ge1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reactivated set is contained in \(E_k^P\), has cardinality at most \(R_k\), and is transferred from \(P_k\) to \(A_k\).

notation.meaning: current reduced cost of pooled column j

children.title: Pool Aging Policies
children.top_down_role: Retention priorities for columns with differing recency or historical value.

knowledge_statements.title: Pool Aging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-memory eviction rule for inactive columns that remain unused or nonimproving.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Attach to every inactive pooled column \(j\) an integer age \(a_j^k\). Set \(a_j^{k+1}=0\) if \(j\) is reactivated or has \(\bar c_j(\pi_k)<-\varepsilon_p\); otherwise set \(a_j^{k+1}=a_j^k+1\). Given an age limit \(H\in\mathbb N\) and pool capacity \(M\), first evict columns with \(a_j^{k+1}>H\); if the pool still exceeds \(M\), evict largest-age columns, breaking ties by weakest current reduced-cost improvement. Columns required by the current restricted master or an incumbent representation are exempt.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unused, nonimproving pooled columns accumulate age and are evicted past a limit or when capacity is exceeded; protected columns remain.
assumptions_latex: \(H\ge0\) and \(M\ge0\) are fixed finite limits.
Current reduced costs are available for pooled columns.
Protected active or incumbent-support columns are identified before eviction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After eviction, \(|P_{k+1}|\le M\), no unprotected retained column has age exceeding \(H\), and protected columns are not deleted.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits Pool Aging Policies, but the age reset, eviction order, and reduced-cost tie-breaker are unsourced implementation choices. The conclusion \(|P_{k+1}|\le M\) is not guaranteed when protected columns are exempt and their number exceeds \(M\).

children.title: Column Deletion
children.top_down_role: Removal policies for inactive, dominated, or low-value columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Deletion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe removal of inactive restricted-master columns while preserving feasibility and lower-bound validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: After solving a minimization restricted master, let \(x_j^k\) and \(\bar c_j^k\) denote each active column's value and reduced cost. Form deletion candidates \(D_k=\{j:x_j^k=0,\ \bar c_j^k\ge-\varepsilon_d,\ j\notin Q_k\}\), where \(Q_k\) contains artificial, basic-feasibility, incumbent-support, and otherwise protected columns. Delete at most \(L_k\) candidates, preferably those inactive longest, and retain a copy in the pool when available. Reoptimize the reduced master; if it becomes infeasible or its objective deterioration exceeds a prescribed safeguard, restore deleted columns. Exact pricing remains necessary for global certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only inactive, nonessential columns are tentatively removed; feasibility or excessive bound deterioration triggers restoration, and pricing still certifies completion.
assumptions_latex: The current restricted master has an optimal solution and reduced costs.
\(\varepsilon_d\ge0\) and \(L_k\ge1\).
The protected set \(Q_k\) includes every column required for the maintained representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted deletion preserves restricted-master feasibility and the prescribed objective safeguard; deletion alone never constitutes an optimality certificate.

children.title: Column Aggregation
children.top_down_role: Grouping of columns through shared structural representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Aggregation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact aggregation of indistinguishable nonnegative master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the master problem \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\ \lambda\geq0\}\). If a class \(G\subseteq J\) satisfies \((a_j,c_j)=(\bar a,\bar c)\) for every \(j\in G\), introduce \(\mu_G=\sum_{j\in G}\lambda_j\) and replace its columns by \((\bar a,\bar c)\mu_G\). The aggregated and original masters have identical feasible images and objective values. Every original solution maps to its aggregate, and every aggregate value \(\mu_G\geq0\) can be reconstructed by assigning it to any one member of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Columns with identical constraint vectors and costs may be replaced by one aggregate variable without changing feasibility or the optimal value.
assumptions_latex: \lambda_j\geq0\text{ and has no individual finite upper bound for }j\in G
a_j=\bar a\text{ and }c_j=\bar c\text{ for every }j\in G
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{\mathrm{agg}}=v_{\mathrm{master}}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exact substitution for identical unbounded nonnegative columns

children.title: Column Compression
children.top_down_role: Compact storage or representation of large column collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Compression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-image compression of a finite-dimensional restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n,r\) be positive integers, let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\), \(T\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R^r\). Consider \(\min\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=b,\ \lambda\in\mathbb R_+^n\}\). If \(A=BT\) and \(c^\top=d^\top T\), define \(z=T\lambda\) and \(K=T\mathbb R_+^n\). The exact compressed formulation is \(\min\{d^\top z:Bz=b,\ z\in K\}\). The two formulations have identical feasible objective-value sets and hence the same infimum. Recovering an original solution from a feasible compressed point requires a lifting operation returning some \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^n\) with \(T\lambda=z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite-dimensional master can be compressed through a linear image without changing its feasible objective values when the constraints, costs, image cone, and lifting operation are represented exactly.
assumptions_latex: m,n,r\in\mathbb N_{>0}
A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n},\ B\in\mathbb R^{m\times r},\ T\in\mathbb R^{r\times n}
b\in\mathbb R^m,\ c\in\mathbb R^n,\ d\in\mathbb R^r
A=BT
c^\top=d^\top T
K=T\mathbb R_+^n\text{ is represented exactly}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=b,\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^n\}=\inf\{d^\top z:Bz=b,z\in K\}

notation.meaning: linear compression map from the original variable space to the compressed space
exact image of the nonnegative orthant under the compression map

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: equality follows from an exact linear image and lifting

children.title: Reduction-Safety Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Cases where aggressive column reduction can impair recovery, bounds, or search performance.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction-Safety Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality boundary and primal-dual certificate for deleting master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\min\{c^\top\lambda:A\lambda=b,\ \lambda\geq0\}\) have a finite optimum, and let \(D\) be a set of columns to delete. Deletion is optimal-value safe exactly when the retained problem \(P_{J\setminus D}\) is feasible and satisfies \(v(P_{J\setminus D})=v(P)\). A sufficient certificate consists of a retained feasible solution \(\lambda^R\), extended by zeros on \(D\), and a dual vector \(\pi\) such that \(a_j^\top\pi\leq c_j\) for every \(j\in J\) and \(c^\top\lambda^R=b^\top\pi\). Deletion can otherwise be unsafe: in \(\min\{\lambda_1:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda\geq0\}\), the full value is \(0\), whereas deleting column \(2\) raises it to \(1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column deletion is safe exactly when the retained master remains feasible with the same optimum; a retained feasible solution and a full-dual-feasible vector with equal objective values certify safety, while deletion can otherwise cause strict loss.
assumptions_latex: P\text{ has a finite optimum}
D\subseteq J
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D\text{ is safe}\iff P_{J\setminus D}\text{ is feasible and }v(P_{J\setminus D})=v(P)

children.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Generation Tailing-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-window diagnostic for slow restricted-master progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v_t\) be the restricted-master objective after iteration \(t\) of a minimization column-generation method, so \(v_{t+1}\leq v_t\). Given a window length \(w\geq1\) and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), iteration \(t\geq w\) is in an \((w,\varepsilon)\)-tailing-off regime when \(v_{t-w}-v_t\leq\varepsilon\) while pricing has produced at least one column of negative reduced cost during iterations \(t-w,\ldots,t-1\). Thus optimality has not been certified, yet total master-bound improvement over the window is small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tailing-off occurs when many iterations yield negligible master improvement even though pricing continues to find improving columns.
assumptions_latex: v_{t+1}\leq v_t
w\geq1
\varepsilon>0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v_{t-w}-v_t\leq\varepsilon\text{ while some generated reduced cost is negative}

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvergence diagnostic for restricted-master dual iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi^t\) be an optimal dual solution of the restricted master at iteration \(t\), selected under a fixed norm. Dual oscillation occurs when the dual objective values converge but the selected multipliers do not; a quantitative sufficient diagnostic is \(b^\top\pi^t\to\bar v\) together with \(\limsup_{t\to\infty}\|\pi^{t+1}-\pi^t\|\geq\delta\) for some \(\delta>0\). Degenerate changes between alternative dual optima therefore count only when the fixed selection rule continues to produce separated iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual oscillation means dual objective values stabilize while consistently selected restricted-master multipliers continue making nonvanishing moves.

\|\cdot\|\text{ is a fixed norm}

knowledge_statements.title: Oscillation-Induced Tailing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Diagnostic linking unstable multipliers to weak master progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tolerances \(\delta,\varepsilon>0\) and window \(w\), oscillation-induced tailing is present at iteration \(t\) when \(\max_{k=t-w}^{t-1}\|\pi^{k+1}-\pi^k\|\geq\delta\), pricing returns a negative-reduced-cost column in that window, and \(v_{t-w}-v_t\leq\varepsilon\). The predicate records concurrence rather than logical causation: multiplier instability repeatedly changes the pricing objective while the restricted-master bound improves little. Establishing causation requires comparison with a stabilized dual-selection or pricing scheme.

knowledge_statements.title: Premature Heuristic-Pricing Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Heuristic pricing cannot certify absence of improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\lambda_1:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda_1,\lambda_2\geq0\}\), initially restricted to column \(1\). The restricted value is \(1\), with dual multiplier \(\pi=1\). Omitted column \(2\), whose cost is \(0\) and coefficient is \(1\), has reduced cost \(-1\) and yields the full optimum \(0\). A heuristic pricing routine that searches only column \(1\) may return no improving column. Terminating on that report is therefore invalid; only exact pricing, or a valid lower bound proving every reduced cost nonnegative, certifies completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic may miss a negative-reduced-cost column, so failure to find one is not an optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: \text{the pricing routine is not exhaustive}
\text{the routine supplies no valid global reduced-cost bound}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{heuristic failure to find a column}\not\Rightarrow\min_{j\in J}\bar c_j\geq0

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Infeasibility Without Farkas Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility restoration requires a Farkas or phase-I pricing mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restricted master may be infeasible although the full master is feasible. For example, let \(b=1\), retain only a zero column \(a_1=0\), and omit \(a_2=1\) in \(A\lambda=b,\lambda\geq0\). The restricted equation \(0\lambda_1=1\) is infeasible, whereas \(\lambda_2=1\) is fully feasible. Because an infeasible restricted master supplies no ordinary optimal dual multiplier, standard reduced-cost pricing is undefined. Without artificial phase-I variables or a Farkas-ray pricing oracle capable of finding a column that violates the infeasibility certificate, column generation can halt before producing a feasible master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible restricted master can coexist with a feasible full master; Farkas or phase-I pricing is needed to discover feasibility-restoring columns.

children.title: Column Generation as Dual Cutting-Plane Method

knowledge_statements.title: Column Generation as Dual Cutting-Plane Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite master LP viewed through its dual constraint system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j=b,\lambda\geq0\}\), the dual is \(D=\max\{b^\top\pi:a_j^\top\pi\leq c_j\ \text{for all }j\in J\}\). Restricting the master to \(J_t\subseteq J\) deletes dual inequalities, producing a relaxation of \(D\). Pricing computes \(\min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^\top\pi^t)\). A negative value identifies a violated dual inequality, and adding its primal column installs that inequality as a dual cutting plane. If pricing proves the minimum nonnegative, \(\pi^t\) is feasible for the full dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each generated primal column adds its associated inequality to the dual, so pricing is separation for a dual cutting-plane method.
assumptions_latex: J\text{ is finite, or pricing attains its minimum}
P\text{ and }D\text{ satisfy strong LP duality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{j\in J}(c_j-a_j^\top\pi^t)\geq0\Rightarrow\pi^t\text{ is feasible for }D

children.title: Simultaneous Row Generation
children.top_down_role: Dynamic introduction of violated rows within a joint generation framework.

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Row Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch separation of omitted constraints in a joint restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I\) and \(J\) index the rows and columns of \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j:\sum_{j\in J}a_{ij}\lambda_j\geq b_i\ \text{for every }i\in I,\ \lambda_j\geq0\ \text{for every }j\in J\}\). Initialize finite active sets \(I_0\subseteq I\) and \(J_0\subseteq J\) defining a solvable restricted master. At iteration \(t\), solve the master over \((I_t,J_t)\), obtaining \(\lambda^t\), and extend \(\lambda^t\) by zero on \(J\setminus J_t\). A row-separation oracle returns a batch \(R_t\subseteq I\setminus I_t\) of indices satisfying \(\sum_{j\in J_t}a_{ij}\lambda_j^t<b_i\). Set \(I_{t+1}=I_t\cup R_t\), coordinate any column additions, and reoptimize. Stop on the row side only when exact separation certifies that no row in \(I\) is violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a restricted master, extend its active-column solution by zero, add a batch of globally separated violated rows, coordinate column additions, and repeat until exact row separation certifies completeness.
assumptions_latex: I_0\subseteq I\text{ and }J_0\subseteq J\text{ are finite}
I_0,J_0\text{ define a solvable restricted master}
\text{the row oracle separates over all }I
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_t=\varnothing\text{ with an exact oracle}\Rightarrow\lambda^t\text{ violates no row in }I

knowledge_statements.title: Simultaneous Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch pricing of omitted variables in a joint restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize finite active sets \(I_0\subseteq I\) and \(J_0\subseteq J\) defining a solvable restricted master. At iteration \(t\), solve it and obtain dual multipliers \(\pi^t\) for active rows. A pricing oracle returns a batch \(C_t\subseteq J\setminus J_t\) whose reduced costs \(\bar c_j(\pi^t)=c_j-\sum_{i\in I_t}a_{ij}\pi_i^t\) are negative. Set \(J_{t+1}=J_t\cup C_t\), coordinate any newly separated rows, and reoptimize. Stop on the column side only when exact pricing certifies \(\bar c_j(\pi^t)\geq0\) for every admissible column.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve the joint restricted master, add a batch of negative-reduced-cost columns, coordinate new rows, and continue until exact pricing certifies completeness.

\text{pricing is exact when termination is declared}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_t=\varnothing\text{ with exact pricing}\Rightarrow\bar c_j(\pi^t)\geq0\text{ for all }j\in J

children.title: Row–Column Coordination
children.top_down_role: Scheduling and information exchange between separation and pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Row–Column Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completion rule for masters with simultaneously omitted rows and columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a joint row-column method, neither oracle may certify global completion using a master that becomes stale after the other oracle adds objects. After adding rows, the master must be reoptimized before reduced-cost certification; after adding columns, the resulting primal solution must be rechecked by global row separation. Termination is valid only at a common restricted-master optimum \((\lambda^t,\pi^t)\) for which the row oracle certifies every omitted constraint satisfied and the pricing oracle certifies every omitted column has nonnegative reduced cost. Under exact oracles and strong LP duality, these two certificates establish full-master primal and dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rows and columns must be rechecked after either side changes; terminate only when one common master solution passes both exact oracles.
assumptions_latex: \text{row separation and pricing are exact at termination}
\text{the full LP satisfies strong duality}
\text{each active master is solved to optimality}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{row certificate}\wedge\text{pricing certificate}\Rightarrow(\lambda^t,\pi^t)\text{ is primal-dual optimal for the full LP}
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: simultaneous primal-feasibility and dual-feasibility certificates imply LP optimality

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coordination principle is standard in spirit and fits its container, but no source is supplied. The full LP, row senses, dual signs, and extension of restricted primal and dual solutions to inactive objects must be specified before the asserted full primal-dual certificate is source-reviewable.

children.title: Joint Completion Certificates
children.top_down_role: Completion criteria accounting for both missing rows and missing columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Joint Completion Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate for finite row-and-column restricted linear masters with exact separation and pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal–dual pair \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax\ge b,\ x\ge0\}\) and \(\max\{b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y\le c,\ y\ge0\}\), with finite row set \(I\) and column set \(J\). For \(\bar I\subseteq I\) and \(\bar J\subseteq J\), a joint completion certificate is a restricted-master pair \((\bar x,\bar y)\) satisfying \(A_{i\bar J}\bar x\ge b_i\) for every \(i\in I\), \(A_{\bar Ij}^{\mathsf T}\bar y\le c_j\) for every \(j\in J\), and \(c_{\bar J}^{\mathsf T}\bar x=b_{\bar I}^{\mathsf T}\bar y\). Extending both vectors by zero yields feasible primal and dual solutions of equal value; hence both are optimal for the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full-row feasibility, full-column dual feasibility, and equal restricted primal and dual objectives jointly certify completion and optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) and \(J\) are finite, and the full primal and dual have finite optimal values.
Row separation and column pricing are exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The zero-extended pair \((x,y)\) is optimal for the full primal–dual pair.

notation.meaning: currently generated row and column index sets

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and fits the terminal certificate container, but no inspectable source is supplied for the joint row-and-column completion formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Node Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column generation for the LP relaxation at the root of a branch-price tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a root-node master \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J}c_j\lambda_j: \sum_{j\in J}a_j\lambda_j\ge b,\ \lambda\ge0\}\) and a finite initial set \(J_0\) yielding a feasible restricted master. At iteration \(k\), solve the master over \(J_k\), obtain an optimal dual vector \(\pi^k\), and solve exact pricing \(r_k=\min_{j\in J}\{c_j-(\pi^k)^{\mathsf T}a_j\}\). If \(r_k<0\), add at least one attaining column to form \(J_{k+1}\); otherwise stop and return the restricted-master primal solution and \(\pi^k\). Under exact solves, the stopping test certifies optimality of the root LP relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve the root restricted master and add negative-reduced-cost columns; stop when exact pricing finds none.
assumptions_latex: The initial restricted master is feasible.
Restricted-master optimization and pricing are exact.
The root master has finitely many columns and a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with \(r_k\ge0\) returns an optimal solution of the full root LP relaxation.

knowledge_statements.title: Descendant-Node Column Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column generation for a descendant LP relaxation after incorporating its branching restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At descendant node \(v\), let \(J(v)\) be the columns satisfying every branching decision on the root-to-\(v\) path. Initialize a feasible restricted set \(J_0(v)\subseteq J(v)\), possibly using eligible inherited columns. At iteration \(k\), solve the node restricted master, obtain dual multipliers \(\pi_v^k\) including multipliers for node constraints, and solve exact node pricing \(r_v^k=\min_{j\in J(v)}\{c_j-(\pi_v^k)^{\mathsf T}a_{vj}\}\). Add an attaining column when \(r_v^k<0\); otherwise return the current solution. The nonnegative pricing optimum certifies optimality for the full LP relaxation at node \(v\), not for other nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each descendant, price only columns compatible with its path decisions and stop when no eligible negative-reduced-cost column exists.
assumptions_latex: The node restricted master is feasible.
Node pricing and restricted-master solves are exact.
The node relaxation has finitely many eligible columns and a finite optimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r_v^k\ge0\), the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full LP relaxation at node \(v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Root-to-Node Pricing Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of root pricing structure to a descendant after imposing node-specific eligibility and dual terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let root pricing minimize \(c(p)-\pi_0^{\mathsf T}a(p)\) over patterns \(p\in P\). At node \(v\), suppose branching restricts patterns to \(P_v\subseteq P\) and adds master coefficients \(d_v(p)\) with dual multipliers \(\mu_v\). Then the transferred pricing problem is \(\min_{p\in P_v}\{c(p)-\pi_v^{\mathsf T}a(p)-\mu_v^{\mathsf T}d_v(p)\}\). The root pricing implementation remains valid only after its feasible set, objective coefficients, and state are modified to represent these node terms. Root columns may seed the node master precisely when they belong to \(P_v\); root reduced costs alone do not certify node optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root pricing transfers by restricting eligible patterns and adding descendant dual terms; root reduced costs cannot replace node pricing.
assumptions_latex: Every descendant branching decision has an exact representation through \(P_v\) or \(d_v\).
The transferred oracle solves the modified pricing problem exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transferred oracle computes the minimum reduced cost over exactly the columns eligible at node \(v\).

notation.meaning: patterns compatible with the path to node v

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Specific Restricted Masters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Restricted Dantzig–Wolfe master associated with one branch-price node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a branch-price node \(v\), let \(J_v\) be a finite subset of columns compatible with the root-to-\(v\) branching decisions. A node-specific restricted master is the linear program \(\min\{\sum_{j\in J_v}c_j\lambda_j: \sum_{j\in J_v}a_j\lambda_j\ge b,\ D_v\lambda\ge d_v,\ \lambda\ge0\}\), where \(D_v\lambda\ge d_v\) encodes all master-side restrictions active at \(v\). It is a restriction of the full node relaxation obtained by replacing the complete eligible set \(J(v)\) with \(J_v\subseteq J(v)\). Its dual multipliers define reduced costs for node pricing, and its objective value is generally only a provisional node bound until pricing proves completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node-specific restricted master uses finitely many eligible columns and all branching constraints active at that search-tree node.
assumptions_latex: Every column in \(J_v\) satisfies column-side branching restrictions at node \(v\).
The displayed restricted master is feasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The program defines the current finite master relaxation solved at node \(v\).

knowledge_statements.title: Column Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe reuse of generated columns from an ancestor at a descendant branch-price node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\) be an ancestor of node \(v\), and let \(P_u\) be the stored columns at \(u\). Initialize inheritance by setting \(P_v^{\mathrm{inh}}=\{p\in P_u:p\in J(v)\}\), where \(J(v)\) is the complete column set satisfying all decisions on the path to \(v\). Insert the columns in \(P_v^{\mathrm{inh}}\) into the node restricted master with their original costs and structural coefficients and with node-row coefficients computed from the column attributes. Columns failing eligibility are discarded for \(v\). Inheritance supplies a warm start only: after solving the inherited restricted master, exact node pricing remains necessary unless a separate node completion certificate is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descendant inherits only ancestor columns satisfying its path decisions, then still performs node-specific pricing.
assumptions_latex: Column attributes suffice to test every branching decision active at \(v\).
Costs and structural coefficients of inherited columns are unchanged.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every column inserted through inheritance is valid at \(v\), but inheritance alone does not certify completion.

columns safely inherited by node v
