knowledge_statements.title: Node Column Pools
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Node-indexed storage of generated columns and their eligibility metadata in branch-price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each search-tree node \(v\), a node column pool is a finite set \(P_v\subseteq J(v)\) together with, for every \(p\in P_v\), its cost \(c(p)\), structural vector \(a(p)\), branching attributes \(h(p)\), and current master-membership flag. The pool may contain eligible inherited, previously priced, or locally generated columns, including columns not presently active in the restricted master. Activating a pooled column means inserting its variable and all coefficients required by the node master. Pool membership does not imply negative reduced cost, and a search over \(P_v\) does not replace exact pricing over the complete eligible set \(J(v)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node column pool stores finitely many eligible columns and metadata, whether or not those columns are active in its restricted master.
assumptions_latex: Every stored column has sufficient metadata to reconstruct all node-master coefficients.
Only columns belonging to \(J(v)\) enter \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_v\) is a reusable finite cache, distinct from both the active master set and the complete pricing domain.

notation.meaning: complete eligible column set at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the node-column-pool container and clearly separates the pool, active master, and complete pricing domain, but it lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Cross-Node Column Eligibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility of inherited columns with node-specific restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Node Column Eligibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Predicate deciding whether a column generated at one node is valid at another.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent every branching decision on the path to node \(v\) by a predicate \(B_{v\ell}(p)\in\{0,1\}\) on a complete column \(p\), for \(\ell=1,\ldots,q_v\). A column generated at any node \(u\) is eligible at \(v\) exactly when \(E_v(p)=\prod_{\ell=1}^{q_v}B_{v\ell}(p)=1\), equivalently when every active predicate is satisfied. If branching is represented by node rows rather than by restricting the pricing domain, eligibility additionally requires that the column’s coefficients in those rows be computable; it need not satisfy the row independently. Eligibility is a validity condition and is independent of the column’s reduced cost under the current node dual solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cross-node column is eligible exactly when it satisfies every column-side path predicate and has coefficients for all node-side rows.
assumptions_latex: The path predicates encode all column-side branching restrictions at node \(v\).
Each predicate is evaluable from the stored column attributes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in J(v)\) if and only if \(E_v(p)=1\) and all required node-row coefficients are defined.

notation.meaning: the l-th column-side path predicate at node v
aggregate eligibility predicate for node v
complete eligible column set at node v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The eligibility condition is precise and appropriately distinguishes column-side predicates from node-row coefficient availability, but no source is cited for this cross-node formulation.

children.title: Original-Variable Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching expressed through variables of the original formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Original-Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary branching on an original variable represented as an aggregate of master columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an original binary variable satisfies \(x_i=\sum_{p\in P}h_i(p)\lambda_p\), where \(h_i(p)\in\{0,1\}\). If the current LP solution has \(0<\bar x_i<1\), create two children with \(x_i=0\) and \(x_i=1\), respectively. In master space these disjunctions are \(\sum_p h_i(p)\lambda_p=0\) and \(\sum_p h_i(p)\lambda_p=1\). Each child’s pricing problem must either restrict candidate patterns consistently or include the corresponding branch-row dual term in reduced cost. Because \(x_i\) is binary, the two children are disjoint and their union contains every integer-feasible solution of the parent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional original binary variable, translating its zero-one disjunction into constraints on the master columns.
assumptions_latex: \(x_i\) is binary in every integer-feasible solution.
The master representation \(x_i=\sum_p h_i(p)\lambda_p\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children \(x_i=0\) and \(x_i=1\) form an exhaustive, disjoint branching disjunction.

notation.meaning: value of original variable i in pattern p

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The branching algorithm is mathematically consistent under the stated exact reconstruction and binary-integrality assumptions, but the branch-price translation and pricing-compatibility claims require a source.

children.title: Attribute Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching expressed through structural attributes of generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Attribute Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on an integer-valued aggregate attribute of generated patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each pattern \(p\) carry an integer attribute \(h(p)\), and define the aggregate master quantity \(z=\sum_{p\in P}h(p)\lambda_p\). If the current relaxation gives \(\bar z\notin\mathbb Z\) while every integer-feasible solution has \(z\in\mathbb Z\), create children \(z\le\lfloor\bar z\rfloor\) and \(z\ge\lceil\bar z\rceil\). Add the selected inequality to each child master and modify reduced costs using its dual multiplier, or impose an equivalent restriction inside pricing. The two children exclude the current fractional solution, are disjoint, and together contain every integer-feasible parent solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional aggregate pattern attribute using floor and ceiling children, while exposing the branch to pricing.
assumptions_latex: \(h(p)\in\mathbb Z\) for every pattern \(p\).
The aggregate \(z\) is integral for every integer-feasible parent solution.
Pricing can represent the attribute coefficient or an equivalent restriction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The floor–ceiling disjunction is exhaustive for integer-feasible solutions and removes the current fractional solution.

notation.meaning: integer branching attribute of pattern p
aggregate attribute value in the master
current relaxation value of the aggregate attribute

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The floor-ceiling attribute branching rule fits the algorithm container and has sufficient stated hypotheses, but no authoritative source is provided for the master-and-pricing formulation.

children.title: Variable-to-Attribute Translation
children.top_down_role: Translation of original-space disjunctions into pricing-compatible attributes.

assumptions_latex: The decomposition reconstructs \(x\) exactly from complete patterns and master weights.
Every pricing output reports the component \(x_i(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Original-variable bounds and their translated attribute inequalities define the same master feasible set.

notation.meaning: original-variable vector encoded by pattern p
component i encoded by pattern p
master weight assigned to pattern p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact expression of an original variable as an aggregate attribute of decomposition columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let every generated pattern \(p\in P\) encode an original vector \(x(p)\in X\), and let the master reconstruction be \(x=\sum_{p\in P}x(p)\lambda_p\). For original component \(i\), define the column attribute \(h_i(p)=x_i(p)\). Then \(x_i=\sum_{p\in P}h_i(p)\lambda_p\). Consequently, any branch \(x_i\le L\) or \(x_i\ge U\) translates exactly into the master inequality \(\sum_p h_i(p)\lambda_p\le L\) or \(\sum_p h_i(p)\lambda_p\ge U\), respectively. Exact translation requires every priced column to expose \(h_i(p)\), so that the branch-row contribution is included in reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An original variable equals the master-weighted sum of its values in columns, allowing exact translation of variable bounds into branch rows.
knowledge_statements.title: Variable-to-Attribute Translation
Master Column-Variable Branching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct branching on an integer-constrained variable associated with one generated master column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda_q\in\mathbb Z_+\) be a master variable for generated column \(q\), and suppose its current relaxation value satisfies \(\bar\lambda_q\notin\mathbb Z\). Create two children with \(\lambda_q\le\lfloor\bar\lambda_q\rfloor\) and \(\lambda_q\ge\lceil\bar\lambda_q\rceil\). Retain the bounds in every later restricted master at the corresponding child. Pricing must also preserve their meaning: copies of column \(q\) cannot bypass its upper bound, and the lower-bound child must maintain or regenerate \(q\). The disjunction removes the current solution and partitions all solutions having integral \(\lambda_q\), but it is applicable only when integrality of that particular master variable is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an integer master column variable, branch at its fractional value using floor and ceiling bounds while preventing pricing from bypassing them.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda_q\) is required to be integral in the target master formulation.
Column identity is stable across restricted-master regeneration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two bound children exclude \(\bar\lambda_q\) and exhaust all solutions with \(\lambda_q\in\mathbb Z_+\).

notation.meaning: integer-constrained master variable for column q

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is carefully restricted to genuinely integer-constrained master variables, but direct master-column branching is delicate in column generation. The stable-identity, duplicate-bypass, regeneration, and pricing-preservation claims need explicit authoritative support.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a set-partitioning model with item set \(I\), column set \(P\), incidence \(a_{ip}\in\{0,1\}\), and variables \(\lambda_p\ge 0\).
The current LP solution \(\lambda^*\) has distinct items \(i,j\in I\) with \(0<\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}a_{jp}\lambda_p^*<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two children exclude disjoint classes of columns and together retain every integer-feasible parent solution.

notation.meaning: Columns admissible at the current node

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-partitioning form of Ryan-Foster branching for column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(i\ne j\) with fractional co-occurrence \(z_{ij}^*=\sum_{p\in P}a_{ip}a_{jp}\lambda_p^*\). Create a together child whose pricing domain permits only columns satisfying \(a_{ip}=a_{jp}\), and a separate child whose pricing domain permits only columns satisfying \(a_{ip}+a_{jp}\le 1\). Continue column generation over the corresponding restricted domains. Stop branching on this pair after producing both children; each integer set partition places \(i,j\) together or in distinct selected columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a fractionally co-occurring item pair, then create one child forcing the items into the same generated column and another forbidding their joint occurrence.
knowledge_statements.title: Ryan–Foster Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Ryan–Foster split is plausible for a set-partitioning master, but this specialized branching rule and its pricing-domain implementation have no cited source.

children.title: Arc Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching decisions expressed through arc usage.

assumptions_latex: Columns are directed paths or routes, with arc incidence \(a_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\).
The aggregate arc usage \(y_e^*=\sum_{p\in P}a_{ep}\lambda_p^*\) is nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integer-feasible parent solution satisfies exactly one of \(y_e\le\lfloor y_e^*\rfloor\) or \(y_e\ge\lceil y_e^*\rceil\).

notation.meaning: Aggregate master usage of arc e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branching on aggregate directed-arc usage represented inside generated paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select an arc \(e\) with nonintegral \(y_e^*\). Create children imposing \(y_e\le\lfloor y_e^*\rfloor\) and \(y_e\ge\lceil y_e^*\rceil\), respectively, where \(y_e=\sum_{p\in P}a_{ep}\lambda_p\). Modify the pricing problem so generated paths record and respect the applicable arc bound, using arc deletion or forcing when the bounds reduce to \(y_e=0\) or \(y_e=1\). Re-solve the restricted master and pricing problem in each child.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional aggregate directed-arc usage and enforce the resulting floor-or-ceiling bound within each child’s path-pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Arc Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required to establish the conditions under which aggregate arc usage is integral and its floor/ceiling branches can be represented correctly in the master and pricing problem.

children.title: Edge Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching decisions expressed through edge usage.

assumptions_latex: Columns use edges of an undirected graph, with incidence \(a_{ep}\in\{0,1\}\).
The aggregate edge usage \(y_e^*=\sum_{p\in P}a_{ep}\lambda_p^*\) is nonintegral.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The floor and ceiling children partition all integer values of \(y_e\) and preserve pricing compatibility when edge restrictions are representable.

notation.meaning: Aggregate master usage of edge e

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Undirected analogue of arc branching for edge-based pricing states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Select an edge \(e\) with nonintegral \(y_e^*\). Create children defined by \(y_e\le\lfloor y_e^*\rfloor\) and \(y_e\ge\lceil y_e^*\rceil\), where \(y_e=\sum_{p\in P}a_{ep}\lambda_p\). Restrict the pricing domain in each child to encode its edge-usage requirement; for binary aggregate usage this forbids \(e\) in one child and requires \(e\) in the other. Resume column generation separately at both children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on fractional aggregate usage of an undirected edge, passing the complementary edge restrictions to each child’s pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Edge Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The undirected edge variant lacks evidence for its integrality assumptions and for the claimed pricing-compatible implementation of aggregate edge bounds.

children.title: Resource Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching decisions expressed through resource states or consumption.

assumptions_latex: Each column \(p\) has an integer resource contribution \(r_p\in\mathbb Z\).
The aggregate resource value \(R^*=\sum_{p\in P}r_p\lambda_p^*\) is nonintegral and is integer in every integer-feasible master solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two resource bounds form a valid exhaustive disjunction for integer-feasible master solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic integer-valued resource branching, conditional on pricing-state representability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose a resource expression \(R=\sum_{p\in P}r_p\lambda_p\) with nonintegral value \(R^*\). Create a lower child imposing \(R\le\lfloor R^*\rfloor\) and an upper child imposing \(R\ge\lceil R^*\rceil\). Augment the pricing state or its resource bounds so that newly generated columns are compatible with the child constraint. Output both child nodes and continue column generation until their restricted-master bounds or integrality conditions terminate processing.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on a fractional aggregate quantity that is integral in every integer solution, and propagate complementary resource bounds into pricing.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The integer disjunction is valid under the stated assumption, but an aggregate master resource bound cannot generally be enforced merely by restricting individual pricing resources. The intended branch-and-price variant needs a direct source and sharper representability conditions.

children.title: Successor Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching decisions expressed through immediate-successor relationships.

assumptions_latex: Columns encode ordered sequences over an item set \(I\).
For some \(i\ne j\), the aggregate immediate-successor value \(s_{ij}^*=\sum_{p\in P}b_{ijp}\lambda_p^*\) is fractional.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integer-feasible sequence solution assigns item \(j\) as the immediate successor of \(i\), or does not, so the children are exhaustive and disjoint.

notation.meaning: Indicator that j immediately follows i in column p

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary successor branching for sequence-structured columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \((i,j)\) with \(0<s_{ij}^*<1\), where \(s_{ij}=\sum_{p\in P}b_{ijp}\lambda_p\). Create a forbid child imposing \(s_{ij}=0\) and a force child imposing \(s_{ij}=1\). In pricing, delete the transition \(i\to j\) for the forbid child; for the force child, admit only complete columns and compatible partial states in which the occurrence of \(i\) is immediately followed by \(j\). Continue column generation independently in both children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branch on whether one item immediately follows another, forbidding that transition in one pricing problem and requiring it in the other.
knowledge_statements.title: Successor Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The assumptions do not ensure that aggregate successor usage is binary in integer solutions; item-covering and unique-occurrence conditions are needed. A direct source is required for the exact successor-branching formulation and pricing enforcement.

children.title: Generic Disjunctive Branching
children.top_down_role: Pricing-compatible branching based on general disjunctive restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The parent feasible region is \(F\), and sets \(D_1,\ldots,D_k\) satisfy \(F\cap\mathbb Z^n\subseteq\bigcup_{t=1}^k D_t\).
Each intersection \(F\cap D_t\) can be represented in the restricted master and its pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The children \(F_t=F\cap D_t\) collectively retain every integer-feasible parent point.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite valid disjunction applied as a branch-and-price node split.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17
source_refs.source_title: Disjunctive Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite valid disjunction \(D_1\lor\cdots\lor D_k\), create child \(t\) with feasible region \(F_t=F\cap D_t\). For every child, restrict both existing master columns and subsequent pricing output to satisfy \(D_t\), then solve its restricted master and pricing subproblem. A child may be discarded when \(F_t=\varnothing\) or its bound proves fathoming; otherwise it remains in the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Split the parent by any finite disjunction covering all integer solutions, and enforce each disjunct consistently in both master and pricing.
knowledge_statements.title: Generic Disjunctive Branching

source_witnesses.locator: Chapter 2. The Convex Hull of a Disjunctive Set p. 17
source_witnesses.source_title: Disjunctive Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited disjunctive-programming chapter supports finite disjunctions generally but does not establish the stated branch-and-price procedure. Moreover, representability of each child does not imply that every disjunct can be enforced by filtering individual columns; aggregate master constraints may be required.

children.title: Set Branching
children.top_down_role: Branching based on membership or incidence over selected sets.

assumptions_latex: The admissible column universe is \(\Omega\), and \(S\subseteq\Omega\) defines a column class.
The aggregate \(z_S=\sum_{p\in S}\lambda_p\) is integer in every integer-feasible master solution and fractional at the current LP solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities \(z_S\le\lfloor z_S^*\rfloor\) and \(z_S\ge\lceil z_S^*\rceil\) define an exhaustive integer-valid split.

notation.meaning: Aggregate weight of columns in S

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Column-class interpretation of set branching; terminology varies across branch-price formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(S\subseteq\Omega\) such that \(z_S^*=\sum_{p\in S}\lambda_p^*\notin\mathbb Z\), while \(z_S\) is integral for every integer-feasible master solution. Create children imposing \(z_S\le\lfloor z_S^*\rfloor\) and \(z_S\ge\lceil z_S^*\rceil\). Equip pricing with a membership test for \(S\) and any state required to enforce the applicable aggregate restriction. Continue column generation in each child and output both restricted nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose a recognizable set of columns whose total selected weight must be integral, then branch on complementary floor and ceiling bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Set Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Terminology and implementations of set branching vary. The proposed column-class aggregate split and its pricing implementation require a direct source and explicit representability conditions.

children.title: Disjunction-to-Set Specialization
children.top_down_role: Structural relationships between general disjunctions versus set-based restrictions.

assumptions_latex: A valid disjunction \(D_1\lor\cdots\lor D_k\) covers every integer-feasible parent solution.
For each \(t\), membership of a column \(p\in\Omega\) in the compatible set \(S_t\) is decidable by pricing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Enforcing child \(t\) by restricting generated columns to \(S_t\) is valid whenever master feasibility under \(D_t\) is equivalent to using only columns in \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Representation of a disjunctive child as a compatible-column set.

source_refs.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59
source_refs.source_title: Disjunctive Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each disjunct \(D_t\), define \(S_t=\{p\in\Omega: p\text{ is compatible with }D_t\}\). If, for every master vector \(\lambda\), satisfaction of \(D_t\) is equivalent to \(\lambda_p=0\) for all \(p\notin S_t\), then the disjunctive child has the set representation \(F_t=F\cap\{\lambda:\lambda_p=0\text{ for }p\notin S_t\}\). Thus pricing for child \(t\) may search exactly \(S_t\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map each disjunct to the set of compatible columns; when the equivalence holds, restricting pricing to that set exactly represents the child.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjunction-to-Set Specialization

source_witnesses.locator: 4.4 Parsimonious MIP Representation of Disjunctive Sets p. 59
source_witnesses.source_title: Disjunctive Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional equivalence is mathematically coherent and the representation content kind fits the leaf, but the cited general disjunctive-representation section does not directly support the column-set/pricing correspondence.

children.title: Pricing-Domain Restriction
children.top_down_role: Node-induced restrictions on feasible pricing objects.

assumptions_latex: The parent pricing problem minimizes reduced cost \(\bar c(p)\) over a column domain \(\Omega\).
A branch decision determines a compatibility predicate \(B(p)\in\{0,1\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The child pricing domain is \(\Omega_B=\{p\in\Omega:B(p)=1\}\), and its oracle value is \(\min_{p\in\Omega_B}\bar c(p)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing-domain restriction induced by one branch-and-price child.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pricing-domain restriction for branch predicate \(B\) is the replacement of \(\Omega\) by \(\Omega_B=\{p\in\Omega:B(p)=1\}\). At the child node, the pricing oracle must compute \(v_B=\min\{\bar c(p):p\in\Omega_B\}\), returning a minimizing column when one exists. The oracle certifies absence of an improving compatible column precisely when \(v_B\ge 0\), under the reduced-cost convention that negative reduced cost improves the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branch restricts pricing to compatible columns; the child oracle minimizes reduced cost only over that restricted domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Domain Restriction

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is plausible, but it lacks branch-and-price evidence and leaves the minimum undefined when the restricted domain is empty. A source should establish the oracle and certification convention.

children.title: Pricing-State Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of branch decisions into pricing states or structural labels.

assumptions_latex: A pricing state \(q\) represents a family \(\Omega(q)\) of completions.
A child branch supplies a restriction operator \(T_B\) on pricing states.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Propagation is sound when \(\Omega(T_B(q))=\{p\in\Omega(q):B(p)=1\}\) for every state \(q\).

notation.meaning: State transformation induced by branch B

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Propagation of branch restrictions into a state-based pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a pricing state \(q\) and branch predicate \(B\). Compute \(q'=T_B(q)\) by deleting incompatible transitions, tightening resource intervals, or appending the finite branch memory needed to decide \(B\). Discard \(q'\) when \(\Omega(q')=\varnothing\); otherwise use it in the pricing search. Initialize with \(T_B(q_0)\), apply the transformation after every state extension, and output only complete columns \(p\) satisfying \(B(p)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transform every pricing state using the child’s branch restriction, discard states without compatible completions, and output only compatible columns.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-State Propagation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed state transformations do not by themselves guarantee that all and only compatible completions are retained. A direct source and sufficient soundness/completeness conditions are required.

children.title: Restriction Propagation Consistency
children.top_down_role: Consistency between node disjunctions and propagated pricing restrictions.

assumptions_latex: The master child is defined by a branch predicate \(B\) on complete columns.
The propagated pricing oracle explores a represented complete-column set \(\widehat\Omega_B\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restriction propagation is consistent exactly when \(\widehat\Omega_B=\{p\in\Omega:B(p)=1\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact soundness-and-completeness condition for branch restriction propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega_B=\{p\in\Omega:B(p)=1\}\). Restriction propagation is consistent if and only if it is sound, \(\widehat\Omega_B\subseteq\Omega_B\), and complete, \(\Omega_B\subseteq\widehat\Omega_B\). Soundness prevents pricing from returning a column forbidden by the master child; completeness prevents omission of an admissible negative-reduced-cost column. Equivalently, for every \(p\in\Omega\), the propagated pricing system accepts \(p\) exactly when \(B(p)=1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propagation is consistent precisely when the pricing states represent every compatible column and no incompatible column.
knowledge_statements.title: Restriction Propagation Consistency

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The equality characterization is internally consistent and the condition content kind fits, but no source supports this branch-and-price interface formulation.

assumptions_latex: Unbranched pricing instances of encoding length \(n\) are solvable in time \(T(n)\).
A branch restriction is representable by an augmented pricing instance of length at most \(q(n,b)\), constructible in time \(P(n,b)\), where \(b\) is the branch-description length.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pricing at the child is solvable in time \(P(n,b)+T(q(n,b))\); polynomial pricing is preserved when \(P\), \(q\), and \(T\) are polynomial.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional complexity preservation under encoding-compatible branching restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an unbranched pricing instance of length \(n\) and a branch description of length \(b\), construct the restricted instance in time \(P(n,b)\) with length at most \(q(n,b)\), then invoke the original pricing algorithm. The total running time is at most \(P(n,b)+T(q(n,b))\). Hence polynomial-time pricing is retained when \(P\), \(q\), and \(T\) are polynomial; this conclusion does not apply when the branch restriction requires exponentially many states or lacks a polynomial-size encoding.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing remains polynomial after branching when the restriction has a polynomial-size, polynomial-time encoding accepted by the original pricing algorithm.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Complexity Under Branching

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional composition bound is plausible, but the computational model, encoding transformation, and preservation claim require a direct complexity source or an explicit standard-field rationale.

children.title: Branching Completeness
children.top_down_role: Coverage of the required integer search space by branching disjunctions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness of a branching rule for an integer master represented by generated columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_I\) be the integer-feasible master set and let \(Q\) be any branch-and-bound node relaxation. A finite disjunction \(Q=\bigcup_{j=1}^k Q_j\) is a complete branching step if \(X_I\cap Q\subseteq\bigcup_{j=1}^k Q_j\) and every integer-infeasible fractional extreme point \(x\in Q\) is excluded from each child containing no integer point equal to \(x\). A branching scheme is complete if repeated application produces, along every infinite descendant path, either an infeasible node, an integral node, or relaxations whose bounds converge to the node's integer optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching scheme is complete when its children retain every integer solution and repeated branching eventually resolves every fractional node or closes its bound gap.
assumptions_latex: \(X_I\) is the integer-feasible set of the master formulation.
Every branching disjunction has finitely many children.
Node relaxations and bounds are solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Every unresolved fractional node is eventually fathomed, made integral, or solved in the limit.}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalizes the usual exhaustive branching requirement for branch-and-price

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition container is appropriate, but the proposed definition is not reliable without a branch-and-price source. Writing Q as the union of its children already makes integer-solution retention automatic, the condition concerning a fractional point and a child containing no integer point equal to it is vacuous, and the infinite-path bound-convergence clause needs precise assumptions and a cited completeness result.

children.title: Pricing Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Preservation of a tractable and valid pricing representation under branching.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility of a branching restriction with the existing pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a column family \(P\), restricted master variables \(\lambda_p\), and pricing objective \(\bar c(p)=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\). A branching disjunction is pricing-compatible if, for every child \(j\), its restriction can be represented by a feasible-set modification \(P_j\subseteq P\) and additive reduced-cost term \(d_j(p)\) such that pricing remains \(\min_{p\in P_j}\{\bar c(p)+d_j(p)\}\), solvable by the same oracle class and state description as the root pricing problem. Compatibility requires the oracle to return a minimum-reduced-cost admissible column or certify that none is improving.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Branching is pricing-compatible when each child can be enforced by modifying the original pricing oracle without changing its essential problem class.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the complete column family.
The original pricing oracle optimizes \(c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in P_j}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p+d_j(p)\}\) remains in the original pricing-oracle class for every child \(j\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: captures the standard oracle-preservation meaning of pricing compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the leaf, and the statement captures a plausible oracle-preservation notion. However, 'same oracle class and state description' is not mathematically defined, and the exact scope of pricing compatibility varies in the branch-and-price literature. A specific authoritative source is required before selecting this formulation.

children.title: Completeness–Compatibility Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural tensions between exhaustive search partitioning versus manageable pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Completeness–Compatibility Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Design principle governing branch selection in branch-and-price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal B_C\) denote branching disjunctions sufficient for completeness and \(\mathcal B_P\) those implementable by the available pricing oracle. A branch-and-price design can guarantee both properties using only its native oracle precisely when it possesses a complete branching scheme contained in \(\mathcal B_C\cap\mathcal B_P\). If no such scheme exists, every complete implementation must either enlarge the pricing state or oracle class, introduce an extended formulation, or accept branching steps whose pricing subproblems are harder. Thus completeness alone does not imply pricing compatibility, and compatibility alone does not imply exhaustive separation of fractional master solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Both goals are achieved only by a complete family of pricing-compatible disjunctions; otherwise completeness requires a stronger oracle or extended formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal B_C\) and \(\mathcal B_P\) refer to the same master formulation and pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Native-oracle completeness holds exactly when a complete scheme exists in }\mathcal B_C\cap\mathcal B_P.\)

notation.meaning: branching disjunctions usable in a complete scheme

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: set-intersection formulation makes the completeness–compatibility tradeoff explicit

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle kind fits the tradeoff leaf, but the asserted precise equivalence depends on the unresolved definitions of completeness and pricing compatibility. The claim that every complete implementation must take one of the listed actions is also presented as exhaustive without support. A branch-and-price source addressing this tradeoff is required.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Robustness relative to a fixed column-generation pricing formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master cut \(\sum_{p\in P}\gamma_p\lambda_p\geq\delta\), call the cut robust relative to a pricing formulation if its coefficient has an additive representation \(\gamma_p=\gamma_0+\sum_{r\in R}q_r z_r(p)\), where the features \(z_r(p)\) already occur in the pricing state or objective. For cut dual multiplier \(\mu\), the modified reduced cost \(c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\mu\gamma_p\) must then be optimizable by the original pricing algorithm after changing only objective coefficients or fixed parameters, without adding state variables or coupling resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust cut changes pricing only through coefficients of features already represented by the pricing model, preserving its formulation and algorithmic structure.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the complete column family.
The pricing formulation exposes the features \(z_r(p)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in P}\{c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\mu\gamma_p\}\) uses the unchanged pricing state space.

notation.meaning: coefficient of column p in the cut
pricing feature already represented in the oracle

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: formalizes robustness as preservation of the pricing formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition is the correct content kind, but the additive feature representation is a proposed sufficient structure rather than an established general definition of a robust cut. Terminology and the degree of pricing-algorithm preservation vary across branch-cut-and-price sources, so a direct source is needed to determine the intended exact definition.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonrobust Cuts
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonrobustness relative to a fixed column-generation pricing formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master cut \(\sum_{p\in P}\gamma_p\lambda_p\geq\delta\), call the cut nonrobust relative to a pricing formulation if incorporating its dual multiplier \(\mu\) makes exact minimization of \(c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\mu\gamma_p\) require information not represented by the original pricing state. Equivalently, no coefficient update within the fixed oracle expresses \(\gamma_p\) for every \(p\in P\). Exact pricing must therefore augment the state or resources, use an extended-master representation, enumerate additional structure, or invoke a different oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonrobust cut introduces column coefficients that the original pricing state cannot evaluate, so exact pricing needs augmentation or reformulation.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is the complete column family.
The original pricing state and admissible coefficient updates are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma_p\) cannot be incorporated exactly by coefficient changes within the original pricing oracle.

notation.meaning: coefficient of column p in the cut

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: defines nonrobustness as failure to preserve the pricing formulation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Definition fits the terminal container, but the stated equivalence is not established: failure to express a coefficient through fixed coefficient updates need not be identical to requiring new pricing-state information. The asserted list of necessary remedies is likewise not exhaustive without a fixed oracle model. A direct source is required.

assumptions_latex: \(A\), \(D\), \(E\), \(g\), \(h\), \(k\), \(b\), and \(f\) have compatible finite dimensions.
\(g^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\beta\) is valid for the intended integer master set.
Projection is taken over all auxiliary variables \(y\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{\lambda}(X^{\mathrm{ext}})=X\cap\{\lambda:g^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\beta\}.\)

notation.meaning: right-hand side of the represented cut

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-preserving representation of a master cut using auxiliary master variables.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X=\{\lambda\geq0:A\lambda\geq b\}\), and let \(g^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\beta\) be a valid cut. An extended-master representation of this cut consists of auxiliary variables \(y\) and linear constraints defining
\[X^{\mathrm{ext}}=\{(\lambda,y):A\lambda\geq b,\ \lambda\geq0,\ D\lambda+Ey\geq f,\ h^{\mathsf T}y+k^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\beta\}\]
such that
\[\operatorname{proj}_{\lambda}(X^{\mathrm{ext}})=X\cap\{\lambda:g^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\beta\}.\]
Relative to a specified pricing oracle, the representation is pricing-compatible if all coefficients contributed by a prospective column to the added extended-master rows can be evaluated by that oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An extended-master representation introduces auxiliary variables and constraints whose projection is exactly the cut-strengthened original master. It is pricing-compatible relative to a specified oracle when that oracle can evaluate every new coefficient of a prospective column.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Induced Pricing Terms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost contribution created by dualized master cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a restricted master with column cost \(c_p\), base coefficients \(a_p\), and added cuts \(\sum_{p\in P}\gamma_{kp}\lambda_p\geq\delta_k\) for \(k\in K\). If \(\pi\) and \(\mu_k\) are the corresponding dual multipliers under a consistent sign convention, then the reduced cost of a prospective column is
\[\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sum_{k\in K}\mu_k\gamma_{kp}.\]
Hence exact pricing must evaluate every active coefficient \(\gamma_{kp}\); the sum involving \(\mu_k\) is the cut-induced pricing term.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each active cut contributes its dual multiplier times the prospective column's cut coefficient to the pricing reduced cost.
assumptions_latex: The master and its dual use a fixed, consistent inequality-sign convention.
Every active cut has a defined coefficient \(\gamma_{kp}\) for each potential column \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_p=c_p-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_p-\sum_{k\in K}\mu_k\gamma_{kp}.\)

notation.meaning: dual multipliers of base master constraints
coefficient of column p in cut k

children.title: Separation Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Timing and frequency of cut separation during node processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Separation Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for deciding when to invoke cut separation during column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a node master, tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and separation policy \(S\). Initialize the restricted master and iteration counter \(t=0\). After solving the current restricted master to obtain \(x^t\), invoke separation exactly when \(S(t,x^t) = 1\). If a valid inequality has violation greater than \(\varepsilon\), add selected violated cuts, invalidate affected dual and pricing data, and reoptimize; otherwise record separation closure for that iterate. Stop separation at the node when the oracle certifies no violation above \(\varepsilon\), or when a declared finite scheduling budget is exhausted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separation schedule triggers the cut oracle at declared iterations, adds sufficiently violated cuts, and stops after certification or an explicit budget limit.
assumptions_latex: The separation oracle returns a valid violated cut or an \(\varepsilon\)-closure certificate.
Added cuts are retained for their declared scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Output is an updated restricted master or an }\varepsilon\text{-separation certificate.}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: algorithmic formalization of separation scheduling in cut-and-price

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the appropriate kind for this scheduling leaf. The proposed policy is plausible, but no source supports the exact trigger, invalidation, budget, or closure rules. In addition, exhausting a finite budget does not produce the separation certificate named in the conclusion. A scheduling source is needed to select and correct the intended algorithm.

children.title: Pricing Scheduling
children.top_down_role: Timing and frequency of pricing relative to master reoptimization.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Scheduling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rule for deciding when to invoke column pricing after master changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a restricted master, tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and pricing policy \(P_s\). After each master solve, obtain dual vector \(u^t\) and invoke pricing when \(P_s(t,u^t)=1\) or whenever added cuts or branching restrictions invalidate the latest pricing certificate. Add any admissible column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\) for minimization and reoptimize. Declare pricing closure only when the exact pricing oracle certifies that the minimum reduced cost is at least \(-\varepsilon\) under all currently active rows and node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pricing schedule invokes pricing after selected master solves and whenever model changes invalidate the prior no-improving-column certificate.
assumptions_latex: Pricing is exact relative to all active master rows and node restrictions.
The problem is stated in minimization form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in P_t}\bar c_p\geq-\varepsilon\) certifies pricing closure for the current master.

notation.meaning: columns admissible at the current node and iteration

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm fits the leaf, and the current-master pricing certificate is mathematically plausible. No source is supplied for the mandatory rescheduling and certificate-invalidation policy, however, so the exact algorithmic statement cannot be validated.

children.title: Alternating Cut–Price Cycles
children.top_down_role: Regimes that alternate separation phases with pricing phases.

knowledge_statements.title: Alternating Cut–Price Cycles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-coordinate schedule alternating pricing closure and separation closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a restricted master and tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\). For cycle \(r=0,1,\ldots\), first solve the master and repeatedly price and add columns until the minimum reduced cost is at least \(-\varepsilon\). Next separate the resulting master solution and add valid cuts whose violation exceeds \(\varepsilon\). Because new cuts change dual multipliers and reduced costs, return to the pricing phase whenever any cut is added. Terminate when one cycle produces both a pricing certificate and a separation certificate without changing the master; otherwise continue with the enlarged row and column sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Alternating cycles close pricing, then separate cuts, and repeat because each added cut invalidates the preceding pricing certificate.
assumptions_latex: Pricing and separation oracles are exact to tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
Generated rows and columns are valid for the current node.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Termination yields simultaneous }\varepsilon\text{-pricing and }\varepsilon\text{-separation closure.}\)
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit alternating closure schedule for row and column generation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role for this leaf, but the exact alternating schedule and its termination claim require a row-and-column generation source. Adding a cut requires pricing to be reconsidered, but it does not logically imply that a previously true reduced-cost certificate becomes false. No convergence or finite-termination conditions are supplied.

children.title: Interleaved Cut–Price Processing
children.top_down_role: Regimes that interleave separation and pricing within node processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Interleaved Cut–Price Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Event-driven schedule mixing cut separation and pricing before either reaches closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a restricted master, tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and a fair event policy selecting separation or pricing. At each iteration solve the current master, then execute the selected oracle: add a cut with violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\), or add a column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\). Reoptimize after every nonempty batch and invalidate certificates affected by the change. Fairness requires that neither oracle remain eligible forever without invocation. Terminate only when, for the same unchanged master, separation certifies no violation above \(\varepsilon\) and pricing certifies no reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interleaved processing selects cut or pricing events fairly, reoptimizes after changes, and stops only with simultaneous certificates for one unchanged master.
assumptions_latex: Both oracles are exact to tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
The event policy is fair among persistently eligible oracle calls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{Output has simultaneous valid separation and pricing certificates for one master state.}\)

notation.meaning: current reduced cost of column p

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: event-driven row-and-column generation requires fair processing and common-state certificates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and event-driven interpretation fit the terminal container. Fairness and common-state certificates are reasonable design requirements, but the record provides neither a source nor conditions ensuring that the process reaches termination. A cut-and-price source is required for this exact scheduling formulation.

children.title: Local Cut Scopes
children.top_down_role: Cut validity restricted to a search node or subtree.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Cut Scopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity domain and inheritance rule for node-local cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_v\) be the relaxation at branch-and-bound node \(v\), and let \(X_v\) be its integer-feasible set. An inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) has local scope rooted at \(v\) if it is valid for \(X_v\) but is not asserted valid outside the subtree rooted at \(v\). It may be installed at \(v\) and inherited by a descendant \(w\) because \(X_w\subseteq X_v\). It must not be transferred to an unrelated node unless validity for that node is established independently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local cut is valid only for one node's integer set and its descendants, so it cannot automatically be used on other branches.
assumptions_latex: Descendant feasible sets satisfy \(X_w\subseteq X_v\).
The inequality is valid for every point in \(X_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\text{ descendant of }v\implies a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\text{ is valid for every }x\in X_w.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Global Cut Scopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global validity within a branch-price tree, including columns absent when the cut is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P\) be the universe of master columns, let \(\Lambda\) be the set of finite-support master vectors representing original integer-feasible solutions, and let \(\Lambda_v\subseteq\Lambda\) be the feasible set at node \(v\). An inequality \(\sum_{p\in P}d_p\lambda_p\leq\beta\) has global scope if its coefficient \(d_p\) is defined for every \(p\in P\) and the inequality is valid for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda\). It is then valid at every node and may remain active throughout the tree without excluding an original integer-feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A global cut is valid for every original integer-feasible master representation and has a coefficient for every priceable column, including columns generated later.
assumptions_latex: \(\Lambda_v\subseteq\Lambda\) for every tree node \(v\).
\(d_p\) is defined for every column \(p\in P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_{p\in P}d_p\lambda_p\leq\beta\text{ is valid for every }\lambda\in\Lambda_v\text{ and every node }v.\)

children.title: Cut-Scope Inheritance

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Scope Inheritance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance rule distinguishing globally valid cuts from cuts valid only below a designated node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\) be an ancestor of \(v\), and let \(X_v\subseteq X_u\) be their feasible sets in a common vector space. If the inequality \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid on \(X_u\), then it is valid on \(X_v\). In a column-generated master, inheritance additionally requires the inequality coefficient to be correctly defined for every column admissible at \(v\). A globally scoped cut may be inherited by every node, whereas a cut whose validity depends on the restrictions at \(u\) may be inherited only within the subtree rooted at \(u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A descendant may inherit an ancestor's cut when its feasible set is contained in the ancestor's and every column admissible at the descendant has the correct cut coefficient.
assumptions_latex: \(u\) is an ancestor of \(v\) and \(X_v\subseteq X_u\).
\(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\) is valid for every \(x\in X_u\).
Cut coefficients are defined for every column admissible at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\leq\beta\text{ is valid for every }x\in X_v.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Completed Node-Pricing Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual reduced-cost certificate for a minimization node master after exhaustive exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), consider the full master \(\min\{\sum_{p\in P_v}c_p\lambda_p:A_v\lambda=b_v,\ \lambda\geq0\}\) and a restricted master over \(R_v\subseteq P_v\). Let \((\lambda^*,y^*)\) be primal-dual optimal for the restricted master. If exact pricing certifies \(c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}y^*\geq0\) for every \(p\in P_v\), then \(y^*\) is dual feasible for the full master. Consequently the restricted-master value equals the full node-relaxation optimum and is a valid lower bound for the minimization node.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restricted-master optimality plus exact confirmation that every admissible column has nonnegative reduced cost certifies the full node LP value and its lower bound.
assumptions_latex: The node master is feasible and has a finite optimum.
Restricted-master primal and dual solutions are optimal.
Pricing examines all columns in \(P_v\) exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{R_v}=z_{P_v}=b_v^{\mathsf T}y^*\), and this value is a valid node lower bound.

notation.meaning: Full and restricted node column sets
Constraint vector and objective coefficient of column p

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted-Master Bound Limitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Why an incompletely priced restricted-master optimum cannot by itself certify the full node bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization node master with \(R_v\subsetneq P_v\), restricting variables gives \(z_{R_v}\geq z_{P_v}\). Thus \(z_{R_v}\) alone need not be a valid lower bound on the node integer optimum. Concretely, the full master \(\min\{0\lambda_1-\lambda_2:\lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda\geq0\}\) has value \(-1\), whereas the restricted master containing only \(\lambda_1\) has value \(0\). The restricted value becomes certifying only after pricing excludes every omitted negative-reduced-cost column or supplies another valid correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization restricted master can overestimate the full relaxation value; without completed pricing, its optimum may incorrectly prune a node.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization master.
At least one admissible column may be absent from the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{R_v}\geq z_{P_v}\), and \(z_{R_v}\) is not generally a certified node lower bound.

notation.meaning: Full and restricted node column sets

knowledge_statements.title: Farkas Node-Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-ray certificate for infeasibility of a full node master, requiring exhaustive ray pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the node feasibility system \(A_v\lambda=b_v\), \(\lambda\geq0\), with columns \(a_p\) indexed by \(p\in P_v\). A vector \(y\) is a node-infeasibility certificate if \(a_p^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\) for every \(p\in P_v\) and \(b_v^{\mathsf T}y<0\). These inequalities are incompatible with feasibility because any feasible \(\lambda\) would satisfy \(b_v^{\mathsf T}y=\sum_{p\in P_v}\lambda_p a_p^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\). In branch-price, exact Farkas pricing must verify the first inequality over all admissible columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Farkas ray with nonnegative value on every admissible column but negative value on the right-hand side certifies that the full node master is infeasible.
assumptions_latex: The full node master has finitely supported nonnegative column combinations.
Farkas pricing is exact over \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\lambda\geq0:A_v\lambda=b_v\}=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: All columns admissible at node v

knowledge_statements.title: Exact-Pricing Tree Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global exactness of branch-price under exhaustive branching and exact node pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization branch-price tree for an integer-feasible set \(F\) and objective \(f\). Suppose every branching disjunction is valid and the children of each branched node collectively contain all integer-feasible solutions represented by that node. Suppose every retained node is solved to full-master optimality by exact pricing, every infeasibility claim is certified over all columns admissible at that node, every bound-based pruning decision uses a certified node lower bound, and every integral solution used to close a node is recorded or compared with the incumbent. If all generated nodes are processed or soundly pruned, then either \(F=\varnothing\) or the best recorded integer solution is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If branching covers every integer solution, node pricing and infeasibility tests are exact, pruning is certified, and integral node solutions update the incumbent, exhaustion of the tree proves global optimality or infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the integer-feasible set of a minimization problem with objective \(f\).
Every branching disjunction validly covers all integer-feasible solutions of its parent node.
Every processed node receives complete exact pricing or an exact full-master infeasibility certificate.
Bound pruning uses only certified lower bounds, and integral solutions used for closure are compared with the incumbent.
Every generated node is eventually processed or soundly pruned.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=\varnothing\text{ or }z^{\mathrm{inc}}=z^{\mathrm{IP}}.\)

notation.meaning: Objective value of the best recorded integer solution

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Search-Tree Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient structural regimes ensuring that branch-price generates only finitely many tree nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A branch-price search tree is finite if there exists a finite family \(\mathcal D\) of node descriptions such that every branching child has a description in \(\mathcal D\), no description repeats along a root-to-leaf path, and every nonterminal node creates finitely many children. A common regime satisfies this condition when finitely many bounded integer variables are fixed or range-split so that each branch strictly removes at least one remaining integer assignment. Under either formulation, the number of generated nodes is finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The tree is finite when branching ranges over finitely many node states, never repeats a state along a path, and gives each node finitely many children.
assumptions_latex: The set \(\mathcal D\) of possible node descriptions is finite.
A child never repeats an ancestral description.
Every branching operation has finite arity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|V|<\infty\), where \(V\) is the generated node set.

notation.meaning: Finite set of possible node descriptions

children.title: Finite Node-Pricing Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Finite Node-Pricing Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for finite column-generation iterations at one feasible branch-price node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a node \(v\) with a feasible restricted master. Let \(P_v\) be its finite admissible column set and \(R_v^0\subseteq P_v\) its initial restricted column set. Suppose every successful pricing round permanently adds at least one previously absent column and exact pricing is invoked when no further column is added. Then objective-price column generation terminates after at most \(|P_v\setminus R_v^0|\) successful rounds and one final certifying round. At termination, exact pricing certifies nonnegative reduced cost for every column in \(P_v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At a feasible node, a finite admissible column set, permanent addition of a new column in every successful round, and an exact final pricing call ensure finite objective-price column generation.
assumptions_latex: \(|P_v|<\infty\) and \(R_v^0\subseteq P_v\).
Every successful pricing round permanently adds at least one column in \(P_v\setminus R_v\).
The master solves and the final exact pricing call terminate correctly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(N_v\leq |P_v\setminus R_v^0|+1\text{ pricing rounds, including the final certifying round}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Node-Processing Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite termination of one node-processing routine under finite pricing and finite cut generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a branch-price node \(v\) whose processing loop solves a restricted master and invokes pricing and cut separation. Suppose only finitely many distinct cuts and columns can be introduced at \(v\), every productive iteration permanently adds at least one previously absent cut or column, every master solve and oracle call terminates, and the routine stops after its first nonproductive iteration. Then the node-processing loop terminates after finitely many iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node processing terminates when only finitely many cuts and columns are addable, each productive iteration permanently adds a new object, every subroutine terminates, and the routine stops when no object is added.
assumptions_latex: Only finitely many distinct cuts and columns can be added at \(v\).
Every productive iteration permanently adds at least one previously absent cut or column.
Every master solve, pricing call, and separation call terminates.
The routine stops after its first iteration that adds neither a cut nor a column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v\text{ is processed in finitely many loop iterations}.\)

children.title: Termination Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Modeling or implementation regimes that obstruct finite completion.

knowledge_statements.title: Termination Failure Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mechanisms invalidating finite-termination claims for branch-price.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Finite termination is not guaranteed if any required finiteness or progress condition is removed. An infinite admissible column family can yield an endless sequence of distinct improving columns whose reduced costs approach \(0\); an infinite cut family can analogously produce perpetual separation; non-strict branching can create an infinite path of nested nodes; and an inexact oracle may repeatedly fail to certify that no improving column exists. Thus bounded objective values or monotone bound improvement alone do not imply finite termination of node processing or of the search tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infinite column or cut families, non-progressing branching, or noncertifying pricing can prevent termination even while bounds converge monotonically.
assumptions_latex: At least one finiteness, strict-progress, or exact-certification condition is absent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\text{monotone bounded node bounds}\not\Rightarrow\text{finite branch-price termination}\).
review_flags: no supplied locator directly supports branch-price termination failure mechanisms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure mechanisms are plausible and fit the failure-boundary container, but the record supplies no source for the asserted infinite improving-column, perpetual-separation, or infinite-branching phenomena.

knowledge_statements.title: Heuristic-Pricing Exactness Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe integration of heuristic pricing with mandatory exact certification before pruning or node closure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), initialize a restricted column set \(R_v\). Repeatedly solve the restricted master and call a heuristic pricing oracle; whenever it returns a column of negative reduced cost, add that column and repeat. If the heuristic returns none, invoke exact pricing over the entire admissible set \(P_v\). Add any negative-reduced-cost column found and resume the loop. Stop only when exact pricing certifies nonnegative reduced cost for every \(p\in P_v\), or when exact Farkas pricing certifies infeasibility. Only then may the resulting bound or infeasibility claim be used for pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic pricing may find columns quickly, but an exact pricing call must confirm failure before a node bound or infeasibility claim becomes certifying.
assumptions_latex: Exact pricing over \(P_v\) is eventually invoked after heuristic failure.
Master problems and exact oracle calls are solved correctly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{p\in P_v}\{c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}y^*\}\geq0\) before bound-based node closure.

notation.meaning: Restricted and full admissible node column sets

review_flags: authoritative heuristic-pricing recovery locator not supplied

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No authoritative locator supports the heuristic-to-exact pricing recovery algorithm. The procedure also does not explicitly specify how Farkas pricing is entered when the restricted master is infeasible, so its infeasibility endpoint cannot be validated as written.

knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Complete Cut-Strengthened Nodes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full node-bound certificate when active cuts alter the reduced-cost pricing expression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), let the cut-strengthened full master use columns \(P_v\), linking equations \(\sum_{p\in P_v}a_p\lambda_p=b_v\), active cuts \(\sum_{p\in P_v}d_p\lambda_p\geq h_v\), and variables \(\lambda_p\geq0\). Let \(R_v\subseteq P_v\), and suppose \(\lambda^*\) and \((y^*,\mu^*)\), with \(\mu^*\geq0\), are attained primal and dual optima of the restricted master with equal objective value. If exact cut-dependent pricing verifies \(c_p-a_p^{\mathsf T}y^*-d_p^{\mathsf T}\mu^*\geq0\) for every \(p\in P_v\), then \((y^*,\mu^*)\) is dual feasible for the full cut-strengthened master, and the restricted value equals the full strengthened node-relaxation value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut-strengthened node bound is certified when an attained restricted-master primal-dual optimum is supplemented by exact pricing that includes every active cut's dual contribution for every admissible column.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\subseteq P_v\), and the restricted cut-strengthened master has attained primal and dual optima with equal finite value.
Every active cut is valid at node \(v\), and every \(p\in P_v\) has a correct coefficient vector \(d_p\).
\(\mu^*\geq0\) under the stated minimization-dual convention.
Exact cut-dependent pricing is performed over all \(p\in P_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{R_v}^{\mathrm{cut}}=z_{P_v}^{\mathrm{cut}}=b_v^{\mathsf T}y^*+h_v^{\mathsf T}\mu^*.\)

notation.meaning: Full and restricted admissible node column sets
Linking and active-cut coefficient vectors of column p
Restricted-master linking and cut dual multipliers

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inheritance concerns descendant restrictions, not transfer to nodes whose column semantics or cut coefficients differ.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v\) be a branch-price node with full master relaxation \(P_v\), and let \(a^{\mathsf T}\lambda\le b\) be valid for every \(\lambda\in P_v\). knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Dependent Pricing Completeness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Completeness is relative to the active cuts because their dual multipliers contribute to every column's reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(v\), suppose the full cut-strengthened master is a feasible, bounded minimization linear program and the restricted master is solved exactly. Let \((\pi,\mu)\) be an optimal restricted-master dual solution, where \(\mu\) contains the multipliers of all active cuts. For every pricing family \(k\), compute \(r_k^*=\min\{\bar c_p(\pi,\mu):p\in\mathcal P_k(v)\}\), including every active-cut coefficient in \(\bar c_p\). If exact pricing gives \(r_k^*\ge 0\) for every \(k\), then \((\pi,\mu)\) is feasible for the full-master dual and the restricted-master value equals the full cut-strengthened master value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If exact pricing includes every active-cut dual contribution and finds no negative-reduced-cost column in any node-feasible family, the restricted and full cut-strengthened master values are equal.
assumptions_latex: The full cut-strengthened master at node \(v\) is a feasible, bounded minimization linear program.
The restricted master is solved exactly and has optimal dual solution \((\pi,\mu)\).
The pricing families \(\mathcal P_k(v)\) cover every admissible full-master column.
Each pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost including all active-cut contributions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(r_k^*\ge0\) for every \(k\), then the restricted-master value equals the full cut-strengthened master value.

notation.meaning: dual multipliers for master rows and active cuts
reduced cost of column p including active-cut contributions

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Started Node Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Warm starting reuses feasible columns and compatible oracle state without altering the termination guarantee associated with the chosen reduced-cost tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For node \(v\), initialize \(C_v^0\) by filtering cached columns through all branching and local-cut restrictions, and initialize compatible pricing state from stored information. For \(t=0,1,\ldots\), solve \(R_v(C_v^t)\), obtain its dual vector, and invoke exact node pricing from the cached state. If pricing returns an admissible column with reduced cost below \(-\varepsilon\), add it to form \(C_v^{t+1}\). Otherwise stop and output the restricted-master solution with the certificate that every admissible column has reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\). For \(\varepsilon=0\), this is a nonnegative reduced-cost certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Filter cached columns for the node, reuse compatible pricing state, and continue exact column generation until all admissible reduced costs are at least the negative tolerance; zero tolerance gives the usual nonnegative certificate.
assumptions_latex: A parent or related node supplies stored columns and compatible pricing state.
Every reused column is tested against all restrictions at node \(v\).
The pricing oracle globally minimizes reduced cost over every column admissible at node \(v\).
The reduced-cost tolerance satisfies \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination every admissible column has reduced cost at least \(-\varepsilon\); if \(\varepsilon=0\), every admissible reduced cost is nonnegative.

notation.meaning: cached columns retained after filtering for node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary separates heuristic branch ranking from certified child bounds and fathoming decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose strong branching tentatively creates children \(u\) and solves only restricted masters, producing estimates \(\widehat L_u\). Because omitted columns can lower a minimization relaxation, \(\widehat L_u\) need not be a valid lower bound on the full child master. Thus scores computed from \(\widehat L_u\) may be used only to rank branching candidates. A child bound or fathoming decision is valid only after complete pricing establishes \(L_u=\widehat L_u\), or after a rigorous pricing-error correction establishes a bound such as \(L_u\ge\widehat L_u-\Delta_u\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partially priced child objectives can guide branch selection, but they are not certified lower bounds unless pricing completes or a rigorous error correction is available.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given generated columns \(C\), form the restricted integer master \(R_C^{\mathrm{IP}}\) with the original master constraints, current node restrictions, and required integrality. Solve it exactly or by an integer heuristic. If it returns \(\lambda\), reconstruct the original-space solution, verify every original constraint and integrality condition, and accept it only if feasible; for minimization update \(U\leftarrow\min\{U,c^{\mathsf T}\lambda\}\). If no feasible restricted-master solution is found, return no incumbent and make no claim that the full master is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve an integer master over generated columns, verify any reconstructed solution in the original model, and use it as an incumbent; failure is inconclusive.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Start from a tentative integer master solution \(\lambda\) and compute its residual vector \(r=b-A\lambda\). Choose nonnegative residual penalties \(w\), and invoke pricing with a repair score \(q_p=c_p-w^{\mathsf T}a_p\), subject to the current node restrictions. Add selected columns with favorable \(q_p\), then reoptimize a restricted integer repair model that minimizes weighted residual violation, breaking ties by original cost. Repeat until zero violation is obtained or a prescribed repair limit is reached. Output a solution only after direct verification of all original constraints and integrality; otherwise report repair failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use residual-weighted pricing to generate columns that repair a tentative integer solution, then accept the result only after full feasibility and integrality checks.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing-Aware Solution Repair

children.top_down_role: Reuse or adaptation of incumbent solutions across search nodes.

assumptions_latex: An incumbent solution \(x^I\) is feasible at a source node.
The target node imposes its own branching and local-cut restrictions.
The incumbent can be represented or reconstructed independently of the target's current column pool.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent transfers exactly when it satisfies every target-node restriction; otherwise it cannot serve as that node's feasible solution.

notation.meaning: original-space feasible set at target node v
master representation of the incumbent at node v

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an incumbent is transferable precisely by feasibility in the target node, while column-pool membership is representational
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer is an original-space feasibility question; absence from the target column pool alone does not invalidate an incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^I\) be an incumbent and let \(X_v\) denote the original-space feasible set after imposing every branching decision and local constraint at target node \(v\). The incumbent is transferable to \(v\) if and only if \(x^I\in X_v\). If the target restricted master lacks columns representing \(x^I\), those columns may be inserted or regenerated to obtain \(\lambda_v^I\), but this representational step does not replace the test \(x^I\in X_v\). A failing incumbent remains a global objective cutoff when globally valid, but is not a feasible solution of node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An incumbent transfers to a node exactly when it satisfies that node's restrictions; missing representation columns may be regenerated but do not determine feasibility.
knowledge_statements.title: Incumbent Transfer Across Nodes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: From an incumbent, fractional solution, or repair residual, define a heuristic score \(h_p\) favoring columns likely to participate in a good integer solution. Search only columns satisfying the current node restrictions, select a finite set \(E\) of valid columns with favorable scores, and update \(C\leftarrow C\cup E\). Reoptimize the restricted master or restricted integer heuristic and retain improving feasible solutions. Stop at a prescribed time, column, or nonimprovement limit. Because the search need not minimize exact reduced cost globally, enrichment alone supplies no pricing-completeness or dual-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate valid columns likely to improve primal solutions, add them to the pool, and rerun the heuristic; this does not certify complete pricing.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing cost may influence node order, but only certified information may eliminate a node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every open node \(v\), maintain a bound field \(L_v\), a certification flag, and an estimate \(T_v>0\) of the effort required to complete pricing. Compute a deterministic score \(S_v=\phi(L_v,T_v,d_v)\), where \(d_v\) is depth and \(\phi\) encodes the chosen bound, depth, and effort tradeoff; select an extremal-score node with fixed tie breaking. Process it by column generation, updating \(L_v\), \(T_v\), and its certification flag. Provisional bounds may affect \(S_v\), but a node is fathomed only by a valid incumbent comparison, certified infeasibility, or pricing-complete bound.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the full master \(\min\{\lambda_1: \lambda_1+\lambda_2=1,\ \lambda_1,\lambda_2\ge0\}\), whose column costs are \(c_1=1\) and \(c_2=0\). With only column \(1\), the restricted master has \(\lambda_1=1\) and value \(1\). If the incumbent value is \(U=1\), fathoming by the test that the node bound is at least \(U\) would discard the node. Yet the omitted column \(2\) gives \(\lambda_2=1\) and full-master value \(0\). Hence fathoming is invalid until pricing proves that no improving omitted column exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted master can equal the incumbent while an omitted column yields a better solution, so fathoming before complete pricing can discard the optimum.
