assumptions_latex: Unbranched pricing minimizes an additive objective over \(x\in\{0,1\}^n\).
Branching may impose arbitrary linear restrictions on pricing variables.
The number of imposed restrictions is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Branching can transform a separable pricing oracle into a general binary linear optimization problem.
review_flags: branching_class_must_be_scoped: arbitrary original-space branching is broader than structure-preserving branch-price rules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The boundary concerns branching rules that introduce nonseparable restrictions into an otherwise tractable pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let unbranched pricing be \(\min\{r^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\{0,1\}^n\}\), which is solved independently by setting each component according to the sign of its coefficient. If accumulated branching decisions introduce constraints \(Bx\le d\), pricing becomes \(\min\{r^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\{0,1\}^n,\ Bx\le d\}\). Because \(B\) and \(d\) can encode a general binary linear program, the original separability and its componentwise oracle are lost. Structure-preserving branching must therefore restrict the admissible form of \(B\), or pricing requires a more general solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Arbitrary branch constraints can couple formerly independent column decisions, turning trivial separable pricing into general binary optimization and destroying the original oracle structure.
knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Destructed Pricing Structure

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The construction is valid for arbitrary binary linear branch restrictions, but the resulting general-complexity claim requires an authoritative source and must not be read as applying to structure-preserving branch-price rules.

assumptions_latex: Base pricing admits a dynamic program with polynomially many states.
Each active cut contributes a separately tracked bounded resource.
The number of active cuts is not fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A direct resource-augmented pricing dynamic program can require exponentially many states in the number of cuts.

notation.meaning: upper bound for cut resource j

knowledge_statements.scope_note: The bound describes state-space growth when cut coefficients require independent resource coordinates in dynamic-programming pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose base pricing has \(S_0\) dynamic-programming states and each of \(k\) active cuts requires tracking an integer resource \(q_j\in\{0,1,\ldots,R_j\}\) to evaluate column reduced cost exactly. The direct augmented state space then has at most \(S_0\prod_{j=1}^k(R_j+1)\) states, and instances can make all such resource vectors reachable and nondominated. In particular, if \(R_j\ge1\) for every \(j\), the state count can be at least \(S_0 2^k\). Thus unrestricted growth in independently tracked cuts can make exact pricing exponential in the number of active cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When each cut adds an independent pricing resource, direct dynamic programming may grow from a base state space to a product-sized, exponentially large state space.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Induced Pricing Explosion

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-size count for direct resource augmentation is plausible and the complexity-bound kind fits, but exponential lower growth requires a sourced construction establishing simultaneous reachability and nondominance of the resource states.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree-Wide Column Proliferation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case storage growth when branch-and-price nodes require distinct columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a complete binary branch-and-price tree of depth \(d\). Suppose every node \(v\) requires at least \(m\) columns to certify its restricted-master bound, and branching makes the required sets \(C_v\) pairwise disjoint. Then the tree-wide pool satisfies \[\left|\bigcup_v C_v\right|=\sum_v|C_v|\ge m(2^{d+1}-1).\] Thus retaining every generated column requires exponential storage in \(d\), even when each node uses only \(m\) columns. The mechanism disappears if columns can be shared, discarded safely, or regenerated without material cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Disjoint node-specific column sets can make total branch-and-price storage exponential in tree depth despite bounded per-node restricted masters.
assumptions_latex: \(d\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) and the search tree is complete through depth \(d\).
\(|C_v|\ge m\) for every node \(v\).
\(C_u\cap C_v=\varnothing\) whenever \(u\ne v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\left|\bigcup_v C_v\right|\ge m(2^{d+1}-1)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counting argument is mathematically correct and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but no source supports the branch-and-price interpretation or the asserted node-specific disjoint-column scenario.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Relaxation and Lagrangian Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality-constrained linear-objective minimization over a retained structured constraint set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(z^*=\min\{cx:\mathcal A x=b,\ x\in X\}\), relaxing \(\mathcal A x=b\) with multipliers \(\mu\) gives the Lagrangian subproblem \(\min\{cx+\mu(\mathcal A x-b):x\in X\}\) and the value function \(L(\mu)=\min_{x\in X}\{cx+\mu(\mathcal A x-b)\}\). A Lagrangian-subproblem optimizer need not satisfy \(\mathcal A x=b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a problem minimizing cx over x in X subject to Ax=b, moving the equalities into the objective with multipliers produces the Lagrangian subproblem. Its value is L(μ), and its optimizer need not be feasible for the original problem.

knowledge_statements.title: Linking-Constraint Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian relaxation of equalities coupling otherwise independent variable blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimization problem \[p^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ \sum_{k=1}^K A_kx_k=b\right\},\] relaxing the linking equality with \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}^m\) gives \[L(x,\lambda)=\sum_{k=1}^K\bigl(f_k(x_k)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_kx_k\bigr)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b.\] Its dual function is \[q(\lambda)=-\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x_k\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x_k)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_kx_k\bigr).\] Hence the relaxed evaluation separates by blocks, and \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\) for every \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing a coupling equality yields independent block minimizations and a valid lower bound for the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X_k\ne\varnothing\) for \(k=1,\ldots,K\).
The original problem is a minimization problem with equality linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)= -\lambda^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_k q_k(\lambda)\le p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Capacity-Constraint Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative-multiplier relaxation of shared resource-capacity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) encode all constraints retained explicitly and consider \[p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax\le b\}.\] Capacity-constraint relaxation assigns \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) to \(Ax-b\le0\) and defines \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\bigr).\] For every feasible \(x\), nonnegativity gives \(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)\le f(x)\); consequently \(q(\lambda)\le p^*\). The strongest bound in this family is \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing capacity violations with nonnegative multipliers removes the capacity inequalities and produces Lagrangian lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Side-Constraint Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relaxation of complicating inequalities outside a tractable core set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X_0\) be a tractable core set and consider \[p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X_0,\ g_j(x)\le0\ \text{for }j=1,\ldots,r\}.\] Relaxing the side constraints with \(\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^r\) yields \[q(\mu)=\inf_{x\in X_0}\left(f(x)+\sum_{j=1}^r\mu_jg_j(x)\right).\] Every primal-feasible point has a nonpositive penalty term, so \(q(\mu)\le p^*\). Side-constraint relaxation is useful precisely when evaluation of this infimum preserves the tractable structure of \(X_0\).

Each relaxed side constraint has the form \(g_j(x)\le0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Constraint-Family Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous Lagrangian relaxation of capacity and side-constraint inequality families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) encode the retained constraints and consider \[p^*=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ Ax-b\le 0,\ g(x)\le 0\},\] where \(Ax-b\le0\) is a capacity family and \(g(x)\le0\) is a side-constraint family. For multipliers \(\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\) and \(\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^r\), define \[q(\lambda,\mu)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl(f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)+\mu^{\mathsf T}g(x)\bigr).\] At every primal-feasible point both multiplier terms are nonpositive, so \(q(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\). Consequently, the joint Lagrangian bound satisfies \[\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,\,\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^r}q(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capacity and side-constraint inequalities can be relaxed together with separate nonnegative multiplier vectors, producing a joint Lagrangian lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\).
The relaxed capacity constraints are \(Ax-b\le0\), and the relaxed side constraints are \(g(x)\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}_+^m,\,\mu\in\mathbb{R}_+^r}q(\lambda,\mu)\le p^*\).

notation.meaning: nonnegative capacity and side-constraint multiplier vectors

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Lagrangian Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive decomposition of a Lagrangian over independent feasible blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\lambda\), let \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_K\) with every \(X_k\ne\varnothing\), and suppose \[L(x,\lambda)=c(\lambda)+\sum_{k=1}^K L_k(x_k,\lambda),\] where \(c(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}\) and each \(L_k(\cdot,\lambda)\) is real-valued on \(X_k\). Then \[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda)=c(\lambda)+\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x_k\in X_k}L_k(x_k,\lambda),\] where the common value may be \(-\infty\). Thus the block infima can be computed independently. If every block infimum is attained, concatenating corresponding block minimizers gives a global minimizer of \(L(\cdot,\lambda)\) over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a product feasible set and a finite sum of real-valued block terms, Lagrangian dual evaluation equals the sum of independently computed block infima; attained block minima concatenate to a global minimum.
assumptions_latex: \(K\in\mathbb{Z}_{+}\) and \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_K\) with every \(X_k\ne\varnothing\).
\(c(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}\), and each \(L_k(\cdot,\lambda)\) is real-valued on \(X_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q(\lambda)=c(\lambda)+\sum_{k=1}^K\inf_{x_k\in X_k}L_k(x_k,\lambda)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Copying-Constraint Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent block-variable reformulation using local copies and consensus equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \[p^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x):x\in\bigcap_{k=1}^K X_k\right\},\] introduce local copies \(x_k\) and a consensus variable \(z\). The copying reformulation is \[p^*=\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ x_k=z\ \text{for }k=1,\ldots,K\right\}.\] Projection of any copied feasible point onto \(z\) is feasible for the original problem, while every original feasible \(x\) lifts by setting \(x_k=z=x\). Thus the reformulation preserves feasible solutions and objective values while isolating block constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local variable copies plus consensus equalities reproduce the original feasible set while separating block-specific constraints and objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Consensus-Multiplier Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected dual subgradient coordination for copied consensus equalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given copied blocks \(x_k\in X_k\), choose \(\lambda^0=(\lambda_1^0,\ldots,\lambda_K^0)\) with \(\sum_k\lambda_k^0=0\), positive steps \(\alpha_t\), and a stopping rule. At iteration \(t\), solve in parallel \[x_k^t\in\arg\min_{x_k\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x_k)+(\lambda_k^t)^{\mathsf T}x_k\bigr),\] set \(z^t=K^{-1}\sum_kx_k^t\), and update \[\lambda_k^{t+1}=\lambda_k^t+\alpha_t(x_k^t-z^t).\] The update preserves \(\sum_k\lambda_k^{t+1}=0\). Stop when the prescribed iteration or residual criterion holds; output the best computed dual value and, when available, a consensus-feasible primal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blocks optimize at current prices, their solutions are averaged, and multipliers ascend along disagreement while remaining sum-zero.
assumptions_latex: Every displayed block minimum is attained.
\(\alpha_t>0\), and all copied variables share a finite-dimensional ambient space.
The stopping rule is specified before execution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_k\lambda_k^t=0\) for all \(t\), and the algorithm returns the best recorded dual bound.

notation.meaning: consensus multiplier of block k at iteration t

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Dual Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consensus dual expressed as a sum of independent block value functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Dualize the copying equalities \(x_k=z\) in \[\inf\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K f_k(x_k):x_k\in X_k,\ x_k=z\right\}.\] Minimization of \(\sum_k[f_k(x_k)+\lambda_k^{\mathsf T}(x_k-z)]\) over unrestricted \(z\) is finite exactly when \(\sum_k\lambda_k=0\). On that subspace, \[q(\lambda)=\sum_{k=1}^K q_k(\lambda_k),\qquad q_k(\lambda_k)=\inf_{x_k\in X_k}\bigl(f_k(x_k)+\lambda_k^{\mathsf T}x_k\bigr).\] Therefore the Lagrangian dual is \[\sup\left\{\sum_kq_k(\lambda_k):\sum_k\lambda_k=0\right\},\] and every feasible multiplier tuple supplies a lower bound on the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualizing copied consensus equalities produces independent block value functions coordinated solely by the condition that their multipliers sum to zero.
assumptions_latex: All copied variables and \(z\) share a finite-dimensional real vector space.
The primal problem is a minimization problem and each \(X_k\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\sum_k\lambda_k=0}\sum_kq_k(\lambda_k)\le p^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Choosing a Lagrangian Relaxation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Design criterion for a minimization MIP with separable easy constraints and complicating coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v=\inf\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le 0,\ h(x)=0\}\). A valid Lagrangian design chooses a subset of constraints to dualize and defines \(L(x,\lambda,\mu)=f(x)+\lambda^{\mathsf T}g(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}h(x)\), with \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\mu\) unrestricted. The retained set \(X\) should make \(\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\mu)\) computationally tractable, preferably separable, while the dualized family should preserve a strong bound. Every such multiplier pair gives a valid lower bound; different choices trade subproblem tractability against dual-bound strength.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dualize coupling constraints whose removal creates tractable subproblems, while retaining enough structure for a strong bound and enforcing multiplier signs required by weak duality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\ne\varnothing\), and every original feasible point belongs to \(X\).
\(g(x)\le0\) and \(h(x)=0\) are the selected relaxed constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}L(x,\lambda,\mu)\le v\) for every \(\lambda\ge0\) and unrestricted \(\mu\).

notation.meaning: Set defined by constraints retained explicitly in each subproblem.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian dual lower bound for side-constrained integer network flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-duality bound obtained by relaxing linear side constraints of an integer network-flow problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\min\{a^\top x:x\in\widetilde F,\ c_t^\top x\le d_t,\ t=1,\ldots,r\}\), where \(\widetilde F\) enforces flow conservation and the arc-flow domains. Define \(L(x,\mu)=a^\top x+\sum_{t=1}^r\mu_t(c_t^\top x-d_t)\) and \(q(\mu)=\min_{x\in\widetilde F}L(x,\mu)\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimizing the Lagrangian after assigning nonnegative multipliers to the relaxed side constraints gives a lower bound on the original minimum. Taking the supremum over those multipliers gives the best bound in this Lagrangian family.

c_t^\top x\le d_t,\quad t=1,\ldots,r
\mu\in\mathbb R_+^r
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: q(\mu)\le p^*\quad\forall\mu\ge0,\qquad \sup_{\mu\ge0}q(\mu)\text{ is the best bound in this Lagrangian family}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Bounds and Monotonicity of the Objective-Restricted Lagrangian Dual
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Properties of the optimal Lagrangian dual value after restricting objective values to \([l,u]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda^*(l,u)\) be an optimal solution of \(D(l,u)\). Then: (i) \(d(\lambda^*(l,u),l,u)\) is nondecreasing in \(l\). (ii) If \(l\le f^*\le u\), then \(d(\lambda^*)\le d(\lambda^*(l,u),l,u)\le f^*\). Let \(\sigma=\max\{f(x):f(x)<f^*,\ x\in X\setminus S\}\). If \(\sigma<l\le f^*\), then \(\lambda^*(l,u)=0\) and \(d(\lambda^*(l,u),l,u)=f^*\). (iii) If \(l<f^*\), then \(d(\lambda^*(l,u),l,u)\ge l\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal objective-restricted Lagrangian dual value is nondecreasing in the lower objective level. When the interval contains the primal optimum, the restricted dual value lies between the unrestricted dual value and the optimum. If the lower level exceeds every smaller objective value attained by an infeasible point, the zero multiplier is optimal and the restricted dual value equals the primal optimum. Below the optimum, the restricted dual value is at least the lower level.
assumptions_latex: \lambda^*(l,u)\text{ is an optimal solution of }D(l,u)
l\le f^*\le u\text{ in part (ii)}
\sigma=\max\{f(x):f(x)<f^*,\ x\in X\setminus S\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian Relaxation, Dual Function, and Lower Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Lagrangian relaxation and dual function for a general inequality-constrained minimization problem and states their lower-bound consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^\star=\inf\{f(x):g(x)\le 0,\ x\in G\}\), where \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) and \(g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) are continuous and \(G\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is arbitrary. For \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m\), define \(L(x;\mu)=f(x)+\mu^Tg(x)\) and \(D(\mu)=\inf_{x\in G}L(x;\mu)\). Then \(D(\mu)\le p^\star\) for every \(\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m\). Hence \(d^\star:=\sup_{\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m}D(\mu)\) is the sharpest bound obtainable from this dual function and satisfies \(d^\star\le p^\star\). For every primal-feasible \(x\), \(f(x)-p^\star\le f(x)-D(\mu)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian relaxation minimizes the Lagrangian over the residual set G. Each nonnegative multiplier gives a dual-function value no larger than the primal optimum; maximizing these values gives the sharpest Lagrangian lower bound. Comparing such a bound with a feasible objective value gives an upper bound on that solution's suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\text{ and }g:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\text{ are continuous}
G\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is arbitrary}
\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m
x\in G\text{ and }g(x)\le0\text{ for the feasible-solution estimate}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: D(\mu)\le p^\star,\qquad d^\star:=\sup_{\mu\in\mathbb R_+^m}D(\mu)\le p^\star,\qquad f(x)-p^\star\le f(x)-D(\mu).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Domain
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplier cone determined by constraint senses in a minimization Lagrangian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem whose relaxed constraints are \(g^-(x)\le0\), \(g^+(x)\ge0\), and \(h(x)=0\), define \(L(x,\lambda^-,\lambda^+,\mu)=f(x)+(\lambda^-)^{\mathsf T}g^-(x)+(\lambda^+)^{\mathsf T}g^+(x)+\mu^{\mathsf T}h(x)\). The weak-duality multiplier domain is \(\mathcal D=\mathbb R_+^{m_-}\times\mathbb R_-^{m_+}\times\mathbb R^p\). Thus multipliers of equalities are free, while each inequality multiplier has the sign making its Lagrangian contribution nonpositive at every feasible point.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Orientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orientation of Lagrangian bounds and dual optimization for minimization and maximization problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be the primal-feasible and retained domains. For minimization, let \(v_{\min}=\inf_{x\in F}f(x)\), and suppose \(L_{\min}(x,y)\le f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(y\in\mathcal D_{\min}\). Defining \(\theta_{\min}(y)=\inf_{x\in X}L_{\min}(x,y)\) and \(d_{\min}=\sup_{y\in\mathcal D_{\min}}\theta_{\min}(y)\) gives \(d_{\min}\le v_{\min}\). For maximization, let \(v_{\max}=\sup_{x\in F}f(x)\), and suppose \(L_{\max}(x,y)\ge f(x)\) for every \(x\in F\) and \(y\in\mathcal D_{\max}\). Defining \(\theta_{\max}(y)=\sup_{x\in X}L_{\max}(x,y)\) and \(d_{\max}=\inf_{y\in\mathcal D_{\max}}\theta_{\max}(y)\) gives \(d_{\max}\ge v_{\max}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization Lagrangian supplies lower bounds that the dual maximizes, whereas a maximization Lagrangian supplies upper bounds that the dual minimizes.
assumptions_latex: \(F\subseteq X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\).
The multiplier domains and residual signs ensure \(L_{\min}(x,y)\le f(x)\) in the minimization case and \(L_{\max}(x,y)\ge f(x)\) in the maximization case for every primal-feasible \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_{\min}\le v_{\min}\) and \(d_{\max}\ge v_{\max}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Sign-Convention Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility rule linking inequality residual orientation to multiplier signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In a minimization problem, a relaxed scalar inequality written as \(r(x)\le0\) must enter \(L(x,\lambda)=f(x)+\lambda r(x)\) with \(\lambda\ge0\); if the same constraint is written as \(-r(x)\ge0\), its multiplier must be nonpositive. Reversing the residual and the multiplier sign together leaves the Lagrangian unchanged. Reversing only one generally destroys the pointwise inequality \(L(x,\lambda)\le f(x)\) on feasible points and therefore invalidates the claimed lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Changing an inequality’s orientation requires changing its multiplier sign; otherwise the weak-duality bound may become invalid.
assumptions_latex: The primal objective is minimized.
The Lagrangian uses additive multiplier terms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda r(x)\le0\) for every feasible \(x\) is the compatibility predicate ensuring the relaxed term preserves a lower bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound Dominance Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison of Lagrangian and LP lower bounds under compatible retained domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(v=\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in X,\ Ax\ge b\}\), with \(X\subseteq P\), where \(P\) is the continuous relaxation of \(X\). Let \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}\) dualize \(Ax\ge b\), and let \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in P,\ Ax\ge b\}\). If the Lagrangian dual is exact for the convexified retained set, so that \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X),\ Ax\ge b\}\), then \(z_{\mathrm{LD}}\ge z_{\mathrm{LP}}\). Equality holds when the LP optimum lies in that convexified set; strict dominance can occur otherwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian bound dominates the LP bound when it optimizes over a tighter convexification of the retained mixed-integer set; equality occurs if that tightening is inactive.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq P\).
Strong duality holds for the convexified relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{LP}}\le z_{\mathrm{LD}}\le v\).

notation.meaning: Closed convex hull of the retained mixed-integer set.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexification Effects on Bound Strength
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotonic effect of tightening the convexified retained set in a minimization relaxation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C_1\subseteq C_2\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be closed convex relaxations containing the retained mixed-integer set \(X\), and define \(z(C)=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:x\in C,\ Ax\ge b\}\). Then \(z(C_1)\ge z(C_2)\): a tighter convexification cannot weaken a minimization lower bound. Moreover, replacing \(X\) by \(\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X)\) does not change any linear Lagrangian subproblem infimum, because a linear function has the same infimum over a set and its closed convex hull.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tighter convex hull descriptions yield at least as strong minimization bounds, while linear Lagrangian subproblem values are unchanged by exact convexification.
assumptions_latex: The displayed infima are well-defined in the extended real line.
The Lagrangian subproblem objective is linear in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C_1\subseteq C_2\Rightarrow z(C_1)\ge z(C_2)\), and \(\inf_{x\in X}q^{\mathsf T}x=\inf_{x\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X)}q^{\mathsf T}x\).

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Duality Gap
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute gap between a minimization primal optimum and its best Lagrangian lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem with finite primal optimal value \(v\) and finite Lagrangian dual value \(d=\sup_{y\in\mathcal D}\theta(y)\), the Lagrangian duality gap is \(\Delta_{\mathrm L}=v-d\). Weak duality gives \(\Delta_{\mathrm L}\ge0\). The relaxation has zero Lagrangian duality gap exactly when \(d=v\); a positive gap measures the residual loss from the chosen relaxation and its associated convexification, independently of whether the supremum defining \(d\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian duality gap is the primal optimum minus the best Lagrangian lower bound; it is nonnegative and vanishes under strong duality.
assumptions_latex: \(v\in\mathbb R\) and \(d\in\mathbb R\).
The multiplier domain is weak-duality compatible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\Delta_{\mathrm L}=v-d\ge0\), with \(\Delta_{\mathrm L}=0\iff d=v\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected subgradient multipliers for capacitated multicommodity flow
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Network-flow specialization of Lagrangian subgradient search obtained by relaxing shared arc-capacity constraints while retaining separate commodity flow-conservation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For multipliers $w_{ij}\ge 0$ associated with the shared constraints $\sum_{k=1}^K x_{ij}^k\le u_{ij}$, the Lagrangian subproblem is
\[
L(w)=\min_{\mathcal N x^k=b^k,\,x^k\ge0}\left\{\sum_{k=1}^K\sum_{(i,j)\in A}(c_{ij}^k+w_{ij})x_{ij}^k-\sum_{(i,j)\in A}w_{ij}u_{ij}\right\}.
\]
For fixed $w$, the variable-dependent objective and retained constraints separate by commodity, giving one minimum-cost-flow subproblem per commodity. If $y^k$ is an optimal subproblem solution at iteration $q$, the multiplier update is
\[
w_{ij}^{q+1}=\left[w_{ij}^q+\theta_q\left(\sum_{k=1}^K y_{ij}^k-u_{ij}\right)\right]^+,
\qquad [\alpha]^+=\max\{\alpha,0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing each shared arc-capacity constraint adds its nonnegative multiplier to that arc's cost for every commodity and contributes a constant negative capacity term. With only commodity-specific flow constraints remaining, the fixed-multiplier problem decomposes into independent minimum-cost-flow problems. The multipliers are updated by a projected subgradient step using aggregate arc-capacity violations.
assumptions_latex: K\in\mathbb N
\sum_{k=1}^K x_{ij}^k\le u_{ij}\quad\forall(i,j)\in A
w_{ij}\ge0\quad\forall(i,j)\in A
\mathcal N x^k=b^k,\quad x_{ij}^k\ge0\quad\forall k,\,(i,j)\in A
\theta_q\text{ is a subgradient step size}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L(w)\text{ decomposes into }K\text{ minimum-cost-flow subproblems, and }w_{ij}^{q+1}=\left[w_{ij}^q+\theta_q\left(\sum_{k=1}^K y_{ij}^k-u_{ij}\right)\right]^+.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(\lambda^0\in\mathbb{R}^m\), repeat for \(k=0,1,\ldots\): evaluate \(q(\lambda^k)\), obtain a dual supergradient \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), and set
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k.
\]
Stop when \(g^k=0\), a prescribed dual-value or iteration criterion is met, or an external termination rule fires; return the best dual value \(\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\) and an associated multiplier. No projection is required because the multiplier domain is \(\mathbb{R}^m\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), obtain \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), choose \(\alpha_k>0\), and update

\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k),\qquad P_\Lambda(z)=\mathop{\arg\min}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\|\lambda-z\|_2.

children.title: Projection Effects on Multiplier Search
children.top_down_role: Structural effects of projection on search trajectories, feasibility, stagnation.

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Effects on Multiplier Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Euclidean projection effects in constrained multiplier ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(z^k=\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k\) and \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(z^k)\). Euclidean projection satisfies
\[
\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda\|_2\le \|z^k-\lambda\|_2\qquad\text{for every }\lambda\in\Lambda.
\]
Consequently, for any \(\lambda^\star\in\mathop{\arg\max}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\),
\[
\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^\star\|_2^2\le \|\lambda^k-\lambda^\star\|_2^2+2\alpha_k\langle g^k,\lambda^k-\lambda^\star\rangle+\alpha_k^2\|g^k\|_2^2.
\]
Thus projection preserves feasibility and cannot increase the trial point's distance to any feasible comparison multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projection preserves multiplier feasibility and never increases distance to a feasible comparison point, including any dual optimum.
assumptions_latex: The set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, and \(P_\Lambda\) denotes Euclidean projection onto \(\Lambda\).
The function \(q:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave, \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\), \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), and \(\alpha_k>0\).
A dual maximizer \(\lambda^\star\in\mathop{\arg\max}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection cannot increase the distance from the trial point to any feasible multiplier and yields the stated distance recursion.

children.title: Deflected Subgradient Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Direction modification strategies for reducing erratic multiplier movement.

assumptions_latex: The concave dual function \(q\) admits supergradients \(g^k\), and the multiplier set \(\Lambda\) is closed and convex.
Parameters satisfy \(\alpha_k>0\) and \(0\le\beta_k<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The search direction combines the current supergradient with directional memory before the multiplier update.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex-combination deflection with one-step directional memory.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\), obtain \(g^0\in\partial q(\lambda^0)\), and set \(d^0=g^0\). For \(k\ge1\), obtain \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), form
\[
d^k=(1-\beta_k)g^k+\beta_k d^{k-1},
\]
and update \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k d^k)\). Stop under a prescribed dual-improvement, direction-norm, or iteration criterion; return the best dual value and corresponding multiplier. The choice \(\beta_k=0\) recovers projected subgradient search, while positive \(\beta_k\) introduces directional memory.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend the current dual supergradient with the previous direction, then take a projected multiplier step and retain the best dual iterate.

children.title: Volume Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Stabilized dual search with aggregate primal information.

assumptions_latex: At iteration \(k\), a Lagrangian oracle returns a dual value, a supergradient \(g^k\), and an associated primal relaxation solution \(x^k\).
A feasible multiplier set \(\Lambda\), positive steps \(\alpha_k\), and averaging weights \(\gamma_k\in(0,1]\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method jointly updates dual multipliers and a primal aggregate, using directional memory to stabilize dual search and primal estimates.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic volume-method template; exact published variant remains source-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\), set \(\bar x^0=x^0\), and choose \(d^0=g^0\). At iteration \(k\), construct a stabilized direction \(d^k\) from \(g^k\) and previous directional information, then set
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k d^k),\qquad
\bar x^{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)\bar x^k+\gamma_k x^k.
\]
Update the step, deflection, and averaging parameters using the selected volume-algorithm acceptance rule. Stop under its prescribed dual-progress or iteration test, and return the best dual multiplier together with the aggregate \(\bar x^k\) as the primal estimate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A volume method couples stabilized dual multiplier steps with weighted averaging of primal relaxation solutions.

children.title: Directional Stabilization Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Contrasts among deflection, aggregation, trajectory smoothing.

assumptions_latex: The current dual supergradient is \(g^k\), the preceding search direction is \(d^{k-1}\), and \(0\le\beta_k<1\).
The compared methods use the same multiplier, projection set, and positive step size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deflection changes direction and may reduce oscillation, whereas primal averaging additionally stabilizes recovered primal estimates without itself changing multiplier feasibility.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural comparison rather than a universal dominance claim.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Classical search uses \(d_{\mathrm{sg}}^k=g^k\), while one-step deflection uses
\[
d_{\mathrm{def}}^k=(1-\beta_k)g^k+\beta_k d^{k-1}.
\]
Thus \(d_{\mathrm{def}}^k-d_{\mathrm{sg}}^k=\beta_k(d^{k-1}-g^k)\), so stabilization disappears exactly when \(\beta_k=0\) or \(d^{k-1}=g^k\). A volume method supplements a deflected direction \(d_{\mathrm{vol}}^k\) with a primal average such as \(\bar x^{k+1}=(1-\gamma_k)\bar x^k+\gamma_k x^k\). These identities distinguish directional memory from primal averaging; they do not imply uniform iteration-wise dominance among the methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Classical search uses the current supergradient; deflection adds directional memory; volume methods also average primal solutions. None uniformly dominates from these identities alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Directional Stabilization Comparisons

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The structural comparison is plausible, but its volume-method component depends on an unspecified variant and has no direct comparative source.

knowledge_statements.title: Diminishing Step-Size Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard diminishing, nonsummable, square-summable step regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A positive step sequence is in the classical diminishing regime when
\[
\alpha_k>0,\qquad \alpha_k\to0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty.
\]
For projected supergradient ascent on a concave dual function over a nonempty closed convex set, with uniformly bounded supergradients and an attained maximum, these conditions imply convergence of the best dual values to the optimal dual value. A canonical family is \(\alpha_k=a/(k+1)^p\) with \(a>0\) and \(1/2<p\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Steps vanish slowly enough to keep moving while their squares remain summable; under the stated assumptions, the best dual values converge to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: The function \(q:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave and is maximized over a nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\).
The iterates satisfy \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\), where \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\).
There is a constant \(G<\infty\) such that \(\|g^k\|_2\le G\) for every \(k\), and the maximum of \(q\) over \(\Lambda\) is attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The step sequence is diminishing and nonsummable, while its squared terms are summable; under the stated assumptions, the best dual values converge to the optimal dual value.

notation.meaning: positive multiplier step size at iteration k

At iteration \(k\), \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\) is nonzero and \(0<\theta_k<2\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\). If \(g^k\ne0\), choose
\[
\alpha_k=\theta_k\frac{q^\star-q(\lambda^k)}{\|g^k\|_2^2},
\qquad
\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k).
\]
If \(q(\lambda^k)=q^\star\) or \(g^k=0\), stop and return \(\lambda^k\); otherwise continue and retain the best dual iterate. For every dual maximizer \(\lambda^\star\), the update satisfies
\[
\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^\star\|_2^2\le\|\lambda^k-\lambda^\star\|_2^2-\theta_k(2-\theta_k)\frac{(q^\star-q(\lambda^k))^2}{\|g^k\|_2^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scale each projected supergradient step by the exact dual optimality gap; parameters between zero and two produce a distance decrease.

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Value Step Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected target-value steps with an exogenous or method-specific target policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), let the selected target policy provide \(T_k>q(\lambda^k)\). If \(g^k\ne0\), choose \(\theta_k>0\) and set
\[
\alpha_k=\theta_k\frac{T_k-q(\lambda^k)}{\|g^k\|_2^2},
\qquad
\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k).
\]
Update \(T_k\) only according to the selected target policy, stop under its prescribed tolerance or iteration limit, and return the best dual iterate. If the exact optimal value \(q^\star\) is known and \(T_k=q^\star\), this update becomes the exact Polyak step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use the positive gap between a selected target and the current dual value to scale each projected supergradient step; the rule for updating the target belongs to the selected policy.
assumptions_latex: The function \(q:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is concave and is maximized over a nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\).
At iteration \(k\), \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\), \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\) is nonzero, \(T_k>q(\lambda^k)\), and \(\theta_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The positive target gap determines the step length; if the target equals the exact optimal value, the update is the exact Polyak step.

children.title: Target Misspecification Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search behavior under optimistic, stale, poorly calibrated targets.

assumptions_latex: Consider the unconstrained concave maximization problem \(\max_{\lambda\in\mathbb{R}}q(\lambda)\) with \(q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure from a target below the true dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q(\lambda)=-|\lambda|\), whose unique maximizer is \(\lambda^\star=0\) with \(q^\star=0\). Fix \(T<0\), take \(0<\lambda^0<-T\), and select \(g^0=-1\). Then
\[
\alpha_0=T-q(\lambda^0)=T+\lambda^0<0,
\qquad
\lambda^1=\lambda^0+lpha_0g^0=-T.
\]
At \(\lambda^1=-T>0\), one has \(q(\lambda^1)=T\), so \(\alpha_1=0\) and all subsequent iterates remain at \(-T\ne0\). Hence allowing a target below \(q^\star\) invalidates the positive-gap mechanism and can cause suboptimal stagnation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a simple absolute-value dual function, a target below the optimum creates a negative step and then stalls at a suboptimal point.

children.title: Level Step Regimes
children.top_down_role: Step control organized around maintained objective levels.

assumptions_latex: The concave dual function \(q\) is maximized over a nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\), and bounded supergradients are available.
A phase maintains a level \(L_s\) strictly above the current best dual value and a positive path-length budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The phase level converts the current level gap into step sizes and is revised when either sufficient ascent or excessive travel occurs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Phase-based level control for dual supergradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\), a phase \(s=0\), a best value \(q_{\mathrm{best}}=q(\lambda^0)\), a level \(L_s>q_{\mathrm{best}}\), and a budget \(B_s>0\). Within phase \(s\), set
\[
\alpha_k=\theta\frac{L_s-q(\lambda^k)}{\|g^k\|_2^2},
\qquad
\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k),
\]
for a prescribed \(\theta>0\). Update \(q_{\mathrm{best}}\). End the phase when the level-progress test succeeds or accumulated travel \(\sum\|\lambda^{j+1}-\lambda^j\|_2\) reaches \(B_s\); revise \(L_s\) and restart. Return the best multiplier at termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hold a target level during each phase, scale steps by its gap, and revise the level after progress or excessive multiplier travel.

children.top_down_role: Step adjustment based on observed search behavior.

assumptions_latex: Projected dual supergradient iterates and their dual values are observable.
The controller specifies positive step bounds \(0<\alpha_{\min}\le\alpha_{\max}\), progress thresholds, and multiplicative factors \(0<\rho_-<1<\rho_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The controller adjusts the step within fixed safeguards according to observed dual progress.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safeguarded feedback control based on observed dual progress.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Initialize \(\lambda^0\in\Lambda\) and \(\alpha_0\in[\alpha_{\min},\alpha_{\max}]\). Compute
\[
\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k).
\]
After evaluating \(q(\lambda^{k+1})\), set \(\alpha_{k+1}=\min\{\alpha_{\max},\rho_+\alpha_k\}\) when the prescribed sufficient-progress test holds, set \(\alpha_{k+1}=\max\{\alpha_{\min},\rho_-\alpha_k\}\) after the prescribed number of unsuccessful iterations, and otherwise retain \(\alpha_{k+1}=\alpha_k\). Stop under a dual-gap, stationarity, or iteration criterion and return the best dual iterate. The progress test and thresholds are part of the selected adaptive regime.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q\) be a concave dual function on a nonempty closed convex set \(\Lambda\), and consider \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\), where \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), \(\alpha_k>0\), and \(\|g^k\|\le G\). Then \(\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|\le \alpha_kG\). If the computed supergradient is changed from \(g^k\) to \(g^k+e^k\) while the current multiplier is fixed, nonexpansiveness of projection bounds the resulting one-step multiplier perturbation by \(\alpha_k\|e^k\|\). Thus larger steps permit greater immediate motion but also greater one-step sensitivity to oracle error. The conditions \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\) balance persistent motion with diminishing exact-oracle steps, but they do not by themselves suppress arbitrary persistent bounded oracle errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Large multiplier steps permit faster immediate movement but increase one-step sensitivity to oracle errors. Nonsummable, square-summable diminishing steps balance persistent motion with shrinking exact-oracle steps, without alone guaranteeing robustness to persistent errors.
knowledge_statements.title: Step Responsiveness versus Stability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer approximation, value bracketing, well-posedness condition, and stopping certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given evaluated multipliers \(\mu^i\) and concave subgradients \(g^i\), define \(Q^k(\mu)=\min_{0\le i<k}\{q(\mu^i)+(\mu-\mu^i)^\top g^i\}\) and choose \(\mu^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\ge0}Q^k(\mu)\). The evaluated dual value bounds the dual optimum from below, while the master value bounds it from above; equality certifies optimality. Initialization or a bounded multiplier region must make the master problem well posed.
assumptions_latex: g^i\text{ satisfies }q(\mu)\le q(\mu^i)+(\mu-\mu^i)^\top g^i\quad\forall\mu\ge0
\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mu\ge0}Q^k(\mu)\ne\varnothing\text{, or the master domain is a bounded polyhedron containing a dual optimum}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a compact convex multiplier set \(\Lambda\), let \(q^*=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\) and choose \(\lambda^1\in\Lambda\). At iteration \(k\), solve the Lagrangian subproblem to obtain \(q(\lambda^k)\) and a supergradient \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\). Form the outer model \(m_k(\lambda)=\min_{1\le i\le k}\{q(\lambda^i)+(g^i)^\top(\lambda-\lambda^i)\}\), which satisfies \(q(\lambda)\le m_k(\lambda)\). Compute \((\lambda^{k+1},U_k)\) by maximizing \(\theta\) subject to \(\lambda\in\Lambda\) and \(\theta\le q(\lambda^i)+(g^i)^\top(\lambda-\lambda^i)\) for every \(i\le k\). Stop when \(U_k-\bar q_k\le\varepsilon\), where \(\bar q_k=\max_{i\le k}q(\lambda^i)\), and return the best evaluated multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Successive Lagrangian supergradient cuts form an outer dual model; a master problem chooses the next multiplier until its upper bound meets the best evaluated dual value within tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Outer Lagrangian Linearization

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A localization system at iteration \(k\) is a nonempty closed convex set \(L_k\subseteq\Lambda\) that restricts the next master trial multiplier. Typical instances are a trust region \(L_k=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:\|\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\|\le R_k\}\), a box around the center, or the level region \(L_k=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:m_k(\lambda)\ge\ell_k\}\). The localized master has value \(\sup_{\lambda\in L_k}m_k(\lambda)\); when this supremum is attained, a maximizing point can be used as the next trial. This value bounds the dual supremum over \(L_k\), and it is a valid global upper bound when \(L_k\) contains a global dual maximizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A localization system restricts the cutting-plane master to a closed convex region near a center or above a model level. A maximizing trial exists when the localized model supremum is attained.

knowledge_statements.title: Master Localization Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Couples model maximization with adaptive restriction and release of the multiplier region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m_k\) be the current outer model, \(\bar\lambda^k\) the stability center, and \(L_k=L(\bar\lambda^k,s_k)\) a localization set controlled by size parameter \(s_k\). The trial multiplier satisfies \(\lambda^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in L_k}m_k(\lambda)\). After evaluating \(q(\lambda^{k+1})\), accept the trial as the new center when its actual improvement is at least a fixed fraction of its predicted model improvement; otherwise retain \(\bar\lambda^k\). The localization parameter is enlarged after boundary-limited productive trials and reduced or retained after unstable or unproductive trials. Consequently, master predictions determine localization updates, while localization controls the region in which those predictions generate trials.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The master chooses a trial inside the current region; agreement between predicted and actual gain determines center movement and localization resizing.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a center \(\bar\lambda^1\in\Lambda\), proximal parameters \(t_k>0\), an acceptance parameter \(\eta\in(0,1)\), a tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), and an exact dual oracle. From stored pairs \((\lambda^i,q_i,g^i)\), where \(q_i=q(\lambda^i)\) and \(g^i\in\partial q(\lambda^i)\), form \(m_k(\lambda)=\min_{i\le k}\{q_i+(g^i)^\top(\lambda-\lambda^i)\}\). Compute \[y^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\left\{m_k(\lambda)-\frac{1}{2t_k}\|\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\|^2\right\}.\] Define the bundle model gap \(\delta_k=m_k(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)\). If \(\delta_k\le\varepsilon\), stop. Otherwise evaluate \(q(y^k)\) and a supergradient there. If \(q(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)\ge\eta\delta_k\), set \(\bar\lambda^{k+1}=y^k\); otherwise set \(\bar\lambda^{k+1}=\bar\lambda^k\). Add the new oracle pair and update \(t_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal bundle method maximizes a cutting-plane model penalized by distance from an accepted center, stops when its declared model gap meets tolerance, and moves the center only after sufficient actual improvement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Bundle Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded serious-step/null-step proximal bundle procedure for maximizing the dual function over \(\mathbb{R}_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(u^1>0\), \(\kappa\in(0,1)\), and \(\mu^1\in\mathbb{R}_+^m\); set \(\lambda^1=\mu^1\), compute \(D(\mu^1)\), and obtain a supergradient \(g^1\) of \(D\) at \(\mu^1\). For \(j=1,\ldots,l\), solve (4.6) to obtain \(\lambda^{j+1}\). Stop if \(\widehat D^j(\lambda^{j+1})-D(\mu^j)<\epsilon\). If \(D(\lambda^{j+1})\ge D(\mu^j)+\kappa\bigl(\bar D^j(\lambda^{j+1})-D(\mu^j)\bigr)\), set \(\mu^{j+1}=\lambda^{j+1}\) (serious step); otherwise set \(\mu^{j+1}=\mu^j\) (null step). Then compute \(D(\mu^j)\) and a supergradient \(g^j\) of \(D\) at \(\mu^j\), choose \(J^{j+1}\subset J^j\cup\{j+1\}\), and update \(u^{j+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize the nonnegative bundle center and positive proximal parameter. At each iteration, solve the proximal subproblem and stop when the stated model-gap test holds. Otherwise accept the trial point as a serious step when it attains the required fraction of predicted improvement, or retain the center as a null step, then perform the stated value, supergradient, bundle, and proximal-parameter updates.

\mu^1\in\mathbb{R}_+^m
g^1\in\partial^+D(\mu^1)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{For each processed iteration, the stopping test terminates the procedure or the acceptance test assigns a serious or null step and the bundle and proximal parameter are updated.}

knowledge_statements.title: Level Bundle Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bundle stabilization by projection onto a model superlevel set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Maintain a center \(\bar\lambda^k\), best dual value \(L_k=q(\bar\lambda^k)\), and a valid model upper bound \(U_k>L_k\). Choose \(\beta\in(0,1)\) and set \(\ell_k=L_k+\beta(U_k-L_k)\). With outer model \(m_k\), define \(S_k=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:m_k(\lambda)\ge\ell_k\}\) and compute \[y^k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{\lambda\in S_k}\frac12\|\lambda-\bar\lambda^k\|^2.\] Evaluate \(q(y^k)\), add its supergradient cut, and update the lower bound and center when sufficient improvement occurs; otherwise retain the center and reduce the upper target using the refined model. Stop when \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A level bundle method projects the center onto a model superlevel set between current lower and upper bounds, then updates the bounds using a new oracle cut.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave on closed convex \(\Lambda\).
\(m_k\ge q\) and \(U_k\) is a valid dual upper bound.
The level set \(S_k\) is nonempty whenever projection is requested.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination certifies \(U_k-L_k\le\varepsilon\); otherwise the oracle evaluation refines the bundle and at least one bound or the center is updated.

knowledge_statements.title: Serious-Step Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Acceptance test for moving a bundle method's stability center.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At center \(\bar\lambda^k\), let \(y^k\) be the bundle trial point and define predicted improvement \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}=m_k(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)>0\) and actual improvement \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}=q(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)\). For a fixed acceptance parameter \(\eta\in(0,1)\), iteration \(k\) is a serious step precisely when \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}\ge\eta\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). The diagnostic authorizes \(\bar\lambda^{k+1}=y^k\); the new value and supergradient are retained in the bundle regardless of classification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A trial is serious when its measured dual improvement achieves a prescribed fraction of the model-predicted improvement, permitting the stability center to move.

The dual value at the center and trial is evaluated exactly.
\(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}>0\).

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Step Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejection test that preserves the center while improving the bundle model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Using \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}=m_k(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)>0\), \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}=q(y^k)-q(\bar\lambda^k)\), and \(\eta\in(0,1)\), iteration \(k\) is a null step when \(\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}<\eta\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). Then the stability center remains \(\bar\lambda^{k+1}=\bar\lambda^k\), but the oracle pair at \(y^k\) is added to the bundle. Its affine majorant is exact at \(y^k\), so the refined model removes or reduces the overprediction responsible for rejection even though the accepted multiplier does not move.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A null step occurs when actual improvement is too small; the center stays fixed, but the trial's cut refines the overoptimistic model.

children.title: Step-Classification Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Borderline acceptance behavior caused by tolerances or weak model improvement.

knowledge_statements.title: Step-Classification Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies the tolerance band where inexact evaluations cannot determine serious versus null status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose computed improvements \(\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}\) and \(\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\) satisfy \(|\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}-\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}|\le e_a\) and \(|\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}-\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}|\le e_p\). With threshold \(\eta\in(0,1)\), define \(\widehat r_k=\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{act}}-\eta\widehat\Delta_k^{\mathrm{pred}}\). If \(\widehat r_k>e_a+\eta e_p\), the step is certainly serious; if \(\widehat r_k<-(e_a+\eta e_p)\), it is certainly null. When \(|\widehat r_k|\le e_a+\eta e_p\), both classifications are consistent with the error bounds, so a deterministic classification requires tighter oracle accuracy or an explicit tie policy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Near the acceptance threshold, bounded value and model errors can support either classification; tighter evaluation or a declared tie rule is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence Regimes for Lagrangian Subgradient Iterations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three step-size regimes for the stated Lagrangian subgradient algorithm; background assumptions defining that algorithm and its dual-value function remain contextual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Z(u^k)\) denote the value generated by the Lagrangian subgradient algorithm, and let \(W_{LD}\) be the optimal value of \(LD\). (a) If \(\sum_k\mu_k\to\infty\) and \(\mu_k\to0\) as \(k\to\infty\), then \(Z(u^k)\to W_{LD}\). (b) If \(\mu_k=\mu_0\rho^k\) for some \(\rho<1\), then \(Z(u^k)\to W_{LD}\) when \(\mu_0\) and \(\rho\) are sufficiently large. (c) If \(\bar W\geq W_{LD}\) and \[\mu_k=\epsilon_k\frac{Z(u^k)-\bar W}{\lVert b-Ax(u^k)\rVert^2},\qquad 0<\epsilon_k<2,\] then either \(Z(u^k)\to\bar W\), or for some finite \(k\), \(\bar W\geq Z(u^k)\geq W_{LD}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual values converge to the Lagrangian-dual optimum under diminishing nonsummable steps and under the stated sufficiently large geometric parameters. With the stated target-value step, they either converge to the target or finitely attain a value between the dual optimum and that target.
assumptions_latex: Z(u^k)\text{ is generated by the stated Lagrangian subgradient algorithm}
W_{LD}=\operatorname{val}(LD)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\sum_k\mu_k\to\infty,\ \mu_k\to0\implies Z(u^k)\to W_{LD};\\&\mu_k=\mu_0\rho^k,\ \rho<1,\ \mu_0,\rho\text{ sufficiently large}\implies Z(u^k)\to W_{LD};\\&\bar W\geq W_{LD},\ \mu_k=\epsilon_k\frac{Z(u^k)-\bar W}{\lVert b-Ax(u^k)\rVert^2},\ 0<\epsilon_k<2\\&\qquad\implies \bigl[Z(u^k)\to\bar W\bigr]\ \lor\ \bigl[(\exists k<\infty)\ \bar W\geq Z(u^k)\geq W_{LD}\bigr].\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Value Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard diminishing-step convergence for projected dual subgradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(q^*=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\) be attained, and generate \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\) with \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\). If \(\|g^k\|\le G\), \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the best-so-far dual values \(q_k^{\mathrm{best}}=\max_{0\le i\le k}q(\lambda^i)\) converge to \(q^*\). Equivalently, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), some finite iteration has \(q^*-q_k^{\mathrm{best}}\le\varepsilon\). This conclusion concerns dual objective values and does not by itself assert convergence of every multiplier iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With bounded supergradients and diminishing, nonsummable, square-summable steps, projected subgradient ascent drives the best observed dual value to the optimal dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave on nonempty closed convex \(\Lambda\), and its maximum is attained.
The selected supergradients are uniformly bounded.
\(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\) and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{k\to\infty}q_k^{\mathrm{best}}=q^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Sequence Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient conditions for convergence of projected subgradient multipliers to the dual solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Lambda^*=\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\ne\varnothing\), and let \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\), where \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\). If supergradients are uniformly bounded and \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the distance sequence to every fixed \(\lambda^*\in\Lambda^*\) has a limit and \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0\). In finite dimensions the multiplier sequence therefore converges to some element of \(\Lambda^*\); in particular, if \(\Lambda^*=\{\lambda^*\}\), then \(\lambda^k\to\lambda^*\). Without these hypotheses, convergence of dual values alone need not imply multiplier convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard diminishing-step and bounded-supergradient conditions, multiplier iterates approach and converge to the dual solution set; dual-value convergence alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave on a nonempty closed convex finite-dimensional set \(\Lambda\), and \(\Lambda^*\ne\varnothing\).
The supergradients are uniformly bounded.
The positive steps are nonsummable and square-summable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0\), and \(\lambda^k\to\bar\lambda\in\Lambda^*\).

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvergent Iterate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of multiplier convergence in projected Lagrangian subgradient ascent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\) be a concave Lagrangian dual function on a closed convex set \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\), and let \(\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k)\), where \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\). The multiplier iterates are in a nonconvergent regime when
\[\nexists\,\bar\lambda\in\Lambda\quad\text{such that}\quad \|\lambda^k-\bar\lambda\|\to0.\]
Equivalently, for a bounded sequence, its cluster-point set \(C=\{\bar\lambda:\lambda^{k_j}\to\bar\lambda\text{ for some subsequence}\}\) is not a singleton. This diagnosis alone neither implies nor excludes convergence of the best dual values \(\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier nonconvergence means the projected subgradient sequence has no single limit; when bounded, it has multiple cluster points. Dual values may nevertheless converge.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave and finite at every generated multiplier.
\(\Lambda\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
\(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\) and \(\alpha_k>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda^k\) is nonconvergent exactly when it has no norm limit; if bounded, this is equivalent to \(|C|>1\).

notation.meaning: Euclidean projection onto the multiplier set
cluster-point set of the multiplier sequence

knowledge_statements.title: Oscillatory Iterate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A quantitative diagnostic for persistent multiplier oscillation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a bounded multiplier sequence \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\Lambda\), define its tail diameter by
\[D_K=\sup_{r,s\ge K}\|\lambda^r-\lambda^s\|.\]
The sequence is persistently oscillatory precisely when \(\lim_{K\to\infty}D_K>0\). Equivalently, there exist \(\varepsilon>0\) and index pairs \(r_j,s_j\to\infty\) such that \(\|\lambda^{r_j}-\lambda^{s_j}\|\ge\varepsilon\) for every \(j\). In finite-dimensional space, boundedness then yields at least two distinct cluster points. This condition distinguishes persistent oscillation from finite transient movement followed by convergence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Persistent oscillation occurs when the diameter of every sufficiently late multiplier tail remains bounded away from zero.
assumptions_latex: \((\lambda^k)\) is bounded in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lim_{K\to\infty}D_K>0\), equivalently the sequence has at least two distinct cluster points.

notation.meaning: diameter of the multiplier tail beginning at iteration K

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(q^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)<+\infty\), and let \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\Lambda\). \[b_k\uparrow q^*\qquad\text{and}\qquad (\lambda^k)\text{ has no limit}.\]
The first condition is equivalent to \(q^*-b_k\downarrow0\) and provides asymptotically optimal dual bounds. It does not require convergence of \((\lambda^k)\), because \(q\) can take values arbitrarily close to \(q^*\) at distinct multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Best attained dual bounds can converge to the optimal dual value even though the multiplier sequence itself has no limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier Oscillation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines oscillation through distinct recurrent multiplier limits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A bounded multiplier sequence \((\lambda^k)\subseteq\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) exhibits multiplier oscillation if there exist two subsequences \((\lambda^{k_j})\) and \((\lambda^{\ell_j})\) and distinct multipliers \(u,v\in\Lambda\) such that
\[\lambda^{k_j}\to u,\qquad \lambda^{\ell_j}\to v,\qquad u\ne v.\]
Thus oscillation means recurrent asymptotic movement between at least two multiplier neighborhoods, not merely a large finite step or a nonmonotone dual-value sequence. The definition allows both periodic cycling and irregular recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiplier oscillation is the existence of two subsequences converging to different multiplier vectors.
assumptions_latex: \((\lambda^k)\) is bounded in \(\mathbb R^m\).
\(\Lambda\) is closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The cluster-point set of \((\lambda^k)\) contains at least two distinct elements.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonunique Dual Optimizers
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines multiplicity of optimal Lagrangian multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty\}\) be the concave dual function for a primal minimization problem, and let \(q^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)\). Its dual-optimizer set is
\[\Lambda^*=\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:q(\lambda)=q^*\}.\]
The dual problem has nonunique dual optimizers when there exist \(u,v\in\Lambda^*\) with \(u\ne v\), equivalently when \(|\Lambda^*|>1\). For concave \(q\) on convex \(\Lambda\), the set \(\Lambda^*\) is convex whenever it is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual optimizers are nonunique when two distinct feasible multipliers attain the same optimal dual value.
assumptions_latex: \(\Lambda\) is nonempty and convex.
\(q^*\) is finite and attained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Nonuniqueness is equivalent to the existence of distinct \(u,v\in\Lambda\) satisfying \(q(u)=q(v)=q^*\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, let \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\Lambda\) be bounded, and let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\). Define
\[q^*=\max_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda),\qquad \Lambda^*=\{\lambda\in\Lambda:q(\lambda)=q^*\}.\]
Suppose that \(q\) is continuous at every cluster point of \((\lambda^k)\) and that \(q(\lambda^k)\to q^*\). Every cluster point \(u\) then satisfies \(q(u)=q^*\), so \(u\in\Lambda^*\). Consequently, oscillation between distinct cluster points implies \(|\Lambda^*|>1\). Conversely, nonuniqueness of \(\Lambda^*\) permits but does not force oscillation; an update rule may select and converge to one optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If dual values converge optimally while multipliers oscillate and the dual function is continuous at recurrent limits, every recurrent limit is optimal and the dual optimizer is nonunique; multiplicity alone does not cause oscillation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Lambda\) be nonempty, let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\), and let \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\subseteq\Lambda\) be a multiplier sequence. Define \(b_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\). Given \(W\in\mathbb N\) with \(W\ge1\) and \(\tau\ge0\), dual-value stagnation is detected at iteration \(k\ge W\) when
\[0\le b_k-b_{k-W}\le\tau.\]
For \(K\in\mathbb N\), persistent stagnation from index \(K\) means that this inequality holds for every \(k\ge K+W\). When \(\tau=0\), no new strictly better dual value is found in any such window. Stagnation is an algorithmic diagnostic and does not certify dual optimality unless an independent upper bound matches \(b_k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual-value stagnation means the best dual bound improves by at most a prescribed tolerance over a fixed iteration window.

knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient-Norm Diagnostics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets the Lagrangian subgradient norm as a stationarity residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(q:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) be concave and let \(g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k)\), where the superdifferential convention is
\[q(\mu)\le q(\lambda^k)+(g^k)^\top(\mu-\lambda^k)\quad\text{for all }\mu.\]
The scalar \(r_k=\|g^k\|\) is a subgradient-norm diagnostic. If \(r_k=0\), then \(q(\mu)\le q(\lambda^k)\) for every \(\mu\), so \(\lambda^k\) is a global dual maximizer. A small positive \(r_k\) is only a residual measure; without scale, curvature, or an error bound, it does not certify a small dual-value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero Lagrangian supergradient norm certifies global dual optimality; a merely small norm is only a scale-dependent stationarity signal.
assumptions_latex: \(q\) is concave on \(\mathbb R^m\).
\(g^k\) satisfies the displayed supergradient inequality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_k=0\Rightarrow\lambda^k\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{\lambda\in\mathbb R^m}q(\lambda)\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian supergradient at the current multiplier

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p,m,n_1,\ldots,n_p\in\mathbb N\). For each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\), \(f_i:X_i\to\mathbb R\), and \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{m\times n_i}\), and let \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). Consider
\[\min\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i):x_i\in X_i,\ \sum_{i=1}^p A_i x_i=b\right\}\]
and its dual function
\[q(\lambda)=\inf_{x_i\in X_i,\ 1\le i\le p}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^p f_i(x_i)+\lambda^\top\left(\sum_{i=1}^pA_ix_i-b\right)\right\},\qquad \lambda\in\mathbb R^m.\]
If \(x_i^k\in X_i\) jointly attain this infimum at \(\lambda^k\), then
\[g^k=\sum_{i=1}^pA_ix_i^k-b\in\partial q(\lambda^k),\]
where \(\partial q\) denotes the superdifferential of the concave function \(q\). Thus each component of \(g^k\) is a signed coupling-constraint imbalance, while \(\|g^k\|\) measures aggregate imbalance in the chosen norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equality-coupled decomposition, a Lagrangian-minimizing primal block solution produces a dual supergradient equal to the coupling-constraint residual, so its components directly diagnose imbalance.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Lambda\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\) be concave, and consider
\[\lambda^{k+1}=P_\Lambda(\lambda^k+\alpha_k g^k),\qquad g^k\in\partial q(\lambda^k),\qquad \alpha_k>0,\]
where \(g^k\) is also the coupling-residual vector. Define \(b_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\), \(r_k=\|g^k\|\), and \(s_k=\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|\). Given \(W\in\mathbb N\) with \(W\ge1\) and thresholds \(\tau_b,\tau_r,\tau_s\ge0\), the diagnostics conflict, for example, when
\[b_k-b_{k-W}\le\tau_b,\qquad r_k>\tau_r,\qquad s_k\le\tau_s.\]
This pattern records a plateaued best dual value and small multiplier movement together with a large current coupling residual. Because \(s_k\) depends on the step size and projection as well as on \(g^k\), small multiplier movement does not imply a small residual; likewise, a bound plateau does not establish stationarity or optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For projected Lagrangian subgradient ascent, a flat dual bound and small multiplier steps can coexist with a large coupling residual, so these signals can conflict without certifying optimality.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a primal minimization problem with finite optimal value \(p^*\), let \(U_k\) be the best objective value of any primal-feasible point found through iteration \(k\). Let \(q:\Lambda\to\mathbb R\) be a valid Lagrangian dual function, let \((\lambda^j)_{j\ge0}\subseteq\Lambda\), and define \(L_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\). Weak duality gives
\[L_k\le p^*\le U_k.\]
Define \(G_k=U_k-L_k\ge0\). For every \(\varepsilon\ge0\), the condition \(G_k\le\varepsilon\) certifies that the incumbent is \(\varepsilon\)-optimal because \(U_k-p^*\le G_k\le\varepsilon\). If \(G_k=0\), then \(L_k=p^*=U_k\), and an iterate attaining \(L_k\) is a dual optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The difference between the best feasible primal value and best attained Lagrangian dual bound is a computable certificate of incumbent suboptimality; a gap at most epsilon certifies epsilon-optimality.

children.title: Bound-Plateau Tracking
children.top_down_role: Periods with little or no improvement in the dual bound.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Plateau Tracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A windowed procedure for detecting primal or dual bound plateaus.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input bound sequences \((L_k)\) and \((U_k)\), window \(W\ge1\), and tolerances \(\tau_L,\tau_U\ge0\), with \(L_k\) nondecreasing and \(U_k\) nonincreasing. At each \(k\ge W\), compute
\[\Delta_k^L=L_k-L_{k-W},\qquad \Delta_k^U=U_{k-W}-U_k.\]
Declare a dual-bound plateau if \(\Delta_k^L\le\tau_L\), a primal-bound plateau if \(\Delta_k^U\le\tau_U\), and a joint plateau if both hold. Continue until an independent stopping test is met; output the plateau labels and intervals. Plateau labels diagnose limited recent progress but do not certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare bound improvement across a fixed window and label primal, dual, or joint plateaus when improvement stays below chosen tolerances.
assumptions_latex: \(L_k\) is a valid nondecreasing lower-bound sequence.
\(U_k\) is a valid nonincreasing upper-bound sequence.
\(W\ge1\) and \(\tau_L,\tau_U\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs windowed plateau labels without asserting \(L_k=U_k\) or optimality.

children.title: Transient versus Persistent Plateaus
children.top_down_role: Distinguishing temporary stalls from sustained loss of bound progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Transient versus Persistent Plateaus
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Operational finite-horizon classification for a monitored Lagrangian gap sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_k\) be the incumbent primal value and \(L_k\) the best Lagrangian lower bound after iteration \(k\) of a minimization method, and define \(g_k=U_k-L_k\ge 0\). Fix \(w,q\in\mathbb N\), \(\varepsilon>0\), and an index \(k\ge w\). The window ending at \(k\) is a plateau when \(g_{k-w+1}-g_k\le\varepsilon\). Conditional on this event, the plateau is transient over the horizon \(\{k+1,\ldots,k+qw\}\) if some \(j\) in that horizon satisfies \(g_k-g_j>\varepsilon\); otherwise it is persistent through that horizon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A current gap plateau is transient if material cumulative improvement resumes within the specified future horizon; otherwise it is persistent through that horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\) and \(L_k\) are finite valid bounds for the same minimization problem.
The reported best-bound sequences make \(U_k\) nonincreasing and \(L_k\) nondecreasing.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{plateau}_k\in\{\text{transient},\text{persistent through the horizon}\}\) according to the complementary tests.

notation.meaning: number of future window lengths in the observation horizon

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: explicit operational diagnostic definition with user-selected thresholds

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Progress Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-aware diagnostic comparing incumbent improvement with Lagrangian-bound improvement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(U_k\) be the best feasible objective value and \(L_k\) the best valid Lagrangian lower bound through iteration \(k\). Fix \(w\in\mathbb N\), an integer \(k\ge w\), and tolerances \(\varepsilon_P,\varepsilon_D>0\). Define \(s_k=\max\{1,|U_{k-w}|,|L_{k-w}|\}\), \(p_k=(U_{k-w}-U_k)/s_k\), and \(d_k=(L_k-L_{k-w})/s_k\). A primal-stalled mismatch occurs when \(p_k\le\varepsilon_P\) and \(d_k>\varepsilon_D\); a dual-stalled mismatch occurs when \(p_k>\varepsilon_P\) and \(d_k\le\varepsilon_D\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Over a defined iteration window, progress is mismatched when exactly one of the incumbent and Lagrangian bound improves beyond its scale-adjusted tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(U_k\) is nonincreasing and \(L_k\) is nondecreasing.
All compared bounds are finite and refer to the same minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inequalities classify the window as primal-stalled mismatch, dual-stalled mismatch, or not mismatched.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem-Solution Repair
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repair of decomposed subproblem solutions against violated coupling constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\), and let \(\hat x\in X\) concatenate Lagrangian subproblem solutions. Choose a repair index set \(R\), fix \(x_j=\hat x_j\) for \(j\notin R\), and solve the restricted problem \[\min\{c^Tx+\rho\|Ax-b\|_1:x\in X,\ x_j=\hat x_j\ (j\notin R)\},\]\(\rho>0\). If an optimizer \(x^R\) satisfies \(Ax^R=b\), return it as a repaired feasible solution. Otherwise enlarge \(R\), increase \(\rho\), or terminate with repair failure; an infeasible penalized optimizer is never reported as primal feasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fix most subproblem decisions, reoptimize selected variables with a coupling-violation penalty, and accept the result only after directly checking all original coupling constraints.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) retains all local integrality and local constraints.
The restricted penalized problem can be solved or certified infeasible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns \(x^R\in X\) with \(Ax^R=b\), or an explicit repair-failure outcome.

children.title: Ergodic Primal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Primal recovery based on aggregate behavior across dual iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted averaging of Lagrangian subproblem iterates in a convexified primal space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given Lagrangian subproblem solutions \(x^1,x^2,\ldots\in X\) and weights \(\alpha_k>0\), set \(S_1=\alpha_1\) and \(\bar x^1=x^1\). For each \(k\ge2\), update \(S_k=S_{k-1}+\alpha_k\) and \(\bar x^k=(S_{k-1}\bar x^{k-1}+\alpha_kx^k)/S_k\). Equivalently, \[\bar x^k=\frac{1}{S_k}\sum_{t=1}^k\alpha_tx^t\in\operatorname{conv}(X).\] At a stopping index \(k\), output \(\bar x^k\) as the ergodic candidate. For a mixed-integer primal problem, accept it as a primal solution only if it satisfies the original constraints and integrality; otherwise pass it to a repair or restricted-master procedure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Form a positive weighted running average of subproblem iterates. The average lies in the convex hull, but mixed-integer feasibility still requires validation or repair.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\in X\) for every generated iteration.
\(\alpha_k>0\) and \(S_k<\infty\) at every reported index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x^k\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\), with primal acceptance conditional on original feasibility and integrality.
