children.title: Convex-Combination Primal Recovery
children.top_down_role: Primal candidates formed through weighted combinations of subproblem solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Combination Primal Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite convex-hull representation assembled from Lagrangian subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^1,\ldots,x^m\in X\) be Lagrangian subproblem solutions. A convex-combination recovery candidate has the representation \[\bar x=\sum_{t=1}^m\theta_tx^t,\qquad \theta_t\ge0,\qquad \sum_{t=1}^m\theta_t=1.\] Consequently \(\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\). The weights may be selected by a master problem that minimizes a recovery objective subject to coupling conditions such as \(A\bar x=b\). Membership in \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\) does not imply \(\bar x\in X\) when \(X\) is nonconvex; original integrality and feasibility must therefore be checked separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A recovered point is a convex combination of stored subproblem solutions. It belongs to their convex hull, while feasibility for a nonconvex mixed-integer set requires a separate check.
assumptions_latex: \(m\) is finite and every \(x^t\) belongs to the subproblem-feasible set \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}\{x^1,\ldots,x^m\}\subseteq\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

children.title: Recovery Feasibility versus Solution Quality
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs between improved feasibility, objective quality, aggregation depth.

knowledge_statements.title: Recovery Feasibility versus Solution Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separation between feasibility certification and objective-quality assessment in primal recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(P=\min\{c^Tx:x\in F\}\), a recovered candidate \(\hat x\) has a primal-quality certificate \(c^T\hat x-L\) only when \(\hat x\in F\) and \(L\le z^*\) is a valid lower bound. Then \[0\le c^T\hat x-z^*\le c^T\hat x-L.\] If \(\hat x\notin F\), its objective value is not a primal upper bound, even when it is smaller than the incumbent. Conversely, feasibility alone gives no prescribed approximation quality: feasible points can have arbitrarily poor objective values unless an independent bound controls their gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only a feasible recovered point supplies an upper bound; its quality is measured against a valid lower bound. Feasibility alone does not guarantee a good objective value.
assumptions_latex: \(P\) is a minimization problem with finite optimum \(z^*\).
\(L\) is a valid lower bound on \(z^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility certifies upper-bound validity, while \(c^T\hat x-L\) separately bounds objective suboptimality.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Primal-Master Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal recovery over a finite pool of generated block solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For blocks \(i=1,\ldots,p\), let \(V_i\subseteq X_i\) be finite pools of Lagrangian subproblem solutions. Solve the restricted master \[\min\sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{v\in V_i}c_i^Tv\,\theta_{iv}\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{i=1}^p\sum_{v\in V_i}A_iv\,\theta_{iv}=b,\quad \sum_{v\in V_i}\theta_{iv}=1,\quad \theta_{iv}\ge0.\] If an original mixed-integer solution is required, impose an appropriate integer selection or reconstruction model. Return a feasible reconstructed point; otherwise enlarge one or more pools and repeat, or report that the current restricted master cannot recover feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimize over finite pools of generated block solutions, enforcing coupling in a restricted master; add integer selection when convex mixing alone cannot produce an original feasible point.
assumptions_latex: Each pool element satisfies its block-local constraints.
The coupling system is represented exactly in the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is feasible for the represented master and becomes primal feasible after successful original-domain reconstruction.

notation.meaning: pool of generated solutions for block i

knowledge_statements.title: Multiplier-Guided Construction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constructive primal heuristic using reduced costs induced by Lagrangian multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min\{c^Tx:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\) and a multiplier \(\lambda\), compute scores from the Lagrangian coefficients \(r(\lambda)=c+A^T\lambda\). Initialize a partial solution with locally admissible variable values favored by increasing \(r_j(\lambda)\) for binary minimization variables, breaking ties by a fixed rule. Repeatedly select an unfixed variable, assign an admissible value, propagate local constraints, and backtrack or repair whenever the partial assignment cannot be extended toward \(Ax=b\). Stop with a fully feasible \(x\in X\) satisfying \(Ax=b\), or report construction failure after the prescribed backtracking or repair limit.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use multiplier-adjusted costs to order constructive decisions, propagate constraints after each assignment, and return a solution only when all local, coupling, and integrality requirements hold.
assumptions_latex: Variables have a defined finite candidate-value ordering.
Feasibility and propagation tests preserve every original constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure returns a verified primal-feasible point or an explicit failure outcome.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Neighborhood Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local primal search centered on decisions suggested by Lagrangian solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^I\in F\) be an incumbent and \(x^L\in X\) a Lagrangian subproblem solution. Choose a discrepancy set \(D=\{j:x_j^I\ne x_j^L\}\), radius \(r\), and neighborhood \[N_r(x^I,x^L)=\left\{x\in F:\sum_{j\in D}|x_j-x_j^L|\le r,\ x_j=x_j^I\text{ for selected }j\notin D\right\}.\] Solve or time-limit the restricted primal problem \(\min\{c^Tx:x\in N_r(x^I,x^L)\}\). Replace the incumbent only with a feasible point of strictly smaller objective value; otherwise retain \(x^I\), optionally modify \(r\), and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search a primal-feasible neighborhood biased toward the Lagrangian solution, accepting only verified improvements and retaining the incumbent when the restricted search fails.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is the original feasible set of a minimization problem.
The neighborhood subproblem preserves all original constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The incumbent objective never increases, and every accepted incumbent belongs to \(F\).

knowledge_statements.title: Feasibility Restoration After Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projection-style restoration of an averaged point to the original mixed-integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\) be an averaged Lagrangian candidate and let \(F\subseteq X\) denote the original feasible set. Select positive weights \(w_j\) and solve the restoration problem \[\min\left\{\sum_j w_j|x_j-\bar x_j|:x\in F\right\}.\] Absolute values may be represented by auxiliary variables. If the restoration problem returns \(x^R\), verify every original constraint and integrality condition before accepting \(x^R\). If it is infeasible or reaches its resource limit without a feasible point, report restoration failure; proximity of \(\bar x\) to \(F\) alone is not a feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find an original feasible point closest to the averaged candidate in a weighted norm, and accept it only after checking all constraints and integrality conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) includes every original local, coupling, and integrality constraint.
\(w_j>0\) for every restored coordinate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A successful output satisfies \(x^R\in F\); otherwise the procedure returns restoration failure.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Lagrangian variable-fixing certificates for better feasible solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Under the proposition's surrounding Lagrangian-heuristic setup, sufficient bound tests fix a binary variable in every feasible solution better than the reference value \(\bar Z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(r_j=c_j-\sum_{i\in M}u_i a_{ij}\). If \(k\in N_1\) and \(\sum_{i\in M}u_i+\sum_{j\in N_0}r_j+r_k\geq\bar Z\), then \(x_k=0\) in every better feasible solution. If \(k\in N_0\) and \(\sum_{i\in M}u_i+\sum_{j\in N_0\setminus\{k\}}r_j\geq\bar Z\), then \(x_k=1\) in every better feasible solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Let each reduced-cost term r_j equal c_j minus the sum of u_i a_ij over i in M. For k in N_1, if the stated Lagrangian bound including r_k is at least bar Z, every better feasible solution has x_k equal to 0. For k in N_0, if the bound excluding k from the N_0 sum is at least bar Z, every better feasible solution has x_k equal to 1.

\text{or, respectively,}\quad k\in N_0,\quad \sum_{i\in M}u_i+\sum_{j\in N_0\setminus\{k\}}r_j\geq\bar Z

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Bounds for Node Fathoming
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Valid lower-bound certificate for pruning a minimization branch-and-bound node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a branch-and-bound node \(v\), let \(F_v\) be its restricted feasible set and define \(z_v^*=\inf\{c^Tx:x\in F_v\}\). Suppose \(F_v\subseteq X_v\) and every \(x\in F_v\) satisfies \(Ax=b\). For \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^m\), define \(L_v(\lambda)=\inf_{x\in X_v}\{c^Tx+\lambda^T(Ax-b)\}\). Weak duality gives \(L_v(\lambda)\le z_v^*\). If a finite globally feasible incumbent value \(U\) is available and \(L_v(\lambda)\ge U\), then node \(v\) contains no solution improving the incumbent and may be fathomed. The certificate consists of \(\lambda\), the certified subproblem value, and the inequality \(L_v(\lambda)\ge U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A node can be pruned when a certified Lagrangian lower bound is at least the globally feasible incumbent value, because no solution in that node can improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The global problem is a minimization problem.
\(F_v\subseteq X_v\) and the relaxed equality \(Ax=b\) holds for every \(x\in F_v\).
\(U\) is the objective value of a globally feasible incumbent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L_v(\lambda)\ge U\Longrightarrow z_v^*\ge U\), so node \(v\) is safely fathomed by bound.

notation.meaning: feasible set at search node v

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Cut Integration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Insertion of valid inequalities generated from Lagrangian separation into exact search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At search node \(v\), solve a Lagrangian relaxation at multiplier \(\lambda\) and use its solution information to generate an inequality \(\alpha^Tx\ge\beta\). Before insertion, establish validity of \(\alpha^Tx\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in F\), where \(F\) is the original global feasible set; node-only validity permits insertion only in the corresponding subtree. Add the inequality to the node relaxation, reoptimize, and retain it globally only when global validity is certified. Stop cut generation when no violated certified cut is found or a prescribed cut or time limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate an inequality from Lagrangian information, certify its validity domain, add it to the exact-search relaxation, and never promote a node-local cut to global status without certification of global validity.
assumptions_latex: The cut-generation routine supplies a checkable validity certificate.
The exact-search relaxation contains every constraint required at node \(v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every inserted cut preserves all feasible points in its certified validity domain while possibly strengthening the search relaxation.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At node \(t\), initialize \(B_t=-\infty\). For each evaluated multiplier \(\lambda^k\ge0\), compute \[q_t(\lambda^k)=\inf_{x\in X_t}\{c^\top x+(\lambda^k)^\top(d-Dx)\}\] and set \(B_t\leftarrow\max\{B_t,q_t(\lambda^k)\}\). Multipliers may be updated by any prescribed Lagrangian-dual procedure. Prune the node when \(B_t\ge U\); otherwise, after the node-bounding termination test, branch into covering child domains \(X_{t_j}\subseteq X_t\) and optionally use admissible multiplier warm starts at the children.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each branch-and-bound node, evaluate Lagrangian lower bounds, retain the best one, prune it against a feasible incumbent, and otherwise create child domains that cover the unpruned node domain.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Evaluating \[q(\lambda)=\min_{x\in X}\{c^\top x+\lambda^\top(d-Dx)\}\] at a fixed \(\lambda\) is optimization of a linear objective over \(X\). If \(X\) is allowed to encode an arbitrary binary linear program, choose \(D=0\) and \(d=0\); then evaluating \(q(0)=\min_{x\in X}c^\top x\) is exactly that binary optimization problem. Hence exact Lagrangian-bound evaluation is NP-hard in this input model, even though all relaxed coupling terms vanish.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lagrangian subproblem can still contain an arbitrary binary program, so exact bound evaluation remains NP-hard despite removal of coupling constraints.

children.title: Multiplier Instability
children.top_down_role: Erratic or excessively sensitive multiplier behavior.

assumptions_latex: The dual iterates satisfy \(\lambda^k\in\Lambda\), and \(q^*=\sup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}q(\lambda)<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Multiplier instability concerns failure of the iterates to settle, even when their bound values approach the dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sequence-level definition separating multiplier convergence from convergence of dual values.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A multiplier sequence \((\lambda^k)_{k\ge0}\) is called unstable if it does not converge in \(\Lambda\); in particular, instability holds if \(\|\lambda^k\|\) is unbounded or if there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that \(\|\lambda^{k+1}-\lambda^k\|\ge\varepsilon\) for infinitely many \(k\). Value convergence \(q(\lambda^k)\to q^*\) does not exclude multiplier instability, because the dual-optimal set may be non-singleton or the iterates may oscillate between distinct dual faces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multipliers are unstable when their iterates fail to converge, through unboundedness or persistent jumps, even if the associated Lagrangian bounds converge.

children.title: Bound Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Persistent absence of meaningful Lagrangian-bound improvement.

assumptions_latex: Let \(B_k=\max_{0\le j\le k}q(\lambda^j)\) be the best bound through iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stagnation is the absence of asymptotically meaningful improvement in the best attained dual bound.

notation.meaning: best Lagrangian bound attained by iteration k

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lagrangian bound sequence is stagnant over a fixed window length \(r\ge1\) if \[B_{k+r}-B_k\longrightarrow0.\] It is finitely stagnant from iteration \(K\) if \(B_k=B_K\) for every \(k\ge K\). Relative stagnation at tolerance \(\tau\ge0\) may instead be declared when \[B_{k+r}-B_k\le\tau\max\{1,|B_k|\}\] for the prescribed number of consecutive windows. This definition concerns the best attained bound, not convergence of the multiplier sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound stagnation occurs when the running best Lagrangian bound has vanishing, or eventually zero, improvement across fixed iteration windows.

A source-backed definition or an explicit failure threshold relative to the target bound is needed before the mathematical version can be fixed.

children.title: Instability-Induced Bound Stagnation
children.top_down_role: Regimes where unstable multiplier search contributes to stalled bound progress.

assumptions_latex: The concave dual function is \(q(\lambda)=\min\{\lambda,2-\lambda\}\) on \(\lambda\ge0\).
Projected subgradient ascent uses constant step length \(2\), initial point \(\lambda^0=0\), and selections \(g(0)=1\) and \(g(2)=-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The multiplier sequence oscillates while its running best bound remains one unit below the dual optimum.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete constant-step oscillation causing permanent loss of dual-bound progress.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the update \[\lambda^{k+1}=\max\{0,\lambda^k+2g(\lambda^k)\},\] the iterates satisfy \(\lambda^{2j}=0\) and \(\lambda^{2j+1}=2\) for every integer \(j\ge0\). Their values satisfy \(q(\lambda^k)=0\), whereas \(\sup_{\lambda\ge0}q(\lambda)=q(1)=1\). Thus the running best bound is constantly \(0\) while the multipliers oscillate between \(0\) and \(2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant-step projected subgradient method alternates between multipliers 0 and 2 and retains bound 0 forever, although the dual optimum is 1.

assumptions_latex: Consider the minimization problem with \(x\in\{0,1\}\), objective \(x\), and constraint \(x\ge1\).

children.title: Row-Generation View
children.top_down_role: Decomposition interpreted through progressive constraint introduction.

assumptions_latex: For fixed \(x\), the continuous subproblem is \(Q(x)=\min\{d^\top y:Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\).
The subproblem is feasible and has finite value for each master point under consideration.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The subproblem value is represented by affine rows indexed by dual extreme points, which may be generated on demand.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Benders epigraph as an iteratively generated family of dual-value rows.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\{u\ge0:W^\top u\le d\}\). Linear-programming duality gives \[Q(x)=\max_{u\in U}u^\top(h-Tx).\] If \(U\) has relevant extreme points \(u^j\), the epigraph condition is \[\theta\ge (u^j)^\top(h-Tx)\qquad\text{for every }j.\] A row-generation method keeps only a subset of these inequalities, solves the restricted master, evaluates the subproblem at its candidate \(x\), and appends a row from a maximizing dual solution whenever its right-hand side exceeds \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Benders decomposition represents the subproblem value by affine inequalities from dual extreme points and generates a violated inequality whenever the restricted master underestimates that value.
knowledge_statements.title: Row-Generation View

children.title: Projection View
children.top_down_role: Decomposition geometry expressed through elimination into a lower-dimensional space.

assumptions_latex: Let \(S=\{(x,y):Wy\ge h-Tx,\ y\ge0\}\) be a nonempty polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Projection eliminates \(y\) by replacing its system with all inequalities generated by the alternative cone \(K\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-inequality representation of a polyhedral projection used by Benders decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(K=\{u\ge0:W^\top u\le0\}\). Farkas' alternative gives \[\operatorname{proj}_x(S)=\{x:u^\top(h-Tx)\le0\ \text{for every }u\in K\}.\] Because \(K\) is a polyhedral cone, it suffices to impose the inequality for generators of its extreme rays. A violated generator certifies that no \(y\ge0\) satisfies \(Wy\ge h-Tx\) at the candidate \(x\), and its inequality is a feasibility row in the projected formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Farkas' lemma projects out the subproblem variables: master feasibility is characterized by inequalities indexed by extreme rays of an alternative cone.
knowledge_statements.title: Projection View

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Projection View
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fiber-based lifting of a projected polyhedron.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q=\{(x,y)\in\mathbb R^n\times\mathbb R^m:Bx+Cy\ge d,\ y\ge0\}\) and let \(P=\operatorname{proj}_x(Q)\). For each \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), define the inverse-projection fiber by \(Q_x=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:(x,y)\in Q\}\). Then \(x\in P\) exactly when \(Q_x\ne\varnothing\), and \(Q=\{(x,y):x\in P,\ y\in Q_x\}\). Thus an extended formulation represents membership in the projection through feasibility of a lifted fiber.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point belongs to a projected feasible set exactly when its associated lifted-variable fiber is nonempty.
assumptions_latex: \(B\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},\ C\in\mathbb R^{p\times m},\ d\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x\in P\iff Q_x\ne\varnothing\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection Polarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas-polar description of a polyhedral projection.

children.title: Lagrangian Dual Bound
children.top_down_role: Bound viewpoint arising from relaxation through dual multipliers.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian Dual Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lower bound obtained by dualizing linking equalities in a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(z^*=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\), where \(X\ne\varnothing\). For \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\), define \(L(\pi)=\inf_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x+\pi^{\mathsf T}(b-Ax)\}\). The Lagrangian dual bound is \[z_L=\sup_{\pi\in\mathbb R^p}L(\pi).\] Every feasible \(x\) has zero linking-constraint penalty, so \(L(\pi)\le z^*\) for every \(\pi\), and consequently \(z_L\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing the relaxed problem over linking-constraint multipliers gives a valid lower bound for the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(c\in\mathbb R^n,\ A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n},\ b\in\mathbb R^p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_L=\sup_{\pi}L(\pi)\le z^*\).

notation.meaning: Lagrangian relaxation value at multiplier pi

children.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Bound

knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig–Wolfe Master Bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Full convexified master associated with a block-feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). For \(z^*=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\), define the full Dantzig–Wolfe master bound by \[z_{DW}=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X)\}.\] If \(X=\{x^k:k\in K\}\) is finite, the same bound is the value of \[\inf_{\lambda\ge0}\left\{\sum_{k\in K}c^{\mathsf T}x^k\lambda_k:\sum_{k\in K}Ax^k\lambda_k=b,\ \sum_{k\in K}\lambda_k=1\right\}.\] Because \(X\subseteq\operatorname{cl}\operatorname{conv}(X)\), one has \(z_{DW}\le z^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The full Dantzig–Wolfe master replaces the block-feasible set by its closed convex hull, yielding a lower bound for the original minimization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\).

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Equivalence Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalence for a full convex-hull master with exact pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and consider \(z^*=\inf\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in X\}\). knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Equivalence Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure caused by an incomplete or mismatched column set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lagrangian–Dantzig–Wolfe bound equivalence need not hold for a restricted master. For example, take \(X=\{0,2\}\subset\mathbb R\), objective coefficient \(c=0\), and linking equation \(x=1\). The exact Lagrangian value is \(\sup_{\pi\in\mathbb R}\min\{\pi,-\pi\}=0\), and the full convexified master also has value \(0\). If the restricted master contains only the column \(x=0\), it is infeasible and has value \(+\infty\). Thus omission of a column needed for full-master feasibility or optimality can destroy bound equivalence; completeness or exact pricing supplies a sufficient safeguard, but is not necessary for incidental equality in every instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted master can fail to match the Lagrangian bound when it omits a column needed for full-master feasibility or optimality.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_L=0\neq +\infty=z_{RMP}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Interpretation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Economic and algebraic interpretation of linking-row multipliers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). For the convexified master \(\min\{c^{\mathsf T}x:Ax=b,\ x\in\operatorname{conv}(X)\}\), let \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\) be a dual multiplier for \(Ax=b\). The Lagrangian value separates as \[L(\pi)=\pi^{\mathsf T}b+\inf_{x\in X}(c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x.\] Thus \(\pi_i\) is a signed shadow price for the \(i\)-th linking equation, while \(c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi\) is the price-adjusted column-cost vector. An exact marginal-value interpretation additionally requires the usual value-function sensitivity conditions, and the sign reverses if the linking equation is written with the opposite orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linking-row multiplier is a signed shadow price, and subtracting the induced prices from column costs produces the pricing objective; an exact marginal interpretation requires sensitivity conditions.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty.
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b,\pi\in\mathbb R^p\).
The linking equations are written as \(Ax=b\).

children.title: Dual Prices in Pricing Oracles
children.top_down_role: Transfer of master dual information into pricing decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Prices in Pricing Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation pricing rule for a convexity master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\). Given a feasible restricted master with columns \(x^k\in X\), solve it to primal-dual optimality and obtain \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\) for \(\sum_k Ax^k\lambda_k=b\) and \(\sigma\in\mathbb R\) for \(\sum_k\lambda_k=1\). Call an exact oracle that returns \[x^{new}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\{c^{\mathsf T}x-\pi^{\mathsf T}Ax-\sigma\}.\] If the returned reduced cost is negative, add \(x^{new}\) and reoptimize. If its reduced cost is nonnegative, no column in \(X\) violates the current dual constraints, and the current restricted-master solution is optimal for the full master.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact pricing oracle minimizes reduced cost using the current master dual prices, adds a column when that cost is negative, and otherwise certifies full-master optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, and the pricing minimum is attained.
\(c\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\).
The restricted master is feasible and solved to primal-dual optimality.
The pricing oracle optimizes exactly over \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}(c^{\mathsf T}x-\pi^{\mathsf T}Ax-\sigma)\ge0\) certifies full-master optimality.

notation.meaning: column returned by the pricing oracle

children.title: Price Consistency across Master Updates
children.top_down_role: Normalization, scaling, validity issues affecting repeated pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Price Consistency across Master Updates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign and normalization invariant for iterative pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\). At master iteration \(t\), let \((\pi^t,\sigma^t)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R\) be an optimal dual solution under the fixed conventions \(Ax=b\) and \(\sum_k\lambda_k=1\). Price every candidate \(x\in X\) by \[r_t(x)=c^{\mathsf T}x-(\pi^t)^{\mathsf T}Ax-\sigma^t.\] Price consistency means that the oracle uses these current dual variables together with the same row orientations, objective scaling, convexity-row normalization, and reduced-cost sign convention at every iteration. Dual values may change after columns are added, but the convention defining \(r_t\) must not change.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every pricing call must use the current master dual solution under unchanged row orientation, objective scaling, convexity normalization, and reduced-cost sign conventions.

knowledge_statements.title: Few Complicating Variables Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural condition favoring Benders-type projection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x\in\mathbb Z^q\times\mathbb R^r\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), \(F\subseteq(\mathbb Z^q\times\mathbb R^r)\times\mathbb R^m\), \(c_x\in\mathbb R^{q+r}\), and \(c_y\in\mathbb R^m\), and consider \(\min\{c_x^{\mathsf T}x+c_y^{\mathsf T}y:(x,y)\in F\}\). If \(q+r\) is small relative to the full formulation and fixing \(x\) leaves a tractable continuous subproblem in \(y\) whose dual supplies valid feasibility or optimality cuts, then a Benders-type method is structurally appropriate: retain \(x\) in the master and refine the projection onto the \(x\)-space using subproblem cuts. knowledge_statements.title: Few Linking Constraints Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural condition favoring Lagrangian or Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(i=1,\ldots,s\), let \(X_i\subseteq\mathbb R^{n_i}\) be nonempty, \(c_i\in\mathbb R^{n_i}\), and \(A_i\in\mathbb R^{p\times n_i}\). Suppose \(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_s\) and the only cross-block restrictions are \(\sum_{i=1}^s A_i x_i=b\), where \(b\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(p\) is relatively small. For \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\), dualizing these rows gives \[L(\pi)=\pi^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^s\inf_{x_i\in X_i}(c_i-A_i^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_i.\] Evaluation therefore separates by block, and the multiplier dimension is \(p\). This structure favors Lagrangian decomposition or its Dantzig–Wolfe master counterpart when the block subproblems are tractable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Few linking rows favor Lagrangian or Dantzig–Wolfe decomposition because dualization separates the blocks and leaves a low-dimensional multiplier problem.

\(X=X_1\times\cdots\times X_s\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^p\).
Each block pricing or Lagrangian subproblem is tractable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(\pi)=\pi^{\mathsf T}b+\sum_{i=1}^s\inf_{x_i\in X_i}(c_i-A_i^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x_i\).

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Combinatorial Oracle Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural condition favoring oracle-driven column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be a nonempty discrete block-feasible set, let \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\). Suppose that for every \(d\in\mathbb R^n\), linear optimization \(\min_{x\in X}d^{\mathsf T}x\) is solved exactly and efficiently by a combinatorial algorithm, while an explicit linear description of \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\) is unavailable or very large. Then Dantzig–Wolfe column generation is structurally favored: for a current linking-row price vector \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\), use the combinatorial solver as the pricing oracle with \(d=c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi\), and represent the convexified block implicitly through generated columns. Exact oracle optimality is required for the usual no-negative-reduced-cost certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column generation is structurally favored when linear optimization over a huge discrete block is exact and efficient even though its convex hull is hard to describe explicitly.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty and discrete.
\(c,d\in\mathbb R^n\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), and \(\pi\in\mathbb R^p\).
Linear optimization over \(X\) is exact and computationally tractable for every oracle objective \(d\).
The master couples columns through comparatively compact linking constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}(c-A^{\mathsf T}\pi)^{\mathsf T}x\) supplies an exact Dantzig–Wolfe pricing oracle.

knowledge_statements.title: Heterogeneous Solver-Oracle Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Selection principle for block-structured mixed-integer models whose subproblems require different exact optimization technologies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a formulation with coordinator variables \(x\in X\) and block value functions \(Q_k(x)=\inf\{q_k(y_k):y_k\in Y_k(x)\}\). A heterogeneous solver-oracle architecture assigns each block \(k\) an oracle suited to \(Y_k(x)\), such as mathematical programming, dynamic programming, or combinatorial optimization. Every returned cut or column must be valid for the common master formulation, and every claimed absence of a violated cut or improving column must satisfy the coordinator's prescribed tolerance. Thus heterogeneous internal solvers may be combined without changing the master problem, provided their outputs share consistent variables, bounds, and validity semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders with Column-Generated Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nested algorithm for a Benders master whose linear recourse problem is itself represented by dynamically generated columns.

From the resulting optimal recourse primal-dual pair, return a globally valid Benders optimality cut \(\theta\geq \alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\); if recourse is infeasible, use an appropriate feasibility certificate and cut. Add the cut to the outer master and iterate until its incumbent satisfies all generated cuts within tolerance.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Reduced-Cost Exploration and Stopping Certificate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost certificate for suspending Lagrangian pricing subproblems and approximately stopping column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\check D_k(\mu)=\min\{L_k(x;\mu):x\in\operatorname{conv}(W_k^j)\}\), \(D_k(\mu)=\min\{L_k(x;\mu):x\in G_k\}\), and \(R_k(\mu)=D_k(\mu)-\check D_k(\mu)\). Since \(\operatorname{conv}(W_k^j)\subseteq G_k\) in the stated construction, \(R_k(\mu)\leq0\). Equality certifies that subproblem \(k\) is explored, permitting its column generation to be suspended temporarily. If \(\widehat\mu^j\) is a dual solution of the restricted master problem \((4.16)\), then \(e(\widehat\mu^j):=-\sum_{k=1}^pR_k(\widehat\mu^j)\) satisfies \(0\leq e(\widehat\mu^j)\leq\operatorname{val}(4.16)-\operatorname{val}(4.14)\); thus a sufficiently small error supplies a stopping criterion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each reduced cost is the original Lagrangian subproblem value minus its restricted approximation value and is nonpositive. A zero reduced cost certifies that the subproblem is explored. At a restricted-master dual solution, the negative sum of reduced costs is a nonnegative approximation error bounded above by the restricted-master value gap, so a small error can be used to stop column generation.
assumptions_latex: \(\check D_k(\mu)=\min\{L_k(x;\mu):x\in\operatorname{conv}(W_k^j)\}\), \(D_k(\mu)=\min\{L_k(x;\mu):x\in G_k\}\), and the restricted inner approximation satisfies \(\operatorname{conv}(W_k^j)\subseteq G_k\).
\(\widehat\mu^j\) is a dual solution of the restricted master problem \((4.16)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_k(\mu)\leq0,\qquad R_k(\mu)=0\Rightarrow k\text{ is explored},\qquad 0\leq-\sum_{k=1}^pR_k(\widehat\mu^j)\leq\operatorname{val}(4.16)-\operatorname{val}(4.14).

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Pricing Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive pricing procedure whose outer reduced-cost minimization invokes subordinate pricing problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given outer dual data \(\pi\), define the pricing value \(r^*(\pi)=\min_{z\in Z}\{c(z)-\pi^{\mathsf T}a(z)\}\). A nested pricing oracle solves this problem through subordinate restricted masters and pricing oracles. It returns either a feasible object \(z\in Z\) with certified reduced cost \(r(z)<-\varepsilon\), or a lower bound \(L(\pi)\leq r^*(\pi)\) with \(L(\pi)\geq-\varepsilon\). In the first case the outer algorithm inserts the corresponding column; in the second it accepts the certificate that no improving outer column exists within tolerance. An unfinished inner solve cannot certify outer pricing termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nested pricing oracle must return an improving feasible column or a lower bound proving that no such column exists within tolerance.

\varepsilon\geq0
\text{Inner bounds are valid for the full outer pricing set }Z

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Cut Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive separation procedure in which an outer cut query is resolved by subordinate optimization or separation oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation point \(x^t\) and a valid-inequality family \(\mathcal C\), define maximum violation \(v^t=\sup_{(a,b)\in\mathcal C}\{a^{\mathsf T}x^t-b\}\). A nested cut oracle invokes subordinate optimization or separation procedures and returns either a globally valid inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\leq b\) with violation exceeding \(\varepsilon\), or a certified upper bound \(U^t\geq v^t\) satisfying \(U^t\leq\varepsilon\). The outer method adds the returned inequality in the first case and declares this cut family separated in the second. A local or heuristic failure to find a cut is not a separation certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Nested Decomposition Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General recursive decomposition contract for value-function queries solved by subordinate decomposition algorithms.

It returns one of: a feasible solution and matching bound whose gap is at most \(\varepsilon\); a valid infeasibility certificate; or a globally valid outer cut derived from a valid inner bound or certificate. The coordinator may close the outer query only when the returned object has the declared validity and accuracy. Inner incumbents without bounds may update an outer upper bound but cannot justify an optimality cut or a completed value-function evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Lazy-Constraint Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-callback contract for enforcing omitted Benders constraints at candidate integer master solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a master model with variables \((x,\theta)\), a Benders lazy-constraint interface is a callback invoked on a candidate integer solution \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\). It evaluates the subproblem at \(\bar x\) and, when necessary, submits either a globally valid feasibility cut excluding \(\bar x\) or a globally valid optimality cut \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\) violated by the candidate. The callback accepts the candidate only if no required Benders constraint is violated beyond tolerance. Any submitted constraint must remain valid for every feasible solution of the original formulation, not merely at the current candidate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lazy callback checks integer candidates and adds globally valid Benders feasibility or optimality constraints whenever an omitted required constraint is violated.

\text{The subproblem returns a valid cut or a no-violation certificate}
\varepsilon\geq0

notation.meaning: candidate master solution presented to the callback

knowledge_statements.title: Benders User-Cut Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solver-callback contract for adding globally valid Benders cuts that strengthen node relaxations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a relaxation solution \((\bar x,\bar\theta)\), a Benders user-cut interface is a callback that may submit a globally valid inequality, typically \(\theta\geq\alpha+\beta^{\mathsf T}x\), violated by more than tolerance. The cut must be valid for every feasible integer solution of the original model and is used to strengthen the current linear relaxation. Failure to generate a user cut does not authorize rejection of an integer candidate and does not replace enforcement of any Benders constraint required for correctness; such constraints must be modeled explicitly or enforced through an appropriate lazy-constraint mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A user-cut callback strengthens fractional relaxations with globally valid Benders cuts but cannot replace correctness-critical enforcement at integer candidates.
assumptions_latex: (\bar x,\bar\theta)\text{ is a node-relaxation solution}
\text{Every submitted cut is globally valid for the original feasible set}
\varepsilon\geq0

notation.meaning: node-relaxation solution supplied to the callback

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the user-cut interface leaf and correctly separates relaxation strengthening from correctness-critical enforcement. Because callback availability and permitted cuts are solver-specific, the claim requires vendor or API documentation with a precise locator.

children.title: Benders Callback Selection Boundaries

knowledge_statements.title: Benders Callback Selection Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Correctness boundary separating relaxation-strengthening user cuts from enforcement-oriented lazy constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a Benders inequality is omitted from the static master. If violating that inequality makes an integer candidate infeasible or gives it an invalid recourse value, treating the inequality only as an optional user cut can permit an incorrect incumbent whenever the solver does not call that interface at the candidate. Such an inequality must instead be explicit or enforced by a supported lazy-constraint mechanism. Conversely, a redundant globally valid Benders inequality used only to tighten fractional relaxations belongs in a user-cut interface. A locally valid inequality belongs in neither interface unless the solver explicitly supports its locality semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Correctness-critical omitted Benders constraints require explicit or lazy enforcement; user cuts are only for globally valid relaxation strengthening.
assumptions_latex: \text{The solver may omit user-cut callbacks at integer candidates}
\text{Lazy constraints are checked according to the solver's documented correctness semantics}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Using only a user-cut interface for a correctness-critical omitted constraint can yield an invalid accepted incumbent.}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind is exactly appropriate and the stated risk is plausible, but whether user-cut callbacks may be skipped and how lazy constraints guarantee enforcement are solver-dependent. A specific supported solver contract is needed before accepting the boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Insertion Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency contract for transferring a priced column into the restricted master.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A column-insertion interface maps a priced object \(j\) to a new restricted-master variable \(\lambda_j\) together with objective coefficient \(c_j\), coefficient \(a^j_r\) for every active master row \(r\), bounds, and integrality type. The inserted data must satisfy the same sign, scaling, and indexing conventions used to compute \(\bar c_j=c_j-\sum_r\pi_r a^j_r\). If rows were added after pricing began, their coefficients must be supplied or the column must be revalidated before insertion. Duplicate handling may reject an existing column but must preserve an equivalent restricted-master representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column insertion must register complete, convention-consistent variable data and account for every active master row before reoptimization.
assumptions_latex: \text{The priced object determines finite coefficients for every active master row}
\text{The master exposes a stable row identity or version}
\text{The column is feasible for its generating pricing set}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The inserted variable represents the priced column and reproduces its computed reduced cost under the current master state.}

notation.meaning: coefficient of column j in master row r
dual multiplier of master row r

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the insertion-interface leaf, but the stable-row-version requirement, treatment of rows added during pricing, integrality metadata, and duplicate-column behavior are substantive API claims without evidence. A column-generation framework or solver API source with a precise locator is required.

children.title: Pricing Lifecycle Coordination
children.top_down_role: Timing, repetition, termination coordination across pricing cycles.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master is a minimization problem with current dual vector \(\pi\).
The pricing oracle can optimize reduced cost over the node-restricted column set \(Y_v\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lifecycle terminates with either an improving validated column or an exact no-improving-column certificate.

notation.meaning: dual vector of the current restricted master
columns admissible at branch-and-bound node v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact column-generation pricing lifecycle at one branch-and-bound node.

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given node \(v\), synchronize the pricing oracle with \(Y_v\), the current master dual vector \(\pi\), and the master-column map. Compute \(y^*\in\arg\min_{y\in Y_v}\bar c_\pi(y)\). If \(\bar c_\pi(y^*)< -\varepsilon\), validate admissibility and recompute the reduced cost from canonical master data; insert the corresponding column and reoptimize the master before invoking pricing again. If an exact oracle proves \(\min_{y\in Y_v}\bar c_\pi(y)\geq-\varepsilon\), return a no-improving-column certificate. An inexact oracle may return only an improving column or an unresolved status, never the exact certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Synchronize pricing state, find and validate a negative-reduced-cost column, insert it, and reoptimize. Stop exactly only when the oracle certifies that no improving admissible column exists.
knowledge_statements.title: Pricing Lifecycle Coordination

children.title: Custom Branching Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver integration points for decomposition-compatible branching choices.

assumptions_latex: At node \(v\), the feasible integer solutions form \(F_v\).
Every child restriction can be enforced by all decomposition oracles.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Accepted children partition or cover \(F_v\) without introducing infeasible incumbents as feasible solutions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mathematical contract for a decomposition-aware custom branching callback.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a fractional node solution, a custom branching interface returns finitely many restrictions \(R_1,\ldots,R_q\) and child sets \(F_{v,k}=F_v\cap R_k\). Before accepting the branch, verify \(F_v=\bigcup_{k=1}^qF_{v,k}\); for a partitioning branch also verify \(F_{v,k}\cap F_{v,\ell}=\varnothing\) for \(k\neq\ell\). Each \(R_k\) must be translated into the master, pricing, and separation representations before solving child \(k\). If translation is unavailable or the coverage check is not justified, reject the proposed branch and use a branching rule whose restrictions all components implement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A custom branch must produce exhaustive children and propagate each child restriction consistently to the master, pricing, and separation components before the child is solved.
knowledge_statements.title: Custom Branching Interfaces

children.title: Custom Separation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Solver integration points for user-controlled cut discovery.

assumptions_latex: The callback is invoked at node \(v\) with relaxation point \(\hat x\).
The node's integer-feasible set \(F_v\) is represented consistently to the separator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every accepted cut is valid for its declared scope and separates \(\hat x\) by more than the feasibility tolerance.

notation.meaning: validity scope of a returned cut

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: separation callbacks must return valid violated inequalities with explicit scope

source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A custom separation interface receives \((v,\hat x)\) and returns inequalities \(\alpha_i^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta_i\) with declared scopes \(S_i\). An inequality is accepted only if \(\alpha_i^{\mathsf T}x\geq\beta_i\) for every integer-feasible \(x\in S_i\) and \(\alpha_i^{\mathsf T}\hat x<\beta_i-\varepsilon_{\mathrm{feas}}\). A global cut uses the root feasible set as \(S_i\); a local cut uses the current node set or an explicitly identified descendant-valid set. The interface must canonicalize coefficients, reject nonfinite data, suppress numerical duplicates, and attach the declared validity scope before insertion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A separator returns finite, canonical inequalities that are valid on their declared global or local scope and sufficiently violated by the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.title: Custom Separation Interfaces

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Branch–Separation Validity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Interactions between branch decisions, cut scope, inherited validity.

assumptions_latex: Branching at node \(v\) creates child feasible sets \(F_{v,k}=F_v\cap R_k\subseteq F_v\).
The inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) has a recorded validity domain \(S\), meaning it is valid for every integer-feasible \(x\in S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The recorded validity declaration justifies inheritance at child \(k\) whenever \(F_{v,k}\subseteq S\); if this inclusion is not established, the cut must be revalidated or removed.

notation.meaning: recorded domain on which the cut is certified valid

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a recorded validity domain justifies reuse on node domains contained in it
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-inclusion criterion coupling a cut's recorded validity domain to branching descendants.

source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let branching at node \(v\) produce children indexed by \(k\in\{1,\ldots,q\}\), with \(F_{v,k}=F_v\cap R_k\). If the inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\geq b\) is recorded as valid on \(S\), then \(F_{v,k}\subseteq S\) is sufficient to install the cut at child \(k\) without a new validity argument. Consequently, a globally valid cut is inherited by every child, and a cut certified on \(F_v\) is inherited by descendants whose feasible sets remain subsets of \(F_v\). If \(F_{v,k}\subseteq S\) is not established, the recorded declaration alone does not justify inheritance; the cut must be revalidated for \(F_{v,k}\) or removed. Pricing and separation must apply the same child restriction \(R_k\) when identifying \(F_{v,k}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A child may inherit a cut without revalidation when the child's feasible set lies inside the cut's recorded validity domain. Otherwise, the recorded scope alone is insufficient and the cut must be revalidated or removed.
knowledge_statements.title: Branch–Separation Validity Coupling

assumptions_latex: Each subproblem object \(y\in Y\) determines an original-space contribution and objective cost.
The restricted master stores columns in a fixed canonical row order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mapping preserves objective and linking-row contributions between the subproblem object and its master column.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical mapping from oracle objects to master coefficients and reconstruction data.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A master-subproblem data mapping is a deterministic map \(M:Y\to\mathbb R^m\times\mathbb R\times X\) with \(M(y)=(a(y),c(y),r(y))\), where \(a(y)\) contains the linking-row contributions in canonical master-row order, \(c(y)\) is the master objective coefficient, and \(r(y)\) reconstructs the original-space contribution. For master weights \(\lambda_y\), consistency requires that the linking contribution equal \(\sum_y a(y)\lambda_y\), the objective contribution equal \(\sum_y c(y)\lambda_y\), and the reconstructed solution equal \(\sum_y r(y)\lambda_y\), subject to the decomposition's convexity or multiplicity constraints. Stable identifiers must associate each stored column with its originating \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each oracle object maps deterministically to its master coefficients, cost, reconstruction data, and stable identifier, preserving linking constraints and objective contributions under aggregation.

children.title: Dual-Price Normalization
children.top_down_role: Scaling choices for prices exchanged between master, oracle components.

assumptions_latex: A master row is \(a^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq b\) with dual multiplier \(\pi\geq0\).
The row is rescaled by a factor \(\tau>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Using \(\pi'=\pi/\tau\) for the rescaled row leaves every reduced cost unchanged.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive row scaling and the corresponding invariant dual-price transformation.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Lagrangian Relaxation and Dual Formulation p. 45
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Normalize the master row \(a^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq b\) by replacing it with \((\tau a)^{\mathsf T}\lambda\geq\tau b\), where \(\tau>0\). If \(\pi\geq0\) is the multiplier for the original row, the normalized multiplier is \(\pi'=\pi/\tau\). For a candidate column with row coefficient \(a_y\) and cost \(c_y\), the normalized reduced cost satisfies \(c_y-(\tau a_y)\pi'=c_y-a_y\pi\). Hence dual prices passed to an oracle must be transformed inversely to row scaling; normalization metadata must include row order, sense, and scaling so the oracle reproduces this invariant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When a master row is multiplied by a positive factor, divide its dual price by that factor. This preserves every column's reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Normalization

source_witnesses.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

children.title: Dual-Price Sign Conventions
children.top_down_role: Sign orientation across constraint senses, solver APIs, pricing logic.

assumptions_latex: The primal master is a minimization problem.
Dual prices are defined using the displayed Lagrangian convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sign domain of each canonical price and its contribution to reduced cost are determined by the associated row sense.

notation.meaning: column j of the master constraint matrix

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lagrangian sign representation for minimization-master dual prices and reduced costs.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Lagrangian Relaxation and Dual Formulation p. 45
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization master, represent a row \(A_i\lambda\geq b_i\) in the Lagrangian by \(\pi_i(b_i-A_i\lambda)\) with \(\pi_i\geq0\). Represent a row \(A_i\lambda\leq b_i\) by \(\pi_i(b_i-A_i\lambda)\) with \(\pi_i\leq0\), and permit \(\pi_i\in\mathbb R\) for an equality row. With these conventions, column \(j\) has reduced cost \(\bar c_j=c_j-A_{\bullet j}^{\mathsf T}\pi\). An interface using solver-reported multipliers must convert them to this canonical representation before pricing; the row sense and any solver-specific sign conversion are part of the interface state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a minimization master, greater-than rows have nonnegative canonical prices, less-than rows have nonpositive canonical prices, and equality-row prices are free. Reduced cost is cost minus canonically priced column activity.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Price Sign Conventions

children.title: Dual-Convention Mismatch Failures
children.top_down_role: Incorrect pricing or certification caused by inconsistent scaling or signs.

assumptions_latex: The restricted master contains a column with coefficient \(1\) and cost \(1\).
Pricing can generate a column with coefficient \(2\) and cost \(3/2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A sign-mismatched oracle can report no improvement although the candidate's true reduced cost is negative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete false-termination failure caused by reversing the dual contribution in pricing.

source_refs.locator: 3.1 Lagrangian Relaxation and Dual Formulation p. 45
source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the restricted master \(\min\{\lambda:\lambda\geq1,\ \lambda\geq0\}\). Under the canonical convention its optimal dual price is \(\pi=1\). Suppose pricing can generate a column with row coefficient \(a=2\) and cost \(c=3/2\). Its true reduced cost is \(\bar c=c-a\pi=-1/2\), so it is improving. If the pricing interface mistakenly computes \(\widetilde c=c+a\pi\), it obtains \(\widetilde c=7/2>0\) and may falsely certify that no improving column exists. Thus a dual-sign mismatch can invalidate column-generation termination even when both master and oracle solve their stated problems exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-row master has an improving column of reduced cost minus one-half, but a reversed dual sign reports positive cost and can cause false termination.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual-Convention Mismatch Failures

source_witnesses.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming

children.title: Warm-Start Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior solution information across related oracle calls.

assumptions_latex: The old and new solver models have an explicit variable-and-row correspondence.
Transferred primal values and bounds can be checked against the new model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only compatible, validated state is installed; otherwise the target solver starts without the rejected components.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: warm starts require identifier mapping and target-model feasibility checks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validated transfer of reusable solver state between related decomposition models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given source state \(s\), target model \(M'\), and correspondence map \(T\), first translate every referenced variable, row, bound, and node identifier. Discard any state component whose identifier is unmapped or whose semantic role changed. Check a transferred primal start \(x'=T(x)\) against all target bounds, integrality conditions, and constraints within declared tolerances; install it only if accepted by the target solver. Transfer dual, basis, or tree information only through separately validated compatibility rules. Record accepted and rejected components, then initialize unspecified target state by the solver's ordinary initialization. The procedure outputs a target warm start, possibly empty, together with its validation status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Translate state through explicit model correspondences, validate each component against the target model, install only compatible data, and fall back to ordinary initialization for everything else.
knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for the detailed warm-start translation and validation procedure. Standard-field rationale alone cannot establish the solver-specific claims about accepted state components, dual or tree information, and target initialization.

children.title: Basis Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of compatible basis information across master or oracle solves.

assumptions_latex: The source LP basis matrix \(B\) is nonsingular.
Source and target rows and columns have stable correspondence identifiers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A basis is transferred only when the mapped target basis is square, nonsingular, and compatible with target bounds and row statuses.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: an LP basis must be square and nonsingular
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural validation of an LP basis transferred between related restricted masters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Map the source basic and nonbasic statuses to the target LP by stable row and column identifiers. If only columns were appended, retain the old basic set and initialize each new column nonbasic at a compatible bound. For general changes, form the candidate target basis \(B'\) from mapped basic columns and required slack columns. Accept the transfer only if \(B'\) has exactly \(m'\) columns, is nonsingular, and every nonbasic status is compatible with the corresponding target bound. If any test fails, discard the candidate and invoke a target crash or basis-repair procedure. The output is either a validated target basis or an explicit no-transfer status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Map basis statuses by stable identifiers and accept them only if the target basis is square, nonsingular, and bound-compatible; otherwise rebuild the basis.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The square-and-nonsingular basis requirement is standard, but no source supports the full transfer algorithm, appended-column rule, slack completion, status compatibility, or crash and repair behavior.

children.title: Oracle-State Transfer
children.top_down_role: Reuse of caches, pools, internal search state across invocations.

assumptions_latex: An oracle cache entry records the model signature and branch context under which it was created.
A translation exists for every identifier retained in the target oracle.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transferred oracle state is reusable only after semantic, scope, and numerical validation under the target oracle context.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: cached oracle artifacts are valid only under their generating model and node assumptions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer contract for pricing or separation caches, incumbents, and internal oracle state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given source oracle state \(q\), target context \(C'\), and translation \(T\), compare model version, objective convention, row ordering, branch restrictions, tolerances, and normalization metadata. Translate cached columns, cuts, incumbent subproblem solutions, and internal bounds only when all referenced identifiers remain defined. Recheck each transferred column or cut for target admissibility and recompute its objective, activity, and reduced-cost or violation value from target canonical data. Invalidate artifacts whose recorded scope does not contain the target node domain. Solver-internal state without a documented compatible serialization is discarded. The output is the validated subset \(q'\) plus invalidation reasons for every rejected component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle caches and internal state transfer only when model signatures, conventions, identifiers, and branch scopes match, followed by recomputation of target activities and costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-State Transfer

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source supports the proposed oracle-cache schema, compatibility tests, recomputation requirements, serialization rule, or invalidation contract. These implementation-dependent claims require authoritative decomposition-framework or solver documentation.

children.title: State-Compatibility Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Model changes that invalidate or weaken transferred computational state.

assumptions_latex: A state artifact \(s\) was produced under context signature \(\sigma\).
The target solve uses context signature \(\sigma'\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Automatic reuse is permitted only inside the artifact's declared compatibility domain; outside it, revalidation or reinitialization is required.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: solver state is conditional on model structure and conventions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between reusable and invalid solver or oracle state after model changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each state artifact \(s\), define \(K_s(\sigma,\sigma')\) to require all dependencies declared by its producer: stable referenced identifiers, unchanged coefficient semantics, compatible bounds and row senses, matching dual normalization, preserved branch scope, and supported solver-state format. Automatic transfer is valid only when \(K_s(\sigma,\sigma')\) holds. Adding an unrelated nonbasic column may preserve a basis, whereas deleting a basic column does not; strengthening a node restriction may preserve globally valid cuts, whereas moving to an incomparable branch need not preserve local cuts. If any required dependency is unknown, the compatibility value is unresolved and the artifact must be revalidated or discarded rather than presumed reusable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: State reuse ends when required identifiers, semantics, conventions, branch scope, or solver format cease to match. Unknown compatibility requires validation or reinitialization.
knowledge_statements.title: State-Compatibility Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the compatibility predicate and its detailed dependencies are unsupported by any citation. The examples concerning basis and local-cut preservation also require an authoritative state-transfer or solver-interface source.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Oracle Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic coordination of concurrently evaluated decomposition oracles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a master state \(s^k\) and finite oracle set \(I\), dispatch the immutable snapshot \((k,s^k)\) to every \(i\in I\). Oracle \(i\) returns \(r_i=(k,i,o_i,\sigma_i,\varepsilon_i)\), containing generated objects, status, and certified error. Reject stale responses whose state identifier is not \(k\). Validate each accepted object against its oracle certificate, then merge accepted responses in a fixed total order on \((k,i)\). Update the master once using the merged set. Stop the round when all mandatory responses arrive or a declared timeout policy marks missing responses unresolved; output the updated state together with the complete response-status vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate independent oracles on one immutable master snapshot, validate and deterministically merge current responses, and retain missing or failed responses as unresolved certification obligations.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) is finite.
Each accepted oracle object has a validity certificate relative to \(s^k\).
The merge operation preserves validity of every accepted object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The round produces a reproducible master update and an explicit certification status for every oracle.

children.title: Global Bound Ownership
children.top_down_role: Responsibility for bounds valid across the full search space.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Bound Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinator ownership of globally valid bounds for a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z^*\) be the optimal value of a minimization problem. A coordinator globally owns \((L,U)\) when it alone may publish these values as the certified global bounds, every accepted update satisfies \(L\le z^*\le U\), and the published sequence obeys \(L^{k+1}\ge L^k\) and \(U^{k+1}\le U^k\). A lower-bound update must carry a certificate valid over the entire feasible set; an upper-bound update must be the objective value of a globally feasible incumbent. Worker-reported values remain proposals until the coordinator validates and commits them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The coordinator exclusively publishes monotone global bounds, accepting lower bounds valid everywhere and upper bounds supplied by globally feasible incumbents.
assumptions_latex: The optimization problem is a minimization problem with value \(z^*\).
All committed updates are checked before publication.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At every committed state, \(L^k\le z^*\le U^k\).

children.title: Local Bound Ownership
children.top_down_role: Responsibility for bounds restricted to a node or search region.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Bound Ownership
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and ownership of bounds restricted to a decomposition region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem and a region \(R_v\), let \(z_v^*\) denote the infimum over globally feasible points lying in \(R_v\), with \(z_v^*=+\infty\) if none exist. A worker locally owns a bound \(L_v\) when it maintains a certificate that \(L_v\le z_v^*\) and labels the bound with region \(R_v\), state version, and oracle assumptions. The worker may strengthen \(L_v\) monotonically, but \(L_v\) is not a global lower bound unless a valid aggregation or coverage certificate promotes it. Invalidating the region or its assumptions invalidates local ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A local lower bound is certified only on its labeled region and cannot become global without a valid coverage or aggregation certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(R_v\) is a specified subset of the decision space.
The local certificate is evaluated under recorded oracle assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local ownership certifies \(L_v\le z_v^*\), not necessarily \(L_v\le z^*\).

children.title: Bound-Ownership Transitions
children.top_down_role: Promotion, restriction, retirement of bounds as search context changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Ownership Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity conditions for transferring local bounds into global bookkeeping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A local-to-global lower-bound transition is admissible only if active regions \(R_1,\ldots,R_m\) cover the global feasible set and each local certificate gives \(L_j\le z_j^*\); the coordinator may then commit \(L=\min_{1\le j\le m}L_j\). If a region is partitioned into children covering it, ownership transfers to the children and its certified bound may be retained as a common inherited lower bound. A local upper-bound proposal transfers globally only when its associated point is globally feasible. Every transition must atomically record the source owner, destination owner, state version, certificate, and superseded bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bound ownership transfers only with coverage, validity, feasibility, and atomic lineage records; covered local lower bounds aggregate by their minimum.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem.
All participating region and bound certificates refer to compatible model versions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every admitted transition preserves the global invariant \(L\le z^*\le U\).
