children.title: Oracle-Status Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of optimality, infeasibility, limit, failure states to coordinating components.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Status Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conservative aggregation of oracle statuses into a master certification status.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For mandatory oracles \(i\in I\), collect statuses \(\sigma_i\) from \(\{\mathrm{exact},\mathrm{inexact},\mathrm{infeasible},\mathrm{unbounded},\mathrm{failed},\mathrm{missing}\}\) and validate their certificates. Return \(\mathrm{exact}\) only if every mandatory oracle is exact. Return \(\mathrm{inexact}\) if all required responses are certified and at least one has a positive accounted error. Propagate \(\mathrm{infeasible}\) or \(\mathrm{unbounded}\) only when the corresponding oracle certificate logically implies that global status under the decomposition. Otherwise, if any mandatory response is failed, missing, contradictory, or uncertified, return \(\mathrm{unresolved}\). Store the individual statuses with the aggregate status.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Aggregate oracle statuses conservatively: exactness requires all exact responses, and global infeasibility or unboundedness requires a decomposition-valid implication certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(I\) contains every oracle required for the current master certification.
Status certificates use a common model version.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The aggregate status never asserts a stronger certification than the validated oracle responses justify.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source and decomposition-specific implication rules are required. As written, the inexact branch does not explicitly exclude certified infeasible or unbounded statuses that fail to imply a global status, so the aggregation precedence is not fully determined.

children.title: Oracle-Tolerance Propagation
children.top_down_role: Transfer of numerical accuracy information through the decomposition hierarchy.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle-Tolerance Propagation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive propagation of certified oracle errors into a master bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a certified master lower bound has the form \(L=F(q_1,\ldots,q_m)\), where \(F\) is coordinatewise nondecreasing and satisfies \(F(a+e)-F(a)\le\sum_{i=1}^m w_i e_i\) for \(e_i\ge0\) and known \(w_i\ge0\). If oracle values obey \(q_i\ge \widehat q_i-\varepsilon_i\) with \(\varepsilon_i\ge0\), then the propagated certified lower bound is \(\widehat L-\Delta\), where \(\widehat L=F(\widehat q_1,\ldots,\widehat q_m)\) and \(\Delta=\sum_{i=1}^m w_i\varepsilon_i\). Termination must use this corrected bound rather than \(\widehat L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Oracle errors propagate through known sensitivity weights; subtracting their weighted sum from the computed lower bound preserves certification.
assumptions_latex: Each oracle error bound \(\varepsilon_i\) is certified.
The stated monotonicity and sensitivity inequality holds for \(F\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat L-\Delta\le L\), so \(\widehat L-\Delta\) is a valid corrected lower bound.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The weighted error-propagation inequality is internally correct under the stated monotonicity and sensitivity assumptions, and property is an appropriate kind. No inspectable source is supplied for this decomposition-certification rule.

children.title: Propagation-Induced Certification Loss
children.top_down_role: Certification degradation caused by discarded, weakened, misinterpreted oracle information.

knowledge_statements.title: Propagation-Induced Certification Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of lower-bound validity when oracle error is not propagated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the minimization problem with the single feasible point \(x=0\) and objective value \(z^*=0\). An inexact oracle reports \(\widehat q=\varepsilon\) with certified error \(\varepsilon>0\), so its guarantee is only \(q\ge\widehat q-\varepsilon=0\). If the master ignores the propagated error and publishes \(L=\widehat q=\varepsilon\), then \(L>z^*\), and the claimed lower bound is invalid. Subtracting the full propagated error gives \(L'=\widehat q-\varepsilon=0\), which restores validity. Thus any unaccounted positive oracle error can destroy global certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a one-point problem loses lower-bound validity if a positive certified oracle error is ignored instead of subtracted.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon>0\).
The reported oracle value is used directly as a minimization lower bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ignoring propagation yields \(L=\varepsilon>z^*=0\); accounting for it yields \(L'=0\le z^*\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The self-contained example correctly demonstrates certification loss and fits a failure-boundary container, but the evidence contract requires source support or an explicit standard-field rationale, neither of which is supplied.

children.title: Cut Provenance
children.top_down_role: Origin, validity domain, generation context for retained cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal auditable lineage record for a generated decomposition cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a generated cut \(a^\top x\ge b\), its provenance record is the tuple \(P_c=(\iota_c,k,s,o,d,\gamma,\nu)\). Here \(\iota_c\) is a unique cut identifier, \(k\) is the master-state version, \(s\) identifies the generating subproblem or oracle, \(o\) identifies the originating point or node, \(d\) stores the dual vector, ray, or other derivation data, \(\gamma\) identifies the validity domain, and \(\nu\) records numerical tolerances and validation status. The cut is certifiably reusable only while its model version and validity domain remain compatible with the current master state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut provenance records identity, generating state and oracle, origin, derivation data, validity domain, and numerical validation needed for safe reuse.
assumptions_latex: The cut is represented as \(a^\top x\ge b\).
Every referenced state and generating object has a persistent identifier.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_c\) determines the cut's derivation context and the domain in which its reuse is certified.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf, but the asserted minimal provenance tuple and its safe-reuse criterion are interface-specific and have no cited source.

children.title: Column Provenance
children.top_down_role: Origin, pricing context, applicability for generated columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Column Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal auditable lineage record for a generated master column.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a generated master column \(v\), its provenance record is \(P_v=(\iota_v,k,s,\pi,y,r,\nu)\). Here \(\iota_v\) is a unique column identifier, \(k\) is the pricing-state version, \(s\) identifies the pricing oracle, \(\pi\) records the dual-price vector and sign convention used for pricing, \(y\) is the originating subproblem solution, \(r\) is the certified reduced cost, and \(\nu\) records pricing tolerances and status. The column may support an exact no-improving-column claim only if the pricing certificate and every relevant oracle status satisfy the recorded tolerance convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Column provenance records identity, pricing state and oracle, dual convention, originating solution, reduced cost, and tolerances governing exact pricing claims.
assumptions_latex: The column is generated by a pricing subproblem.
Dual prices and reduced costs use a recorded common sign convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_v\) identifies how the column was priced and whether it supports a certified pricing conclusion.

source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

children.title: Node Provenance
children.top_down_role: Branch history, local context, inherited certification for search nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Node Provenance
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lineage and certification metadata for a decomposition search node.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a search node \(v\), its provenance record is \(P_v=(\iota_v,p,b,k,R,B,\sigma)\). Here \(\iota_v\) is a unique node identifier, \(p\) is its parent identifier or null at the root, \(b\) is the branching or partition decision, \(k\) is the model-state version, \(R\) is the node region, \(B\) lists inherited and locally derived bounds with certificates, and \(\sigma\) records node status. A node may be fathomed only when its recorded infeasibility, integrality, or bound-dominance certificate is valid on \(R\) under version \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Node provenance records ancestry, branching decision, model version, region, certified bounds, and the certificate supporting any fathoming decision.
assumptions_latex: Each nonroot node has exactly one recorded parent.
The branching decision defines the child region from its parent region.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P_v\) permits reconstruction and validation of the node region, inherited information, and terminal status.

source_refs.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming
source_refs.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

source_witnesses.source_title: Nonlinear Integer Programming
source_witnesses.locator: 2.2.1 Outline of the general branch-and-bound method p. 15

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited branch-and-bound section may support node regions and fathoming, but not the proposed provenance tuple. In addition, P_v and v are already used for column provenance in this shard, creating an avoidable cross-record notation conflict.

children.title: Cross-Object Lineage
children.top_down_role: Traceability links among generated objects, oracle calls, search regions.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Object Lineage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed acyclic representation linking nodes, cuts, columns, and oracle records.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent decomposition lineage by a directed graph \(G=(V,E)\), where \(V\) contains persistently identified nodes, cuts, columns, master states, oracle responses, and certificates. An edge \((u,v,\ell)\in E\) means that object \(v\) was derived from object \(u\) under relation label \(\ell\). Every noninitial object has at least one incoming derivation edge, every edge joins compatible model versions or records an explicit version transformation, and timestamps strictly increase along derivation edges. Consequently, \(G\) is acyclic. The transitive predecessor set of an object is its complete cross-object lineage and contains every dependency needed to audit its validity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A timestamped acyclic graph links every generated object to its states, oracle responses, certificates, and predecessor objects for complete auditing.
assumptions_latex: Every generated object has a persistent identifier and creation timestamp.
Derivation edges point from an existing object to a later object.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each object \(v\), its ancestors in \(G\) represent its complete auditable derivation lineage.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Increasing timestamps do justify acyclicity, but the assumptions do not ensure that every immediate dependency is represented by an edge; therefore they do not justify the claimed complete auditable lineage. The interface-specific representation also lacks a source.

knowledge_statements.title: Certified Decomposition Termination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gap-based termination certificate for a minimization decomposition algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, a certified termination record consists of a globally feasible incumbent \(\bar x\) with \(U=f(\bar x)\), a globally valid lower bound \(L\), tolerances \(\tau_{\mathrm{abs}},\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\ge0\), and complete oracle-status records. Termination is certified when every mandatory oracle obligation is exact or its error has been incorporated into \(L\), no unresolved status can invalidate either bound, and \[U-L\le \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}.\] The record certifies that \(\bar x\) is feasible and its objective value is within the displayed absolute-relative tolerance of the global optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Termination is certified by a feasible incumbent, a valid error-corrected lower bound, resolved oracle obligations, and satisfaction of the declared optimality-gap tolerance.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a minimization problem with finite optimal value \(z^*\).
\(L\le z^*\le U\).
All mandatory oracle errors and statuses are recorded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(0\le U-z^*\le U-L\le \tau_{\mathrm{abs}}+\tau_{\mathrm{rel}}\max\{1,|U|\}\).

notation.meaning: certified global lower and upper bounds

children.title: False Reduced-Cost Signs
children.top_down_role: Incorrect reduced-cost orientation caused by numerical or convention errors.

knowledge_statements.title: False Reduced-Cost Signs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sign inconsistency in minimization-based column generation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization restricted master with column cost \(c_j\), column vector \(a_j\), and dual vector \(\pi\), define the reduced cost by \(\bar c_j=c_j-\pi^{\mathsf T}a_j\). A false reduced-cost sign occurs when an implementation reports \(s_j\) with \(s_j\bar c_j<0\). In particular, a pricing rule accepting columns when \(s_j< -\varepsilon\) can reject a genuinely improving column satisfying \(\bar c_j< -\varepsilon\), or accept a nonimproving column, whenever the pricing oracle and master use opposite objective or dual-sign conventions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A master–pricing sign mismatch can reject improving columns or accept nonimproving ones because the reported reduced cost has the opposite sign.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge 0\).
The restricted master is formulated as a minimization problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s_j\bar c_j<0\) invalidates any pricing decision based on the sign of \(s_j\).

notation.meaning: reduced cost under the master convention
reduced cost reported by the pricing interface

review_flags: implementation-specific sign conventions require a direct source
no supplied locator explicitly supports this failure boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary and content kind fit the leaf, and the sign convention is mathematically coherent. No cited source or inspectable locator supports the implementation-interface claim.

children.title: False Cut-Violation Signs
children.top_down_role: Incorrect cut-violation orientation caused by numerical or convention errors.

knowledge_statements.title: False Cut-Violation Signs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-sign inconsistency for generated master cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a valid master cut be written as \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\), and define its signed feasibility residual by \(r(x)=\alpha^{\mathsf T}x-\beta\); the cut is violated beyond tolerance exactly when \(r(x)<-\varepsilon\). A false cut-violation sign occurs when the interface instead tests \(-r(x)<-\varepsilon\), or otherwise returns a value \(v(x)\) satisfying \(v(x)r(x)<0\). The resulting separation decision can omit a violated cut or submit a satisfied cut as violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reversing a cut residual’s sign makes separation misclassify satisfied and violated master points.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The cut orientation \(\alpha^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) is fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A violation test is correct only if it declares violation precisely when \(r(x)<-\varepsilon\).
review_flags: implementation-specific residual conventions require a direct source
no supplied locator explicitly supports this failure boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The residual convention correctly characterizes sign reversal and fits a failure-boundary leaf, but no source is cited for the interface failure claim.

children.title: Shared Sign-Error Sources
children.top_down_role: Scaling, normalization, sense-conversion issues affecting both signal classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Sign-Error Sources
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common transformations that corrupt both pricing and separation signs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(z\) be a dual value or constraint residual in the declared orientation. Suppose the producer emits \(z_P=\sigma_P z\) and the consumer converts the received value as \(z_C=\sigma_C z_P\), where \(\sigma_P,\sigma_C\in\{-1,1\}\). The composed interface preserves the declared orientation exactly when \(\sigma_C\sigma_P=1\); it reverses the orientation when \(\sigma_C\sigma_P=-1\). Uncoordinated objective-sense reversal, inequality normalization, dual-variable negation, or row multiplication by \(-1\) can therefore reverse both reduced-cost and cut-violation classifications.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing and separation signs are corrupted when the producer’s and consumer’s sign conversions compose to a reversal rather than preserving the declared orientation.
assumptions_latex: Master and oracle exchange signed dual or residual quantities.
Each producer and consumer uses a fixed sign-conversion convention.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Correct sign classification requires \(\sigma_C\sigma_P=1\).
review_flags: direct source for interface sign normalization remains required

knowledge_statements.title: Inconsistent Master–Oracle Tolerances
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tolerance gaps that invalidate decomposition stopping decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(v(x)\ge0\) denote the magnitude of an omitted cut violation or of a column's improving reduced cost. Suppose the master requires corrective information whenever \(v(x)>\varepsilon_M\), while the oracle returns it only when \(v(x)>\varepsilon_O\). If \(\varepsilon_O>\varepsilon_M\), every value in \((\varepsilon_M,\varepsilon_O]\) forms a blind band: the master regards correction as necessary, but the oracle returns none. Declaring convergence from an empty oracle response is therefore invalid unless the stopping tolerance is at least \(\varepsilon_O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the oracle’s reporting tolerance exceeds the master’s acceptance tolerance, an unresolved blind band can cause false convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(0\le\varepsilon_M<\varepsilon_O\).
The oracle response is complete above \(\varepsilon_O\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An empty oracle response certifies only \(v(x)\le\varepsilon_O\), not \(v(x)\le\varepsilon_M\).
review_flags: supplied decomposition locators do not identify tolerance contracts

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The blind-band argument is precise and fits the failure-boundary container, but the master–oracle tolerance contract has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Stale Cut State
children.top_down_role: Cuts retained beyond their valid model or search context.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Cut State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut processing against a mismatched model snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_k\) be the feasible region and variable mapping recorded when a cut \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_k\) is generated, and let \(S_\ell\) be the state in which it is installed. The cut state is stale when its coefficients, locality scope, or variable identifiers are interpreted using state \(\ell\ne k\) without a validity-preserving translation. Installation is unsafe if there exists \(x\in S_\ell\) with \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x<b_k\), because the stale cut then excludes a feasible point of the receiving state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut becomes unsafe when installed under a different model state without translating coefficients, variable identities, or locality scope.
assumptions_latex: The generated cut is valid for \(S_k\).
State changes may alter mappings, bounds, or local scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Safety in state \(\ell\) requires \(a_k^{\mathsf T}x\ge b_k\) for every \(x\in S_\ell\).
review_flags: stateful cut-management boundary needs a direct solver or algorithm source
supplied locators do not address stale-state handling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The validity condition fits stale cut state, but the state, mapping, and locality behavior is implementation-specific and unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Stale Column State
children.top_down_role: Columns retained with obsolete pricing, indexing, applicability information.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Column State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pricing or classification using inconsistent restricted-master states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\pi_k\) be the dual vector of restricted-master state \(M_k\), and suppose a column \((a_j,c_j)\) satisfies \(c_j-\pi_k^{\mathsf T}a_j< -\varepsilon\). After the master changes to \(M_\ell\), its current reduced cost is \(c_j-\pi_\ell^{\mathsf T}a_j\). The column state is stale when the classification computed under \(M_k\) is reused as a classification under \(M_\ell\) without recomputation. The classifications can differ, although inserting a structurally valid nonimproving column is not by itself invalid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A column classified as improving using old duals may have a different classification after the restricted master changes; this does not by itself make insertion invalid.
assumptions_latex: \(\varepsilon\ge0\).
The column remains structurally representable in \(M_\ell\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any decision that requires the column's current improvement classification must use \(c_j-\pi_\ell^{\mathsf T}a_j\), not the cached value from \(M_k\).

notation.meaning: dual vectors for the respective states

review_flags: direct source for stale pricing classifications remains required

children.title: Stale Branching State
children.top_down_role: Branch metadata inconsistent with the active search region.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale Branching State
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle work consumed under obsolete branch-node restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let branch node \(u\) have feasible set \(S_u=S\cap B_u\), and let descendant node \(v\) have \(S_v=S_u\cap B_v\). An oracle response computed at \(u\) has stale branching state when it is consumed at \(v\) without checking the restrictions, validity scope, and representation active at \(v\). A returned primal object \(z\) is inadmissible at \(v\) when \(z\notin S_v\). An inequality valid on all of \(S_u\) remains valid on \(S_v\subseteq S_u\), but it may still be unusable if its recorded locality excludes \(v\) or its variable representation is incompatible with the receiving state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An ancestor-node result must be checked against the descendant’s active restrictions, recorded locality, and representation; ancestor validity alone does not establish that every returned object is admissible there.
assumptions_latex: \(v\) is a descendant of \(u\).
Oracle responses may contain primal objects or scoped inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A primal response may be consumed at \(v\) only if it belongs to \(S_v\); an inequality additionally requires a scope containing \(v\) and a representation compatible with the state at \(v\).

notation.meaning: branching restrictions used to define the node domains

review_flags: direct source for node-local oracle reuse remains required

children.title: Cross-State Synchronization Failures
children.top_down_role: Inconsistent lifecycle updates across cuts, columns, branch records.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-State Synchronization Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incoherent combinations of independently versioned decomposition state.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent committed decomposition state at version \(k\) by \(D_k=(C_k,P_k,B_k)\), where the components are the active cuts, columns, and branching restrictions. A consumer snapshot \(\widehat D=(C_i,P_j,B_m)\) is coherent if it equals some committed \(D_k\), or if declared compatibility invariants certify that the mixed component versions define one valid model interpretation. A cross-state synchronization failure occurs when neither condition holds. Feasibility, reduced-cost, and validity tests based on such an incoherent snapshot need not correspond to any committed decomposition state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixture of cut, column, and branching versions is a synchronization failure when it is neither a committed state nor a combination certified as compatible.
assumptions_latex: Each state component carries a committed version identifier.
Declared compatibility invariants, when used, are checked before consumption.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The snapshot \(\widehat D\) is consumable only if it equals a committed \(D_k\) or satisfies the declared cross-version compatibility invariants.

notation.meaning: committed decomposition state at version k
state snapshot observed by a consumer

review_flags: made the coherence criterion internally consistent
direct implementation source for cross-state synchronization remains required

children.title: Callback Scope Errors
children.top_down_role: Operations issued from solver contexts that do not permit them.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Scope Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Invoking solver operations outside their permitted callback contexts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\) be the set of callback contexts and \(A(q)\) the solver operations permitted in context \(q\in Q\). A callback scope error occurs when a decomposition callback invoked in context \(q\) requests an operation \(o\notin A(q)\), such as submitting a node-local cut through a global-cut interface or querying unavailable relaxation data. Even if the underlying mathematical object is valid, the callback action is inadmissible because its lifetime, locality, or solver-state requirements are not satisfied in \(q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mathematically valid decomposition action still fails when invoked in a callback context that does not permit its scope or lifetime.
assumptions_latex: Every callback invocation has a well-defined context \(q\).
The solver specifies an admissible-operation set \(A(q)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Callback execution is scope-correct only if every requested operation belongs to \(A(q)\).
review_flags: callback permissions are solver-specific and require API documentation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The abstract permitted-operation formulation fits the callback-scope failure leaf, but callback permissions are solver-specific and no API documentation or locator is supplied.

children.title: Callback Validity Errors
children.top_down_role: Objects submitted outside their legitimate model or search domain.

knowledge_statements.title: Callback Validity Errors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Submitting callback inequalities invalid for the required feasible region.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_q\) be the feasible region on which callback context \(q\) requires a submitted inequality \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) to be valid. A callback validity error occurs when there exists \(x\in S_q\) such that \(a^{\mathsf T}x<\beta\). For a globally scoped cut, \(S_q\) is the global feasible set; for a node-local cut, it is the specified node domain. Such an error can exclude a feasible solution independently of whether the inequality separates the current relaxation point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback cut is invalid if it excludes any feasible point in the global or node-local region required by its submission scope.
assumptions_latex: The callback declares a global or node-local validity scope.
The submitted inequality is intended to restrict the relaxation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible submission requires \(a^{\mathsf T}x\ge\beta\) for every \(x\in S_q\).

notation.meaning: feasible region required by callback context q
coefficient vector and right-hand side of the submitted inequality

review_flags: repaired malformed LaTeX and defined the inequality
solver-specific global and local validity rules require a direct source

children.title: Context-Dependent Callback Admissibility
children.top_down_role: Differences in permissible actions across relaxation, incumbent, node contexts.

knowledge_statements.title: Context-Dependent Callback Admissibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal admissibility predicate for decomposition callback actions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For callback context \(q\), let \(A(q)\) be the permitted operation set, \(S_q\) the required validity domain, and \(L(q)\) the data and object lifetimes available in that context. A decomposition action \(d\) is admissible in \(q\) exactly when its operation belongs to \(A(q)\), every submitted inequality is valid for every \(x\in S_q\), every submitted column conforms to the current model and branching schema, and every datum read or retained by \(d\) belongs to \(L(q)\). Thus admissibility depends on both the mathematical object and its invocation context.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A callback action is admissible only when its operation, validity domain, model schema, data access, and object lifetime all match the current context.
assumptions_latex: The solver specifies \(A(q)\), \(S_q\), and \(L(q)\) for each context.
The decomposition action has declared inputs, outputs, and requested operations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The action \(d\) is callback-admissible in \(q\) if and only if all operation, validity, schema, access, and lifetime conditions hold.

notation.meaning: available data and valid object lifetimes

review_flags: repaired malformed notation and removed the undefined action relation
grounding in solver callback specifications remains required
